findings.title: No 'update from source' and no staleness signal: edited parts never reach the assembly, and re-insert silently creates a second snapshot
findings.lines: assembly.py:377-395 (snapshot keyed by sha+object), 899-911 (inspect source/policy fields), 603-619 (cascade removal of joints on delete), 738-741 and 894-896 (in-document tamper signal only), 745-757 (validation checks references on suppressed joints too); ui.py:911 (only policy hint), 1787-1793 (tooltip id only); docs/assembly-workflow/WORKFLOW.md:9, 48
findings.evidence: EXP3: after rewriting block.FCStd (sha 7e64… -> 8c47…), inspect still reports solver_status 'solved' and every instance keeps sha 7e64…; inserting again created EmbeddedPart001 and a new instance 'Fresh' while Base/Fastened/Rotor kept the old geometry and joints. No ui.py code reads `source`/`sha256`; the words 'source', 'snapshot' or 'update' never appear in the assembly history or status.
findings.scenario: Kurt changes a hole position in the bracket Part Studio, saves, switches to the assembly and expects the bracket to update (SolidWorks/Onshape behaviour). Nothing changes and nothing says why. To update he must delete the occurrence (which cascades its joints), re-insert, re-ground and re-create joints.
findings.consequence: The documented policy is defensible for portability, but it is invisible in the UI, and the manual update path destroys joints. This is the biggest expectation gap for a mainstream-CAD user.
findings.reproduction: exp_assembly.py EXP3; or GUI: insert a part, edit and save its source, observe no change and no indicator.
findings.proposed_change: Phase 1 (S): surface the policy. Instance tooltip/row: 'from bracket.FCStd · Body · snapshot'; add a READ op `assembly_source_status` that hashes SourcePath on explicit command/open only (keeps the 'no idle source reads' invariant, assembly.py:702-712) and marks rows ' · source changed' with a status line 'N occurrences have newer sources · Update'. Phase 2 (M-L): `replace_assembly_source` ASSEMBLY op: read the source via _source_document, build the new EmbeddedPart, `setLink` every App::Link that used the old snapshot, keep placements, remove the orphaned snapshot, `solve`; joints referencing FaceN/EdgeN that no longer resolve are reported by validation_errors (assembly.py:751-755 'Broken or unsupported joint reference') and left suppressed for re-pick rather than deleted. Expose both in the Assembly bar ('Update') and the history context menu.
findings.risk: medium-high: OCCT topological naming across source edits; keep origin-referenced joints stable and document FaceN fragility.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_assembly.py: insert, modify source, `replace_assembly_source` -> occurrences report new sha, placements equal, origin-referenced joints still solve, FaceN joint reported by name; GUI check that an instance row shows ' · source changed' after the source is rewritten and that Update refreshes the viewport.
findings.refute_reasoning: Confirmed at HEAD. assembly.insert (assembly.py:377-395) keys the embedded snapshot on SourceSHA256+SourceObject, so a changed source file yields a new EmbeddedPart and a new instance while existing instances keep the old geometry; inspect (899-911) reports source path/sha and the literal policy string 'embedded solid snapshots; no external dependencies or automatic updates', but no GUI code reads instance['source'] (grep: SourceSHA256/SourcePath/sha256 appear only in assembly.py). refresh_assembly tooltips (ui.py:1791-1793) show only the id; the only wording about the policy is the Insert dialog's 'Its geometry is stored in this assembly' (911), which does not say edits will not propagate. The finder's probe (exp_assembly.log EXP3, lines 20-25) shows solver_status 'solved' with the old sha after the source was rewritten and a second snapshot EmbeddedPart001 after re-insert. The existing 'embedded source geometry changed' status (assembly.py:894-896, 738-741) detects in-document tampering with the snapshot, not a changed source file, so there is no staleness signal. WORKFLOW.md:9 documents the policy and :48 lists 'automatic source updates' as deferred, so this is a known design choice, which makes 'opportunity' the honest classification. Impact if a user relies on it stays high: the manual update path is delete occurrence with cascade (assembly.py:603-619, joints removed), re-insert, re-ground, re-create joints.
findings.refute_evidence: The finder's claim that the UI never mentions snapshots is slightly overstated: ui.py:911 says the geometry is stored in the assembly; it still does not say that later source edits are ignored.

judge.kurt_would_notice: On the first revision of a part he has inserted: he edits the bracket in its studio (GUI or bridge), saves, inspects the assembly and sees solver_status 'solved' with nothing changed and no flag; through the bridge he could at least compare source.sha256 against the file himself, but there is no replace operation, so he must delete with cascade and rebuild joints.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: The biggest expectation gap: Onshape and SolidWorks propagate part edits into assemblies; here nothing updates, nothing says why, and the fix destroys every joint on the occurrence. They would assume the assembly is broken.
judge.risk: Phase 1 (surface the policy and an explicit on-demand source check) is low risk if source reads stay on explicit commands; SourcePath may be unavailable after relocation (allowed by policy), so the status must show 'source unavailable' rather than fail. Phase 2 (replace_assembly_source via setLink) carries real risk: FaceN/EdgeN numbering can shift on the new snapshot, and validation_errors (assembly.py:745-757) checks references on suppressed joints too, so solve() at 822-827 would raise invalid_assembly and abort the whole transaction; the proposal's 'leave broken joints suppressed for re-pick' needs validation to tolerate suppressed joints with unresolved references or the op must detach those joints explicitly. The 'no idle source reads' invariant (702-712, VALIDATION.md:14) must be preserved.

findings.title: Native saveCopy is the single largest avoidable-feeling GUI stall and is taken by five callers; SaveBinaryBrep/CompressionLevel are untested levers
findings.lines: recovery.py:40-46; core.py:390, 632, 1839, 1898, 2798; extrusion_preview.py:371, 876; ui.py:2854-2877
findings.evidence: recovery.py:46 `doc.saveCopy(str(stage))` on the GUI thread after the 2 s idle gate (ui.py:2861 `not self.responsiveness.is_idle()`) and 30 s/revision gate (recovery.py:40). extrusion_preview.py:876 `evaluator.document.saveCopy(str(worker.snapshot))` for the first exact preview; core.py:390/632 for check/STEP capture; core.py:2798 for Save. Only GUI measurement: 1.30 s median / 1.69 s max on Plate60, whole-run largest timer gap 1.74 s (docs/responsive-modeling-upgrade/IMPLEMENTATION.md table); 250 ms on 20 pockets; probe: 48-68 ms on 12 pockets. FreeCADApp.dll contains the preference strings `SaveBinaryBrep` and `CompressionLevel`; probe saveCopy on the 12-hole plate: default 68.0 ms, CompressionLevel=1 61.6, =0 63.1, SaveBinaryBrep 48.2 ms (reopen volume exact in all variants).
findings.scenario: Edit a feature on a deep-history part, stop moving for ~2-3 s (recovery), or start Extrude on a big part (first exact snapshot), or press Check geometry / Export / Save.
findings.consequence: A 1-2 s freeze that arrives shortly after Kurt pauses, and again when the Extrude dialog is opened; on larger models proportionally longer (PartDesign stores every feature's full solid, so archive size grows roughly quadratically with history depth).
findings.reproduction: tools/run_gui_recipe.ps1 -Recipe bench-gui -Holes 60 -Repeat 5 (reports 'Native recovery snapshot in the GUI'); -Recipe responsiveness-preview (preview_snapshot_gui). Then repeat with the isolated profile's Document preferences SaveBinaryBrep=1 and CompressionLevel in {1,3} and compare recovery_snapshot_gui/preview_snapshot_gui medians; verify archives with tools/native_validation_snapshot.py and the STEP/geometry-check child equivalence checks.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Measure and, if material, enable SaveBinaryBrep (and a lower CompressionLevel) in the app profile at start() (ui.py:4313-4317 already sets Document preferences); prove archive equivalence for `_snapshot_equivalence_state`, `canonical_brep` fingerprints and native_validation_snapshot on binary archives before adoption. (2) Paint feedback before the stall: adopt the S15 paint-marker pattern so 'Saving recovery…'/'Preparing preview…' is painted before saveCopy, and defer idle recovery while the pointer is over the 3D view and a wheel/orbit happened within the last 2 s. (3) Share own-captures: when the exact preview or a check/export captures its own archive, publish it to SnapshotStore on the file executor so the other two paths can lease it within the same accepted key. What cannot be done: moving saveCopy off the GUI thread (live document, GIL) or chunking it (single native call).
findings.dependencies: Measurement on Plate60/deep-history fixture; S15 private pending helper for painted feedback; native_validation_snapshot compatibility with binary BRep.
findings.risk: Binary BRep archives are unreadable by FreeCAD < 1.0 and change byte-level fingerprints (SHA of archive) but not shape-level canonical_brep; verify selector/element-map persistence with UseHasher=false.
findings.acceptance: recovery_snapshot_gui and preview_snapshot_gui medians on Plate60 reduced by a measured factor with identical strict snapshots; new native test: save with SaveBinaryBrep, reopen, strict native_validation_snapshot equality; regression gate: bench-gui 'Native recovery snapshot' median and preview 'Native snapshot on the GUI thread'.

findings.title: Finish sketch runs the managed recompute three times; with two or more native sketch commands the dependent chain is natively recomputed twice
findings.evidence: core.py:1638 `self._recompute(doc)` + `_build_status`, then 1642 `self._commit_sketch_edit(doc)` which, when `doc.UndoCount > editing['undo_before'] + 1 or created` (1170), undoes the native commands (1177-1178), `restore_sketch_content(sketch, final)` (1184) and calls `self._recompute(doc)` again (1186) + `_build_status`; back in the branch 1645 `self._recompute(doc)` a third time and `_new_revision` (1803-1810) runs `_build_status` once more. Restoring content re-touches the sketch, so every dependent Pad/Pocket/Boolean re-executes in the second pass.
findings.scenario: Open the base sketch of a deep-history part (e.g., the Plate60 plate rectangle), draw or dimension two or more things, press Finish.
findings.consequence: Finish takes roughly twice the dependent-chain recompute (Plate60 upstream recompute is 6.5-8.8 s per pass in S10/REVIEW), plus three O(objects) `_build_status` passes and selector/auto-scope traversals per `_recompute`.
findings.reproduction: GUI recipe (sketch-lifecycle or sketch-behavior) on Plate60: enter the plate sketch, add two constraints/lines via native commands, Finish; count `native_recompute` timing events and `observer.state(doc)['recomputed_objects']` sizes per pass; expect two passes each touching all pockets. Headless: same via Controller begin_sketch_edit + two native addGeometry commands in separate transactions + finish_sketch_edit.
findings.proposed_change: Make `_commit_sketch_edit` the single recompute site when grouping will run: compute `grouping = created or doc.UndoCount > undo_before + 1` first; if grouping, skip the 1638 recompute/validation and validate once after the grouped restore (the `grouping_started` draft-preservation path already handles failure); skip the trailing 1645 `_recompute` when the previous pass left nothing touched (check `recomputed_objects`/Touched flags) or fold it into `_new_revision`. Cancel path (1143-1151) similarly runs undo+restore+recompute then 1645 again.
findings.dependencies: Existing sketch lifecycle tests (tests for SKETCH_CREATE_CONTENT grouping, draft preservation).
findings.risk: Build-failed detection must still restore the draft; keep the validation semantics identical (one _build_status after the grouped recompute).
findings.acceptance: Exactly one `native_recompute` event per Finish with grouped commands; Plate60 base-sketch Finish wall time about halves; all sketch history/lifecycle tests unchanged; add a native test asserting recompute count and identical final BRep/history to the current three-pass result.

findings.title: Native Sketcher Tasks dock is unmanaged during managed sketch edits: clipped solver verdict, duplicated accept/close controls (Close commits, floating X cancels), dead title bar, ~25% of the canvas lost
findings.evidence: hide_native_panels only moves/hides the dock: 'elif dock.windowTitle() == "Tasks": if main.dockWidgetArea(dock) != RightDockWidgetArea: main.addDockWidget(...)' (101-105); no resizeDocks, title bar, label or button handling anywhere. docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6): solver line reads 'Under-constrainec 3 Degrees of Free' (clipped both ends), Constraints section ~400 px of white, dock ~330 logical px wide at 150%. validation/onshape-theme-repair/sketch-editor-1440.png (Oct 4): three ways to end the sketch are visible at once: toolbar check/cross, floating 'Profile' box check/cross, Tasks 'Close'; the dock title 'Tasks' shows float/close as two near-invisible dots (x~1958/1985). Source: Tasks 'Close' ends native edit, then tick() sees sketch_lease_needs_finish() and calls finish_sketch() (1246-1247, 1267-1268, 3376-3383), i.e. Close silently commits.
findings.scenario: Every sketch edit; also native feature dialogs (Hole, helix, primitives) that use Tasks OK/Cancel.
findings.consequence: Kurt cannot read the solver verdict he needs most, loses a quarter of the canvas to empty panel, and has a 'Close' button whose effect (commit) differs from the floating box's cross (cancel) with no cue.
findings.reproduction: Start a sketch, draw a circle: read the Sketch Edit line in the Tasks dock; count accept/close controls on screen.
findings.proposed_change: In sync_edit_ui/hide_native_panels when a managed sketch is active and the Tasks dock becomes visible: dock.setTitleBarWidget(QWidget()) (drop the dead bar); main.resizeDocks([dock], [max(340, dock.minimumSizeHint().width())], Qt.Horizontal) once per show; find the solver QLabel (Sketcher TaskSketcherMessages, objectName to verify at runtime) and setWordWrap(True) + setToolTip(text), or mirror its text into KurtShape's sketch box verdict (editor.set_status) so the native line becomes redundant; hide the native TaskView control box buttons (dock.findChildren(QDialogButtonBox)/QPushButton 'Close') only while self.active_sketch() and the lease exists, so Finish/Cancel live in one place; collapse the Elements TaskBox by default. Phase 2: main.tabifyDockWidget(self, tasks_dock) or FreeCAD's overlay docking (Std_DockOverlayAll / View/DockOverlay prefs) so the viewport keeps its width; Phase 3: a KurtShape-owned constraints list in the sketch box.
findings.dependencies: Verify widget names in the live app (offscreen sketch edit crashes on QOpenGLWidget, see experiment 3). Keep native OK/Cancel for non-sketch Tasks dialogs.
findings.risk: Hiding native Close must not strand native dialogs; guard on active_sketch() and restore on leave. Overlay docks change picking geometry; validate with the sketch recipes.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: during sketch edit, solver label sizeHint().width() <= label.width(); exactly one visible accept/cancel pair outside the toolbar; MDI viewport width >= 60% of the window at 1440; docs/sketch-interaction-reliability recipes still pass.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py 96-108: hide_native_panels only re-parents the Tasks dock to the right area and hides it when no Gui.Control dialog is active; no resizeDocks, setTitleBarWidget, label or button handling exists anywhere in src (grep for resizeDocks/setTitleBarWidget/TaskView hits only the history dock at 4324 and the FeaturePanel header). tick() 1246-1247 and 1267-1268 call finish_sketch() whenever sketch_lease_needs_finish() (3376-3383) is true, and finish_sketch (3309) defaults cancel=False, so the native Tasks 'Close' does commit; docs/M1_PROGRESS.md:207 records this as intended ('Native task Close also finalizes the sketch lease'), and it matches stock FreeCAD, where Close leaves edit mode keeping changes. Screenshots hold: circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6, current shell) shows 'Under-constrainec 3 Degrees of Free' clipped at both ends, an empty Constraints box, and the dock occupying ~490 of 2000 displayed px; sketch-editor-1440.png (Oct 4) shows toolbar check/cross, the floating Profile box check/cross and Tasks 'Close' at once, with two faint float/close dots in the dock title. The solver verdict is not mirrored anywhere in KurtShape (grep 'constrained' in src hits only core/sketch_colors, not any label), so the clipped line is the only on-screen DOF readout. What did not hold: 'high' severity. The dock is an ordinary QDockWidget the user can widen with the splitter, Close-commits is undoable and consistent with FreeCAD, and the finder itself rates confidence medium. git log -S shows this code unchanged since the Oct 2 baseline / Oct 13 refactor; commits 24bab02/1f0001e/f57d592 do not touch it, so it is not already solved.
findings.refute_evidence: docs/M1_PROGRESS.md:207 documents 'Native task Close also finalizes the sketch lease' (deliberate). DESIGN.md:224 says 'Native Tasks stay available for operations outside the owned editor framework' but says nothing about managing them inside a managed sketch. theme.py:136 only recolors 'QDockWidget#Tasks'. No test under tests/ covers Tasks dock geometry or button semantics. Bridge-driven sketches (add_polyline/add_circle etc.) never open native edit mode, so the problem is confined to manual sketching.

judge.kurt_would_notice: When sketching by hand he gets the clipped DOF line and a mostly empty right panel on every sketch; he knows FreeCAD's Close semantics so the commit/cancel ambiguity will not surprise him. When he drives the app through the bridge the Tasks dock never appears, so a large share of his daily work is unaffected.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape/SolidWorks user sees three ways to end the sketch, a 'Close' that keeps changes while the Profile box's X discards them (Onshape's X discards), foreign 'Constraints'/'Elements' boxes, a title bar with two near-invisible dots and an unreadable solver verdict; the sketch workflow feels unfinished.
judge.risk: Medium: the cheap fixes (setTitleBarWidget(QWidget()), resizeDocks once per show, mirroring the solver text into the sketch box verdict) are low risk, but hiding the Sketcher task buttons or wrapping Sketcher's internal QLabel depends on FreeCAD 1.1.4 objectNames and could break native feature dialogs (Hole, Fillet) that share the dock; fighting FreeCAD's own window-state restore for dock width needs care.

findings.title: Default tessellation leaves fillets and holes visibly faceted (7 facets per 90 deg, 26 segments on a 3 mm hole)
findings.lines: 231 (only control); ui.py:4311-4336 start() sets no Mod/Part default
findings.evidence: exp2: Part::Box ViewObject defaults Deviation 0.2, AngularDeflection 28.65 deg; Mod/Part group empty in a fresh profile; KurtShape writes no Mod/Part key (grep 'Preferences/Mod/Part' in src: none). exp4 (MeshPart.meshFromShape with the display rule, linear = extents/300*0.2 %): quarter cylinders r=0.5..2 on a 30 mm host -> 7 segments per 90 deg at 28.65 deg, 15 at 12 deg, 36 at 5 deg; r=3 hole in a 120x80 plate -> 26 / 60 / 144 segments per circle. Angular deflection, not Deviation, is the binding limit on fillets (exp1 'limited_by': angular).
findings.scenario: Any part with small fillets, chamfer blends, holes or revolved rounds, viewed closer than full fit.
findings.consequence: Kurt sees flat facets on every fillet (sagitta 0.062 mm on r=2 is small, but the shading discontinuity per facet is obvious under the specular default material) and polygonal hole walls; the preview ghost he just confirmed looked smooth, so the committed part appears to have lost quality.
findings.reproduction: Headless counts: scratch exp4_fillet_segments.py and exp3_display_vs_overlay.py (deterministic). Visual: in the app, fillet a 30 mm block with r=2 and zoom to the edge; count facets.
findings.proposed_change: Standard preset MeshAngularDeflection=12 deg, MeshDeviation=0.2 (plate60 facets 6.5k -> 14.7k, fillet 7 -> 15 segments per 90 deg); presentation 5 deg / 0.05 % (34.8k facets, 36 per 90 deg); draft keeps 28.65 / 0.5. Apply through the preset mechanism in the previous finding; keep export untouched (core.py:2834 is already absolute).
findings.risk: Re-tessellation cost on large STEP imports (hundreds of faces); mitigate by applying lazily per visible object and offering draft.
findings.acceptance: On the r=2 fillet fixture the top rim mesh has >= 15 segments per 90 deg at standard; plate60 recompute+tessellate stays within the existing responsiveness budget in tools/perf (no new benchmark claim); STL export facet count unchanged (30492 at 0.05 mm / 0.1 rad).
findings.refute_reasoning: No KurtShape source writes any Mod/Part key (grep over src: only View, OutputWindow, MainWindow, Measure, Sketcher groups are touched in theme.py/navigation.py), start() at ui.py:4311-4336 sets no tessellation default, and the finder's fresh-profile probe lists Mod/Part as empty with Part::Box ViewObject defaults Deviation 0.2 / AngularDeflection 28.65 deg (exp2_result.json). The finder's own numbers were internally inconsistent (exp1/exp3 report 4 segments per 90 deg at defaults, exp4 reports 7), so I re-measured headlessly with the display rule ViewProviderPartExt uses ((dx+dy+dz)/300*Deviation, absolute angular): r=2 fillet on 30x20x20 and 30x30x30 blocks at 0.2 %/28.65 deg gives 8 arc points = 7 segments per 90 deg, 15 at 12 deg, 36 at 5 deg; r=1.5 and r=3 holes in a 120x80x10 plate give 26 / 60 / 144 segments per circle. The title's numbers are right and angular deflection binds (dropping Deviation to 0.05 changes nothing at 12 or 5 deg; at 28.65 deg it only lifts the fillet to 11). One correction: the consequence's 'sagitta 0.062 mm on r=2' is the pure-angular-step bound; at the measured 7 segments it is 0.013 mm, so the visible artifact is the polygonal silhouette and per-vertex shading banding, not depth error. Export is unaffected (core.py:2834 absolute 0.05 mm / 0.1 rad). Root cause is FreeCAD's stock default that KurtShape ships unchanged; Kurt's live profile was not read, so whether he lowered it by hand is unknown. Nothing at HEAD addresses it.
findings.refute_evidence: My probe scratch/verify2/probe_facets.py + probe_facets_out.txt (FreeCAD 1.1.4, OCCT 7.8.1, 0.12 s, no GUI): fillet r=2 on block ang28.65/dev0.20 -> 7 segments per 90 deg, dev0.05 -> 11, ang12 -> 15, ang5 -> 36; holes r=1.5 and r=3 in 120x80x10 plate -> 26/60/144 segments per circle; sagitta at 7 segments on r=2 = 0.0126 mm. The earlier verifier's scratch/verify/out.txt agrees (7/15/36 and 26/60/144) and shows the preview ghost rule tessellate(0.15) gives 36 per 90 deg and 144 per circle, i.e. the committed model is 5x coarser than the ghost Kurt just approved. Cost from exp3: plate60 6.5k facets at defaults, 14.7k at 12 deg (~0.2 s), 34.8k at 5 deg/0.05 % (~0.9 s).

judge.kurt_would_notice: Polygonal hole walls and banded fillet shading on every part when zoomed past full fit, and a quality drop at Confirm because the preview ghost is tessellated five times finer than the committed feature.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape and SolidWorks tessellate adaptively and smoothly; seven flats on a quarter round looks like a low-poly STL, not a CAD model.
judge.risk: Two Mod/Part keys at startup plus applying to open documents through the B-01 mechanism; the 12 deg standard preset roughly doubles facet counts (re-mesh ~0.2 s on plate60), acceptable; 5 deg/0.05 % is 5x and ~1 s on plate60 so it must stay an explicit preset. Export tessellation stays independent.

findings.title: Controller error details (failing feature, conflicting constraints, ambiguous matches) are dropped before they reach the user
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 656-666 (notify), 702-716 (append_message), 772-787 (native Report mirror), 849, 900, 1328, 1349 (notify sites), 1696-1704 (row tooltip); src/kurtshape/core.py 1310-1332 (_build_status), 1397-1399 (inspect payload), 1856 (preview failure flattening), 2199-2206 (constraint_conflict details); src/kurtshape/general_actions.py 263
findings.evidence: ui.py:1349 self.notify(response["error"]["message"], "error") and notify() appends only str(message) to Messages. Experiment 1 §5: a mutation on a document with an over-constrained sketch returned {"code":"build_failed","message":"Native feature rebuild failed","features":[{"feature":"S4","message":"Over-constrained sketch\nRemove at least one of the following conflicting constraints:1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7"}]}; only 'Native feature rebuild failed' would be shown. core.py:2206 constraint_conflict carries constraints=added; selectors carry 'matches'; build_errors from _build_status (core.py:1327-1328) are never read by ui.py (grep: no build_errors use).
findings.scenario: An upstream dimension edit breaks a downstream feature; a fillet query becomes ambiguous after a rebuild; a sketch gets a redundant constraint from a native tool.
findings.consequence: Kurt sees a red one-liner and a red '!' with a tooltip naming only type·id; he has to open Messages and hope the native report mentions the object, then find it in history himself. An Onshape user expects the failing feature named and selected.
findings.reproduction: Headless: create two conflicting DistanceX constraints natively on a finished sketch, then dispatch any mutation; compare the error payload with what notify() would display. GUI: open a sketch, add a conflicting dimension with D, Finish — status shows the bare message.
findings.proposed_change: In Panel._operation, on failure build the status text from message plus the first detail (features[0].feature + ': ' + its message, or 'N matches' for ambiguous_reference) and append the full error dict (pretty JSON) to Messages; when the error names a feature that exists in history, select_feature() it and put the native status string in the row tooltip (refresh: add state['build_errors'] messages to the tooltip at ui.py:1699-1702). Keep the one-line status short; the detail lives in Messages and the tooltip.
findings.risk: Longer status text; keep it elided with a tooltip.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: after a forced build failure the status names the feature, the row tooltip contains the native status string, and Messages holds the JSON detail. Native test: notify receives message + detail for build_failed/constraint_conflict/ambiguous_reference.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read every error surface in ui.py: the four failure sites (849, 900, 1328, 1349) all call self.notify(response['error']['message'], 'error'), and notify (656-666) sets the status label and append_message with str(message) only; grep for error.get/['error'][ shows no other reader of the error dict, and grep for build_errors in src finds it consumed only by general_actions.py:263 for the saved problem-report JSON. Panel.refresh (1696-1704) builds the tooltip from type·id plus reference_health entries; a native Invalid/Error state only appends '  !' and red colour, while the per-feature getStatusString that core _build_status gathers (core.py 1310-1332, as build_errors[{feature,message}]) is never shown. core.py 1856 flattens preview failures to {code,message} too. OperationError payloads such as constraints=added (core.py 2199-2206 _require_fixed), features=errors (1850) and selector 'matches' therefore never reach the status, the tooltip or Messages. Partial mitigation the finder under-weighted: ui.py 772-787 mirrors the native Report view into Messages, so FreeCAD's own recompute lines can land there, but they are unstructured, not tied to the history row, and absent for typed-only failures (constraint_conflict, ambiguous_reference, open_profile detail). Classification design_weakness is honest: nothing is wrong per se, the information is simply discarded.
findings.refute_evidence: build_errors are already in every inspect result the panel stores as self.state (core.py:1399), so the row tooltip and a failing-feature selection need no new controller work. tests/test_holes.py:125 and test_multi_edge_references.py:570 read build_errors[{feature,message}] headlessly, confirming the shape the UI could display.

judge.kurt_would_notice: When an upstream dimension edit breaks a downstream feature in the GUI he gets a red one-liner ('Native feature rebuild failed') and a red '!' whose tooltip only says the type and id; he opens Messages and hopes the mirrored native text names the object. Through the bridge he already receives the full JSON, so the gap is GUI-only and he feels it most when hand-editing.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Strongly: Onshape and SolidWorks name the failing feature, select it and show the reason inline; here they have to guess which feature failed and why.
judge.risk: Low. Compose the status line from message plus the first detail, append the error dict as JSON to Messages, select the named feature when it exists in history, and add build_errors messages to the row tooltip; keep the one-line status short and avoid selecting during an active sketch edit or dialog.

findings.title: Enter confirms Extrude from its Depth field but does nothing in the Fillet/Chamfer/Revolve/Shell/Plane quantity fields
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 4257-4272, 2176-2181, 2462-2478, 3811-3817, 4203; src/kurtshape/shortcuts.py 225-227; src/kurtshape/feature_panel.py 29-70, 105-108
findings.evidence: ui.py:4257-4272 handles Return only for self.depth.lineEdit(), self.value.lineEdit() and self.formula. studio_tool's QuantityField widgets (2176-2181) get no key filter; feature_panel.py and quantity_field.py define no keyPressEvent/returnPressed (grep). shortcuts.py:226 returns False for any text input except Escape and Ctrl+S/N/O, so the registry's general.accept (Enter) never fires while a QAbstractSpinBox has focus.

findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py eventFilter 4257-4272: Return is handled only when watched is self.depth.lineEdit(), self.value.lineEdit() or self.formula; the filter is installed app-wide (ui.py:230) so it does see Studio spinbox keys but ignores them. studio_tool's quantity() (2176-2181) builds a QuantityField (Gui::QuantitySpinBox wrapper, quantity_field.py, no key handling) and the wiring loop (2462-2478) connects only textChanged/valueChanged. findings.title: Feature suppression is absent; Hide/Show and rollback are the only ways to take a feature out of the build
findings.evidence: history_menu offers Hide/Show, Edit…, Rename, Delete, Feature settings and Roll back/forward only; grep for 'suppress' in ui.py/studio.py/core.py finds only the assembly joint 'suppressed' suffix (ui.py:1789-1790) with no toggle. Rollback is contiguous (studio rollback_index).
findings.scenario: Kurt wants to compare the hub with and without the rim fillet, or temporarily drop a failing hole while fixing its sketch, without deleting it.
findings.consequence: He must delete and redo (losing picks/queries) or roll back everything after it. Onshape/SolidWorks users reach for suppress constantly.
findings.reproduction: Right-click any feature row.
findings.proposed_change: Add a studio operation 'set_feature_suppressed {feature, suppressed}' that marks the representative (KurtShapeSuppressed) and makes studio.order()/_state() skip it during rebuild as if it were beyond the bar (reuse the rollback machinery per feature), native PartDesign features via the native Suppressed property; show suppressed rows struck-through/gray with a 'suppressed' tooltip; expose Suppress/Unsuppress in history_menu and search.
findings.dependencies: Studio rebuild semantics (consumers of a suppressed op must rebind to its inputs); auto merge scope reevaluation.
findings.risk: High in studio part lineage; start with native-Body features (Pad/Pocket/Fillet/Hole) where FreeCAD already supports Suppressed.
findings.acceptance: Native tests: suppress/unsuppress round-trips volumes and is one Undo step; downstream features rebuild; save/reopen keeps the flag; GUI recipe shows the row state.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py history_menu 3950-4003 and refresh_assembly 1787-1790, grep -i suppress over src/, docs/, tests/, tools/, studio.py order/_cutoff/_state/held_part_ids 186-338, _snapshot 454-468, _inputs 1083-1096, core.py 1265-1272, docs/2026-10-03-claude-review/CODEX_PROMPT.md 1619-1693 and 1954-1975, AGENTS.md known gaps. Held: the context menu offers Hide/Show, Edit sketch/Extrude/dress-up/feature, Rename, Delete, Feature settings and the three Roll actions only. No feature-suppress operation exists: the only 'suppress' hits are assembly joints (assembly.py 535-551, 887; ui.py 1789-1790 shows a ' · suppressed' suffix with no toggle), core.py:1272 _expects_shape merely tolerating the native Suppressed flag, document_state tracking SuppressedShape, onshape.py 156-157 rejecting suppressed features on import, and hover/navigation internals. The October 3 plan scheduled a suppress_feature op (Increment 8, Suppressed property, build_failed rejection, undo) and the suppress UI with Shift+U (Increment 12b); neither was built, and the AGENTS.md gap list does not mention it. Rollback is a contiguous cutoff (_cutoff 257-270, _state 273-302), as claimed. Did not hold: the effort framing 'reuse the rollback machinery per feature'. Rollback leaves downstream native links intact and merely reads state up to a cutoff; studio features consume snapshot Bodies bound to a specific output tip (_inputs -> _snapshot with a ShapeBinder on that feature), so skipping feature N requires relinking every downstream consumer of N's outputs, which is the reorder/insert problem, not rollback. Native PartDesign features inside a Body (Pad, Pocket, Hole, native fillet/chamfer) already carry Suppressed and the build-status code tolerates it, so a native-only Suppress is a tractable M; covering studio features (Part::Revolution/Sweep/Loft, booleans, patterns, split) pushes it to L-XL. Kurt's compare use case is partly served today by preview (disposable clone) and rollback, but neither skips a single feature.
findings.refute_evidence: docs/2026-10-03-claude-review/CODEX_PROMPT.md:1643-1645 already specifies the native-only contract (targets must have a Suppressed property and not be script-owned; downstream failures rejected with build_failed and rolled back), which is a ready first increment. Studio features would also need the history row styling to distinguish suppressed from held (rollback) and failed, which refresh 1703-1704 currently collapses into one gray/red color.

judge.kurt_would_notice: When fixing a failing hole or comparing the hub with and without the rim fillet he must delete and re-run the step or roll back everything after it; with scripted builds that is tolerable, so he feels it as friction rather than a blocker.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Right-click on a feature with no Suppress is the first thing an Onshape or SolidWorks user reaches for and misses; they would assume the app cannot do what-if comparisons.
judge.risk: Medium-high for studio features: relinking consumed snapshot Bodies, part identity continuity (KurtShapeOutputParts/ConsumedParts), interplay with the rollback bar and undo. Low-medium for a native-only first step: suppressing a Body's base feature breaks downstream shapes and must be rejected and rolled back as the plan specifies.

findings.title: Exact preview reloads the clone and runs a whole-model display boolean per proposal; Confirm waits on it (7.4 s first / 6.2 s update on Plate60)
findings.lines: extrusion_preview.py:383 (clone load), 401 and 441 (before/after whole-body shape copies), 462 and 472-473 (display boolean), 191-196 (_world_shape copy); preview_worker.py:315; ui.py:2403, 3743 (Confirm gating)
findings.evidence: extrusion_preview.py:383 `_load_preview_clone(...)` per uncached proposal; 401/441 `_aggregate_shape(clone)`/`_world_shape(body)` before and after; 472-473 `previous.cut(shape)` or `shape.cut(previous)` to derive the displayed material. Probe phases on a 12-hole plate (noisy): first 296 ms = snapshot 66 + load 57 + model 58 + material 102; update 235 ms = load 62 + model 59 + material 102 (recompute 1 ms). S10 Plate60: preview_first 7.4 s, preview_update 6.2 s (headless evaluator). The worker reuses one process but still reloads the clone per evaluation (preview_worker.py:315 -> evaluate).
findings.scenario: Typing depths in Extrude on a deep part; Confirm stays disabled until the exact result arrives.
findings.consequence: Whole-action latency to an enabled Confirm of several seconds per depth change on Plate60-class parts even though the GUI stays responsive; the material boolean alone is a full-model cut done purely for display.
findings.reproduction: bench_core.py --fixture plate --holes 60 --sections preview, then read `preview_phase_*` medians from `core.timings` (bench_core currently drops them, see the harness finding) to attribute load vs model vs material.
findings.proposed_change: (1) For pad/pocket (and edit_extrusion) take the displayed material from the created PartDesign feature's `AddSubShape` (world-placed) instead of `previous.cut(shape)`/`shape.cut(previous)`; keep the boolean path for studio-scoped operations where the aggregate matters. (2) Retain the loaded clone between proposals of the same (profile, op, body) and apply the new depth as a forward parameter edit on the preview feature followed by recompute — a forward edit, not the transaction-abort reset that S05 rejected; fall back to a fresh clone whenever proposal structure or the source generation changes. Use the existing fresh-clone evaluation as the oracle in tests.
findings.dependencies: Preview native tests (11 focused) and extrusion-preview GUI recipe; S05/S06 counterexamples as regression inputs.
findings.risk: Retained-clone drift (Touched flags, element maps) — mitigate by comparing material volume/BRep against a fresh-clone evaluation in tests and by resetting on any mismatch.
findings.acceptance: `preview_worker_phase_material` near 0 for pad/pocket with identical material volume (1e-7) to the boolean path; preview_update_ms on Plate60 reduced by load+material phases; exact-preview tests and recipe pass.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read src/kurtshape/extrusion_preview.py:340-520 (ExtrusionEvaluator.evaluate). Per uncached proposal it really does: `_load_preview_clone` at 383 (App.openDocument / clone.load of the FCStd snapshot), `_world_shape(body)` (a full Body.Shape.copy, lines 191-196) before the model at 401 and after it at 441, then the display boolean `previous.cut(shape)` / `shape.cut(previous)` at 472-473 (462 for edit_dress_up), with an 8-entry LRU keyed by the proposal JSON and the clone closed in `finally`. preview_worker.py:315 calls `evaluator.evaluate` per request inside the resident worker process, so process reuse without clone reuse holds. Confirm gating holds: ui.py:2403 `dialog.set_accept_enabled(valid)` and ui.py:3743 `set_accept_enabled(bool(result and result.valid))`; provisional results are built with provisional=True and are not valid (extrusion_preview.py:186, ui.py:3756), so Confirm stays disabled until the exact worker answers. The cited S10 numbers are real: docs/architecture-responsiveness-upgrade/S10-MEASUREMENTS.md rows 75-76 give plate60 preview_first 7377.72 ms and preview_update 6226.69 ms (final medians); the review's own HEAD benchmark (docs/fable-deep-review/evidence/controller-benchmarks-2026-10-17.md:17-18) shows 8657-8715 / 7186-7192 ms under noise. The 12-hole phase split (snapshot 66 + load 57 + model 58 + material 102 of 296 ms) is the finder's own probe and was not reproduced here, but the `_preview_phase` labels it reads from exist in the code. Nothing at HEAD solves this: EXECUTION.md:331-366 records S05 assessing transaction-abort as a resident-clone reset and closing it as no-go (native Touched state persists after abort); a forward parameter edit was never assessed and 'resident-clone reset assessment' is still listed as deferred (EXECUTION.md:184, 217, 292, 329). What did not fully hold: proposal (1) is not semantically free. AddSubShape is the tool prism, so for a pad or pocket whose prism overlaps existing material it differs from the current net material (`shape.cut(previous)` / `previous.cut(shape)`); the after-shape copy is also still needed for the facts and the outline mesh, so only the before-copy and the boolean disappear. Proposal (2) carries the real risk and cost given the strict equivalence guards this codebase already demands (S01/S05 history), so effort M is understated.
findings.refute_evidence: S10-MEASUREMENTS.md rows 75-76 (plate60 preview_first 7377.72 / preview_update 6226.69 ms) and fable evidence controller-benchmarks-2026-10-17.md rows 17-18 (8657-8715 / 7186-7192 ms at HEAD f57d592). EXECUTION.md:331-366 S05 no-go for transaction-abort reset; forward-edit reuse unassessed. Codex notes (docs/2026-10-03-claude-review/CODEX_PROMPT.md:300) measured copying AddSubShape at ~0.5 ms vs 160-250 ms for a 60-hole feature.Shape, supporting part (1) of the proposal.

judge.kurt_would_notice: On his fillet/pattern-heavy parts (Dodec Hub, mallet) each depth keystroke shows the translucent provisional prism at once but the Confirm button and the exact material stay pending for one to several seconds; on Plate60-class geometry 6-7 s per change. Through the bridge he pays the same clone load plus boolean on every `preview` op.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Compared with Onshape's near-instant extrude preview they see a 'Provisional preview · checking exact result…' banner and a greyed Confirm after every edit on anything beyond a simple part; on small parts (~250 ms) they will not notice.
judge.risk: Part (1) changes what is displayed when the tool prism overlaps existing material and must keep the aggregate/boolean path for studio-scoped ops; part (2) needs its own equivalence oracle (fresh-clone evaluation) and fallback rules, in a module whose previous reuse attempt (S05) failed on native Touched-state semantics. Medium-high regression risk for the exact preview, mitigated by the existing fresh-clone tests.

findings.title: Every refresh rasterizes a new grayscale Part icon per body into a never-evicted cache (~217 KB and ~1.5 ms per body per refresh) and re-sets every feature-row icon
findings.lines: presentation_icons.py:20-48 (no 'part' label), 72-73 (unbounded dicts), 107-118 (cacheKey keying + 36 rasterizations), 132-150, 153-156 (clear_cache has no callers); ui.py:1698, 1726, 1737, 1796, 1813; history_model.py:49-51
findings.evidence: ui.py:1737 `icon_for('Part', native=body.ViewObject.Icon)`; 'part' is not in LABEL_ICONS (20-48) so icon_for falls to `grayscale_icon(native)` (147) which caches by `int(native.cacheKey())` (107) into the unbounded `_native_cache` (117) after rasterizing 9 sizes x 4 modes (RASTER_SIZES, 110-116). Probe under the bundled Qt: two QIcons built from the same QPixmap have different cacheKeys; a copy-constructed QIcon shares the key. FreeCAD's `ViewObject.Icon` wraps a fresh QIcon per call, so (if confirmed) every refresh rasterizes anew and adds one entry per body. Feature rows use `obj.ViewObject.Icon` directly (1698) and reconcile compares cacheKeys (history_model.py:50-51), so `setIcon` runs on every row every refresh. S08 measured ~1.7 ms per icon evaluation (1003 evaluations = 1.8 s).
findings.scenario: Any refresh (every operation, status change, bridge request, document switch) over a session of hours; multi-part studios multiply it.
findings.consequence: A few ms of rasterization per body per refresh, QTreeWidget relayout from per-row setIcon, and a slow unbounded memory leak of QIcon pixmap sets (tens to hundreds of KB per body per refresh) in a process Kurt keeps open for days.
findings.reproduction: In the bench-gui or parts-refresh recipe: record `len(presentation_icons._native_cache)` and count `QTreeWidgetItem.setIcon` calls before/after 50 unchanged `panel.refresh()` calls on a 4-part studio; also check `body.ViewObject.Icon.cacheKey()` twice in a row.
findings.proposed_change: Key the native grayscale cache by a stable signature (object TypeId + view-provider icon pixmap image hash, or `icon.pixmap(20).toImage()` bytes) and bound it; in refresh pass a row 'icon signature' (type, failed, held, visible) and only call setIcon when it changes; prefer original art for 'Part' via LABEL_ICONS to skip the native path entirely.
findings.dependencies: parts-refresh GUI recipe (S08) can host the assertions.
findings.risk: Icon staleness if a view provider legitimately changes its icon (e.g., error overlay) — include the native State flags in the signature.
findings.acceptance: `_native_cache` length constant across refreshes; zero setIcon calls on an unchanged refresh; refresh median in bench-gui equal or lower; icons visually unchanged in the recipe screenshots.
findings.refute_reasoning: Code reading confirmed every cited anchor: presentation_icons.py:17 RASTER_SIZES, 20-48 LABEL_ICONS has no 'part' entry (only 'new part'), 72-73 `_original_cache`/`_native_cache` are plain unbounded dicts, 103-118 grayscale_icon keys by `int(native.cacheKey())` and rasterizes 9 sizes x 4 modes, 132-150 icon_for falls through to grayscale_icon for an unmapped label, and `clear_cache()` (153-156) has no caller anywhere in src/. ui.py:1726 and 1737 call `icon_for('Part', native=body.ViewObject.Icon)` per studio part / per non-empty native body on every Panel.refresh (also 1813 for assembly instances); feature rows pass `obj.ViewObject.Icon` straight through at 1698 and 1796, and history_model.py:49-51 compares `cacheKey()` before `setIcon`. The finder's open question ('if confirmed') was settled with an isolated offscreen probe (bundled pythonw, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, private FREECAD_USER_HOME/APPDATA/TEMP under the scratch folder, Gui.showMainWindow, 3.2 s total): `body.ViewObject.Icon.cacheKey()` returned 5 distinct keys in 5 calls, `pad.ViewObject.Icon` 3 of 3 distinct, `Gui.getIcon('PartDesign_Body')` 3 of 3 distinct, while a copy-constructed QIcon shares its key and the same Python object is stable. `original_icon_name('Part')` is None. Fifty `icon_for('Part', native=vo.Icon)` calls took 77 ms and left 50 entries in `_native_cache` (1.5 ms and 1 entry when the same QIcon is reused); each entry holds 28 pixmaps from 20 to 64 px, about 217 KB. A QTreeWidgetItem's stored icon key never equals a freshly read `ViewObject.Icon` key, so `setIcon` runs for every feature row every refresh (the compare+setIcon itself is cheap, ~9 us per row detached; the 'relayout' wording is an overstatement, it is a per-row dataChanged/update). Refresh frequency is one per model-changing event, not per bridge read: ui.py:1359 `_operation` refreshes after every GUI operation and `tick` (1250-1256) refreshes when the revision, document or build status changes; read-only bridge requests do not trigger it. S08 (EXECUTION.md:551-562) already cut the per-solid icon calls to one per body, so the remaining growth is one ~217 KB entry per body/part/instance per refresh, unbounded for the life of the process. Not fixed at HEAD: presentation_icons.py last changed in 4681ddf.
findings.refute_evidence: Probe output (scratch verify2/e11/out.txt): body_icon_distinct_keys_of_5=5, gui_geticon_distinct_of_3=3, copy_constructed_shares_key=true, original_icon_name_Part=null, icon_for_Part_x50_ms=76.96 with native_cache_len_after_50_calls=50 versus 1.56 ms / 1 entry for a retained QIcon, entry_pixmap_count=28, entry_bytes_estimate=217600, tree_item_icon_key_equals_fresh_icon_key=false. Scale: a scripted multi-part build of 300 operations on a 4-part studio adds ~1200 entries, roughly 250 MB, never released until the app exits.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing per operation (a few ms), but his days-long sessions driven by bridge build scripts (hundreds of mutations on multi-part studios) grow the process by hundreds of MB that never come back, eventually showing up as a bloated or sluggish FreeCAD process he restarts without knowing why.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing in a short session; the leak is invisible until memory pressure in a long one.
judge.risk: Low. Keying the grayscale cache by a stable signature (type id plus a pixmap image hash, or mapping 'part' to an original SVG in LABEL_ICONS) and bounding it touches only presentation; the parts-refresh GUI recipe (tools/parts-refresh-validation.FCMacro) and S08 timing harness already cover the refresh path.

findings.title: Managed rebuild re-resolves every selector consumer and recomputes object-by-object across the whole document per edit; studio tip-edit overhead (~1.0-1.3 s) is 5-6x the kernel time and grew with HEAD's query features
findings.lines: selectors.py:1580-1600 (_refresh_feature_impl re-resolves every input), 1624-1672 (recompute: 1666-1668 per-object refresh + doc.recompute([obj]), 1670-1671 whole-document walk); core.py:867-895 (879-885 scope loop, worst case len(order)+1); studio.py:839-851, 854-925 (859-860 all-domain token key), 928-1057; ARCHITECTURE.md:53
findings.evidence: selectors.py:1656-1671 rebuilds every object (`for obj in doc.Objects: rebuild(obj)`) with `_refresh_feature` for each consumer and `doc.recompute([obj])` per object when consumers exist; core.py:879-885 loops `sync_auto_scopes` + `prepare_recompute` + another native pass up to len(order)+1 times; `_scope_parts_full` (839-851) does pairwise `_pair_matches` (bbox then exact common volume) for every part x tool. S10 Studio: tip_edit total 1156 ms of which native 193 ms, overhead 963 ms; selector evaluation 367 ms in Q00b. Since 5e9824f selectors.py grew by 497 lines (parameter filters, multi-edge fillet/chamfer references re-evaluated at each managed rebuild) and d95cc2e made studio booleans exact.
findings.scenario: Editing a dimension in a multi-part studio with query-backed fillets, patterns and auto-scoped cuts.
findings.consequence: Edit latency dominated by bookkeeping rather than the kernel on multi-part models; growth with (consumers x objects) and (parts x tools).
findings.reproduction: bench_core.py --fixture studio --repeat 5 at HEAD (lead); compare tip_edit.overhead_ms, selector_evaluation_ms, auto_scope_sync_ms with S10; tools/measure_selector_rebuild.py.
findings.proposed_change: Affected-consumer scheduling: refresh only consumers whose dependency versions (observer per-object versions already maintained in document_state.py:40-48) changed since their last refresh, and keep the full traversal as an oracle under a flag; cache auto-scope membership per (operation, part-version, tool-version) instead of the all-domain token so an unrelated edit does not evict it. ARCHITECTURE.md explicitly records affected-consumer scheduling as not implemented.
findings.dependencies: S06 ordering counterexamples; `_resolve_full` oracle; U2 selector tests.
findings.risk: Missed dependency through global/creator/owner selectors (ARCHITECTURE notes QuerySources/OutList cannot prove complete dependencies) — keep fail-closed full refresh when any query kind lacks a provable dependency set.
findings.acceptance: Studio tip_edit.overhead_ms reduced with byte-identical selector resolutions versus the oracle across the U2 fixtures; reference_errors unchanged; S06 counterexamples still rejected.
findings.refute_reasoning: selectors.py:1624-1672 `recompute(doc)` is exactly as described: inside a transaction it walks `for obj in doc.Objects: rebuild(obj)` (1670-1671), calls `_refresh_feature` for every active consumer (1666-1667), and `native([obj])` i.e. `doc.recompute([obj])` for every object, consumer or not (1668), so the per-object native calls are O(objects) per managed rebuild regardless of what changed; `_refresh_feature_impl` (1580-1600) re-resolves every selector input of every consumer each time. core.py:867-895 `_recompute` runs prepare_recompute + a native pass and then loops sync_auto_scopes/prepare_recompute/native pass; the loop breaks as soon as sync_auto_scopes returns False, so steady state is one extra scope check and `len(order)+1` is the worst-case bound, not the typical count. studio.py:839-851 `_scope_parts_full` does `_pair_matches` for every part x tool, and `_scope_parts` (854-925) memoizes only under a token over every document_index domain (859-860), so any edit evicts every cached membership. The measurements are real and in-repo: S10-MEASUREMENTS.md rows 85-87 give the studio tip_edit final medians total 1155.78 / native 192.98 / overhead 962.80 ms (the finder's 1156/193/963); Q24b and STATUS.md record Q00b selector evaluation 367.172 ms. ARCHITECTURE.md:53 states verbatim that 'affected-consumer scheduling is not implemented' and ARCHITECTURE.md:122 that the S12 summary-reuse probe never reached production. `git diff --stat 5e9824f..HEAD -- src/kurtshape/selectors.py` is +497 lines (parameter filters, group/multi-edge references re-evaluated via `_refresh_group` each rebuild) and d95cc2e made studio booleans exact; the three HEAD commit messages cite test counts only, no benchmark numbers, so 'without new measurements' is true of the commits. One correction: the review itself measured HEAD (docs/fable-deep-review/evidence/controller-benchmarks-2026-10-17.md rows 7-8, 24-25): studio tip_edit total 1343-1463 ms, overhead 1190-1298 ms, tip_edit.selector_evaluation 652-711 ms and auto_scope_sync 444-491 ms at f57d592, noisy but consistent with growth over S10's 963 ms overhead, and showing auto-scope sync is a larger share than the Q24b 20 ms figure suggests. The finding is better classified as a design weakness: a documented architectural gap with a measured user-facing cost (overhead 5-6x the kernel time on studio edits), not merely a possible improvement.
findings.refute_evidence: S10-MEASUREMENTS.md rows 85-87 (studio tip_edit 1155.78 / 192.98 / 962.80 ms). Fable evidence at HEAD: tip_edit.total 1343.4-1462.7, overhead 1190.5-1298.0, native 211.4-236.1, selector_evaluation 651.6-710.6, auto_scope_sync 444.0-491.1 ms (controller-benchmarks-2026-10-17.md rows 7-9, 24-25). Q24b-native-validation-hardening.md:70 selectors 367.172 ms / auto-scope 20.315 ms on Q00b code. diff --stat 5e9824f..HEAD selectors.py +497, studio.py +105. tools/measure_selector_rebuild.py exists for attribution.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Editing one dimension in a multi-part studio with query-backed fillets, patterns and auto-scoped cuts (his Dodec Hub workflow) costs about 1.2-1.5 s per edit of which only ~0.2 s is the kernel; every `set_parameter` through the bridge pays the same bookkeeping, and it grows as he adds more query references.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: A visible pause after each dimension edit in a multi-part studio that Onshape or SolidWorks would do nearly instantly for an unrelated feature; on single-body parts the overhead is ~50-90 ms and they would not notice.
judge.risk: High: skipping a consumer whose dependency changed yields stale native references (the reference-health machinery would report them, but only after the fact); FreeCAD's touched propagation and the group/multi-edge rebinding order must be proven equivalent to the full traversal. The proposal's full-traversal oracle under a flag and the observer per-object versions (document_state.py:40-48) are the right mitigations, but S12's unfinished equivalence proofs show how much proof this codebase demands.

findings.title: No KurtShape build identity: window, bridge capabilities/diagnostics, Messages and STEP provenance cannot name the running source revision
findings.evidence: Help menu offers only "Shortcuts" and "Example" (ui.py 528-531); start() (4311-4341) logs nothing about the source tree; src/kurtshape/__init__.py is a one-line docstring with no __version__; capabilities returns contract/session_id/engine/operations only (core.py 1446-1458, confirmed by headless probe: keys = assembly, contract, contract_revision, engine, geometry_check, import_formats, measurement, operations, preview_operations, request_size_limit_bytes, retry, session_id); diagnostics returns timings/engine/recovery_directory/checkpoint_interval_seconds (core.py 1461-1463, probe); launch-kurtshape.ps1 writes no identity file.
findings.scenario: Kurt launched freecad.exe at 01:28 from a build that predates 24bab02/1f0001e/f57d592; later he or an agent reads docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md (which documents hole/add_polyline) and sends those ops to the bridge, or reports a bug that is already fixed.
findings.consequence: Kurt cannot tell from the window, Messages, a Copy-all paste or an exported STEP sidecar which KurtShape code produced it; agents only discover a stale build by diffing capabilities.operations by hand (this is exactly how the review had to date the running app).
findings.reproduction: Open the app; look at the title bar, Help menu, Messages and the Settings dialog: no version or commit. Send {"op":"capabilities"} and {"op":"diagnostics"} via the bridge: engine git hash is present (App.Version()[7] = 4fd3bf320...), KurtShape revision is absent. Export a STEP and read the .json sidecar: provenance has engine/settings/document revision, not a source commit.
findings.proposed_change: Add src/kurtshape/build_identity.py: at import compute {git_head (via `git -c safe.directory=<root> rev-parse HEAD`, falling back to a runtime/build-id.json the launcher writes), dirty flag from `git status --porcelain -- src`, sha256 over src/kurtshape/*.py + shortcuts.json, engine git hash App.Version()[7]}. Surface it in: main window title suffix (QMainWindow.setWindowTitle in start()), the first retained Messages line, `capabilities.build` and `diagnostics.build` (core.py 1446/1461), export provenance `program` field (core.py ~523), the Copy-all header (ui.py 731), and `launch-kurtshape.ps1 -PrintOnly`. Have launch-kurtshape.ps1 warn (Write-Warning + Messages line via env KURTSHAPE_LAUNCH_NOTE) when another freecad.exe already runs from a different checkout against the same SessionRoot (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process command lines, as update-green-copy.ps1 already does).
findings.dependencies: None; the AGENTS.md workflow (check capabilities before modeling) benefits immediately.
findings.risk: git may be unavailable or blocked by ownership checks at runtime; the fallback file must be written by the launcher and marked 'unverified'.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_runtime_layout.py asserts capabilities.build has a 40-hex git_head or a 'launcher' source, a boolean dirty flag and a src sha256; a GUI recipe asserts the window title and first Messages line contain the same short SHA; export sidecar JSON contains program.git_head. Regression gate: the capabilities snapshot test fails if the field disappears.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read: ui.py 500-560 (Help menu has only Shortcuts/Example at 528-531; the only setWindowTitle calls at 1756/1828 write '<name> — KurtShape'), ui.py 4311-4341 (start() logs nothing about the tree), src/kurtshape/__init__.py (one docstring line, unchanged since b65f066), core.py 1446-1463 (capabilities carries contract/contract_revision/session_id/engine; diagnostics carries timings/engine/recovery dir), core.py 520-530 (_step_export_provenance has engine/settings/document revision, no program field), ui.py 731-734 (copy_messages copies raw text, no header), launch-kurtshape.ps1 (writes no identity file), bridge.py 97-98 (session file carries contract/contract_revision/pid only). Headless probe with the bundled pythonw confirmed App.Version()[7] = 4fd3bf320d95... and [3] = '20260928 (Git shallow)'. contract.py pins CONTRACT_VERSION=3, CONTRACT_REVISION=0 and git log shows it untouched since 559e034, i.e. not bumped for 24bab02/1f0001e/f57d592, so contract_revision cannot stand in for a build id. No docs mention a build/source identity. What did not hold: the consequence 'agents only discover a stale build by diffing capabilities.operations by hand' overstates it; AGENTS.md line 7 already prescribes capabilities as the op inventory, and an unsupported op fails loudly with unsupported_operation, so work is not silently wrong. The remaining real cost is attribution: bug reports, Messages pastes and STEP sidecars cannot name the KurtShape revision, and Kurt must remember when he last restarted (AGENTS.md line 44 tracks 'needs an app restart' by hand). Design weakness stands; severity high is inflated for an observability gap with no geometry or data impact.
findings.refute_evidence: contract.py CONTRACT_REVISION=0 unchanged across the three newest op-adding commits (git log -- src/kurtshape/contract.py: 559e034, 259a61b). Probe output: version[3]='20260928 (Git shallow)', version[6]='(HEAD detached at 4fd3bf320)', version[7]=full engine hash; OCCT 7.8.1. AGENTS.md line 44 lists five separate 'needs an app restart' items for 2026-10-16/17, the manual workaround this gap forces.

judge.kurt_would_notice: He cannot tell whether the window he has had open since early morning includes today's hole/add_polyline/multi-edge-fillet commits without an agent probing capabilities; when he reports a bug or hands an agent a Copy-all paste there is no revision to cite, and a STEP sidecar cannot be traced to the code that wrote it. With four worktrees and agents committing daily this bites several times a week.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: No Help > About, no version in the title bar or Settings, nothing in the export sidecar; SolidWorks users expect a version/SP in About and Onshape users expect the build to be implicitly current. They would not know whether a documented operation exists in the build they launched.
judge.risk: Low. Adding a build field to capabilities/diagnostics and the session file is additive; the one trap is export provenance, which core.py 684/688/727/765 compares dict-for-dict across the job lifetime, so the build value must be computed once at import and never change within a session. git may be absent at runtime, so a file-hash or launcher-written fallback is required.

merged_from.title: Agents cannot tell which KurtShape build is running: capabilities and the session file carry engine and contract only, no source revision; argument tables are not exposed
merged_from.symbol: Controller._dispatch capabilities branch; Bridge.__init__ session file; Controller.ARGS
merged_from.evidence: capabilities returns contract, contract_revision, session_id, measurement, geometry_check, operations (names only), preview_operations, import_formats, assembly, retry, request_size_limit_bytes, engine (probe B1 key list); no build/git field and no per-op argument lists although `Controller.ARGS` has 73 entries (B10). Session file keys: contract, contract_revision, pid, session_id, token, url (probe A9). AGENTS.md:44 keeps a hand-written list of which commits need an app restart; Kurt's running app (started 01:28) lacks hole/add_polyline/describe_dress_up and only op-name probing reveals that. The assistant_client never checks that the session `pid` is alive (bridge.close unlinks the file only on clean shutdown, 120-128), so a crashed app leaves a stale file that AGENTS.md step 1 treats as 'running'.
merged_from.scenario: Every agent session today: read capabilities, compare op names against docs, guess whether a fix is loaded; after a crash, read a stale session file and fail with a connection error.
merged_from.consequence: Wasted probing, wrong assumptions about behavior differences between checkout and running app (exactly the situation this review had to caveat).
merged_from.proposed_change: At Controller import compute `BUILD = {git_head, git_dirty?, source_sha256 of src/kurtshape/*.py, started_at}` (read .git/HEAD and refs/packed-refs with stdlib; fall back to source hash when .git is unreadable due to the Windows ownership check) and return it in capabilities, diagnostics and the session file; add `arguments:{op:sorted(ARGS[op])}` and `required` to capabilities; assistant_client.send verifies the session pid is alive (ctypes OpenProcess) and prints 'app build X vs checkout Y' on mismatch.
merged_from.dependencies: Required-field table from the validation finding.
merged_from.acceptance: test: capabilities.build.git_head == `git rev-parse HEAD` of the checkout under test (or source_sha256 matches a recomputed hash); session file includes build and started_at; client refuses a session whose pid is dead with a clear message.

findings.title: Hosted CI has failed on all 13 runs since the first push (Oct 13): 19 ruff errors at HEAD, native-tests cannot find runtime/test-tmp on a fresh checkout, 12/15 GUI recipes crash on the hosted runner, and README says CI is not running
findings.lines: .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml 36-39, 59-67, 78-81, 143-150; tests/support.py 102-104; README.md 119, 121
findings.evidence: windows-ci.yml 150 matrix: `[interface, ui-refinement, extrusion-preview, sketch-behavior, review-interaction, review-lifecycle, review-copy, messages, assembly, part-studio, step-import, assembly-step, review-recovery, review-startup, bench-gui]` (15) vs tools/run_gui_recipe.ps1 2-4 ValidateSet (45 recipes, none of the Oct 13-15 ones: extrusion-edit, history-lifecycle, everyday-ui, dress-up-edit, headless-open, rollback-history, sketch-regions); lines 81 and 146 `continue-on-error: true`; the workflow file last changed Oct 3 (git log d2e1b35); every packaged evidence file carries `"ci": {"status": "not_run", "reason": "push not authorized", "run_url": null}` (tools/record_evidence.py 61; 20 files under validation/2026-10-03-upgrade); README 119 'S19 does not run native suites or hosted CI', 121 'Hosted GUI rendering remains unverified'; `ruff --version` on this machine: command not found, so run-checks.ps1 36 only warns.
findings.scenario: A commit breaks the everyday-ui or dress-up-edit GUI flow or introduces an undefined name in a FCMacro; Kurt pushes main.
findings.consequence: Nothing hosted catches it: the GUI job runs only on schedule/dispatch, skips the new recipes and cannot fail the workflow; lint has never run on Kurt's machine; no artefact anywhere records a hosted result, so 'CI' is a file, not a gate.
findings.reproduction: Compare the matrix list with the ValidateSet; grep -r run_url validation docs (all null); `ruff --version` (absent); origin/main == HEAD (f57d592) so a run may exist on GitHub, but nothing local shows it.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Generate the GUI matrix from run_gui_recipe.ps1's recipe table (a tiny script `tools/ci/list-recipes.ps1` + a CI step that fails when the committed matrix differs) or run `-Recipe all`; (2) make `native-tests` + `lint` required and keep `perf`/`gui-recipes` non-blocking but visible, and have tools/record_evidence.py accept `--run-url` so published evidence can record the hosted run; (3) `tools/ci/ensure-ruff.ps1` that installs ruff==0.16.10 into the bundled Python (`python.exe -m pip install --target runtime/tools ruff==0.16.10`) so run-checks -Lint works offline; (4) add the stage-2 recipes to the matrix now.
findings.dependencies: Kurt confirming GitHub Actions is enabled on kazzurt/KurtShape and whether a Windows runner budget exists.
findings.risk: Hosted FreeCAD GUI under software OpenGL may be flaky; keep gui-recipes non-blocking until two consecutive scheduled green runs are recorded.
findings.acceptance: A hosted run URL is recorded in validation/ evidence for HEAD; the matrix equals the runner's recipe set (CI step asserts); run-checks.ps1 -Lint runs ruff locally with exit 0; README's 'Hosted GUI rendering remains unverified' sentence is replaced by a dated run link.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml (last changed d2e1b35, 2026-10-03), tools/run_gui_recipe.ps1 1-4 and its $recipes table, run-checks.ps1 32-37, tools/record_evidence.py 56-61, README 119/121, and then checked the real hosted history read-only with `gh run list -R kazzurt/KurtShape` (origin is github.com/kazzurt/KurtShape; HEAD f57d592 == origin/main). The finder's 'unverified' framing is wrong in letter and understated in substance: the workflow has run 13 times since the first push on 2026-10-13 (every push plus the daily 09:23 UTC schedule) and every run failed. Why: (1) `lint` fails with 19 real ruff F401/F841 hits at HEAD (src/kurtshape/core.py:535, reference_tools.py:4,6, selectors.py:1651, ui.py:622, four tests, nine FCMacros); ruff is not on this machine and run-checks.ps1 only warns, so nobody ever saw them. (2) `native-tests` fails on both OS images in ~1 min because tests/support.py 102-104 (isolated_session, added 77af50c 2026-10-04, one day after the workflow) hard-requires ROOT/runtime/test-tmp to exist; a fresh checkout has no such folder (install-runtime.ps1 does not create it and the CI step points KURTSHAPE_TEST_TMP at runtime/ci-local/github-tests/test-tmp instead), so ~25 fixture tests ERROR with 'Native fixtures require the runner's test-tmp directory'. (3) `perf` is skipped on every run (needs native-tests). (4) `gui-recipes` does run on the schedule: on 2026-10-17 3 of 15 passed (review-startup, review-copy, review-recovery) and 12 exited -1073740940 (0xC0000374 heap corruption) on windows-2025 with QT_OPENGL=software; continue-on-error hides this. Matrix facts hold: 15 entries vs 46 ValidateSet entries (finder said 45), none of extrusion-edit, history-lifecycle, everyday-ui, dress-up-edit, headless-open, rollback-history, sketch-regions; 23 packaged evidence files carry ci.status not_run. README 119 'S19 does not run native suites or hosted CI' (blame 4681ddf, 2026-10-13, the day CI started) and 121 'Hosted GUI rendering remains unverified' are therefore false: it runs, and it is red. Classification raised to verified_defect because two concrete, reproducible breakages (lint content, test-tmp precondition) make the gate non-functional, not merely unproven.

He gets no hosted protection for the bridge ops he relies on daily.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Opens the repo, sees every commit marked red, runs `ruff check .` and gets 19 errors, reads README 119 saying hosted CI does not run, and concludes the project's checks are broken or abandoned.

findings.title: Support diagnostics are thin: no crash handler, kurtshape.log only sees unknown bridge exceptions, Copy all and the diagnostics op carry no identity or log context
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/core.py 1461-1463, 1786-1793, 1402; src/kurtshape/ui.py 437, 731-734; src/kurtshape/general_actions.py 268-270; launch-kurtshape.ps1 41
findings.evidence: core.py 1785-1794 writes a traceback to <session>/kurtshape.log only when `not known_error` inside dispatch; the live runtime/kurtshape.log is 2,168 bytes dated Oct 2 (size/date only read); ui.py has no sys.excepthook or faulthandler (`grep -nE 'excepthook|faulthandler' src/kurtshape/ui.py` → none); diagnostics op (1461-1463, probe) returns timings, engine, recovery_directory, checkpoint_interval_seconds; Copy all (ui.py 731, 747-748) copies retained messages only; problem reports go to validation/user-reports (general_actions.py 268-270), which is gitignored and outside any session dir.
findings.scenario: Kurt hits a native crash or a Qt-callback exception during a sketch and pastes 'Copy all' into chat.
findings.consequence: The paste lacks build/engine identity, document ids/revisions and the log tail; a hard crash leaves only FreeCAD's own log; an agent cannot correlate the report with a commit or session.
findings.reproduction: Trigger any exception in a toolbar callback (e.g. a failing `self.operation` path): it appears in FreeCAD's Report view / freecad-launch.log, not in kurtshape.log; run {"op":"diagnostics"} and note the four keys.
findings.proposed_change: At start(): `faulthandler.enable(open(session/'crash-<pid>.log','w'))` and a sys.excepthook that appends to kurtshape.log and calls panel.notify; prefix Copy all output with a header block (build identity, engine incl. git hash, session dir, open documents with ids/revisions, active sketch, worker pids, UTC time); extend diagnostics with build, session_dir, log_tail (last 50 lines), retained_messages (last 50), workers (pids/states), last_failures; add a Document-menu 'Save diagnostic bundle…' that zips kurtshape.log, freecad-launch.log, settings.json, shortcuts.user.json, the recovery manifest list and the Copy-all text into the chosen folder.
findings.risk: Privacy: the bundle contains paths; keep it a user-chosen explicit action and say so in the dialog.
findings.acceptance: A test asserts diagnostics contains build/session_dir/log_tail; a GUI recipe injects an exception in a callback and asserts it lands in kurtshape.log and Messages; the Copy-all text starts with the identity header.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read src/kurtshape/core.py 1458-1463 and 1784-1798, ui.py 430-446, 656, 720-760 and 1287-1312, general_actions.py 255-272, .gitignore 19, launch-kurtshape.ps1 36-47, README.md 75 and docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md 95; grepped src/kurtshape, tools/*.py, launch-kurtshape.ps1 and KurtShape.FCMacro for excepthook/faulthandler. HELD: the diagnostics op returns exactly timings, engine, recovery_directory and checkpoint_interval_seconds (1461-1463), and OPERATION_CONTRACT.md 95 defines it that narrowly ('bounded timing samples and checkpoint location'), so the thin payload is by contract. kurtshape.log is appended only at 1786-1793 for exceptions that are not OperationError/AssemblyError inside dispatch; nothing else writes it. No sys.excepthook or faulthandler exists anywhere in the shell or launcher; ui.tool() at 437 connects callbacks straight to QAction.triggered with no try/except, so an exception in a toolbar callback propagates to Python's default hook (FreeCAD Report view / the --log-file freecad-launch.log that launch-kurtshape.ps1 41 passes), never to Messages or kurtshape.log. copy_messages (731-734) copies messages.toPlainText() only, and no startup message carries App.Version(), a commit hash or the session dir (grep found none in ui.py). Problem reports write to validation/user-reports (268-270), gitignored at .gitignore 19 and outside the session dir. PARTLY REDUNDANT in the proposal: per-document last failures are already exposed by inspect as last_failed_attempt (core.py 1402), and a checkpoint/recovery system plus the review-recovery-crash recipe already handle crash data recovery; what is missing is crash diagnostics and identity, not recovery. UNVERIFIED: the 2,168-byte Oct 2 size of the live runtime/kurtshape.log (I did not stat the live runtime). Classification design_weakness and severity medium are right: nothing is broken, but the gap has a recurring cost in this project's agent-driven workflow - AGENTS.md warns the running app keeps the code it started with, and this very review notes Kurt's app is on an older build, so a Copy all paste without build identity routinely costs a round trip. Effort is S for faulthandler/excepthook/header and diagnostics keys, M if the diagnostic-bundle menu item is included.
findings.refute_evidence: grep -rnE 'excepthook|faulthandler' src/kurtshape tools/*.py launch-kurtshape.ps1 KurtShape.FCMacro -> no matches. docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md 95: '`diagnostics` | No document/revision: bounded timing samples and checkpoint location'. README.md 75 tells Kurt to use Copy all and paste into chat, which is exactly the path that lacks identity. .gitignore 19 'validation/user-reports/'. ui.py 818 'Part Studio ready ...' is the only ready-style notify and carries no version.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Every time he pastes Copy all into chat and the agent has to ask which build is running, which document id/revision was open and what the kurtshape.log tail says; after a native crash he finds only freecad-launch.log and the recovery checkpoints, with no KurtShape-side record of what the shell was doing.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: After a crash or a silent toolbar failure they would have nothing to attach to a bug report beyond the Messages text; Report a problem writes a JSON they cannot easily find (validation/user-reports) and that is not bundled with logs.
judge.risk: Low. faulthandler.enable and a sys.excepthook are additive; the header block must not include anything from runtime/user-data or the bridge token. Keep the diagnostics contract change documented in OPERATION_CONTRACT.md so bridge clients see the new keys.

findings.title: The 'Part Studio | Assembly' combo reads as a mode of the current document but is a document switcher, and the assembly's name is not the document's name
findings.category: assembly workflow / workspace switching clarity and identity
findings.symbol: Panel.make_toolbars (mode_choice) / Panel.set_workspace_mode / Panel.create_assembly / Panel.save / GeneralActions._activate / GeneralActions.tab_manager
findings.lines: ui.py:523-526 (combo + tooltip), 796-838 (set_workspace_mode; switch/create at 807-820), 860-887 (create_assembly; unmodeled branch 879-884 keeps the document label, modeled branch 880-883 names a new document after the assembly), 1804 (features_title = assembly name), 1828 (window title = state name = doc.Label via core.py:1397), 2976-2980 (Save default my-assembly.FCStd regardless of label); core.py:1482-1485 (`new` sets doc.Label from name); general_actions.py:209 ('Active part studio:'), 232 ('Open part studios')
findings.evidence: validation/assembly-step-import/failure.png (Oct 2, dialog structure unchanged since: ui.py:860-887 last touched 10c333ff/eb3baf1 on 2026-10-02) shows document label 'Untitled part' with history title 'Direct STEP assembly'. EXP4 headless: state['name'] 'Exp' vs assembly name 'Exp assembly'. reopened-native-assembly.png shows the status 'Active part studio: gui-solved-assembly-65028' on an assembly.
findings.scenario: Kurt names his assembly 'Hub mount', the tab says 'Untitled part : 1*', Ctrl+S proposes my-assembly.FCStd, and choosing 'Part Studio' in the combo unexpectedly jumps to a different tab (or creates a new empty one) instead of changing anything about the assembly.
