findings.reproduction: GUI: New part (empty) -> Assembly -> Create Assembly 'Hub mount' -> look at tab/title -> Ctrl+S.
findings.proposed_change: (a) In create_assembly set `doc.Label`/state name to the assembly name in both branches (send `name` to the 'new' op as today, and for the unmodeled branch dispatch `rename_feature` on the document or extend create_assembly to relabel) and use that label for the Save default. (b) Relabel the combo as a document switcher: 'Hub mount (Assembly) ▾' listing open documents grouped Part Studios/Assemblies plus 'New Part Studio', or remove the combo and let the tab strip plus a 'Create Assembly' entry in the Document menu carry the workflow. (c) Change _activate's toast to 'Active document: …' and the tab manager title to 'Open documents'.
findings.risk: low-medium; the bridge auto-switch and tool_search contexts depend on workspace_mode, which stays derived from the document.
findings.acceptance: GUI check: after Create Assembly 'Hub mount' the tab, window title, identity label and Save default all read 'Hub mount'; switching documents via the combo shows the document names; shortcut/tool-search tests unchanged.
findings.refute_reasoning: Every cited behaviour is present at HEAD. The combo's tooltip says 'Return to an open Part Studio or Assembly; a new Part Studio opens if none is available' (ui.py:523-526) and set_workspace_mode (ui.py:796-838) does exactly that: choosing the other mode activates a different open document matching that kind or, for Part Studio, dispatches `new` with name 'Untitled part' and toasts 'Part Studio ready · your assembly stays open in its document tab' (ui.py:807-820); only when no target exists for Assembly does it fall through and merely flip the toolbars on the current document. create_assembly (ui.py:860-887, blame 10c333ff 2026-10-02, line 875 touched by 559e034 on Oct 4 without changing the logic) names a new document after the assembly only in the modeled branch (`operation('new', name=...)`, core.py:1482-1485 sets doc.Label); in the unmodeled branch, which is the New -> Create Assembly path, the document keeps 'Untitled part' while the assembly object gets the typed name (assembly.py:107-114). state['name'] is doc.Label (core.py:1397), so the identity label, the window title (ui.py:1828) and the MDI tab say 'Untitled part' while the history header says the assembly name (ui.py:1804); Panel.save ignores the label entirely and defaults to 'my-assembly.FCStd' (ui.py:2976-2980, assembly-save-dialog.png). _activate toasts 'Active part studio: ...' for any document and the tab manager is titled 'Open part studios' (general_actions.py:209, 232). The finder's probe log line 7 reads 'doc label after create_assembly: Exp | assembly name: Exp assembly'; failure.png (Oct 2) shows identity 'Untitled part', tab 'Untitled part : 1*' and history header 'Direct STEP assembly'; reopened-native-assembly.png shows 'Active part studio: gui-solved-assembly-65028' on an assembly document. Classification and severity are honest: a pervasive identity/affordance inconsistency with no data loss.
findings.refute_evidence: Panel.new always names documents 'Untitled part' (ui.py:2922-2924). assembly.create sets only asm.Label (assembly.py:107-114) and never touches doc.Label. WORKFLOW.md:21 describes the chooser as 'returns to a separate Part Studio document', confirming the switcher semantics are intended but unlabeled. VALIDATION.md:18 notes the GUI recipe drives 'the actual workspace chooser', so a redesign must update that recipe.

judge.kurt_would_notice: The title bar, tab and Save default all say 'Untitled part'/'my-assembly.FCStd' for an assembly he just named; the bridge's `new` op lets him pre-name documents so scripted flows avoid it, but the 'Active part studio' toast on an assembly and the combo jumping tabs are visible every session.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Coming from Onshape, the Part Studio | Assembly chooser looks like Onshape's tab kinds; selecting Part Studio silently switches to another tab or opens an empty 'Untitled part', and the assembly they named 'Hub mount' is still 'Untitled part : 1*' in the tab and proposes my-assembly.FCStd on Ctrl+S.
judge.risk: Relabeling the document in the unmodeled branch changes state['name'] returned to bridge clients (low). Replacing or relabeling the combo touches workspace_modes/workspace_documents memory, the toolbar visibility logic in set_workspace_mode, and the recorded GUI validation recipe that drives the chooser (VALIDATION.md:18). Part (a) alone, naming the document after the assembly and using the label as the Save default, is S.

findings.title: Insert reads the saved file; unsaved changes in an open tab for that part are silently ignored
findings.category: assembly workflow / insert and document state
findings.lines: ui.py:889-937 (no open-document/modified check before assembly_candidates); ui.py:910 (dialog text omits 'saved'); ui.py:1819 (hint only before an assembly exists); assembly.py:169-220 (_preflight_source), 304-343 (_source_document copies the on-disk file); core.py:1236-1242 (_modified available); docs/assembly-workflow/WORKFLOW.md:7, 9; NATIVE_API.md:29, 33
findings.evidence: The documented policy snapshots the saved file (WORKFLOW.md:7). The GUI offers the file dialog with the part Kurt is editing in another tab and embeds whatever is on disk; `core._modified(doc)` (core.py:1236) is available but unused here.
findings.scenario: Kurt edits the bracket, forgets Ctrl+S, inserts bracket.FCStd into the assembly and gets the previous geometry; the discrepancy only shows when a hole does not line up.
findings.consequence: Silent stale data in the assembly; compounds finding 4 because there is no later update path.
findings.reproduction: GUI: edit a saved part without saving, Assembly -> Insert that file.
findings.proposed_change: In insert_assembly_part before dispatching assembly_candidates: find an open managed document with `Path(doc.FileName).resolve() == Path(path).resolve()`; if `self.core._modified(doc)` show a QMessageBox 'bracket has unsaved changes. The assembly stores the saved geometry.' with 'Save and insert' (dispatch save on that document via core), 'Insert saved version', 'Cancel'.
findings.risk: low; saving another document from the assembly panel must respect busy/sketch-lease guards (reuse Panel.save logic with an explicit document).
findings.acceptance: GUI check: modified open source -> prompt appears; 'Save and insert' results in the inserted sha equal to the new file hash; unmodified source -> no prompt.
findings.refute_reasoning: insert_assembly_part (ui.py:889-937) goes straight from the file dialog to `assembly_candidates` and `insert_assembly_part` with the chosen path; neither it nor _preflight_source (assembly.py:169-220) nor _source_document (assembly.py:304-343, which sha256-hashes and copies the on-disk file into a temporary document) consults core.documents for an open managed document whose FileName is that path, and core._modified (core.py:1236-1242) is unused here. The policy is documented (WORKFLOW.md:7 'Original files are read'; NATIVE_API.md:29 'Insertion reads a saved FCStd'; NATIVE_API.md:33 'insert the revised saved source explicitly'), but at the moment of insertion the dialog only says 'Its geometry is stored in this assembly' (ui.py:910) and the 'Insert saved FCStd parts' hint shows only before an assembly exists (ui.py:1819). The result is a silent snapshot of stale geometry, and because accepted occurrences never update (WORKFLOW.md:9) the fix is delete-with-cascade and re-insert. Medium severity for a silent wrong-geometry outcome is honest; design_weakness is right since the behaviour is the documented policy, not a bug.
findings.refute_evidence: KurtShape's own save path (core.py:2793-2811) writes via doc.saveCopy to a staged file and replaces the target, so the on-disk file is exactly the last Ctrl+S; the open tab's unsaved edits never reach it. AGENTS.md lists 'inspect does not expose the unsaved-changes flag' as a known gap, so a bridge client cannot check either. No test under tests/test_assembly.py or test_review_followup.py inserts a source that is simultaneously open and modified.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only in a scripted sequence that edits a part and inserts its file without a `save` in between: the assembly embeds the previous geometry and the bridge gives no modified flag to catch it. His usual pattern (save then export) avoids it, but the failure is silent when it happens.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: SolidWorks inserts the in-memory component and Onshape has no files at all, so a newcomer who edits a bracket tab and inserts bracket.FCStd expects the current geometry; they get the last saved one and discover it only when a hole does not line up, then have to remove the instance (cascading its joints) and re-insert.
judge.risk: 'Save and insert' has to dispatch `save` on a non-active managed document through core.dispatch with that document's own revision token rather than Panel.operation's active-document path; the match must compare resolved FileName paths and skip unsaved tabs (empty FileName) and STEP tabs whose import_source is the file being inserted. Saving also rotates that document's .recovery.FCStd and clears its Modified flag, which is the expected outcome.

findings.title: Icons mix four vocabularies (originals, grey native, colour native in history, Fusion standard); fallback weight is inconsistent (0.7–4.5x comparators, ~15x spread overall), not uniformly heavier
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/presentation_icons.py 87-118, 132-150; src/kurtshape/ui.py 1681, 1698, 1726, 1737, 1796, 1813; src/kurtshape/feature_panel.py 15-25, 241-245, 318; src/kurtshape/theme.py 301
findings.evidence: grayscale_icon rasterises the native QIcon and _gray_image keeps luminance only ('result=source.convertToFormat(Format_Grayscale8)'). Experiment: 63 of 104 installed catalog tools resolve to the fallback (out/runtime_catalog_icon_resolution.json). Ink density at 20 px: Hole 0.520 vs original remove 0.188; Use 0.308 vs pierce 0.068; Shape binder 0.382 vs plane 0.119; Coincident 0.206 vs point 0.058; history Fillet 0.412 vs fillet 0.219 (out/native_gray_metrics.json, out/native_gray_vs_original_2x.png). Originals themselves split: solids 0.15-0.23 (fillet 0.219, shell 0.215, modify-menu 0.234) vs hairlines 0.035-0.065 (construction 0.035, axis 0.044, line 0.054) (out/icon_metrics_20px.json). Parts list uses icon_for('Part', native=body.ViewObject.Icon) -> grayscale (ui.py 1726, 1737) while feature rows use obj.ViewObject.Icon in color (ui.py 1698); sweep-dialog.png (Oct 5) shows red/yellow/blue feature rows above gray body rows. feature_panel.py 241-245 uses Fusion standard icons (SP_ArrowDown renders as a green circle) in the otherwise monochrome editor: fillet-dialog-controls.png (Oct 5).
findings.scenario: Opening the Constraints or Geometry menu in a sketch, the More menu in Part Studio, or scanning the sketch bar where Use sits among originals.
findings.consequence: Kurt sees a toolbar where some glyphs are dark blobs and others nearly vanish, menus that look like two products spliced together, and a left dock where the same object type is colored in one list and gray in the other; the editor's only colored glyph is an accidental green arrow.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced headlessly: see experiments 1-2. In the app: sketch -> Constraints menu (all 18 entries are fallbacks), sketch bar 'Use' button, More -> Cut -> Hole.
findings.proposed_change: One rule per surface. Command surfaces monochrome ink; object surfaces (history + parts) native colored type glyphs on BOTH lists (drop icon_for('Part', ...) in refresh 1726/1737 or, if monochrome is preferred, apply the same tint to feature rows at 1698). Fallback: replace _gray_image with alpha-mask tinting (QPainter CompositionMode_SourceIn fill with COLORS icon_ink #51575d over the alpha, then paint into a 20 px canvas with a 2 px inset) so weight matches originals; keep RASTER_SIZES. Generator: raise stroke-width 0.95 -> 1.4 for line-art assets, minimum feature 2 px at 20 px. Author originals for the ~25 fallbacks users meet (constraints family, slot/polygon, Hole, helix, binders, Use, Help). Editor: replace SP_ArrowDown/SP_DialogCloseButton with original 'more'/'cancel' SVGs in feature_panel._icon_button.
findings.dependencies: Finding on ambiguous silhouettes (same generator pass); DESIGN.md 'Shapes' section update.
findings.risk: Tinting hides native icon shading; verify legibility of constraint glyphs at 150% with the contact-sheet script.
findings.acceptance: Contact sheet (reuse scratch icons_sheet.py + native_gray.py): max/min ink ratio across toolbar+menu glyphs <= 2.5 (today ~15), no fallback above 0.30; design-surface recipe asserts every QAction icon in model/sketch bars is non-null and not the 'tools' asset; both history lists use the same icon policy in a GUI check.
findings.refute_reasoning:
The structural claims hold at HEAD f57d592 and nothing has fixed them: (1) presentation_icons.py 87-118 rasterises the native QIcon at RASTER_SIZES and keeps luminance only (Format_Grayscale8 + restored alpha); icon_for at 132-150 falls through to that for any label/command absent from LABEL_ICONS/COMMAND_ICONS, and to the generic 'tools' glyph when no native icon exists (the Help menu button hits this path: no 'help' key). (2) The finder's runtime resolution file (scratchpad area-a-shell/out/runtime_catalog_icon_resolution.json) lists 104 installed catalog tools with 63 unmapped; every listed fallback label (Hole, Use, Shape binder, all constraints except Dimension, slots/polygons, etc.) is indeed absent from both maps in the source. (3) ui.py at HEAD: feature rows take obj.ViewObject.Icon in colour (1698, and 1796 for assembly), part rows take icon_for('Part', native=...) which greys them (1726, 1737, 1813), and origin planes take the original 'plane' glyph (1681) — three policies in one dock; git blame puts all these lines at 4681ddf (2026-10-13) with no later change and no working-tree diff; validation/sketch-presentation/part-studio/sweep-dialog.png (Oct 5) shows exactly this (red/yellow/blue feature rows, grey cube part rows). (4) feature_panel.py 241-245 (and 318) use style().standardIcon(SP_DialogCloseButton / SP_ArrowDown); theme.py:301 sets Fusion, and fillet-dialog-controls.png (Oct 5) shows the green circled arrow beside a grey X. (5) DESIGN.md 'Shapes' documents the grayscale native fallback as the intended policy, so this is a documented design choice, not a defect — design_weakness is the right class.

What does not hold as stated is the headline weight claim. The finder's own native_gray_metrics.json gives fallback/comparator ink ratios from 0.72x (Sketch fillet vs fillet) and 1.04x (Offset surface vs shell) up to 4.53x (Use vs pierce), not '1.5-4.5x'. The top of the range comes from choosing the two lightest originals (pierce 0.068, point 0.058) as comparators. Against the originals' median ink (0.133, n=74), fallbacks span 0.54x (Horizontal) to 3.9x (Hole): the heavy solid-type native glyphs (Hole, Shape binder, Intersect shapes, Regular polygon, native Fillet) are 2-4x heavier, while several constraint fallbacks (Horizontal, Equal, Extend) are lighter than the typical original. The real problem is weight inconsistency (~15x spread, Hole 0.520 vs construction 0.035), to which the originals' own hairline-vs-solid split contributes as much as the fallbacks. Two smaller corrections: the Constraints menu has 19 entries of which 18 are fallbacks (Dimension maps to the original 'dimension' glyph); and there are four vocabularies, not three (originals, grey native, colour native in history, Fusion standard icons). Severity medium stands: persistent bars are almost entirely originals (only 'Use' on the sketch bar and the generic Help glyph break them), so the mixing is met mainly in overflow menus and in the history/parts dock on every document.
findings.refute_evidence:
- Finder's own metrics (scratchpad area-a-shell/out/native_gray_metrics.json) recomputed: ratios Use 4.53, Coincident 3.55, Shape binder 3.21, Tangent 3.08, Hole 2.77, ... Slot 1.49, Horizontal 1.31, Equal 1.25, Extend 1.23, Offset surface 1.04, Sketch fillet 0.72. Originals' 20px ink: min 0.035 (construction), median 0.133, max 0.234 (modify-menu).
- Constraints group in feature_tools.SKETCH_TOOLS has 19 tools; Sketcher_Dimension -> LABEL_ICONS['dimension'] is an original, the other 18 fall back (runtime JSON: Constraints True=18, False=1).
- Persistent-bar audit from ui.py make_toolbars: model bar, assembly bar and document bar buttons all map to originals except Help (icon_for('Help') -> _original('tools')); sketch bar maps all buttons except 'Use' (Sketcher_Projection, grey native). All other fallbacks sit inside More/Geometry/Constraints/Edit menus.
- ui.py 1681 gives Origin planes the original 'plane' glyph while 1698 gives features native colour and 1726/1737 give parts grey native — the same dock already shows three policies; assembly refresh repeats the split at 1796 (colour) vs 1813 (grey).
- history_model.reconcile (lines 49-51) applies row['icon'] verbatim; no later tinting.
- DESIGN.md lines 202 and 249 record grayscale native fallback as approved policy; README line 71 and docs/onshape-design-audit/EXECUTION.md line 7 likewise, so the behaviour is intended rather than regressed. docs/fable-deep-review/ is untracked finder output, not a fix.
- Oct 5 screenshots predate HEAD (they still show toolbar Undo/Redo removed in a558615) but the icon-policy lines are unchanged at HEAD, so they remain representative.

judge.kurt_would_notice: The left dock, every session: feature rows carry FreeCAD's red/yellow/blue type glyphs (ui.py 1698 uses obj.ViewObject.Icon raw) while the Parts list directly below is grayscale (ui.py 1726/1737 route through icon_for). He already lives with it; the validation screenshots from Oct 5 show exactly this and DESIGN.md documents the gray fallback as intended. Interactively he would meet the heavy gray Hole glyph in More > Remove material and the green Fusion SP_ArrowDown in the Fillet editor's reference row. Because he models mostly through the bridge he rarely opens the sketch Constraints menu, so the worst surface (18 of 19 entries are gray FreeCAD rasters) is one he seldom sees. Nothing stops his work; hover labels, menu text and search still name every tool.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape/SolidWorks user clicks Constraints in a sketch and gets a column of FreeCAD's shaded raster icons under a KurtShape chevron; the sketch bar's Use button is a dark shaded block sitting between hairline Construction (ink 0.035) and the Geometry menu glyph. More > Hole, Helical sweep, Shape binder, Part tools look the same way. The feature history being colored while Parts is gray reads as two products stitched together. First-impression damage only: every button still has a usable icon and a name on hover, so they would not be blocked or misled.
judge.reasoning: Sources confirmed at HEAD f57d592: presentation_icons.py 87-118 keeps luminance only (Format_Grayscale8 then alpha restored) and 132-150 falls back gray-native then 'tools'; ui.py 1698 vs 1726/1737 apply different icon policies to the two history lists; feature_panel.py 241-245 use style().standardIcon(SP_DialogCloseButton / SP_ArrowDown). validation/sketch-presentation/part-studio/sweep-dialog.png and fillet-dialog-controls.png (both 2026-10-05, current light shell) show the colored-over-gray dock and the green arrow. The cited out/*.json live at docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/icon-audit/ (untracked, written 2026-10-17 04:08); native_gray_metrics.json and native_gray_vs_original_2x.png contain the quoted numbers. A tiny probe under the bundled python with PySide stubbed reproduced the resolution count exactly: 104 tools, 41 originals, 63 fallbacks; Constraints 1 original (Dimension) + 18 fallback, Geometry 8 + 20, Edit 3 + 14, Part tools 7 + 4; Use is the only fixed sketch-bar button without an original. Honest classification is design_weakness, not verified_defect: DESIGN.md's Shapes section states the gray fallback is intended, nothing is functionally wrong, and the problem is that the stated rule (one original vocabulary) covers only 41 of 104 commands and the fallback renders at a different weight class. Two small overstatements worth correcting in the write-up: the title's '1.5-4.5x heavier' is the upper band; the reviewer's own data has Offset surface at 1.04x, Horizontal 1.3x and Sketch fillet 0.72x (lighter), so the honest range is roughly 0.7-4.5x, and the ratios compare against a nearest-neighbour original rather than the same glyph. Also Constraints is 18 of 19 fallbacks, not all 18. The underlying claim (fallbacks are filled shaded rasters next to thin line art, originals themselves span 7.4x in ink per icon_metrics_20px.json) is visible on the contact sheet and stands. Severity medium: the impact is cosmetic and never blocks or misleads a modeling task, but KurtShape's reason to exist is the shell presentation and DESIGN.md makes icon-only rows the rule, so the icon is the whole affordance on a surface where 63 of 104 tools violate the vocabulary; I would place it at the low end of medium. Effort L is fair for the full proposal because authoring ~25 CAD-specific originals and re-rendering all 75 SVGs with a thicker stroke is slow design work with review; the parts that remove most visible damage (alpha-mask tint in _gray_image, one icon policy across both lists, two editor SVGs) are S and could ship first. Severity is judged separately from that effort split.
judge.risk: Low functional risk: no modeling, bridge or document code is touched and icon caches are keyed by QIcon cacheKey, so changes are confined to presentation. Visual regression risk is real for the generator pass: raising stroke width re-renders all 75 originals, so the contact sheet must be re-run at 100% and 150% DPI before accepting. Alpha-mask tinting flattens native shading into silhouettes; shape-based glyphs (Hole, binders, primitives) may become indistinct blobs even if constraint line-art tints well, so tint should be judged per family rather than applied blindly. Choosing colored type glyphs for both history lists reverses the documented monochrome parts list, so DESIGN.md and any GUI checks that assert the gray policy need updating in the same change. The validation screenshots and the reviewer's audit tree under docs/fable-deep-review are untracked and dated 2026-10-17, so they should be committed or cited by stable path before being used as acceptance baselines.

findings.title: Hover labels drop every single-key shortcut because Panel.tool keeps a tip suffix only when it contains '+' (Fit F, Normal N, Planes P, Insert I, Fixed M, Line L, Rectangle G, Circle C, Arc A, Dimension D, Trim M, Construction Q)
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 445 (tips at 549-550, 572, 586-588, 596-598, 607-608, 615, 620); src/kurtshape/toolbar_labels.py 72-75, 123, 187-190
findings.evidence: ui.py 445: 'self.toolbar_labels.register(button, text, tip.split(" · ")[-1] if " · " in tip and "+" in tip.split(" · ")[-1] else "")' - a shortcut is kept only when it contains '+'. QActions carry no QKeySequence (the router owns keys), so _scan_toolbar's 'action.shortcut().toString()' is empty and falls back to the same stored value (toolbar_labels.py 72-75). Native tooltips are swallowed for registered buttons ('event.accept(); return True' at 187-190), so the tip text 'Fit · F' is never shown anywhere on hover. validation/onshape-theme-repair/hover-label-below-1440.png (Oct 4, current mechanism) shows the label 'Fit' with no '(F)'.
findings.scenario: Learning shortcuts by hovering: Fit, Normal, Show planes (P), Insert (I), Fixed (M), every sketch drawing tool.
findings.consequence: Kurt sees '(Shift+S)' on Sketch but nothing on Circle or Fit and concludes those have no shortcut; the README's keyboard-first workflow is undiscoverable from the toolbar.
findings.reproduction: Hover Fit: label reads 'Fit'. Hover Sketch: label reads 'Sketch  (Shift+S)'.
findings.proposed_change: Stop parsing tips. Pass the shortcut explicitly from the router registry: in Panel.tool add a shortcut_id/keys parameter resolved via self.router.available_actions() (key for 'view.fit' etc.) or accept the last ' · ' segment when it matches r'^(\S+\+)?[A-Za-z0-9\[\]`/]$'. Also set QAction.setShortcut with a disabled context (Qt.WidgetShortcut) purely for display so menus and search show keys from one source.
findings.risk: Menus would start displaying keys; ensure the router remains the only handler (WidgetShortcut context).
findings.acceptance: tools/design-surface-validation.FCMacro asserts popup text == 'Fit  (F)', 'Circle  (C)', 'Show planes  (P)'; tests/test_shortcuts QtRoutingTests gains a label-text case.
findings.refute_reasoning: ui.py 445 reads exactly as cited: the shortcut passed to toolbar_labels.register is tip.split(' · ')[-1] only when that segment contains '+', else ''. Tool definitions confirm the consequence: 'Fit · F' (572, 597), 'Normal · N' (572), 'Show / hide planes · P' (572), 'Insert ... · I' (586), 'Fixed ... · M' (588), sketch tools 'Line · L', 'Rectangle · G', 'Circle · C', 'Arc · A', 'Dimension · D', 'Trim · M', 'Construction · Q' (607-608), 'Normal to sketch · N' (620) all lose their key, while 'Create sketch · Shift+S' (549), 'Isometric · Shift+7' and 'Save project · Ctrl+S' keep theirs. toolbar_labels.py 72-75: no QAction anywhere in src calls setShortcut (grep), so action.shortcut() is always empty and the scan falls back to the stored value; 123 formats 'label  (shortcut)'; 187-190 swallow QEvent.ToolTip for registered buttons so the tip string 'Fit · F' is never shown by Qt either. hover-label-below-1440.png (Oct 4, current mechanism) shows 'Fit' with no key. DESIGN.md 'Delayed command labels' ('show the command name and available shortcut') and docs/onshape-design-audit/EXECUTION.md:8 ('Labels include shortcuts when available') make this a spec violation, not a design choice; the '+' test is a crude way of filtering descriptive suffixes like 'mouse navigation' or 'STEP / STL'. Unchanged since 4681ddf (Oct 13); not fixed at HEAD. Partial mitigations exist (sketch footer lists L/G/C/N, the Profile box button says 'Normal to sketch N', Shift+/ opens help), so the consequence 'keyboard-first workflow is undiscoverable' is somewhat overstated, but severity medium remains fair for ~15 everyday tools.
findings.refute_evidence: grep setShortcut/QKeySequence in src: only toolbar_labels.py reads shortcuts, nothing sets them, so the fallback path is the only path. Tips with '+' that are not shortcuts do not exist today, but tips like 'Show or hide joints · J / H' show the heuristic cannot express two keys either. No test under tests/ exercises ToolbarLabels.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Barely for his own use (he knows the keys and uses Shift+/), but he would notice the inconsistency that Sketch shows '(Shift+S)' while Fit, Circle and Dimension show nothing, and that it contradicts the design doc he approved.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape users learn keys from hover tooltips; here they conclude Fit, Normal and every sketch tool have no shortcut and keep clicking the toolbar.
judge.risk: Low: pass the key explicitly (or accept a last segment matching a key pattern) and guard that descriptive suffixes such as 'STEP / STL', 'mouse navigation', 'undoable' never leak into the label; setting display-only QAction shortcuts must not re-register keys that shortcuts.py's router already owns.

findings.title: Feature editors are re-floated to the canvas corner on every open and the shell layout (editor placement, history width, window/monitor) is rebuilt from constants each launch
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/feature_panel.py 35-38, 123-155 (147-153); src/kurtshape/ui.py 2585-2586, 2678, 3235, 3417-3419, 3473, 3585, 4314-4324; src/kurtshape/startup.py 5-11
findings.evidence: show_compact: 'self.setFloating(True); self.resize(width, height); ... self.move(x, y)' is called by extrude() 3473, edit_extrusion() 3585, start_sketch() 3235, sync_edit_ui 3417-3419 and every studio_tool dialog (2585-2586) after complete_editor() hid it (2678). start(): maximize_on_primary_screen(main) then 'main.resizeDocks([panel], [250], Qt.Horizontal)' (4320-4324); no saveState/restoreState/restoreDockWidget or QSettings anywhere in src (grep). DESIGN.md Layout says editors 'can move or dock left/right'.
findings.scenario: Kurt docks the editor to the right (or drags it off the model) and starts the next Extrude; or resizes the history dock and restarts.
findings.consequence: Every feature opens on top of the geometry at the top-left of the canvas again; the dock width, splitter, Messages height and monitor choice reset each launch, so the workspace never becomes 'his'.
findings.reproduction: Open Extrude, drag the editor to the right dock area, Confirm, open Extrude again: it floats at the canvas corner.
findings.proposed_change: Remember editor placement: in show_compact, only float+place when the panel has never been shown or was floating last time; if not isFloating() at hide, re-show in its dock area (store area via main.dockWidgetArea). Persist layout with QSettings('KurtShape','shell') in the session dir: main.saveState() on close (objectNames already exist: KurtShapeHistory, KurtShapeEditor, KurtShapeMessages, toolbars) and main.restoreState() + restoreDockWidget(editor) after the docks are created in start(); keep maximize_on_primary_screen only when no saved geometry exists or the saved screen is gone.
findings.dependencies: startup.py mixed-DPI note (fetch screen after state changes) must be preserved.
findings.risk: Restoring a floating editor onto a disconnected monitor; clamp with the existing available-geometry code.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: dock editor -> Confirm -> reopen Extrude -> editor still docked; restart isolated session -> history dock width and splitter sizes equal the saved values.
findings.refute_reasoning: feature_panel.py 123-155: show_compact unconditionally calls setFloating(True) (147), resize (148) and move (153) to the canvas's top-left, with no check of isFloating() or the previous dock area. Callers verified at the cited lines: studio_tool dialogs 2585-2586 (addDockWidget then show_compact), start_sketch 3235, sync_edit_ui 3417-3419 (show_compact whenever the editor is hidden or the mode changes), extrude 3473, edit_extrusion 3585; complete_editor hides the editor at 2678, so the next tool always re-floats it. The reproduction is valid because the panel explicitly allows Left|Right docking (feature_panel.py 35-38) and DESIGN.md:188 promises editors 'can move or dock left/right'. grep for saveState/restoreState/restoreDockWidget/QSettings/saveGeometry across src and tools returns nothing; start() (4314-4324) calls maximize_on_primary_screen and resizeDocks([panel],[250]) every launch, and startup.py 5-11 documents opening on the primary monitor each time as intended. KurtShape's docks are created inside start(), after FreeCAD has already applied its own saved window state, so FreeCAD's native persistence cannot cover them. Nothing in 24bab02/1f0001e/f57d592 touches this. Classification design_weakness and severity medium are honest: nothing is lost, the editor is movable each time, but the DESIGN.md promise of a dockable editor is hollow without memory.
findings.refute_evidence: History dock width is clamped to 235-430 px (ui.py 134-135) and reset to 250 at 4324. The monitor reset is a deliberate choice per startup.py's docstring ('Open on the primary monitor'), so only the editor placement and dock sizes are unintended losses. No test under tests/ covers show_compact placement or layout persistence.

judge.kurt_would_notice: During manual Extrude/Fillet/Hole sessions the floating editor lands on top of the model every time and any docking he did is undone; bridge-driven modeling never opens the editor, so he mostly hits this when iterating by hand.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape/SolidWorks users expect the feature dialog in one stable place; a box that floats over the geometry on each open and ignores where it was dragged reads as unfinished, though they do not expect per-launch layout memory as strongly as desktop CAD users.
judge.risk: Medium-low: main.restoreState can resurrect the hidden native Combo/Property docks and toolbars unless restricted to KurtShape objectNames or followed by hide_native_panels; saved geometry must still fall back to maximize_on_primary_screen when the saved screen is gone; remembering a docked editor must not break the compact-height logic that keys off the canvas.

findings.title: Shift+R quality toggle marks the document Modified, re-tessellates every visible object synchronously, skips objects created afterwards, and persists into the file if saved while on
findings.evidence: Lines 229-238: `for obj in doc.Objects: vp = obj.ViewObject ... setattr(vp, name, min(value, maximum))` for Deviation 0.05 / AngularDeflection 10.0 on every object, hidden helpers included; no Modified handling. exp2 (offscreen Gui, fresh profile): Gui document Modified before=False, after Deviation change=True (also True after AngularDeflection and Transparency changes). core.py:1236-1242 `_modified` returns gui_doc.Modified and ui.py:1766-1771 appends ' · Modified' from it. docs/VIEWPORT_ACTIONS.md:49 admits 'Objects added after enabling quality retain their native defaults'.
findings.scenario: Kurt opens a saved part, presses Shift+R to look at a fillet, then adds a feature or closes the tab.
findings.consequence: The document title gains ' · Modified' and close/open guards treat a pure display change as unsaved work; the next pad/hole is drawn coarse while older features are fine; on a dense model every ViewObject re-meshes on the GUI thread in one burst (plate60: 6.5k -> 17.5k facets, ~0.3 s on this busy machine, more on real assemblies). The running app has the same code (file unchanged since b65f066).
findings.reproduction: In the app: open the acceptance plate, note the title has no suffix, press Shift+R, observe ' · Modified'. Headless: exp2_gui_defaults.py in scratch (sets vo.Deviation and reads Gui.getDocument(...).Modified).

findings.title: add_line keeps line-to-line junctions as coordinate dimensions by documented contract; legacy add_line chains still open silently when a junction dimension is edited (add_polyline is the HEAD remedy)
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/core.py 2145-2166 (_add_line), 2174-2184 (_anchor_points), 2285+ (_add_polyline); docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md 42-44; tests/test_sketch_polylines.py 197-213
findings.evidence: core.py:2152-2154 '# Line-to-line junctions keep their coordinate dimensions' with anchors = _anchor_points(sk, lambda curve: not isinstance(curve, Part.LineSegment)). Experiment: after add_line (0,0)->(10,0) and (10,0)->(10,5) the constraints were Coincident(origin), DistanceX 'EndX', PointOnObject, DistanceX 'StartX', PointOnObject, DistanceX 'EndX_2', DistanceY 'EndY'; set_parameter EndX=12 gave geo0 (0,0)->(12,0), geo1 (10,0)->(10,5): gap 2 mm, 2 open wires. A later add_line (10,5)->(0,5) onto a polyline's free end also received its own StartX/StartY instead of a Coincident.
findings.scenario: Kurt or an agent builds a profile with add_line (the only typed line op in the running app; bone-mallet steps use it), finishes, then edits a corner dimension from Feature settings or the bridge to tweak the part.
findings.consequence: The profile silently opens; the next recompute fails with 'Native feature rebuild failed' or an open-profile error, and the user has to re-add coincidences by hand or rebuild the sketch. Mixing add_polyline with a trailing add_line has the same hole.
findings.reproduction: Headless Controller (isolated env): new → create_sketch S1 XY → add_line 0,0→10,0 → add_line 10,0→10,5 → set_parameter S1 EndX '12 mm' → sk.getPoint(1,1) still (10,0). Script: scratchpad/area-c-everyday/exp_continuity.py (§1, §2b).
findings.proposed_change: In core.py _add_line let _anchor_points accept Part.LineSegment too (as _add_polyline and _add_arc already do), so an endpoint within ENDPOINT_TOLERANCE of a fixed line endpoint gets Sketcher.Constraint('Coincident') and only the free endpoint is dimensioned; keep _require_fixed. Document in docs/SKETCH_PLANE_CONTRACT.md and AGENTS.md that add_line joins. Optionally deprecate add_line in favor of add_polyline in the contract.
findings.dependencies: Restart of the running app to load any change (it predates 24bab02).
findings.risk: Existing scripts that intentionally built overlapping separate lines could now join; the DoF/diagnostic guard in _require_fixed rejects redundant cases, so failures become explicit rather than silent.
findings.acceptance: New native test in tests/test_sketch_polylines.py: add_line onto an add_line/add_polyline endpoint produces a Coincident, DoF stays 0, and set_parameter on the shared X moves both segments (gap < 1e-6). Regression gate: tests/test_sketch_polylines.py, tests/test_sketch_arcs.py, tests/test_sketch_planes.py unchanged.
findings.refute_reasoning: The behaviour is real at HEAD: core.py _add_line (2145-2166) passes `lambda curve: not isinstance(curve, Part.LineSegment)` to _anchor_points (2174-2184) with the explicit comment 'Line-to-line junctions keep their coordinate dimensions', so two add_line calls sharing an endpoint get independent EndX/StartX dimensions and no Coincident; editing one does open the profile. But it is not a defect: docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md:42 documents exactly this ('line-to-line junctions keep coordinates'), the add_polyline row (:44) states 'lines included, unlike add_line', and tests/test_sketch_polylines.py:199-200 pins it ('Unlike add_line, a polyline vertex on a fixed line end joins it'). Commit 24bab02 (2026-10-17, at HEAD) added add_polyline precisely so 'editing a profile corner keeps it closed instead of opening a gap', and AGENTS.md line 44 tells bridge users to 'prefer it over chains of add_line'. The finder's 'only typed line op in the running app' is true only because Kurt's running build predates 24bab02; the source under review has the remedy. What survives is a design weakness: add_line still lays a silent trap for legacy sketches (every bone-mallet profile built before the restart keeps coordinate-only corners forever), mixing add_polyline with a trailing add_line is documented but easy to miss, and nothing in inspect or set_parameter warns when a dimension on a coordinate-matched junction is changed. The proposed one-line change (accept LineSegment anchors) would also silently change which parameter names exist (joined endpoints lose StartX/EndX), so it is a contract change, not a bug fix.
findings.refute_evidence: git blame: the exclusion comment is from 3df4faa (2026-10-16, add_arc commit) and 24bab02 the next day chose a new op rather than changing add_line; AGENTS.md line 44 ('prefer it over chains of add_line') is the stated migration. The finder's headless experiment matches the contract text, so no probe was needed.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only on sketches he built with add_line before restarting into 24bab02, or if a script still chains add_line: a later set_parameter on a corner opens the profile and the next rebuild reports a bare failure. New work via add_polyline is unaffected, and AGENTS.md already steers him there.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Through the bridge only. In the GUI they draw with the native Sketcher, which creates coincidences itself, so they never hit it.
judge.risk: Medium if add_line's semantics are changed: existing bridge scripts and tests that set_parameter on StartX/EndX of joined endpoints would break and saved sketches would differ from new ones. Lower-risk alternatives: keep the contract, add a warning in set_parameter/inspect when a dimension sits on a coordinate-matched junction, and formally deprecate add_line chains in the contract and AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Sketch angles are shown and edited in radians (Feature settings and bridge); a bare '30' becomes 30 rad
findings.evidence: core.py:117 '"unit": "rad" if c.Type == "Angle" else "mm"'; ui.py:2691 self.value.setSuffix(" " + info["unit"]). Experiment 2 §A: inspect reported Tilt (0.785398, 'rad'); set_parameter '30 deg' → 30°, '0.5 rad' → 28.65°, '30' → stored 30 rad = 1719°, '1' → 57.3°.
findings.scenario: Editing a chamfer/draft/revolve angle or a sketch Angle dimension from Feature settings or through an agent.
findings.consequence: The value field reads '0.7854 rad'; typing 30 without a unit yields a 1719° angle and a silently rotated sketch. Onshape and SolidWorks users think in degrees.
findings.reproduction: Headless script scratchpad/area-c-everyday/exp2_units_expr.py §A; GUI: select a sketch with an angle dimension, choose it in Feature settings.
findings.proposed_change: Report angles with unit 'deg' (value math.degrees(c.Value)) in native_parameters and accept both deg and rad strings in number(); keep set_parameter's internal conversion to radians (core.py:2705 Quantity with unit). For contract 3.0 compatibility add an additive 'display_unit':'deg' and 'value_deg' field first, then switch the GUI field to degrees; update docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md ('Driving angles use radians').
findings.dependencies: Bridge clients (dodec/mallet scripts) that pass radians today; a one-release dual-accept keeps them working.
findings.risk: Contract change; mitigate by accepting explicit units and documenting.
findings.acceptance: Native test: inspect returns deg for Angle constraints and revolve/pattern angles; set_parameter '30' on an angle stores 30°; GUI value field shows '45 deg'. Regression gate: tests/test_core.py, test_pattern_tools.py, test_datum_planes.py (line-angle planes).

judge.kurt_would_notice: Through the bridge: nothing new. docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md lines 63/110/209 say angles are radians, number() accepts "108 deg", and his agent scripts and tests already pass quantity strings or math.radians(). In the GUI: if he picks an arc Sweep, a hole PointAngle, a revolve Angle or a line-angle plane Angle in Feature settings, sees "90.00°", types 120 and presses Enter, the sketch/feature snaps to 6875° and the field refreshes to that number. He would spot it instantly, undo, and learn to type "120 deg" or click Apply instead of Enter (focus-out makes the spin box interpret the text first, which then parses correctly). He would also notice the GUI is inconsistent: the Studio Revolve/Pattern/Assembly forms are QuantityField("deg") (ui.py 1068, 1079, 2237, 2267, 2291) while this one editor leaks radians.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape/SolidWorks user sees a field reading "45.00°", types 30, hits Enter, and watches the sketch rotate wildly while the field now says "1718.87°". Nothing on screen explains it; the workaround (type "30°"/"30 deg", or commit with Apply/Tab rather than Enter) is undiscoverable. It reads as "the dimension editor is broken", which is a trust hit early in the first session. Recovery is one Undo, so no work is lost.
judge.reasoning:
Source confirmed: src\kurtshape\core.py:117-123 reports Angle constraints with unit "rad" (also 134-153 for Revolution Angle / Hole PointAngle, modeling_geometry.py:440 for line-angle planes); core.py:53-61 number() treats a bare number as the target unit, so "30" with unit "rad" is 30 rad; core.py:2686/2705 set_parameter. ui.py:2687-2697 parameter_value sets the field unit from info["unit"]; ui.py:2704 apply_parameter sends self.value.lineEdit().text() raw; ui.py:4264 the Return event filter calls apply_parameter and returns True, so the Gui::QuantitySpinBox never interprets the text. The finder's headless experiment (scratchpad/area-c-everyday/exp2_units_expr.out.txt) is real and matches: "30 deg" -> 30°, "0.5 rad" -> 28.65°, "30" -> 30 rad = 1719°.

One detail of the finding is wrong, and it changes the classification. src/kurtshape/quantity_field.py wraps Gui::QuantitySpinBox and setSuffix only sets the "unit" property; Base::Unit is a dimension, so "rad" == Unit::Angle, and the spin box renders through FreeCAD's units schema. The app profile uses UserSchema 0 (Standard, degrees; runtime/*/user.cfg). My one headless probe (bundled pythonw, isolated env under scratchpad/verify/angle-probe) gives Quantity("0.785398 rad").UserString == '45.00°' and Quantity("30 rad").UserString == '1718.87°'; number("45.00 °", unit="rad") parses correctly to 0.7854. So the GUI field shows degrees, not "0.7854 rad" as the finding says, while a bare number committed with Enter is interpreted as radians. A field that displays one unit and interprets input in another is a defect, not a design choice, hence verified_defect rather than the finder's design_weakness (which is the honest label only for the bridge side, where radians are the documented contract and consistent with Onshape FeatureScript internals). Confidence high: the Enter path is unambiguous in code, the display is the same formatting FreeCAD's own Sketcher angle spin boxes use, and the finder's own experiment confirms the parse. Not observed in the live GUI (no app launch allowed); opening Feature settings on an arc Sweep would confirm the "°" text.

Severity medium: silent wrong geometry on a primary edit path, but immediately visible, fully undoable, no crash or data loss, and only hits angle parameters committed with Enter. Not high because the bridge (Kurt's daily path) behaves per contract and the Studio creation forms are already in degrees. user_value medium: for Kurt it is an occasional nuisance; for a newcomer it is a real first-hour trust problem, and the fix is nearly free. Effort S: the GUI defect is one line (call self.value.native.interpretText() before reading the text in apply_parameter, or build an explicit-unit string), which also makes the field consistent with the other deg forms; the finder's bridge-side proposal (report deg, dual-accept) is still S but is a contract change with test fallout (tests/test_datum_planes.py:211, test_sketch_arcs.py:95, test_sketch_planes.py:426 assert unit "rad"). Recommend fixing the GUI first and treating the bridge unit as a separate, optional contract decision; a safer bridge option than flipping bare-number meaning is to reject unit-less angle values in set_parameter with a clear message.
judge.risk: GUI-only fix: negligible. Bridge-side change as proposed (inspect reports "deg", bare numbers become degrees) silently flips the meaning of unit-less angle values for existing callers that pass math.radians(...) today, and breaks three native test assertions plus docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md statements (lines 63, 110, 209). Mitigate by keeping the radian contract and adding additive value_deg/display_unit fields, or by rejecting unit-less angle input on the bridge rather than reinterpreting it; the one-release dual-accept the finder suggests still leaves bare numbers ambiguous.

findings.title: Escape with no active sketch tool most likely falls through to native Sketcher and silently commits the sketch
findings.evidence: sketch_references.py:657-673 handles Escape only when a native tool or reference picking is active. Otherwise shortcuts.py:237-240 invokes general.cancel → cancel_task(); in a plain sketch every branch is false and it returns False (3845), so the KeyPress is not accepted and reaches the viewport. FreeCAD's ViewProviderSketch leaves edit mode on Escape when 'LeaveSketchWithEscape' is true (its default; nothing in src sets it, grep). After native resetEdit, tick() sees sketch_lease_needs_finish() and calls finish_sketch() (commit, not cancel).
findings.scenario: An Onshape user presses Escape to 'deselect' or to abandon a half-drawn sketch.
findings.consequence: The sketch closes and is committed as Finish (one Undo step), not cancelled; the README documents Escape only as 'cancels the current drawing tool or placement'. Surprising but recoverable with Ctrl+Z.
findings.reproduction: GUI: Shift+S, Top, draw a rectangle, press Escape twice (first ends the tool). Expect: sketch still open. If it closes, check the Undo stack has 'KurtShape: new sketch contents'. Also read the Sketcher preference LeaveSketchWithEscape in the app's profile.
findings.proposed_change: Decide the semantics explicitly: either make cancel_task() return True inside a sketch (consume Escape, keep the sketch open, status 'Escape ends the tool; Finish or Cancel closes the sketch') or set Mod/Sketcher LeaveSketchWithEscape=False in the owned profile like sketch_snapping does for Snap. Document in README/ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.
findings.dependencies: Confirm native default in FreeCAD 1.1.4 first.
findings.risk: None if consumed; the native exit path remains via Finish/Cancel.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe (sketch-behavior): Escape with no tool keeps panel.active_sketch() and the lease; the responsibility is documented. Regression gate: sketch-behavior recipe 'Escape ends Line without leaving sketch edit'.

findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py studio_tool 2120-2560, geometry_references 2066-2075, SelectionObserver 110-125, capture_feature_selection 2103-2118, studio.py sweep 1286-1313 and _plane 1459-1484, core.py 2551-2556, feature_panel.ReferencePicker 207-286, git -S on path_hint/values["face"], tools/*.FCMacro.
