findings.title: Post-commit inspection failure is reported as a rejected request although the change was committed
findings.evidence: After `doc.commitTransaction()` (1697) and `self._new_revision(doc)` (1701), `result = self.inspect(doc, measure)` (1731) still runs inside the mutation's try; the except (1750) maps any exception to `code = "operation_failed"` (1785) and writes `{"request": request, "error": error, "rejected": True}` to last_failures and `meta.LastFailure` (1795-1797). Headless reproduction: create_sketch with an injected summary failure returned ok:false/operation_failed while `doc.getObject("ExpSketch")` existed, the revision had advanced, UndoNames == ['KurtShape: create_sketch'], last_failures[...].rejected == True, LastFailure was set, ledger status 'failed', and an identical request_id replay returned the same failure.
findings.scenario: Any exception raised while building the inspection payload (native_feature_summary over a native property that raises, a corrupt QueryHealth JSON, a FreeCAD wrapper error) after a successful typed mutation, from the bridge or from Panel.operation.
findings.consequence: An agent sees ok:false with rejected:true, retries with the same request_id and gets the stored failure forever, then re-inspects and finds the feature already there; the document carries a persisted LastFailure that says the request was rejected. In the GUI, `_operation`'s error path (ui.py:1344-1345) calls the raw `self.core.inspect`, which raises again and escapes the Qt slot, so the panel keeps stale state while the model changed.
findings.reproduction: Run scratchpad/area-d-architecture/exp2_inspect_failure_after_commit.py under the bundled pythonw with the isolated env (output in exp2_out.txt). Verification in the app: patch `core.native_feature_summary` the same way in a GUI recipe, press Shift+S/plane, observe the status bar error and the feature in the viewport.
findings.proposed_change: Split `_dispatch` into three phases with separate exception scopes: admit(request) -> mutate(doc, request) under the transaction/rollback scope -> report(doc). A failure in report() must not abort/rollback anything (nothing is pending) and must not mark the request rejected: return `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "inspection_failed", "applied": true, "revision": <new>}}`, leave LastFailure alone, and record the ledger status as `completed_unreported` so an identical replay returns the same honest answer. In ui.py `_operation`, replace the raw `self.core.inspect` in the error path with `self.core.dispatch({"op":"inspect",...})` and notify. Document `applied` in OPERATION_CONTRACT.md (contract 3.1).
findings.acceptance: New native test (modelled on exp2) asserting: committed feature exists, response code inspection_failed with applied:true, LastFailure unchanged, replay identical; existing 426 native passes and bridge tests unchanged. Regression gate: test_core / test_core_safety / test_bridge_native plus the sketch-lifecycle GUI recipe.
findings.risk: Agent scripts that branch on code strings see a new code; keep `operation_failed` for genuine mutation-phase unknown exceptions.

findings.title: Panel.tick has no backoff for a persistently failing inspect: 40 Hz silent failure loop with one traceback appended per attempt
findings.lines: 1245-1269 (tick), 1344-1345 (_operation error path); src/kurtshape/core.py:1786-1793
findings.evidence: tick: `result = self.core.dispatch({"op": "inspect", ...})` (1250) followed by `if result["ok"]:` (1251) with no else branch; `self.core.observer.state(doc)["refresh"] = False` (1266) is only reached on success, so `needs_refresh` stays True and the 25 ms timer (ui.py:223) re-runs the failing inspect every tick. core.py:1786-1793 appends `traceback.format_exc()` to kurtshape.log for every unknown exception with no deduplication. Headless half verified: five consecutive failing inspects appended five tracebacks (exp2).
findings.scenario: Same trigger as the previous finding, or any object whose summary read raises persistently (foreign-document link, a script-owned object with a failing property getter).
findings.consequence: Kurt sees the history panel freeze at its last good state with no message; CPU is spent re-raising at 40 Hz and runtime/kurtshape.log grows by one traceback every 25 ms (about 140 KB/s) until restart.
findings.reproduction: GUI recipe: inject the same summary failure via a monkeypatch in a validation macro, let the app idle 2 s, assert kurtshape.log grew by about 80 tracebacks and no Messages entry/status text appeared. Headless half: exp2.
findings.proposed_change: In tick, on `not result["ok"]`: notify once per document ("Inspection failed: ... see Messages"), store `self.inspect_failure = (doc.Name, generation)` and skip re-inspection until the observer generation/change_serial moves or 2 s elapse; in `_dispatch`, rate-limit log writes (dedupe by the last traceback line, at most one per second per code) and route a one-line summary to Messages via App.Console.PrintError. Use `core.dispatch` in `_operation`'s error path.
findings.acceptance: Unit test: a controller whose inspect raises logs one traceback per second at most; GUI recipe asserts exactly one Messages entry and a status-bar error, and that a successful inspect resumes refresh. Gate: test_responsiveness, gui-validation recipe.
findings.dependencies: Pairs naturally with the previous finding.
findings.risk: Low; only the failure path changes.

findings.title: Session retry ledger refuses every mutation after 4096 tracked requests per app session; evicted ids are never forgotten
findings.evidence: `self.session_request_limit = limit * 8` (15); `if len(self.records) + len(self.expired) >= self.session_request_limit: return request_capacity_reached` (38-39); complete() moves evicted ids into `self.expired` (52) which is never pruned. Experiment 1: the 4097th distinct tracked request returns request_capacity_reached with records=512, expired=3584; a fresh id afterwards is still refused. Tested as intended behaviour in tests/test_bridge.py:443 and test_review_followup.py:309.
findings.scenario: Kurt keeps one GUI instance running for days (today's started 01:28) while agents model through the bridge; every mutation (pad, fillet, set_parameter, save, export) is tracked. dodec_steps.py alone has 22 typed calls per run; iterative rebuilds, retries and multi-part sessions accumulate.
findings.consequence: After the ceiling, every mutation, including `save`, is rejected with request_capacity_reached until Kurt restarts the app; inspect/preview keep working, so the agent appears connected but cannot change or save anything. The message tells the agent to 'restart', which it cannot do without Kurt.
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/area-d-architecture/exp1_ledger_capacity.py (exp1_out.txt). Field sizing: count `request_id` mutations in a day of bridge traffic (capabilities exposes result_limit/session_request_limit).
findings.proposed_change: Make the ceiling a soft LRU: cap `expired` at, for example, 8*limit entries and drop the oldest (their status becomes not_recorded, which the contract already defines as non-proof of non-execution), and/or expire by age (24 h). Keep request_id_reused protection for live records. Expose `remaining_capacity` in capabilities and warn in Messages at 90 percent. Smaller alternative: raise limit to 4096 (cap 32768) and keep semantics.
findings.acceptance: test_bridge capacity test updated: 100k tracked requests still accepted; len(records)+len(expired) bounded; request_expired still returned for ids inside the retention window; OPERATION_CONTRACT retry paragraph updated. Gate: bridge suite.
findings.risk: An id reused with a different payload after it has been forgotten is accepted as new instead of request_expired; mitigated by the retention window and by agents' existing inspect-before-mutate discipline.

merged_from.title: Session retry cap (4096 IDs) is reachable in a day of iterative agent builds and the only remedy is an app restart
merged_from.evidence: request_ledger.py:15 `session_request_limit = limit * 8` (4096); 38-39 rejects `request_capacity_reached` once records+expired reach it; `expired` never shrinks. A full dodec-hub bridge build is ~70 tracked mutations (projects/dodec-hub/build-bridge.log, 73 lines); bone-mallet rebuilds in place every run (build_mallet_kurtshape.py:52-56 delete_features then full rebuild, ~40 mutations); failed attempts consume IDs too. ~60-100 iterations in one app session exhaust it. Memory is not the issue: a 26-feature plate inspect result is 15 KB (probe B1), so 512 cached results are ~8 MB.
merged_from.scenario: A long modeling day against the same running app (Kurt leaves it open; AGENTS.md discourages restarts) ends with every mutation rejected as request_capacity_reached; the agent must ask Kurt to restart with unsaved work open.
merged_from.consequence: Hard stop mid-build with a message that reads like a server fault.
merged_from.reproduction: Count: `grep -c '^ok' build-bridge.log` per run x number of runs in a session; or register 4096 IDs in a unit test (test_bridge.py:443 shows the path with limit=1).
merged_from.proposed_change: Make the tombstone set an LRU bounded by count and age (e.g. 65536 entries or 24 h), keep the 512-result cache, and report `retry.remaining_requests` in capabilities and `queue_wait_ms`-style in each mutation response so clients see the ceiling coming; document that eviction of a tombstone re-enables the ID (acceptable: IDs are UUIDs).
merged_from.risk: A replay of a very old ID after tombstone expiry would execute again; UUID clients never resend old IDs, and a 24 h floor keeps the exactly-once window realistic.
merged_from.acceptance: Test registers 10000 unique IDs without capacity error while the result cache stays at 512; capabilities exposes remaining count. Verification still needed: confirm with Kurt how long the app typically stays up and how many rebuild iterations a session sees.

findings.title: Command metadata lives in seven places and has drifted: registry status/native_command disagree with the wired callbacks, keys are embedded in tooltip strings, hover labels ignore rebinding
findings.lines: 430-446 (tool, key parsed from tip at 445), 548-551 and 607-608 (keys as literals), 2043-2051 (primary_feature_tool typed-vs-native map), 4195-4228 (shortcut_callbacks); shortcuts.json:39-44,110; src/kurtshape/tool_search.py:12-45; src/kurtshape/toolbar_labels.py:39-53,66-83,110-123; docs/ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md:63
findings.symbol: Panel.tool / Panel.make_toolbars / Panel.primary_feature_tool / ShortcutRouter / ToolbarLabels / tool_search
findings.evidence: shortcuts.json:40 `feature.fillet ... status:native, native_command:PartDesign_Fillet` and :44 `feature.revolve ... native PartDesign_Revolution`, but ui.py:4199-4200 wires `feature.fillet` to `studio_tool("fillet")` and `feature.revolve` to `studio_from_sketch("revolve")` (callbacks win in ShortcutRouter.invoke); ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md:63 publishes 'Edge fillet | Shift+F | native | PartDesign_Fillet'. Shortcut keys are literals in tips ('Extrude · ... · Shift+E', ui.py:550) and in the sketch bar tuple list ('L','G','C','A','Shift+S','D','M','Q', ui.py:607), re-parsed by `tip.split(" · ")[-1]` (445) and `tool_search.shortcut_from_tip` (45). ToolbarLabels.register stores that static key (39-53) and `_scan_toolbar` falls back to it because the QActions carry no QKeySequence (66-83), so `_show_pending` (123) renders the default after a rebind. tool_search.ALIASES is keyed by display label (12-42). Op semantics are repeated in `_operation` (1296-1297, 1300, 1305-1308, 1312-1318, 1335-1339, 1366) and in `_dispatch` (1567, 1693).
findings.scenario: Kurt rebinds Shift+E via Shift+/ Rebind; hovers Extrude; reads ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md; a developer adds the typed `hole` op to the GUI.
findings.consequence: Hover label shows Shift+E while help and search show the new key; documentation claims native backends that are not used; adding a command touches shortcuts.json, feature_tools, make_toolbars, shortcut_callbacks, primary_feature_tool, ALIASES, the `_operation` op lists and the contract, with no test catching a missed place (the Move face defect is one instance).
findings.reproduction: Code reading above; rebind check: set shortcuts.user.json bindings {"feature.extrude":"Ctrl+E"}, start the app, hover Extrude (label) vs Shift+/ (help) vs Alt+C (search). Drift check: compare registry entries with status 'native' against ids present in Panel.shortcut_callbacks().
findings.proposed_change: Registry design: a `commands.py` table of CommandDescriptor{id, label, aliases, icon, tip, category, contexts, default_key, kind in {typed_op, native_command, ui_task, builtin}, native_command?, typed_ops?, availability predicate name, help}. shortcuts.json becomes the binding layer (id -> key, user overrides unchanged); toolbars, menus, search, help, ToolbarLabels and ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md are generated from the table; ToolbarLabels looks up the current key by id at show time. Keep these distinctions separate in the schema: runtime context availability (predicate) vs native FreeCAD command id (may be absent on other installs, filtered by available_catalog) vs typed bridge op(s) vs UI task (Extrude dialog fans out to pad/pocket/studio ops/edit_extrusion; Sketch is create_sketch+begin_sketch_edit+native setEdit) vs key binding vs presentation. GUI commands with no bridge op (all Sketcher_* and native PartDesign dialogs, view/selection/measure/isolate, workspace switching, Recovery) and bridge ops with no GUI command (sketch_rectangle/sketch_circle/add_*, resolve_selector, preview, list_documents, capabilities, request_status, diagnostics, assembly_candidates, orphan_helpers) remain representable because kind is per descriptor. Smaller alternative (S): keep JSON + feature_tools, stop embedding keys in tips (pass shortcut_id to ToolbarLabels.register and resolve at show time), key ALIASES by id, and add a drift test asserting every registry entry with status 'native' has no Python callback and every 'callback' entry has one. Migration: descriptors for the Part Studio bar first, then sketch/assembly bars, menus, search and help; regenerate ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md from the table. Compatibility: shortcuts.user.json format unchanged. Failure modes: duplicate ids, missing icon names; rollback is deleting the table and restoring the inline tuples. Evidence before promotion: test_shortcuts/test_tool_search extended, toolbar-validation and everyday-ui recipes green, generated doc diff reviewed.
findings.acceptance: Drift test passes (registry backend == wiring); hover label equals the current binding after a rebind in a GUI recipe; ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md regenerates without a diff; Move face/Fillet search cases from the previous finding pass; no toolbar icon or label changes in the theme-repair screenshots (validation/onshape-theme-repair/*.png, Oct 4 era) beyond intended ones.
findings.dependencies: Previous finding (search merge id) is the first step.
findings.risk: Medium: touches every toolbar; mitigate by generating the same QActions and comparing action lists before/after in a test.

findings.title: Error taxonomy: 122 emitted codes, about 26 documented, with synonyms and one code covering ten conditions
findings.lines: 1437 (unsupported_operation) vs src/kurtshape/assembly.py:934 (unknown_operation); core.py:906-928 (_body translates studio missing_part to missing_body) vs modeling_geometry.py:506, hole_tools.py:429, reference_tools.py:130 (missing_body with 'part' messages); core.py:1470,1477,1481,1566,1573,1579,1820,1824 (sketch_edit_active); core.py:1785,1856 (operation_failed/preview_failed fallbacks); docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md (284 lines, no error table)
findings.evidence: Inventory (grep of OperationError("…"), _error("…"), AssemblyError("…"), incompatible("…")): 122 distinct codes across core (65), assembly (26), selectors (11), studio (11), modeling_geometry (12), hole_tools, reference_tools, extrusion_preview, step/geometry workers, plus 8 transport-only codes in bridge.py/request_ledger.py (queue_full, timeout, outcome_unknown, request_pending, request_expired, request_id_reused, request_capacity_reached, invalid_request_id). Backticked identifiers in OPERATION_CONTRACT.md that are error codes: about 26; 96 emitted codes do not appear there at all (e.g. stale_revision, busy, unknown_document, unmanaged_document, sketch_history_changed, empty_history, save_failed, export_failed, path_outside_workspace, invalid_format). Families mix prefixes for the same meaning: no_solid/no_orphans/no_sketch_edit vs empty_cut/empty_profile/empty_history vs missing_body/missing_file/missing_directory.
findings.scenario: An agent (or ks.py / build_bridge.py) branches on error codes to decide retry vs re-inspect vs abort; a developer adds an op in a satellite module and invents a code.
findings.consequence: Clients cannot know the retryable set (stale_revision, busy, outcome_unknown) from the contract; identical situations surface as different codes depending on which module raised; sketch_edit_active hides whether the blocker is a managed lease, a native Task dialog or an assembly edit, so the agent cannot pick the right remedy.
findings.reproduction: Re-run the inventory: grep -oh 'OperationError("[a-z_]*"\|_error("[a-z_]*"\|AssemblyError("[a-z_]*"' src/kurtshape/*.py | sort -u, then compare against docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md backticks.
findings.proposed_change: Add `errors.py` with a frozen CODES table (code -> category in {admission, validation, reference, geometry, history, io, transport}, retryable bool, remedy hint, contract anchor). OperationError asserts membership in dev/test mode. Collapse synonyms behind aliases for one contract revision (unknown_operation -> unsupported_operation; missing_part accepted but documented as missing_body), split sketch_edit_active into lease_active / native_editor_active / assembly_edit_active with `blocker` detail, and append an error table to OPERATION_CONTRACT.md. Add a unit test that scans src for emitted codes and fails on any code absent from CODES or from the contract table.
findings.acceptance: The scanning test passes; capabilities reports `error_codes` version; AGENTS.md/OPERATION_CONTRACT list retryable codes; bridge and native suites green. Gate: the scanning test itself plus test_bridge/test_core.
findings.dependencies: Coordinate with Area (bridge/observability) if another finder owns capabilities.
findings.risk: Agent scripts matching old codes; keep aliases for one revision and list them.

findings.title: Two disposable-clone evaluators with different acceptance rules: Controller._preview vs ExtrusionEvaluator.evaluate
findings.lines: 1812-1884 (_preview; valid rule 1864-1867, one-solid rule 1851-1854); src/kurtshape/extrusion_preview.py:340-524 (evaluate; aggregate rule 398, acceptance 431-433, cleanup 505-524)
findings.evidence: Both: saveCopy -> hidden openDocument -> openTransaction + getActiveTransaction id -> _model_operation -> studio.reconcile -> _recompute -> _build_status -> commit/closeActiveTransaction -> closeDocument + geometry.drop_document + observer.states.pop + setActiveDocument + _restore_gui, each with its own busy handling. Rules differ: `_preview` accepts `build_status in {"valid","sketch_only"}` (1865) and applies the one-solid rule only when `not studio.enabled(clone)` (1851-1854); `evaluate` requires 'valid' except create_plane (431) and skips the one-solid rule whenever `"operation" in normalized or op not in {pad,pocket}` (398, 432). `_preview` uses tempfile per call; evaluate caches eight results and reuses a snapshot per generation.
findings.scenario: An agent runs `preview` for a pad with an explicit `operation` on a non-studio Body, then the same proposal through the GUI Extrude dialog; or a fix lands in one path (for example the closeActiveTransaction(True) cleanup) and not the other.
findings.consequence: The bridge preview and the GUI preview can disagree on validity for the same proposal; two cleanup paths to keep correct; the worker process (preview_worker.run_worker) depends on the evaluate variant only, so bridge previews never exercise the worker-proven path.
findings.reproduction: Native test: build a two-Body non-studio document, propose `pad` with operation:'add' on one Body producing two solids; compare `_preview` verdict with `ExtrusionEvaluator(core, doc, rev).evaluate(proposal).valid`. Code reading above establishes the rule difference.
findings.proposed_change: Extract `preview_clone.py` with a `DisposableClone(controller, source_doc, snapshot_path, borrowed)` context manager owning busy flag, GUI capture/restore, transaction id, close/drop/states.pop, and one `evaluate_proposal(controller, clone, proposal, *, rules)` where the acceptance rule set is a function of op and studio state. `_preview` becomes a thin wrapper that returns the bridge payload; ExtrusionEvaluator keeps caching/snapshot reuse but calls the shared function.
findings.acceptance: Parity test over a proposal matrix (pad/pocket/create_plane/fillet x studio/non-studio x valid/invalid) asserting identical valid/invalid/error.code from both entry points; test_extrusion_preview, test_borrowed_preview, test_preview_worker_leases and test_core preview cases green; preview GUI recipe unchanged.
findings.risk: Medium: the evaluate path carries S16 borrowed-snapshot validation calls at three points (362, 395, 483) that must stay in order.

findings.title: Geometry-check and STEP-export background jobs are two hand-duplicated state machines in Panel; their controller halves live in core.py but are only used by ui.py
findings.lines: 137-154 (12 fields, 2 timers), 1412-1628 (check family), 2999-3177 (STEP family), 3819-3823 (cancel_task returns None vs True); src/kurtshape/core.py:338-847 (prepare/accept pairs, _replace_export_pair)
findings.evidence: The two families mirror each other method for method (`_context_current`, `_current`, `_retire`, `_cancel`, `_restore_status`, `_poll`, fallback) with the same generation/ownership fences and the same magic status strings duplicated into set literals (1505-1506 vs 3102). Already diverged in small ways: `cancel_task` does `return` for STEP (3821) and `return True` for check (3823); `_poll_step_export` carries an `invalid_state` branch (3151-3164) the check twin lacks. core.py:338-847 (~510 lines) implements prepare_geometry_check/accept_geometry_check/prepare_step_export/accept_step_export used by no bridge op (bridge check_geometry/export stay synchronous).
findings.scenario: Adding a third job (for example a background Rebuild or an STL export worker), or fixing an ownership-fence bug found in one twin.
findings.consequence: Fixes must be applied twice; the S17/S18 guard ordering ('context first, native reads last, pure ownership') is encoded by position in two 200-line methods and cannot be unit-tested without a QApplication and FreeCAD.
findings.reproduction: Read the two families side by side; diff after normalising the kind name.
findings.proposed_change: Introduce `jobs.py` (move the controller prepare/accept pairs and `_replace_export_pair` out of core.py; Controller keeps thin delegating methods) and `job_controller.py` with a `WorkerJobController(kind, prepare, accept, present, status_texts)` holding generation/job/preparing/closed and one QTimer; Panel owns two instances. Keep the exact fence order as named helper methods so a headless test with a fake worker can assert the sequence (prepare -> context recheck -> submit -> poll -> accept(is_current, owns_job) -> present).
findings.acceptance: Headless unit tests for WorkerJobController phases with fake workers (cancel during prepare, document switch during poll, stale generation at accept); tests/test_geometry_check_jobs.py and test_step_export_jobs.py unchanged and green; geometry-check-lifecycle and step-export GUI recipes (91 checks) green; core.py shrinks by about 500 lines with no behaviour change.
findings.risk: Medium: the STEP recipe's exact exception-cause assertions depend on message text; keep messages verbatim.

findings.title: Sketch session and modal interaction state are implicit: seven Panel flags, a tick auto-finisher, a hand-ordered Escape chain, and an untyped lease dict in the controller
findings.lines: 155-165 (flags), 3190-3421 (start_sketch .. sync_edit_ui), 1236-1248 and 1267-1268 (tick forcing document and auto-finish), 3819-3845 (cancel_task chain), 4273-4276 (close guard only for main window); src/kurtshape/core.py:1106-1214, 1601-1646 (lease dict with optional keys created/use_sources/grouping_started)
findings.evidence: States are encoded in `pending_sketch`, `selecting_support`, `placement_document`, `plane_visibility`, `finishing_sketch`, `entering_sketch`, `native_edit_failure` plus `state["active_sketch_edit"]` and `Gui.getInEdit()`; `sketch_lease_needs_finish` (3376-3383) derives 'lease open but editor closed' from four of them; tick (1246-1247, 1267-1268) auto-finishes. `cancel_task` (3819-3845) is a seven-way priority chain over unrelated subsystems (STEP job, check job, plane editor, reference picking, studio dialog, placement, extrusion task). In core, `sketch_edits[id]` is a dict whose phase is implied by `editing.pop("grouping_started", False)` (1196) and `editing.get("created")` (1169). tool_session.py already shows the explicit alternative.
findings.scenario: Any new modal surface (a typed Hole dialog, a Measure tool, the plane editor) or any change to Finish/Cancel behaviour, like the Oct 6 'right-click fully ends continuous drawing' repair.
findings.consequence: Escape semantics depend on insertion order with no test enumerating them; invariants (a lease exists iff the editor is open or a teardown failure is recorded) are enforced in six methods; a headless state-machine test is impossible today, so regressions are only caught by GUI recipes.
findings.reproduction: Code reading; try to write a unit test for 'Escape during plane-pick while a STEP job is pending' without a GUI.
findings.proposed_change: UI: a `SketchSession` object with explicit phases {idle, placing, entering, editing, finishing, teardown_failed} owning the current flags and exposing `needs_finish()`, `can_switch_document()`, `on_escape()`; a small `ModalStack` where each subsystem pushes/pops an interrupt handler so `cancel_task` becomes `stack.cancel_top()`. Core: `SketchLease` dataclass (feature, initial, undo_before, signature, undo/redo deques, created: bool, phase: Enum{open, grouping, restoring}) replacing the dict; `_commit_sketch_edit`/`_preserve_sketch_draft`/`_rollback_sketch_edit` become methods. No behaviour change intended.
findings.acceptance: Headless tests for SketchSession/ModalStack transitions and for SketchLease phases (begin, native commit, finish grouping failure -> draft preserved, cancel after external history change -> sketch_history_changed); sketch-lifecycle, sketch-edit-state, sketch-behavior and line-endpoint-freeze GUI recipes green; test_sketch_planes/test_history_lifecycle unchanged.
findings.dependencies: Do after the job-controller extraction so cancel_task's first two branches become stack entries.
findings.risk: High if rushed: this code embodies the Oct 5-6 interaction repairs; land as pure refactor with recipe gates per step.

findings.title: STEP acceptance re-exports the full world BRep of every target about six times (and preparation 2-3 times) on the GUI thread
findings.lines: 594-646 (prepare), 669-693 (_step_export_current), 695-846 (accept), 2855-2881 (_replace_export_pair guards)
findings.evidence: prepare: 594 `roundtrip_digest` (exportBrepToString + importBrepFromString per target), 612 `initial_world_fingerprints` (export again unless the single-target ticket), 646 `_step_export_current` -> 685 `world_fingerprints` (export again) plus 684/688 two provenance builds. accept: `current()` (700-702 -> _step_export_current) is called at 703, 806 and inside `commit_current` (809-817) which `_replace_export_pair` calls before and after each of the two renames (2876, 2880): six full exports of every target plus twelve provenance builds and six target rescans. S15 measured 522-555 ms per fingerprint pass and 929 ms roundtrip on 1000 solids; S09B measured 2.34 s launch and 3.42 s completion polling. Geometry checks, by contrast, guard with `check_key` hashCodes only (core.py:411-430).
findings.scenario: Export STEP from a multi-part Part Studio or an imported model with many solids.
findings.consequence: The GUI freezes for ~2 s before the child starts and ~3 s when it finishes, even though the child only needed ~1 s of real export; multi-target exports get none of the S16 reuse.
findings.reproduction: tools/run_gui_recipe.ps1 -Recipe step-export on the retained 1000-solid S09B fixture (runtime/architecture-upgrade-working) with `world_fingerprints` wrapped by a counting patch; observe 2-3 calls in prepare and 6 in accept; time step_export_snapshot_gui and the accept call.
findings.proposed_change: Compute world fingerprints once per phase under `busy`, then guard the later checks with the pure observer fence already used by step_capture._pure_current/_require_current (states identity, instance_id/generation/change_serial, snapshot_key, document identity, `check_key` hashCode per target) instead of re-exporting BRep; extend the one-use digest ticket to multi-target (one canonical hash per target carried from roundtrip admission). Keep the child's independent archive comparison and the final independent fingerprint for the single eventful acceptance read. Cannot be threaded (native shape reads).
findings.dependencies: S16/S17/S18 focused tests and STEP GUI recipe as regression oracle.
findings.risk: Reentrancy argument: native reads can pump events; mitigated because the fence compares change_serial captured before and after the single fingerprint read, which is exactly the S16 ticket discipline.
findings.acceptance: Counted `world_fingerprints` calls: prepare <= 1 per target, accept 0 BRep exports when change_serial is unchanged; step_export_snapshot_gui and acceptance wall time on the 1000-solid fixture drop by the measured fingerprint phases; S17/S18 recipes pass unchanged; destination/provenance bytes identical.

findings.title: Sketch region fill rebuild is unbounded per sketch and runs on the GUI thread after every geometry change: 1.1 s per rebuild on a 300-circle sketch
findings.lines: 30-75 (region_faces), 179-190 (slotChangedObject), 346-347 (timer), 371-432 (_rebuild)
findings.evidence: sketch_regions.py:63 `Part.makeCompound(closed_edges).makeWires(...)` and 72 `Part.makeFace(wires, 'Part::FaceMakerBullseye')` over every closed wire of the sketch; 184-188 marks the entry dirty on each `Geometry`/`Shape` change; 346-347 starts the 80 ms timer; 371-432 runs the whole-sketch rebuild synchronously ('bound each turn to one sketch', not to time). Probe (headless, noisy): `region_faces` on a 300-circle sketch = 1145 ms median (300 faces), while inspect/signature/dumpContent on the same sketch were 2-7 ms. Sibling path: ProvisionalExtrusion.evaluate runs the same FaceMakerBullseye on the profile (extrusion_preview.py:175).
findings.scenario: Drawing or dragging in a sketch with a few hundred closed entities (converted or hole-pattern sketches), or selecting a part whose dense sketches are visible.
findings.consequence: Each placed or dragged entity is followed ~80 ms later by a freeze that grows superlinearly with region count (~1 s at 300 circles), on top of the native solver.
findings.reproduction: Build a sketch with 300 circles + 300 diameter constraints (probe_sync_paths.py section 1), make it visible/active in the GUI, add one circle, watch `sketch_region_build` in the diagnostics op or event_loop_delay; compare with 50 and 100 circles.
findings.proposed_change: (a) Do not rebuild while a native drawing tool is active (`panel.sketch_references.native_tool`) or while `panel.core.busy`; rebuild on tool end/commit and on Finish. (b) Budget: skip the fill above N closed wires or when the last build exceeded ~100 ms for that sketch (record `build_ms`, already stored per entry). (c) Incremental: group closed wires into connected components and rebuild only components whose geometry ids changed. Process isolation is possible here (pure geometry Content strings -> faces/triangles in a child) but (a)+(b) remove most of the pain. Cannot be threaded (Part calls hold the GIL).
findings.dependencies: sketch-regions GUI recipe; SketchRegionFill counters (builds, discarded_builds, build_ms).
findings.risk: Fill briefly absent during drawing (acceptable; it is a hint) and above the cap (document it).
findings.acceptance: `sketch_region_build` p95 < 50 ms while a tool is active on the 300-circle fixture; no build events during an active Sketcher_Create* command in the presentation-scheduling recipe; existing sketch-regions checks pass.

findings.title: Escape during a long native recompute may abort FreeCAD's sequencer and make the error path run a second full recompute
findings.lines: core.py:1750 (except Exception), 1775 (abortTransaction), 1780 (unguarded second _recompute), 1783 (_build_status), 1800 (busy released in finally); selectors.py:1624-1636 (re-raises); ui.py:184 (native status bar shown); ARCHITECTURE.md:101 (not 230)
findings.evidence: core.py:1775 `doc.abortTransaction()` then 1780 `self._recompute(doc)` synchronously inside the exception handler, for any exception including a native abort. FreeCADApp.dll contains the 'Recompute...' SequencerLauncher strings and FreeCADGui.dll contains 'Press ESC to cancel' and `processEvents`; the extrusion_preview.py:354-355 and 737 comments confirm native loading/recompute/saveCopy pump Qt events inside KurtShape. ARCHITECTURE.md:230 states queued Escape cannot interrupt a non-yielding native call but does not cover a sequencer-aborted one.
findings.scenario: Kurt changes an upstream dimension on a deep part (8+ s), regrets it, presses Escape.
findings.consequence: If the abort reaches the kernel, the 'cancel' triggers abortTransaction plus another full recompute (same duration again); a second Escape inside that recompute would raise out of the except block, leaving `self.state` stale until the next tick.
findings.reproduction: GUI recipe on Plate60: `set_parameter` Pad Length (6-9 s), QTest keyClick Escape after 500 ms on the main window; record outcome (ok/error code), number and duration of `native_recompute` events, and whether an exception escapes `Panel._operation`.
findings.proposed_change: If confirmed: detect the native abort (exception text/type) and treat it as a deliberate cancel: abort the transaction, mark `needs_rebuild` with reason 'cancelled' instead of recomputing synchronously, notify 'Canceled — Rebuild to recompute'. If not confirmed (progress bar filters Escape), document that cancellation is impossible during commit and provide painted 'Recomputing… n features' feedback instead.
findings.dependencies: GUI recipe; FreeCAD sequencer behavior under KurtShape's app-level event filters.
findings.risk: A half-recomputed document after abort must be left consistently Touched; the existing needs_rebuild/Rebuild path already handles that state.
findings.acceptance: Escape during a long edit returns control within one progress step without a second recompute; model status is needs_rebuild; Rebuild restores valid; no unhandled exception in the FreeCAD console.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read core.py 1690-1810 and 862-895 (_recompute), selectors.py 1624-1676 (recompute wrapper), ui.py 170-230 (shell setup) and 4230-4275 (app event filter), ARCHITECTURE.md (126 lines; the cited line 230 does not exist, the relevant sentence is line 101). The structural half is verified from source: the handler at core.py:1750 catches every Exception; for a non-sketch transaction it calls doc.abortTransaction() (1775), closes the native transaction (1776-1779), then runs self._recompute(doc) synchronously (1780) and _build_status (1783), with no try/except around that second recompute, so a second abort propagates out of _dispatch (busy is released in finally at 1800, but dispatch's ledger.complete and Bridge.tick's reply.put are skipped). selectors.recompute (1624-1636) only times doc.recompute and re-raises. Nothing in src/kurtshape names FreeCADAbort, AbortException or Sequencer, so FreeCAD's default behaviour applies. The trigger half remains a hypothesis I could not exercise (no GUI runs allowed), but it is better grounded than the finder stated: ui.py:184 shows the native status bar, which hosts FreeCAD's progress bar; FreeCADGui.dll contains 'Press ESC to cancel' (4 occurrences) and FreeCADApp.dll 'Recompute...' plus the FreeCADAbort Python exception type (3 occurrences; 1 in FreeCADBase.dll); no 'Do you really want to abort the operation?' string exists, so a cancel would not be confirmed by a dialog. The sequencer pumps Qt events and grabs the keyboard while running on the GUI thread, which is exactly why extrusion_preview.py:354-355 and 737 warn that native recompute pumps events. Severity medium is fair if true: the user pays the full rebuild time twice, gets an 'operation_failed' error with a FreeCAD exception text, and a second Escape leaves an unhandled exception in a Qt slot (state stale for one tick, bridge caller left waiting until its 30 s timeout). Classification 'hypothesis' is honest and should stay until the GUI recipe in the finding is run.
findings.refute_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:110 (S05) records that a native transaction abort leaves the Body Touched with a changed shape hash, which supports the claim that the post-abort _recompute is a full-duration rebuild rather than a cached no-op. For undo/redo (core.py ~1710-1725) transaction is False, so an abort there skips the second recompute but leaves touched objects and a recorded failure instead. Bridge callers whose request dies in the handler get no reply: Bridge.tick (bridge.py:113-117) only puts the reply after dispatch returns.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only if he presses Escape during a multi-second rebuild (the native status bar does say 'Press ESC to cancel'): the edit is reverted but the app stays frozen for roughly the same time again, then reports an operation_failed error with a FreeCAD traceback message instead of 'Canceled'; if he presses Escape twice the shell logs a Python traceback and the status line lags one tick. A bridge mutation interrupted this way would hang his client for the 30 s timeout.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape/SolidWorks user expects Escape to either do nothing or cancel cleanly; a doubled freeze followed by a cryptic error would read as a crash-like bug.
judge.risk: Low. Treating FreeCADAbort as a deliberate cancel (abort the transaction, mark needs_rebuild with reason 'cancelled', skip the synchronous recompute) must still refresh signatures/build status so inspect reports needs_rebuild consistently; the finding's own GUI recipe (Escape 500 ms into a Plate60 Pad length edit, count native_recompute events) is the cheap confirmation step before changing anything.

findings.title: Switching the active document cancels an in-flight STEP export or geometry check by design, but without any notification
findings.lines: ui.py:1180-1196 (tick cancels on active-document change), 3088-3092 and 1509-1515 (context predicates require App.activeDocument() == doc), 3111-3123 and 1531-1543 (notify=False default -> restore_status only); core.py:669-694 and 411-430 (Controller predicates do not need the active document)
findings.evidence: ui.py:1181-1183 `if geometry_document is not self._step_export_document: ... self._cancel_step_export()` and 1191-1193 for geometry checks, on every tick where `App.activeDocument()` changed; `_cancel_step_export(notify=False)` (3111) only calls `restore_status()` (3122), so no message is shown; the child is killed (3109 -> worker.close()). The acceptance itself only needs the source document open and the destination unchanged.
findings.scenario: Kurt exports a large part (tens of seconds), clicks another tab to keep working, returns.
findings.consequence: The export never appears and nothing says why; the same for a long geometry check. Also the exact-preview editor is cleared on switch (extrusion_preview.py:979), which is correct for an editor but confusing when combined.
findings.reproduction: step-export GUI recipe: start an eligible export, call Gui.activateDocument on another open document before completion; observe status text, absence of the file and absence of any notification.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the job bound to its document, not to the active document: let `_step_export_context_current` accept 'document still open' and defer only the `self.state`/refresh publication until that document is active again (files and provenance do not depend on the view); at minimum notify 'STEP export canceled: switched documents' (notify=True). Same for geometry checks.
findings.dependencies: S17/S18 recipe cases that currently assert cancellation on switch would change to assert continuation or an explicit notification.
findings.risk: Acceptance while another document is active must not touch `self.state` of the wrong document — publish files, store the result per document, refresh when active.
findings.acceptance: Recipe: switching documents mid-export yields either the completed files plus a notification on return, or an explicit cancellation message; no silent restore_status.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py 1175-1200 (tick), 1120-1121 (Panel.document is App.activeDocument()), 1505-1545 (geometry check context/cancel), 2998-3060 (start_step_export), 3088-3160 (export context/cancel/poll), 655-690 (notify/restore_status); core.py 411-470 and 669-740 (Controller currency and acceptance predicates); tests/test_step_export_jobs.py 597-608; docs/architecture-responsiveness-upgrade/EXECUTION.md 469, 687 and STATUS_REPORT.md 48. The mechanics hold: on every tick where the active document differs from the one the job was started on, tick calls _cancel_step_export() (1181-1183) and _cancel_geometry_check() (1191-1193) with the default notify=False, which retires the job, closes the child worker (_retire_* -> worker.close()) and only calls restore_status(), so the 'Exporting STEP... Escape to cancel' text is replaced by the ordinary status and no 'canceled' message is ever shown; returning to the source document shows nothing. The Controller-level acceptance (accept_step_export core.py:695-702, _step_export_current 669-694; accept_geometry_check 432-470, _geometry_check_current 411-430) indeed does not require the active document, only identity, open state, snapshot key, topology/provenance and no active transaction, so the finder's claim about what acceptance needs is right. What does not hold is 'verified_defect': binding the UI job to the active document and cancelling on 'document switch/close' is the documented, deliberately tested lifecycle (EXECUTION.md:469 for geometry checks, :687 'Capture/document switch ... execute and pass' for STEP, S18 OSError cases after 'allocation/document switch'), and the UI poll path assumes the active document when it publishes (ui.py ~3150: self.state = invalid_state; self.refresh()). The defect-like part is the missing notification, not the cancellation. Blame: lines 1180-1196 come from 4681ddf (2026-10-13), unchanged by the three later commits, so not fixed at HEAD. Severity stays medium: a multi-second export lost with no message is a real workflow hit for a user who routinely Ctrl+Space's between a part studio and an assembly, though recovery is a single re-export.
findings.refute_evidence: _operation also calls _cancel_step_export() silently for every non-inspect op (ui.py:1292-1295), so any GUI action during an export drops it without a message too; only the post-completion discard path (ui.py ~3178) notifies 'STEP export discarded because the project or destination changed'. tests/test_step_export_jobs.py:597 covers Controller-level foreign-document rejection, not the UI's silent tick cancellation.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Yes, intermittently: exporting a part then Ctrl+Space to the assembly (or clicking another tab) during a multi-second export leaves no STEP file and no message; he would find out when BumpMesh or the project folder lacks the file and would have to guess why. Same for a long geometry check that simply never reports.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape user expects an export to finish regardless of which tab is active; the file silently not appearing would look like a broken export.
judge.risk: Low for the minimal fix (pass notify=True at the two tick call sites, ideally with the source document label). Keeping the job alive across switches is M, not S: the poll/accept path publishes into self.state/refresh for the active document, so publication would have to be deferred until the source document is active again, and the S17/S18 GUI recipes that assert cancellation on document switch would need updating.

findings.title: Session token file inherits a Modify ACL that includes the sandboxed-agent accounts and six orphaned SIDs; threat model does not match the machine
findings.evidence: bridge.py:98 `self.path.write_text(json.dumps({"url":...,"token":self.token,"pid":...}))` with no ACL handling. icacls runtime\assistant-session.json: every ACE is inherited (I): the local sandbox-agent group:(I)(M), six unresolved S-1-5-21-*:(I)(M), Kurtz/SYSTEM/Administrators:(F). icacls C:\Users\Kurtz\Documents\KURT shows those ACEs set explicitly (non-inherited) at that level. Get-LocalGroupMember the local sandbox-agent group = two sandbox-agent accounts (both Enabled). Seven enabled local users exist.
findings.scenario: Any process running as a Codex sandbox account (or under one of the six unresolved SIDs if they ever map to an account) reads the token and can drive Kurt's live app: mutate open documents, save/export anywhere under CADkz\Codex or CADkz\projects, open any FCStd. The loopback port itself is reachable from every local account.
findings.consequence: Kurt would notice nothing until a sandboxed agent (or a bug in one) edits or saves over an open project. Today the ACL is probably intentional so sandboxed agents can use the bridge, but nothing states that trust decision; the docs say only "loopback" and "do not publish session files".
findings.reproduction: PowerShell: icacls runtime\assistant-session.json ; Get-LocalGroupMember the local sandbox-agent group ; Get-LocalUser | ? Enabled. A `runas /user:a sandbox-agent account` shell could read the file (not attempted).
findings.proposed_change: 1) Write the session file with an explicit DACL: after write_text, run `icacls <file> /inheritance:r /grant:r "%USERNAME%:F" SYSTEM:F` (or win32security/ctypes SetNamedSecurityInfo), with an opt-in `KURTSHAPE_SESSION_READERS` list (e.g. the local sandbox-agent group) when Kurt wants sandboxed agents to connect. 2) Add a "Threat model" section to docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md stating: loopback reachable by all local accounts; token readable by X; bridge writes bounded by write roots; browser CSRF blocked. 3) Optionally bind the token to the client PID via a second header? Not worth it; the ACL is the lever.
findings.dependencies: Kurt's decision whether the sandbox accounts are meant to reach the bridge.
findings.risk: Restricting the ACL silently breaks sandboxed-agent bridge use; hence the opt-in list and an explicit error message in assistant_client when the file is unreadable.
findings.acceptance: icacls shows no (I) ACEs on the session file and only the allowed principals; new tests/test_bridge.py case on win32 asserts the DACL via icacls output; AGENTS.md documents who can connect. Regression gate: existing bridge suite unchanged.

findings.title: Handler threads have no socket timeout and no concurrency cap; a local client can pin unlimited threads; some disconnects print tracebacks
findings.evidence: Handler defines only log_message/send_json/do_POST (27-39): no `timeout`, so `rfile.read(size)` (53) and header parsing block forever; `ThreadingHTTPServer` with `daemon_threads=True` (95-96) spawns one thread per connection with no bound. except clause (90-93) catches ValueError, queue.Full, BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError only. Probe A1-A3: 200 idle sockets -> active threads 2 -> 202; 50 sockets with `Content-Length: 1000` and a 6-byte body (valid token) -> 252; still 252 after 15 s. A8: a 60 KB `[[[[...` body raised RecursionError inside json.loads, escaped do_POST, client saw RemoteDisconnected and socketserver printed a traceback. A10: closing the 50 partial-body sockets produced 50 `ConnectionAbortedError: [WinError 10053]` tracebacks (send_error(400) on a dead socket is not in the except tuple).
findings.scenario: A buggy or hostile local process (any account; no token needed for the header stage) keeps connections open; each costs a thread (1 MB reserved stack) for the life of the app. Partial-body disconnects and pathological JSON spam the native log/Report view with tracebacks.
findings.consequence: In the probe the app kept answering legitimate requests (A4), so this is resource exhaustion and log noise, not a lockout. With thousands of connections the FreeCAD process would bloat and eventually fail to spawn threads while Kurt has unsaved work.
findings.reproduction: Run scratch bridge_probe.py (transport-only, DummyController): sections A1-A3, A8, A10. Output: ...\scratchpad\area-f-reliability\bridge_probe.out.txt.
findings.proposed_change: In bridge.py Handler: set `timeout = 15` (socket timeout; BaseHTTPRequestHandler then ends the request with 408 on `socket.timeout`); override `ThreadingHTTPServer.process_request` with a `threading.BoundedSemaphore(64)` that answers 503 JSON when exhausted; widen the except to `ConnectionError` (covers ConnectionAbortedError) and add `RecursionError` -> 400; keep protocol HTTP/1.0 (no keep-alive, verified) so threads end after one response.
findings.risk: A 15 s socket timeout must not cut legitimate slow writers: bodies are <= 64 KiB over loopback, so it cannot.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_bridge.py: idle socket and lying-Content-Length socket both end within timeout+1 s and thread count returns to baseline; 65th concurrent connection gets 503 JSON {code:"too_many_connections"}; partial-body disconnect leaves no traceback on stderr (capture with contextlib.redirect_stderr). Gate: existing 7 bridge tests unchanged.

findings.title: Queue-full and malformed-body both answer a bare HTTP 400 HTML page; assistant_client raises HTTPError instead of returning a typed error
findings.lines: 74-79, 90-91; tools/assistant_client.py:25-26
findings.evidence: bridge.py:76-79 on queue.Full completes the ledger with code queue_full then re-raises; 90-91 `except (ValueError,queue.Full): self.send_error(400)`. Probe A5 with 32 blocked requests: 33rd request -> (400, 'text/html;charset=utf-8', '<!DOCTYPE HTML>...Error response'); a tracked mutation likewise 400, while ledger.status reports {status:'cancelled', error.code:'queue_full'}. assistant_client.send does `with opener.open(message,timeout=35) as response: return json.loads(response.read())` so urllib raises `HTTPError: 400`.
findings.scenario: An agent runs a burst (parallel inspects, or a retry storm after outcome_unknown) while the GUI thread is inside a long recompute; the 33rd request fails with a Python exception indistinguishable from a malformed request, and the build script aborts.
findings.consequence: Kurt sees an agent script crash with 'HTTP Error 400: Bad Request' and no CAD error; the ledger knows the real reason but nobody reads it.
findings.reproduction: bridge_probe.py section A5; or against a running app: send 33 `inspect` requests concurrently while a fillet runs.
findings.proposed_change: bridge.py: on queue.Full send 503 with JSON body {ok:false,error:{code:'queue_full',retry_after_ms:250}} and a Retry-After header; on JSON/ValueError send 400 with JSON {code:'invalid_request'}; add a `send_json(result, status)` parameter. assistant_client.send: catch HTTPError, parse a JSON body when Content-Type is application/json and return it as the dict; optional bounded retry on 503.
findings.risk: Clients that relied on HTTPError must adapt; ks.py/bone-mallet scripts only look at res['ok'].
findings.acceptance: tests/test_bridge.py: full queue -> status 503, JSON code queue_full; invalid JSON -> 400 JSON code invalid_request; assistant_client.send returns dicts for both. Gate: A5 oracle tests still see 32 timeouts.

findings.title: 30 s request timeout is within 2x of measured dodec-hub operation times, and no client helper reconciles outcome_unknown
findings.symbol: Bridge.__init__ request_timeout, do_POST timeout branch; assistant_client.send
findings.lines: 16, 80-88; tools/assistant_client.py:16-26; projects/dodec-hub/ks.py:33-44
findings.evidence: bridge.py:16 `request_timeout=30`; 81-88 after `queue.Empty` returns outcome_unknown when started. assistant_client.py:25 `timeout=35`, no handling of outcome_unknown. ks.py:39-41 `if not res.get('ok'): ... raise BridgeError`. projects/dodec-hub/build-bridge.log: `ok fillet RimAndNotches (15.1s)`, `ok fillet SocketBreakouts (9.8s)`, `ok transform_part PlaceHub (7.9s)`, `ok set_part_appearance (5.0s)`, `ok save (3.0s)`; the saved file is 9.7 MB (dodec-hub/Dodec Hub Conformal.FCStd).
findings.scenario: A part twice the hub's complexity, or the same hub while a geometry check or STEP export runs, pushes one fillet past 30 s. The app completes the fillet; the client gets outcome_unknown, raises, and the next run finds a half-built document it must delete_features and rebuild (or hits stale_revision).
findings.consequence: Kurt watches the model finish in the viewport while the agent reports failure and starts over; wasted minutes per iteration and a confusing history.
findings.reproduction: tests/test_bridge.py already shows the mechanics (test_started_timeout_reports_unknown...). Live: run dodec build_bridge.py with Bridge(request_timeout=10) in a private session; RimAndNotches returns outcome_unknown while the feature appears.
findings.proposed_change: tools/assistant_client.send: on error.code == 'outcome_unknown', poll {op:'request_status',request_id} (canonical fast path, bridge.py:56-64) every 0.5 s until status in {completed,failed,cancelled} (cap e.g. 10 min) and return the stored response; document this as the standard client behavior in OPERATION_CONTRACT.md. Server side, optionally accept `timeout_s` (<= 600) per request so a known-long op can wait in-band.
findings.dependencies: None; AGENTS.md should tell agents to use send() rather than raw urllib.
findings.risk: A client that polls forever on a crashed app: bound by the cap and a pid liveness check.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_bridge.py: DummyController delay 0.5 s with request_timeout 0.1 -> send() returns the completed result once; project helpers (ks.py) drop their BridgeError on outcome_unknown. Gate: existing timeout tests unchanged.

findings.title: Save/export over a destination another process holds open fails with a raw WinError and leaves stage-file orphans beside the project
findings.evidence: _save (2797-2811): on any exception only `doc.FileName=old_name; raise` — the `.saving.FCStd` stage is never removed and the `.recovery.FCStd` copy (2804-2806) was already made. _export writes `stage`/`temp` (2817, 2851-2852) and `_replace_export_pair` rolls back targets (2883-2896) but never unlinks the stages. Probe B5: hold probe.FCStd open with a plain read handle, bridge save -> `operation_failed | [WinError 5] Access is denied`, folder afterwards: probe.FCStd, probe.recovery.FCStd, probe.saving.FCStd; a traceback was appended to kurtshape.log. B6: export over an open probe.step -> `export_failed` (pair restored correctly) but probe.exporting.step and probe.step.json.saving remain. Real folders already show the pattern: projects/bone-mallet holds four *.recovery files; nothing cleans stages.
findings.scenario: An agent (or BumpMesh step) reads the STEP/FCStd the app just wrote while the next save/export runs; OneDrive, Defender or a FreeCAD preview handler holds the file; Kurt's own Save gets 'Access is denied' with no hint what holds it, and the project folder slowly fills with .saving/.exporting litter.
findings.consequence: Confusing error text in Messages, orphan files that look like real outputs (an agent could pick up probe.exporting.step), no retry.
findings.reproduction: scratch controller_probe.py sections B5/B6 (isolated session); or GUI: open the project's .step in a Python `open()` and press Export to the same path.
findings.proposed_change: _save: `try/finally` unlink of the stage on failure; map PermissionError/OSError from os.replace to `OperationError('destination_locked', 'Another program holds <name> open; close it and retry', path=...)`; retry os.replace up to 5x with 100 ms backoff for transient AV locks before failing; keep the recovery copy only after success or document that it is intentionally kept. _export/_replace_export_pair: unlink `stage`/`temp` in a finally when not committed; same locked-destination code. Also report the GUI error with the file name, not the WinError text.
findings.risk: Retrying replace while the user genuinely has the file open adds up to 0.5 s to a failing save; acceptable.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_core_safety.py: new cases hold the destination open, assert error code destination_locked, original bytes unchanged, no *.saving/*.exporting files, FileName restored; a success-path assertion that no stage remains (extend test_build_status.absent_export). Gate: existing readonly-sidecar test unchanged.

findings.title: Bridge save can overwrite another project's FCStd (different DocumentId) and re-point the document at it; adopt has the check, save does not
findings.evidence: _save only checks write_path and `if path.exists(): shutil.copy2(path, path.with_suffix('.recovery.FCStd'))` then os.replace (2804-2808). _adopt refuses an existing destination (1888-1889 `adoption_destination_exists`). The GUI Save As path relies on the QFileDialog overwrite prompt (ui.py:2975-2984); the bridge has no equivalent. projects/ folders already contain stray files (`Untitled part.FCStd` in bone-mallet and dodec-hub, `Dodec Hub Conformal2.FCStd`), i.e. path mistakes happen.
findings.scenario: An agent builds a destination from a part name and lands on Kurt's other project file (or a second agent session saves its dry-run document over the live project); the file is replaced, one generation survives as .recovery.FCStd, and the open document's FileName now points at the victim path.
findings.consequence: Kurt discovers his osteotome file now holds a drill; one undo of the mistake exists (.recovery) and is itself overwritten by the next save.
findings.reproduction: Headless: save doc A to a.FCStd, new doc B, bridge `save` B to a.FCStd -> succeeds, a.recovery.FCStd holds A (not run today; logic is unambiguous at 2804-2808).
findings.proposed_change: Before replacing an existing FCStd, read its `Document.xml` from the ZIP (cheap, stdlib) and extract KurtShapeProject.DocumentId; if present and != this document's DocumentId, raise `destination_is_another_project` (details: existing_document_id, existing_name) unless the request has `overwrite:true`. The GUI passes overwrite:true after its dialog confirmation. Unmanaged FCStd destinations (no metadata) also require overwrite:true from the bridge.
findings.risk: Reading Document.xml of a 10 MB archive adds ~tens of ms; acceptable. Scripts that intentionally overwrite must add the flag.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_core_safety.py: save B over A's file rejects with the code and leaves A's bytes and A's FileName intact; with overwrite:true behaves as today. GUI Save As over another project still works after confirmation.

findings.title: inspect has no modified/unsaved flag although the controller already reads it and the GUI title shows it
findings.evidence: _inspect returns native_file but no modified key (probe B10 key list); `_modified(doc)` (1236-1243) already returns `Gui.getDocument(doc.Name).Modified` (None headless) and ui.py:1770-1771 uses it for the '· Unsaved'/'· Modified' suffix. AGENTS.md:42: 'Ask Kurt before restarting KurtShape... (the bridge does not report the modified flag)'.
findings.scenario: An agent wants to restart the app to load a fix, or to close a document, and cannot tell whether Kurt has unsaved work.
findings.consequence: Agents interrupt Kurt with questions, or (worse) assume saved state.
findings.reproduction: list_documents / inspect output has no such key.
findings.proposed_change: Add `modified: self._modified(doc)` and `saved_revision` (revision recorded in _save after success; None for unsaved) to _inspect; include in list_documents; mention in OPERATION_CONTRACT inspect row.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: edit -> inspect.modified true; save -> false; headless -> null documented.

findings.title: No close_document (or feature-visibility) operation; with duplicate_document_id this blocks reopening relocated copies and cleaning up dry-run documents
findings.evidence: OPS (252) has new/open/recover/import_step/adopt but no close; attach raises duplicate_document_id when the same UUID is open (1021-1023). AGENTS.md:22 'Never write an FCStd that is open in the app: the app rejects a second copy... the open tab goes stale' and :44 'no feature-visibility or close-document operation'. set_part_appearance only toggles parts (OPERATION_CONTRACT.md:173).
findings.scenario: Agent rebuilds a part headless, wants the live app to show the new file: it cannot close the stale tab, so Kurt must click; agents that `new` per run leave tabs (and recovery pairs) behind.
findings.consequence: Manual steps and stale tabs; Kurt is asked to close documents the agent opened.
findings.reproduction: capabilities.operations contains no close op.
findings.proposed_change: `close_document {document_id, expected_revision, discard_unsaved:false}`: reject `sketch_edit_active`/`busy` as usual, reject `unsaved_changes` when `_modified(doc)` is True and discard_unsaved is false, then release sketch_edits, snapshots.retire_document(instance_id), geometry.drop_document, App.closeDocument; GUI tick already handles a vanished document (ui.py:1270-1275). `set_feature_visibility {feature, visible}` mapped to ViewObject.Visibility with the existing presentation guard (studio.present).
findings.dependencies: modified flag finding; recovery retire hook for pruning.
findings.risk: Closing while a worker borrows a snapshot: retire_document already handles pinned leases (snapshots.py:135-140).
findings.acceptance: Native tests: close unsaved without flag rejects; with flag closes and a later open of the same UUID succeeds; GUI recipe shows the tab disappearing without prompts.

findings.title: An agent mutation cancels the feature editor Kurt has open, and bridge requests are dispatched while modal GUI dialogs are up
findings.symbol: Panel.tick (bridge dispatch and studio_dialog revision check); Controller._dispatch native-edit guard
findings.lines: 1216-1218, 1231-1235; src/kurtshape/feature_panel.py:39; src/kurtshape/core.py:1573-1580
findings.evidence: ui.py:1216-1218 dispatches a queued bridge request every 25 ms tick unconditionally; 1233-1235 `elif self.studio_dialog and ... Revision != self.studio_dialog.base_revision: self.studio_dialog.reject(); self.notify('Feature canceled because the project changed...')`. The KurtShape feature editor is NonModal (feature_panel.py:39), so core.py:1573-1580 (which blocks only native Gui.Control dialogs and getInEdit) does not stop a bridge pad while Kurt has Extrude/Fillet open. Modal `dialog.exec_()` sites (ui.py:930, 1032, 1091) run nested event loops in which the 25 ms timer still fires.
findings.scenario: Kurt is adjusting a fillet radius in the editor; an agent sends its next step; Kurt's editor closes with 'Feature canceled because the project changed'; he re-picks edges. In a modal assembly dialog the agent's edit lands under the dialog (staged_revision then rejects Kurt's OK with stale_revision).
findings.consequence: Lost dialog input and a feeling that the app fights him; the agent gets no signal that a human is mid-edit.
findings.reproduction: GUI: open Extrude on a sketch, then from a shell send any mutation through tools/assistant_client.py; observe the editor close and the notification. Not run today (no GUI control allowed).
findings.proposed_change: Expose a human-edit lease to the bridge: in Panel.tick, when `self.studio_dialog`, `self.task`, a placement task or `QApplication.activeModalWidget()` is set, answer queued mutations (not READ_OPS) with `{code:'user_editing', retry_after_ms:1000}` instead of dispatching (do it in Bridge.tick via a controller/panel predicate so HTTP threads stay out of Qt); keep inspect/preview flowing. Agents retry on that code (same helper as queue_full).
findings.dependencies: JSON error finding (clients must see the code).
findings.risk: An agent build stalls while Kurt dawdles in a dialog: that is the desired precedence; document it.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: with the Extrude editor open, a bridge pad returns user_editing and the editor stays; after Cancel the same request succeeds. Native: predicate False keeps today's behavior (bridge suite unchanged).

findings.title: Capability gaps ranked by the real projects they unblock: helix path, spline, typed sketch constraints, nth/created_by-through-Hole selectors
findings.lines: 248-252; src/kurtshape/studio.py:16; src/kurtshape/reference_tools.py:8; src/kurtshape/modeling_geometry.py:18
findings.evidence: No op creates a Part::Helix or a sketch BSpline (grep: only core.py:2177-2178 recognizes BSplineCurve endpoints); typed constraints are limited to pierce and project_geometry (OPERATION_CONTRACT.md:99,177); 'No nth-element selector exists' (243). AGENTS.md:22 routes helix/spline work to the headless Controller, which is why zimmer-8mm-drill (helical flute sweeps, build_drill.py docstring) and smith-peterson-osteotome were built headless, not in the live app. dodec-hub/README.md:72 'created_by selectors cannot trace through the Hole features yet'. Hole, add_polyline, add_arc, arbitrary planes and multi-edge references all exist at HEAD (commits 3df4faa..f57d592) but not in the running app.
findings.scenario: Any threaded/fluted part (drill, screw, knurl base) cannot be modeled live; bridge-made sketches have independent endpoint dimensions so hand edits open gaps (PRELIMINARY_REVIEW lead 4; add_polyline fixed this for polylines only); fillets on faces downstream of a Hole must be picked by adjacency.
findings.consequence: Kurt watches the osteotome/drill appear only as finished files instead of live, editable history.
findings.reproduction: capabilities.operations lacks create_helix/add_spline/add_constraint.
findings.proposed_change: In priority order: (1) `create_helix {pitch,height,radius,angle,left_handed,placement}` as a Part::Helix in the Body with a stable id usable as `sweep.path` (S-M; unblocks the drill live); (2) `set_feature_visibility` (S, see close op); (3) `add_constraint {sketch, kind: coincident|tangent|equal|horizontal|vertical|symmetric|point_on_object, refs}` validated with the same DoF/conflict rules as add_polyline (M); (4) `add_spline {sketch, poles|points, periodic}` with pole dimensions optional (M); (5) selector `nth {query, index, order_by}` and Hole-aware created_by element-name parsing (M).
findings.dependencies: App restart to load; AGENTS.md known-gaps paragraph.
findings.risk: Constraint ops must keep the 'fully constrained, unmoved by solve' contract or agents will produce drifting sketches.
findings.acceptance: zimmer drill rebuilt through the live bridge with a helix sweep and valid check_geometry; dodec notch fillets selected by created_by through Hole; native tests per op.

findings.title: Launcher and worktree sprawl: five launchers and five checkouts; KurtShape-green.cmd and KurtShape-sweep.cmd run other checkouts' code against main's live session folder and silently replace its bridge token
findings.lines: tools/update-green-copy.ps1 7-11, 31-53, 147-153; bridge.py 97-98, 121-128; launch-kurtshape.ps1 4-5; recovery.py 15
findings.evidence: Codex/KurtShape-green.cmd and Codex/KurtShape-sweep.cmd run `kurtshape-green\launch-kurtshape.ps1` / `kurtshape-sweep\launch-kurtshape.ps1` with `-RuntimeRoot "%~dp0kurtshape\runtime" -SessionRoot "%~dp0kurtshape\runtime"` (file contents read); `git worktree list` shows kurtshape (f57d592), kurtshape-green (660acc5, Oct 3), kurtshape-opus-review (7d1c56a), kurtshape-sweep (f607984), extrude-review (30f16b2); README 31: 'Earlier local workflow/green-copy launchers ... are historical'; docs/long-run/STATUS.md 12: 'Green copy: still at longrun/Q24a ... updater refused'.
findings.scenario: Kurt double-clicks whichever shortcut is on the desktop (CADkz/KurtShape.lnk per AGENTS.md); an agent starts a second instance from kurtshape-sweep for a test.
findings.consequence: Two processes from different checkouts share runtime/settings.json, shortcuts.user.json, project-recovery and runtime/assistant-session.json (the second overwrites the bridge token), and the 'green' rollback path is 35 commits and two weeks behind the features Kurt uses daily, so it is not a rollback of anything current.
findings.reproduction: cat Codex/KurtShape-green.cmd and Codex/KurtShape-sweep.cmd; `git -c safe.directory=... worktree list`; compare green HEAD 660acc5 to main f57d592 (git log 660acc5..HEAD --oneline | wc -l).
findings.proposed_change: Decide one supported launcher (KurtShape.cmd) and delete or move the other .cmd files into docs/archive with a note; make launch-kurtshape.ps1 default SessionRoot to `<checkout>\runtime` only for the main checkout and require an explicit `-SessionRoot` otherwise; refuse to start when `runtime/assistant-session.json` belongs to a live pid from another checkout (reuse Get-KurtShapeGreenGuard logic from update-green-copy.ps1 31-53). Either retire the green copy or make `tools/update-green-copy.ps1 <tag>` part of the release step (see maintenance process finding) so 'green' means 'last tagged release'.
findings.dependencies: Build identity finding (the guard needs to name checkouts).
findings.risk: Kurt may rely on the sweep/review launchers for side-by-side comparison; keep an explicit `-SessionRoot` path for that.
findings.acceptance: Only one top-level launcher remains; launching a second instance against a session dir that already has a live bridge prints a clear refusal; a PowerShell-level test (tools/ci) runs launch-kurtshape.ps1 -PrintOnly for the main checkout and asserts the session root; docs/long-run/STATUS.md 'Green copy' line is either current or removed.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read: Codex/KurtShape-green.cmd and Codex/KurtShape-sweep.cmd (both run the sibling checkout's launch-kurtshape.ps1 with -RuntimeRoot and -SessionRoot pointing at kurtshape\runtime, exactly as cited), Codex/KurtShape-design-update.cmd (main code, separate SessionRoot runtime\design-workspace, harmless) and Codex/KurtShape-workflow-update.cmd (main code, defaults, harmless duplicate of the in-repo KurtShape.cmd); tools/update-green-copy.ps1 7-11 and 147-153 (generates the green launcher with both roots on main/runtime, as cited; guard logic at 31-53); git worktree list (five worktrees exactly as listed; green 660acc5 Oct 3, sweep f607984 Oct 16 on claude/sweep-tool, opus-review 7d1c56a, extrude-review 30f16b2; all clean); README.md 31 and 41 (as cited); docs/long-run/STATUS.md 12 (as cited); docs/long-run/Q01-green-copy.md (green copy was designed to share main's runtime/profile deliberately); bridge.py 97-98 and 121-128 (assistant-session.json is written unconditionally with the new pid, so a second instance on the same SessionRoot replaces the first instance's url/token; close() only unlinks when the pid matches, confirming the overwrite is known); recovery.py 15 (project-recovery keyed by DocumentId under the shared session dir, no instance lock); settings.py 27-31 (atomic but last-writer-wins). The CADkz/KurtShape.lnk target (read via WScript.Shell, no desktop control) is main's launch-kurtshape.ps1, so Kurt's daily path is main; the hazard needs someone to use the green/sweep .cmd while main runs. AGENTS.md line 33 documents the safe alternative (projects/dodec-hub/start-session.ps1 with its own session dir and port), which mitigates but does not prevent. Corrections: green is 24 commits behind (git log 660acc5..HEAD | wc -l), not 35; the two-week age is right (Oct 3 -> Oct 17). The sibling launchers' launch-kurtshape.ps1 copies are byte-identical to main's modulo CRLF, so the only difference is the Python source they load. Finding stands as a design weakness at medium: a stale bridge token mid-session breaks Kurt's agents, and two instances can interleave checkpoints for the same DocumentId into one project-recovery folder; the saved FCStd itself is not at risk.
findings.refute_evidence: Codex/ holds four .cmd files (design-update Oct 4, green Oct 3, sweep Oct 16, workflow-update Oct 4) plus kurtshape/KurtShape.cmd (Oct 2), which README 31/41 names as the supported one. CADkz/KurtShape.lnk -> powershell -File ...\Codex\kurtshape\launch-kurtshape.ps1. kurtshape-sweep is a live agent branch (claude/sweep-tool, Oct 16 16:34) and its .cmd was created the same day, so the collision path is current, not historical. docs/long-run/STATUS.md 12 confirms the green updater was last refused (process inventory denied), explaining why green is frozen at longrun/Q24a.

judge.kurt_would_notice: If he or an agent double-clicks KurtShape-sweep.cmd or KurtShape-green.cmd while his main window is open, his other agents' bridge calls start landing in the wrong instance (the token file now points at it), and settings.json/recent projects and project-recovery checkpoints interleave between the two. He would also find that 'green' is two weeks and 24 commits behind the features he uses daily, so it is not a rollback of anything current.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Five launchers with similar names and no indication which is current; picking the wrong one loads two-week-old code against the live profile with no warning.
judge.risk: Low. Deleting or archiving the green/sweep .cmd files and adding a pid-ownership refusal in launch-kurtshape.ps1 (stale pid must be tolerated, as bridge.close already does) touches no modeling code. Making -SessionRoot mandatory for non-main checkouts could break an agent script that relies on the default; a warning first is safer.

findings.title: Validation evidence is local-only and unstamped: newest tracked content is Oct 5, 300 screenshots are gitignored, the Oct 15 stage-2 GUI receipts live in another worktree on an unmerged branch, and no runner except bench_core records the commit
findings.lines: .gitignore 13-15; tools/record_evidence.py 46-61; docs/EVERYDAY_UI.md 61-65; tools/perf/bench_core.py 103-107
findings.evidence: .gitignore 13-15: `validation/**`, `!validation/**/`, `!validation/**/*.json` so only JSON is tracked: `git ls-files validation | grep -c png` = 0 (305 PNGs exist locally, dated Oct 1-6; 5 PNGs tracked under docs/); newest tracked validation JSON is validation/sketch-presentation/acceptance-summary.json 2026-10-05 16:06; acceptance-summary.json keys contain regression counts, engine, source_sha256 but no git field (checked validation/sketch-presentation and docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence); only validation/2026-10-03-upgrade/* carry `base_commit`; the Oct 15 Windows validation exists only as bullet prose in docs/EVERYDAY_UI.md 61-65 (no validation/everyday-ui, extrusion-edit, history-lifecycle, dress-up-edit or headless-open folder exists); commits 24bab02/1f0001e/f57d592 (Oct 17) add 1,500+ test lines with no GUI evidence and no README change.

(a) CONFIRMED: README 15 and 117 and ARCHITECTURE.md 5 say '426 native passes/four opt-in skips'; an AST count of every class in tools/run_native_tests.py SUITES gives 558 native test methods (554 + 4 StatusPerformanceTests), 610 across all suites, matching f57d592's '554 passed, 4 opt-in skips'; README 15 presents this under 'Current accepted architecture checkpoint'. (c) CONFIRMED: STATUS_REPORT.md 87 recommends `--suite native ... --timeout 210`; run_native_tests.py 324/456 applies --timeout per suite process (default 1800); the native suite took 321 s on Oct 17 (536 tests) and 287 s on Oct 16 versus 177 s on Oct 8 (430 tests), so the documented command now times out. (d) CONFIRMED and stronger: STATUS_REPORT 3/108 and README 15 say publication is pending, yet HEAD == origin/main and 13 hosted runs were triggered by pushes since Oct 13; README 119 ('S19 does not run ... hosted CI') and 121 ('Hosted GUI rendering remains unverified') are also false, CI runs and fails (see G-04). (e) WEAK: docs/M1_PROGRESS.md 3 'Updated October 6' is true of its content: 5e9824f (Oct 16) only committed Oct-6-dated sections; this is stale coverage, not a contradiction. (f) WEAK: CONTRACT_REVISION has been 0 since 559e034 (Oct 4) while OPERATION_CONTRACT.md changed in 8 commits since Oct 13 and the op set grew to 73 (52 Controller.ARGS keys + studio 12 + reference_tools 6 + modeling_geometry 3, matching the finder's number); hole, add_polyline, add_arc, create_plane and edit_dress_up are documented in the contract, so the doc does not contradict the code; no written policy requires a revision bump and `capabilities` is the discovery mechanism, so this is a design weakness, not a doc defect. (g)/(h) were truncated in the batch file and could not be verified; README 51 (four opt-in perf methods, three external-fixture skips) and 89 (126 + 3 = 129 records in shortcuts.json) check out. Net: six verifiable contradictions, two of the eight weak; classification and severity stand because the false CI/publication statements actively hide a red pipeline and the stale totals/button list mislead the agents that work this repo.
