findings.scenario: Kurt returns after a week, or a new agent session starts, and needs: what is the current build, what works, how to run checks, where evidence is.
findings.consequence: Hours of reconstruction (this review needed git log, runtime/test-tmp and commit messages to date the state); stale pages are indistinguishable from current ones; every milestone report re-states totals that immediately go stale.
findings.reproduction: Open README.md and try to find 'how do I run the tests' and 'what is the latest validated commit' within one screen; open docs/ and pick which of M1_PROGRESS.md, STATUS_REPORT.md, long-run/STATUS.md, INTERFACE_PASS.md is current.
findings.proposed_change: Adopt a small maintenance process: (1) docs/CURRENT.md generated by `tools/evidence_index.py` + `tools/check_docs.py` (never hand-edited): HEAD SHA/date, engine hash, suite totals from the last run report, GUI recipe table with last-run commit/date/result, open limitations list (hand-maintained block), launcher name; README links to it in its first paragraph. (2) README reorganised to What / Launch / Model / Assistant / Verify / Contribute (≤ 80 lines), with the dated paragraphs moved to CHANGELOG.md (one line per commit group) and milestone reports moved under docs/archive/<date>-<name>/ with a one-line index in docs/README.md. (3) 'Keep current' set = README, ARCHITECTURE, OPERATION_CONTRACT, DESIGN, docs/CURRENT.md, docs/EVIDENCE.md, the per-feature guides (EXTRUSION_EDIT, FILLET_CHAMFER_EDIT, EVERYDAY_UI, HISTORY_LIFECYCLE, STEP_IMPORT, SOLIDWORKS_NAVIGATION, ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS); everything else is archive and gets a top banner 'Historical (<date>, commit <sha>)'. (4) Release ritual per tag: run-checks -Full, the recipe set, evidence_index, update green copy to the tag, bump CONTRACT_REVISION if OPS changed.
findings.risk: Archiving may hide context agents rely on; keep the archive index searchable and keep links working.
findings.acceptance: A newcomer can answer 'current commit, test totals, how to run checks, where evidence is' from docs/CURRENT.md alone; README under 80 lines with headings; check_docs.py enforces that no non-archive doc quotes a native total other than the inventory; every archived page carries the banner.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read README.md in full and counted: no heading before '## Launch' at line 25; lines 3-23 are seven dated status paragraphs (U2, extrusion edit, fillet/chamfer, everyday UI, history lifecycle, M1, S18/S19, Oct 6, Oct 5, Q03, Oct 2 review); verification instructions are spread over 104-129 and point to STATUS_REPORT (prepared Oct 8), INTERFACE_PASS (Oct 2-3) and M1_PROGRESS (content Oct 6). findings.title: Coverage gaps: real window-close path, extrusion-preview worker on shutdown, DPI matrix, settings schema and contract inventory have no automated tests (worker shutdown for geometry check and STEP export is already covered by GUI recipes)
findings.lines: ui.py 4273-4276, 4279-4309, 4328; settings.py 10-16; tools/run_gui_recipe.ps1 93-95; tools/geometry-check-lifecycle-validation.FCMacro 318-333; tools/step-export-validation.FCMacro 872-881
findings.evidence: No test imports kurtshape.ui (`grep -lE 'kurtshape\.ui' tests/*.py` → none) although ui.py is 4,341 lines; shutdown() (4279-4309) cancels STEP/geometry workers, stops three timers, closes 12 helpers and the bridge; the Close guard (4271-4277) runs finish_sketch; `main.destroyed.connect(panel.shutdown)` (4328) is the only trigger; GUI recipes end with `QApplication.quit` (gui-validation.FCMacro 27/311, history-lifecycle-validation.FCMacro 261) and check exit code, not that workers exited or logs are clean; DPI: tests/test_sketch_cursor.py 97-125 cover cursor DPR only, startup.py has no test, docs/INTERFACE_PASS.md 5 'The tested display scale is 150%'; preferences: settings.py 10-16 has no schema version; headless coverage of topology/parameters/rollback/cancellation/workers/recovery/focus is strong (see architecture_notes).
findings.scenario: Kurt closes the window with an active sketch while an exact preview child and a STEP export child are running, or opens the app on a 100%/200% monitor, or a future build renames a settings key.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the close path show up as orphaned freecad python children, lost recovery pairs or a hung exit; DPI regressions show up only on Kurt's 150% screen; preference breakage silently resets state.
findings.reproduction: Verification needed: write the recipes below; today there is nothing to run.
findings.proposed_change: Prioritised missing tests: (1) GUI recipe `shutdown-lifecycle`: open the plate, start a sketch, start an Extrude preview, trigger an eligible STEP export, then close the main window; assert the finish-sketch path, that every child pid recorded by the worker modules has exited within 10 s, no 'Traceback' in freecad.log, recovery pair published, exit code 0. (2) GUI recipe `tab-close-during-worker`: close the document tab while preview/check/export children run; assert no stale publication (pairs with test_step_export_jobs.py 634 at GUI level). (3) DPI matrix: add `-ScaleFactor` to run_gui_recipe.ps1 setting QT_SCALE_FACTOR (already in the restored env list) and run startup-view, theme-startup and sketch-origin-snap at 1.0/1.5/2.0 with DPR-relative pixel assertions. (4) tests/test_preferences.py (headless): settings.json with unknown keys, wrong types and a legacy shape loads without data loss and persists a schema_version; shortcuts.user.json with one stale id keeps the others (see shortcut finding). (5) tests/test_contract_inventory.py: capabilities.operations equals the op set parsed from OPERATION_CONTRACT.md and equals the union of core/studio/reference_tools/modeling_geometry OPS. (6) A headless `Panel` construction smoke test using FreeCADGui offscreen (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, `FreeCADGui.showMainWindow()`) that builds Panel(Controller()), calls shutdown(), and asserts timers inactive and event filters removed; if FreeCADGui cannot start offscreen, make it a hidden-GUI recipe instead.
findings.dependencies: Orphaned-recipe finding (runner changes), build identity (for log headers).
findings.risk: Hidden-GUI recipes are slower (minutes); keep them out of run-checks default and in the scheduled set.
findings.acceptance: Recipes (1)-(3) pass on HEAD and are in the runner table and CI matrix; tests (4)-(5) are in SUITES; a deliberate regression (comment out `self.extrusion_preview.close()` in shutdown) makes recipe (1) fail.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read: ui.py 4255-4341 (Close guard is actually 4273-4276, shutdown 4279-4309, main.destroyed.connect at 4328 as cited), tests/ listing (49 files; grep confirms none imports kurtshape.ui), tests/test_sketch_cursor.py 90-130 (DPR cursor coverage as cited), settings.py 1-45 (no schema version; invalid JSON/non-dict silently resets to {}), startup.py (no unit test), docs/INTERFACE_PASS.md line 5 ('tested display scale is 150%'), tools/run_gui_recipe.ps1 1-115 and 159-185. What did not hold: (1) 'ui.py has no automated protection' is wrong in spirit: 13 GUI recipe macros under tools/ import kurtshape.ui and run through run_gui_recipe.ps1, and 20 of the 52 recipes are devicePixelRatio-aware; (2) 'recipes end with QApplication.quit and check exit code, not that workers exited' is false for the two worker kinds the scenario names: tools/geometry-check-lifecycle-validation.FCMacro 318-333 starts a geometry check child, calls panel.shutdown(), asserts the job is invalidated, polling stops, the child exits and releases its archive, then asserts 'Every owned child has confirmed cleanup' and records worker_pids; tools/step-export-validation.FCMacro 872-881 does the same for a STEP export child (shutdown invalidates export without destination writes; cleanup_complete and pid recorded); closing the source document mid-job is also covered (geometry-check-lifecycle 311-316, step-export 861, test_step_export_jobs.py 634, test_geometry_check_jobs.py 529); (3) 'QT_SCALE_FACTOR already in the restored env list' is false: run_gui_recipe.ps1 line 95 restores QT_QPA_PLATFORM, not QT_SCALE_FACTOR; (4) startup-view-validation.FCMacro 78-104 already asserts maximize on the primary screen. What held: nothing exercises the real exit path (QEvent.Close guard with an active sketch, then main.destroyed -> shutdown, whose Python slot may or may not run before interpreter teardown), the extrusion preview worker is not covered on shutdown (extrusion-preview-validation only closes documents), every recipe runs at the host's DPI only, settings.json has no schema version and a corrupt file silently drops project_roots/recent_projects, and no test compares capabilities.operations to OPERATION_CONTRACT.md (test_runtime_layout 44-50 checks only the contract constants). The classification 'opportunity' is honest; severity high is not, since the named worker-orphan scenario is already guarded and the uncovered paths are annoyance-level.
findings.refute_evidence: grep -l 'kurtshape.ui' tools/*.FCMacro -> 13 recipes; grep -l devicePixelRatio tools/*.FCMacro -> 20 recipes; run_gui_recipe.ps1 line 4 registers startup-view, theme-startup and sketch-origin-snap, so the proposed DPI matrix has recipes to reuse but needs QT_SCALE_FACTOR plumbing added. settings.py 11-16: json/OSError or non-dict -> self.data = {} with no message, so a damaged settings.json silently loses user-granted project_roots (then save outside the default roots is rejected with path_outside_workspace until re-granted; see test_review_followup.py 393-401).

judge.kurt_would_notice: Day to day nothing; he would notice only after a regression in the close path (an orphaned freecad child or a hung exit after closing with a sketch open and an Extrude preview running) or after a damaged settings.json silently forgets his granted project folders and recent list. Both are recoverable annoyances, not lost geometry.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: On a 100% or 200% monitor they might hit cursor/snap/toolbar layout glitches that no recipe has ever run at; otherwise nothing visible.
judge.risk: Low to product code; the work is tests and runner plumbing. GUI recipes are slow and host-dependent, so a DPI matrix triples runtime and a window-close recipe must tolerate FreeCAD's own exit prompts. A settings schema_version must migrate the current shape without dropping project_roots.

findings.title: One unknown id in shortcuts.user.json discards every user rebinding, the message does not name it, and the help dialog's Rebind/Reset cannot clear it
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/shortcuts.py 49-51, 92-96, 375-389
findings.evidence: shortcuts.py 50: `if set(overrides["bindings"]) - known: raise ValueError("Unknown shortcut override")`; 91-96: `except (ValueError, OSError) as exc: self.status_callback("User shortcuts rejected: " + str(exc)); self.registry = load_registry(registry_path, ROOT / "runtime" / "no-user-shortcuts")`. Headless probe (scratch probe_shortcut_override.py): a file with one unknown id raises ValueError; constructing ShortcutRouter with it yields 129 default entries and the message 'User shortcuts rejected: Unknown shortcut override'; a valid override in the same file is not applied.
findings.scenario: Kurt rebinds a few keys; a later build renames or removes one shortcut id in shortcuts.json (the registry has changed in 617c537/a558615 era commits), or Kurt hand-edits the file.
findings.consequence: All his rebindings stop working at once with a single Messages line that does not say which id was unknown; the help dialog's Rebind path then rewrites the file from scratch.
findings.reproduction: Write <session>/shortcuts.user.json = {"schema_version":1,"bindings":{"sketch.pierce":"Ctrl+Alt+G","feature.gone":"Ctrl+Alt+H"}}; start the app (or run the probe): pierce stays Shift+G and Messages shows the rejection.
findings.proposed_change: In load_registry, collect unknown ids into `registry["ignored_overrides"]` instead of raising, apply the known ones, and have ShortcutRouter report 'Ignored unknown shortcut overrides: feature.gone' once; keep raising for schema/JSON errors; show ignored entries greyed in the help dialog with a 'Remove' button. Add a RouterTests case.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_shortcuts.py RouterTests: stale + valid overrides → valid applied, stale listed in ignored_overrides, one status message naming it; existing conflict test still raises.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read src/kurtshape/shortcuts.py 40-96 and 366-390, tests/test_shortcuts.py 23-36 and 122-128, docs/ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md 7, and the git history of shortcuts.json and shortcuts.py; ran a headless probe under the bundled pythonw.exe with an isolated KURTSHAPE_SESSION_DIR under the scratch folder. HELD exactly as stated: with {sketch.pierce: Ctrl+Alt+G, feature.gone: Ctrl+Alt+H} the router emitted 'User shortcuts rejected: Unknown shortcut override', loaded 129 default entries and left sketch.pierce at Shift+G (overridden None); the same file with only the valid id applied Ctrl+Alt+G (overridden True). The code path is lines 49-51 (set difference, raise without naming the id) and 92-96 (whole-file fallback to runtime/no-user-shortcuts). No test exercises partial application; test_shortcuts.py 23-36 asserts only the conflict ValueError. STRONGER than stated: the help dialog cannot repair the file. change() at 375 re-reads the existing file so the stale id stays in data, stages the edit, then validates the stage with load_registry (383), which raises the same error, so every Rebind and Reset fails with 'Shortcut unchanged: Unknown shortcut override' and os.replace never runs; the finder's 'rewrites the file from scratch' is wrong - the file is untouched and only a hand edit recovers. WEAKER than stated: the scenario's premise that the registry changed in the 617c537/a558615 era is wrong; shortcuts.json last changed in df26c91 (Oct 3) and a558615 only added a search_provider hook to shortcuts.py, so no id rename has happened in this repo's history. The realistic triggers today are a typo in a hand edit or a future id rename. ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md 7 documents 'invalid startup files fall back to usable defaults', so the fail-closed fallback is intentional design; the defect is that one unknown id poisons the known ones, the message names nothing, and the UI is locked out of fixing it. Classification verified_defect and severity medium stand: when it bites, all rebindings vanish at once, the message gives no clue which id, and the built-in Rebind/Reset path cannot clear it; the narrow trigger lowers priority, not impact.
findings.refute_evidence: Headless probe (scratch verify2/g10/probe_g10.py, bundled pythonw.exe -B, isolated session/home/temp): messages ['User shortcuts rejected: Unknown shortcut override'], entries 129, pierce Shift+G; valid-only file: messages [], pierce Ctrl+Alt+G, overridden True. git log -- shortcuts.json: df26c91 2026-10-03 is the latest change; git show a558615 -- src/kurtshape/shortcuts.py adds only the search_provider branch in show_search. Help-dialog table rows come from registry entries, so an unknown id cannot be selected for Reset.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only if he rebinds keys and later a build renames an id or he mistypes one by hand: every custom binding reverts to Onshape defaults, Messages shows one line that names no id, and Help > Shortcuts > Rebind/Reset answers 'Shortcut unchanged: Unknown shortcut override' until he edits runtime/shortcuts.user.json himself. If he uses the Onshape defaults, never.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: A SolidWorks user who rebinds a handful of keys to their habits is the most likely rebinder; the same all-or-nothing loss and dead-end dialog would read as the app forgetting their settings.
judge.risk: Low. Applying known ids and reporting the unknown ones by name changes only the error path; keep raising for schema/JSON errors and add a RouterTests case for the partial-apply path.

findings.title: Stale per-document workspace mode: a modeled Part Studio renders as an empty Assembly workspace after the canonical Create Assembly path
findings.lines: ui.py:821-823 (stale write), 879-886 (create_assembly new-document branch), 1636-1639 and 1645-1650 (refresh honours remembered mode), 1818-1819 (empty-assembly status), 3405-3407 (Create Assembly enabled when no assembly), 1244-1256 (tick refresh on document switch), general_actions.py:198-210 (_activate -> tick); workspace_modes resets only at ui.py:813
findings.evidence: Choosing 'Assembly' in the combo on a modeled Part Studio P with no assembly document open falls through to line 821-823: `self.workspace_mode = mode` / `self.workspace_modes[self.state['document_id']] = mode`. Create Assembly then creates a NEW document A (879-882) and only sets workspace_modes[A]. Nothing ever resets workspace_modes[P]. Returning to P by clicking its tab or Ctrl+Space runs tick() -> refresh(); P has no assembly, so line 1639 returns the remembered 'assembly' and line 1649 calls refresh_assembly, which shows 'Instances (0) / Joints (0)', the Assembly toolbar with Create Assembly enabled, and the status 'Create Assembly to begin. Insert saved FCStd parts...' (1818-1819). The feature history and model toolbar are hidden.
findings.scenario: Kurt models a bracket, picks Assembly, clicks Create Assembly, names it, inserts parts, then clicks the bracket's tab to tweak a dimension.
findings.consequence: His part appears to have lost its features and tools; the combo says 'Assembly' on a document that has none. Clicking Create Assembly here (enabled, since P has no assembly) spawns a second assembly document. Recovery requires choosing 'Part Studio' in the combo, which is not obvious.
findings.reproduction: GUI: New part -> sketch+extrude -> combo Assembly -> Create Assembly 'Asm' -> Insert any FCStd -> click the first tab (or Ctrl+Space). Expect: Part Studio toolbar and features. Observe: assembly chrome with empty Instances/Joints. (Source trace above; a Panel-level test can stub `state` and `workspace_modes`.)
findings.proposed_change: In Panel.create_assembly, after `self.operation('new', ...)` succeeds, set `self.workspace_modes[tokens['_document_id']] = 'part_studio'` for the source document. Harden Panel.refresh: treat a remembered 'assembly' mode as valid only when the document actually contains an Assembly object or is the document currently being prepared (`self.workspace_documents.get('assembly') == doc.Name`); otherwise fall back to 'part_studio'. Optionally drop the 'empty assembly workspace' state entirely by making Create Assembly available from the combo/Document menu in Part Studio mode.
findings.risk: low; only the mode dictionary changes. Keep the bridge-created-assembly auto-switch (ui.py:1637) intact.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe (validate-review-gui assembly scenario) gains a check: after Create Assembly from a modeled Part Studio, activating the original Part Studio tab shows the model toolbar, Features list and combo 'Part Studio'. Unit test on Panel.refresh with workspace_modes pre-seeded to 'assembly' and no assembly in state asserts workspace_mode == 'part_studio'.
findings.refute_reasoning: Source trace holds at HEAD f57d592. Picking 'Assembly' on a modeled Part Studio P with no assembly document open falls through set_workspace_mode to ui.py:821-823 and writes workspace_modes[P]='assembly'. create_assembly (ui.py:879-886) then runs operation('new') because P is modeled, creates the assembly in the new document A and only ever writes workspace_modes[A] (via refresh at 1636-1637 and set_workspace_mode at 821-823). Nothing resets P: grep shows workspace_modes is written only at 813, 823, 1637 and 1639. Returning to P by MDI tab or Ctrl+Space goes through general_actions._activate (198-210) -> tick -> refresh (ui.py:1244-1256), where assembly_state() is empty so 1639 returns the remembered 'assembly' and 1645-1650 calls refresh_assembly: 'Instances (0) / Joints (0)', status 'Create Assembly to begin...' (1818-1819), model bar hidden (3408-3409) and Create Assembly enabled because P has no assembly (3405-3407). A second Create Assembly there spawns another assembly document because P is modeled. The only reset path is choosing 'Part Studio' in the combo while in A, which hits line 813 (workspace_modes[target]='part_studio') before activating P; the GUI recipe tools/assembly-gui-validation.FCMacro:239-247 and :363-365 returns to the original project only that way, so the tab/Ctrl+Space path is untested. No fix in the git log (workspace_modes unchanged since 10c333f). Verified by deterministic code reading, not a runtime probe; no Panel-level test exists.
findings.refute_evidence: workspace_documents['part_studio'] is also left pointing at the assembly document A after the operation('new') refresh (ui.py:1640-1641), so the combo's 'remembered' Part Studio target is stale too; it still works because line 811 falls back to candidates[-1].

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only in the GUI: after Combo->Assembly->Create Assembly from a modeled part, tabbing back to the part shows an empty Assembly workspace with no feature history and the combo reading 'Assembly'; he would hunt for his features before trying the combo. Through the bridge he never hits it (bridge-created assemblies land in the correct mode via refresh, and the stale flag is only written by the combo).
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Immediately and alarmingly: the part looks converted into an empty assembly, the modeling toolbar is gone, and the enabled Create Assembly button invites creating a second assembly document. Recovery (choose Part Studio in the combo) is not discoverable.
judge.risk: Low. Resetting workspace_modes[source]='part_studio' after the operation('new') in create_assembly, plus making refresh treat a remembered 'assembly' mode as valid only for the document being prepared (workspace_documents['assembly']) or one that actually holds an Assembly object, touches only the Panel's mode bookkeeping. Keep the empty-assembly state reachable for the Combo->Create Assembly path or the GUI recipe check at line 240 breaks.

findings.title: Assembly failures reach the user as one sentence; residuals, feature names and native reasons in the error payload are discarded
findings.symbol: Panel._operation (failure branch) / Panel.notify; core.Controller.dispatch error dict; assembly.solve / assembly._reference
findings.lines: ui.py:1343-1352 (failure branch), 656-666 (notify), 1220-1229 (bridge failure notification, also message-only); core.py:1794-1797 (error dict with details, last_failures); assembly.py:443 (reason), 826-827 (features), 849-856 (residuals)
findings.evidence: EXP1 payload from the real controller: message 'Native Assembly did not satisfy every requested joint' plus residuals naming Base ('The grounded occurrence moved'), FixedJoint (rotation 2.22 rad), SecondFixed (1.41 mm, 3.93 rad) and Conflict. EXP1b: 'This occurrence does not have a supported selected subelement' with reason 'Shape index 99 out of bound 6'. The GUI path shows and retains only the first sentence; `last_failed_attempt` (core.py:1402) is never rendered by ui.py (no reference to it).
findings.scenario: Kurt adds a third fixed joint that over-constrains two blocks, or types 'Face12' when the part has six faces.
findings.consequence: He sees a red one-liner and has no idea which joint conflicts or that the face index is out of range; the only diagnostic is a generic sentence in Messages. Compared with SolidWorks' over-defined mate highlighting this is a dead end.
findings.reproduction: Run scratchpad\area-h-assembly\exp_assembly.py (EXP1/EXP1b) and compare the payload with what Panel._operation forwards.
findings.proposed_change: In Panel._operation failure branch, after notify, append structured detail lines to Messages: for each entry in error.get('features', []) + error.get('residuals', []) write `<label>: <message> (<residual values>)` using the history labels; append `Reason: <reason>` when present; set the status text to '<message> — see Messages'. Select/scroll the offending joint in the history (`self.select_feature(entry['feature'])`) when exactly one non-grounded joint is named. Same path serves STEP import failures (`step_import_failed` reason) and `invalid_assembly_source` reasons.
findings.risk: low
findings.acceptance: GUI assembly recipe: after the deliberate conflicting joint, Messages contains the lines 'FixedJoint: Native solution does not satisfy the joint' and 'Conflict: ...'; the status ends with 'see Messages'. tests/test_assembly.py already asserts residual names; add a Panel-level unit test for the formatter.
findings.refute_reasoning: Panel._operation's failure branch (ui.py:1343-1352) forwards only response['error']['message'] to notify, and notify (656-666) writes that same string to the status label, tooltip and Messages. The bridge-failure notification in tick (1220-1229) is likewise message-only. core.py:1794 builds the error dict as {'code','message', **details} so features/residuals/reason/native_code reach the GUI and are dropped; last_failed_attempt (core.py:1402) is never referenced in ui.py (grep: no matches for last_failed_attempt, residuals, 'reason'). assembly.py:443 attaches reason (EXP1b: 'Shape index 99 out of bound 6'), 826-827 attaches features, 849-856 attaches residuals per joint with mm/rad values. The finder's probe log (exp_assembly.log lines 11-14) shows the real payloads. The GUI recipe (assembly-gui-validation.FCMacro:308) only asserts that 'did not satisfy' lands in Messages, consistent with the one-liner. Not fixed in the git log. WORKFLOW.md:19 documents 'Native solver errors appear in red status text and are retained in Messages', so the one-liner is the current design, which makes design_weakness the honest class.
findings.refute_evidence: core.py:1938 raises step_import_failed with reason=str(exc) through the same path, so STEP open failures also lose the native reason in the GUI.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Through the bridge he already receives the full error dict (residuals, reason, native_code) in the JSON response, so the bridge path is unaffected. In the GUI he would see only 'Native Assembly did not satisfy every requested joint' and have to open the bridge or guess which joint conflicts.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: A red one-liner with no joint name and no hint that 'Face12' is out of range; compared with SolidWorks' over-defined mate flags or Onshape's mate error list it reads as a dead end, and the Messages panel adds nothing beyond the same sentence.
judge.risk: Low: additive lines in Messages plus a status suffix. Format rotation residuals in degrees rather than radians and label joints by history name, otherwise the detail is as opaque as the one-liner. Selecting the offending joint in the history is safe only when exactly one non-grounded joint is named.

findings.title: Joint and Move dialogs are modal and validate only after closing; a rejected joint or a constrained-instance Move discards the form, with references recoverable only from the surviving viewport selection
findings.lines: ui.py:980-1043 (assembly_joint: modal QDialog, exec_() at 1032, dispatch at 1040), 1045-1100 (move dialog, type-only pre-check at 1056-1058, instance branch 1074-1084); assembly.py:426-444 (_reference validation inside the mutation), 580-587 (move_instance rejects constrained occurrences); feature_panel.py:1-46 (modeless FeaturePanel)
findings.evidence: assembly_joint builds a QDialog, calls exec_() at line 1032, and only then dispatches create/edit (1040). Any rejection (EXP1b typo, EXP1 conflict) arrives after the dialog is gone; the typed name, type and references are lost. move_assembly_selection does not consult `connected_to_ground` or joint references before showing six fields (1074-1084); EXP1c shows the core rejects afterwards with 'Use joint movement for constrained occurrences'. The help text itself admits the workaround: 'Ctrl-select a reference on each instance before opening this tool' (998). Extrude/Fillet already use the modeless FeaturePanel with viewport picking.
findings.scenario: Kurt opens Fixed, realises he wants a different face, cannot click the viewport (modal), types 'Face7' wrongly, presses Enter, gets a red status line and an empty dialog on retry.
findings.consequence: Joint creation is slower and more error-prone than in any mainstream CAD; mistakes cost the whole form. Keyboard access is fine (Enter/Escape via QDialogButtonBox), but the interaction model is the problem.
findings.reproduction: GUI: Insert two parts, click Fixed without pre-selection, try to click a face (blocked), type Face99, Create joint -> status error, dialog closed.
findings.proposed_change: Rebuild the joint editor on FeaturePanel (modeless dock, Confirm/Cancel header): a Gui.Selection observer fills First/Second from viewport clicks (reuse Panel.assembly_references), each reference row shows the picked element and validity, Confirm is enabled only when both references pass a read-only check (new READ op `assembly_reference_check` wrapping assembly._reference without mutation, or run the proposal through the existing `preview` clone). On operation failure keep the panel open and show the error inline (ties to finding 2). For Move: disable 'Move free instance' for instances referenced by any joint/ground (inspect already returns joints[*].first/second and instances[*].grounded) and offer 'Move <joint>' instead; keep the numeric dialog for typed coordinates.
findings.dependencies: finding 2 for inline error text; FeaturePanel reuse
findings.risk: medium: selection observers must not conflict with sketch/reference pickers (sketch_references.py, edge_picking.py); gate on workspace_mode == 'assembly'.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: open Fixed with nothing selected, click a face on each of two instances, see both rows populate, Confirm creates the joint; type an invalid element -> inline error, panel stays open, previous values retained. Existing 58 assembly GUI checks still pass.
findings.refute_reasoning: The mechanics are confirmed: assembly_joint builds a QDialog and calls exec_() (ui.py:994-1032), reads the fields after the dialog is gone (1034-1035) and only then dispatches create/edit (1040); any core rejection (assembly.py:426-444 reference checks, 849-856 solver residuals) arrives with the dialog closed and no retry. move_assembly_selection (1045-1100) screens only joint type (1056-1058) and opens six placement fields for any instance; assembly.py:580-587 rejects grounded or jointed instances afterwards (EXP1c), although inspect already returns instances[*].grounded, connected_to_ground and joints[*].first/second. The FeaturePanel (feature_panel.py:1-46) is a modeless dock that Extrude/Fillet already use, so the better pattern exists in the codebase. Severity is overstated, though: the dialog pre-fills both references from the current viewport selection (ui.py:990, 1013-1019), that workflow is documented in the dialog help (998) and WORKFLOW.md:46, and a rejected operation does not clear Gui.Selection (the failure branch at 1343-1352 does not call refresh or clear selection), so reopening re-populates the references; only the typed name and type are lost. The cost is friction and lost typing, not blocked work or data loss, which is medium impact. The GUI recipe drives the dialogs by object name (assembly-gui-validation.FCMacro:154-178), so a rebuild must update it.
findings.refute_evidence: Keyboard access through QDialogButtonBox (Enter/Escape) works as the finder notes; the interaction model, not accessibility, is the issue.

judge.kurt_would_notice: In the GUI he would feel the modal block when he wants to re-pick a face mid-dialog, and he would lose the joint name on a solver rejection. Through the bridge he types instance/subelement references from inspect output and gets structured rejections, so the dialogs do not affect him there.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Immediately: in Onshape or SolidWorks a mate dialog stays open while you click faces; here the viewport is blocked, references are typed as 'Face7', and a typo or over-constraint closes the dialog with a red one-liner. Move on a jointed part opening six fields and then failing reads as a bug.
judge.risk: Moderate. A FeaturePanel-based joint editor needs a Gui.Selection observer, a read-only reference check (a new READ op or a preview-clone run), error display that keeps the panel open, and rework of the GUI validation macro that finds the QDialog by name. The cheap interim fixes are small: disable 'Move free instance' for grounded or jointed instances from inspect data (S), and re-show the joint dialog pre-filled with the previous values after a rejection (S).

findings.title: Assembly documents opened with an engine/build rebuild reason stay 'Rebuild required' (Solve never clears it, export is blocked) and the Assembly workspace offers no Rebuild
findings.symbol: Controller._rebuild_reason_on_open / Controller._build_status / dispatch ASSEMBLY_OPS branch; Panel.make_toolbars (assembly_bar); tool_search._context_reason
findings.lines: core.py:1281-1292 (reason only for ProgramVersion or FreeCAD/OCCT stamp change), 1339-1341, 1515-1517, 1647-1665, 1686-1687, 2815-2816; ui.py:584-598 (assembly_bar, no Rebuild), 183 (native menu bar hidden), 807-820, 1820-1821, 2765-2768 (tool search contexts), 2820-2822 (activate refuses 'Switch to' entries), 3408; tool_search.py:140-141
findings.evidence: EXP2 (headless, real Controller): with RebuildReason='saved_by_other_build' on an assembly document, build_status 'needs_rebuild'; `solve_assembly` returns ok but build_status stays 'needs_rebuild'; dispatching `rebuild` sets it to 'valid'. The GUI offers no way to dispatch `rebuild` in assembly mode: the model bar is hidden (ui.py:3408), tool search refuses ('Switch to Part Studio'), and the combo switch activates another document.
findings.scenario: After any KurtShape/FreeCAD update (the running app is already an older build than HEAD), Kurt opens last week's assembly: status 'Rebuild required · saved by another application build', Export refuses, Solve 'succeeds' but the status never clears.
findings.consequence: Assembly looks broken with no visible remedy; only the bridge `rebuild` op (or editing in Part Studio mode, which is a different document) clears it.
findings.reproduction: exp_assembly.py EXP2; GUI: open an assembly saved by a different build, press Solve, try Export.
findings.proposed_change: Add `self.tool(self.assembly_bar, 'Rebuild', lambda: self.operation('rebuild'), 'Rebuild the assembly after an engine or build change', 'Std_Refresh', command='Std_Refresh')` to Panel.make_toolbars and add it to assembly_actions so it follows the managed/enabled rules; and/or in the ASSEMBLY_OPS branch (core.py:1657-1665) call `self._mark_rebuilt(doc)` after a successful solve when `meta.RebuildReason` is an engine/build reason and no object is Touched/missing. Mirror the 'Rebuild required · …' toast (ui.py:1373-1374) with the hint 'Assembly → Rebuild'.
findings.risk: low; `rebuild` already works on assembly documents (EXP2).
findings.acceptance: tests/test_assembly.py: set RebuildReason, dispatch `rebuild` -> build_status valid and export succeeds; GUI assembly recipe: Rebuild action discoverable/enabled in Assembly mode and clears the status. Regression gate: any new rebuild reason must keep a GUI path in both workspaces (test asserts assembly_bar contains 'Rebuild').
findings.refute_reasoning: The mechanism holds exactly as the finder's EXP2 log shows (exp_assembly.log lines 15-18): with RebuildReason set on an assembly document, build_status is needs_rebuild, solve_assembly returns ok but leaves it needs_rebuild, and only `rebuild` flips it to valid. Code confirms it: the ASSEMBLY_OPS branch (core.py:1647-1665) recomputes and calls _build_status but never _mark_rebuilt; only op == 'rebuild' does (core.py:1686-1687); _build_status keeps needs_rebuild while meta.RebuildReason is non-empty (core.py:1339-1341); _export refuses anything but 'valid' (core.py:2815-2816). The GUI gap is also real: the assembly bar (ui.py:584-598) has Solve but no Rebuild; the model bar with Rebuild is hidden in assembly mode (ui.py:3408); tool search tags model-bar tools context 'model' (ui.py:2765) so in the assembly workspace Rebuild reports 'Switch to Part Studio' (tool_search.py:140-141) and activate() refuses any 'Switch to' entry (ui.py:2820-2822); the workspace combo leaves an assembly document for another one or creates 'Untitled part' (ui.py:807-820); the native menu bar is hidden (ui.py:183) and shortcuts.py has no rebuild binding. Files are identical to HEAD f57d592, so this is not already solved. What is inflated is the trigger: _rebuild_reason_on_open (core.py:1281-1290) only sets a sticky reason when the file's FreeCAD ProgramVersion differs from the running build or the recorded FreeCAD/OCCT stamp differs; a KurtShape git update (what 'the running app is an older build than HEAD' refers to) does not change ProgramVersion, and engine stamps (5f91ba2) predate assembly support (10c333f), so 'engine_unrecorded' cannot occur for a KurtShape assembly. Touched objects and missing_shapes reasons are cleared by Solve's recompute. So the scenario needs a FreeCAD runtime/OCCT change, which is rare but inevitable for a pinned-runtime app, and Kurt has the bridge `rebuild` op as a workaround. Severity high -> medium: a hard export block with no in-GUI remedy when it happens, but narrow trigger and a bridge workaround.
findings.refute_evidence: git log order: 5f91ba2 (engine stamps) precedes 10c333f (assembly), so no KurtShape assembly file lacks engine properties. test_build_status.py:642-659 covers saved_by_other_build only for Part Studio documents via the `rebuild` op; no test exercises the assembly GUI path. Working tree core.py/ui.py/tool_search.py are byte-identical to HEAD.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only after the bundled FreeCAD/OCCT changes: the status pill reads 'Rebuild required · saved by another application build' (or 'geometry engine changed') and stays after Solve, Export refuses. He would send {"op":"rebuild"} over the bridge and move on, but nothing in the window tells him that is the fix.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: The same status with no Rebuild button anywhere in Assembly; typing 'rebuild' in tool search says 'Switch to Part Studio', which jumps to a different document; the assembly cannot be exported from the app at all. In Onshape/SolidWorks a rebuild is always one click away in any workspace.
judge.risk: Adding a Rebuild action to assembly_bar/assembly_actions is low risk. Auto-calling _mark_rebuilt after Solve is riskier: an assembly document may hold Part Studio geometry that preceded Create Assembly, and Solve does not rebuild those features against the new engine, so stamping on Solve could hide a genuinely required rebuild.

findings.title: Recovered documents are labelled with their UUID and Save proposes a generic 'my-part.FCStd' instead of the checkpoint's original name
findings.lines: core.py:1496-1502 (opens <uuid>.FCStd), 1528-1529 (FileName cleared; record name/source_file unused), 1397-1398 (name/native_file in inspect); ui.py:1756, 1772, 1828 (title/identity from state['name']), 2976-2981 (Save default); recovery.py:54-55
findings.evidence: EXP6: after `recover`, `doc.Label == '6913e47a-c655-479e-baeb-647cec6be3e5'`, state['name'] is the UUID, native_file None. The tab, window title and document identity label will all show the UUID; Ctrl+S opens a Save dialog proposing my-part.FCStd in last_directory rather than the original bracket.FCStd.
findings.scenario: KurtShape crashes while Kurt edits bracket.FCStd. He picks 'bracket · checkpoint' from Recovery, gets a tab called '6913e47a-…', presses Ctrl+S and saves 'my-part.FCStd' next to whatever he last opened — now two diverging copies exist.
findings.consequence: Recovery works technically but produces an unrecognisable document and invites duplicate files; the one moment the user is stressed is the moment the naming breaks.
findings.reproduction: exp_assembly.py EXP6 (headless, real recover op).
findings.proposed_change: In the recover branch after attach: `doc.Label = recovery_record.get('name') or doc.Label`; store `recovery_record.get('source_file')` in `self.observer.state(doc)['recovered_from']` and expose it in _inspect as `recovered_from`. In Panel.save, when native_file is None and state.get('recovered_from') exists, default the dialog to that path (the native dialog handles overwrite confirmation) and add a toast 'Recovered from checkpoint of bracket.FCStd · Save to replace it or choose a new name'.
findings.risk: low
findings.acceptance: New test in tests/test_core.py or test_assembly.py: checkpoint, close, recover -> state['name'] equals the pre-close label and state['recovered_from'] equals the original path; GUI recipe asserts the tab title after recovery.
findings.refute_reasoning: Both halves are verified. EXP6 (exp_assembly.log lines 31-32) shows that after `recover` doc.Label is the document UUID and FileName is ''. The recover branch opens '<uuid>.FCStd' from project-recovery (core.py:1497, 1502), FreeCAD names the document after the file stem, and recovery_record['name'] (stored at recovery.py:54-55) is never applied; FileName is cleared deliberately (core.py:1529). inspect reports name=doc.Label and native_file=None (core.py:1397-1398), which feed the window title (ui.py:1756/1828) and identity label (ui.py:1772). Panel.save then falls to the generic default 'my-part.FCStd' / 'my-assembly.FCStd' in last_directory (ui.py:2976-2981). Nothing in ui.py's post-recover handling renames (grep 'recover'). Files are identical to HEAD, so not fixed. Where the finding overstates: clearing FileName is documented intent ('recovered documents require choosing a Save destination', docs/2026-10-02-claude-review-follow-up/IMPLEMENTATION.md:16; test_assembly.py:290 asserts native_file is None), so Ctrl+S does not silently write anywhere; it opens a Save dialog where the user can type the real name and folder. The original bracket.FCStd is untouched. The UUID label is a real defect; the generic default name is a design weakness. Severity high -> medium: confusing and duplicate-inviting at a stressful moment, but no data loss and the user sees and controls the dialog.
findings.refute_evidence: git blame core.py:1528-1530 -> 5f91ba2 (2026-10-02), unchanged since. tests/test_review_followup.py:438-452 and tests/test_assembly.py:286-295 exercise recover but never assert the Label, so the UUID label is untested rather than intended.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Immediately after picking a Recovery entry: the tab, window title and identity label read '6913e47a-…', and Ctrl+S opens a Save dialog proposing my-part.FCStd in whatever folder he last used. He would retype the project name, but a second copy next to the original is one Enter away.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: SolidWorks auto-recover and Onshape keep the document's name; a UUID title plus a generic save name during crash recovery reads as 'the wrong file came back', and saving as proposed leaves two diverging files.
judge.risk: Setting doc.Label from the record is trivial. Defaulting the Save dialog to the original source path puts overwrite of the last good save one click behind the native overwrite confirmation; that is usually what the user wants but should be a deliberate choice, and the recovered document shares the source file's DocumentId so saving elsewhere creates two projects with one ID.

findings.title: Recovery menu lists both checkpoint generations with identical undated labels, never prunes abandoned checkpoints, and offers entries for documents that are still open
findings.lines: recovery.py:96-102 (previous pair written on every replacement), 154-166 (glob '*.json', source-mtime filter only, no open-document check, no pruning); ui.py:2843-2852 (label/tooltip, no date, no forget); core.py:1021-1023 (duplicate_document_id on recover of an open document)
findings.evidence: EXP5: after two forced checkpoints and closing without saving, available() returned two entries both named 'Exp' (…json and ….previous.json) with no source_file; four files stayed in project-recovery. In the GUI they render as two identical 'Exp · checkpoint' rows. Untitled documents (source_file None) never satisfy the mtime filter, so every 'Untitled part' edited for >30 s accumulates two rows for the life of the profile. Picking an entry for a document that is still open fails with the duplicate_document_id error.
findings.scenario: After a few weeks the Recovery submenu is a wall of 'Untitled part · checkpoint' rows in unknown order with no dates; Kurt cannot tell today's crash from last month's discarded scratch part, and picking the entry for the tab he has open errors.
findings.consequence: Recovery loses credibility exactly when needed; disk usage grows by two full FCStd copies per abandoned document.
findings.reproduction: exp_assembly.py EXP5; inspect fill_recovery with that store.
findings.proposed_change: Add `RecoveryStore.listing()` that groups manifests by document_id, returns the newest with `saved_at`, `previous` manifest, `source_file`, and `open` (core.documents has a live doc with that id). Panel.fill_recovery renders 'bracket · unfinished sketch · 5 min ago' with the previous checkpoint in a submenu, disables entries for open documents ('already open'), and adds 'Forget checkpoint' plus automatic pruning of pairs older than N days whose source_file is newer (or whose document was explicitly discarded—record a 'discarded' flag when our own close prompt from finding 9 is answered Discard).
findings.risk: low-medium: pruning must never delete the last checkpoint of a document with no saved file.
findings.acceptance: Unit tests on listing(): two checkpoints of one document -> one row with a previous entry; open document -> flagged; GUI: Recovery menu shows relative times and no duplicate labels.
findings.refute_reasoning: Every factual claim checks out, but the store behaves as designed and the gap is in presentation and lifecycle, so this is a design weakness rather than a defect. available() globs '*.json' (recovery.py:157), which includes the '.previous.json' manifest that every replacement writes (recovery.py:98-102) and, transiently, '.saving.json'; EXP5 (exp_assembly.log lines 29-30) lists two 'Exp' entries with no source_file and four files on disk. The previous pair is retained on purpose as the corruption fallback (read() error 'inspect the previous checkpoint', recovery.py:151; tests test_review_followup.py:454-467 and test_responsiveness.py:359-360 read it directly), so listing it is not wrong, but fill_recovery (ui.py:2843-2852) labels both rows record['name'] + ' · checkpoint' with no date, and the tooltip is source_file or path, so for saved documents the two rows are indistinguishable. No code unlinks or prunes project-recovery (grep: the only unlinks are STEP-export stages at core.py:844, bridge token, snapshots, workers); untitled documents (source_file None) never satisfy the mtime filter at recovery.py:160-162, so they accumulate for the life of the profile. An entry for a document that is still open is listed and `recover` fails at attach with duplicate_document_id (core.py:1021-1023), which is at least a clear message rather than a crash. Disk growth is real: two FCStd copies per abandoned document, including embedded assembly sources. Files identical to HEAD. Severity medium stands (recovery menu degrades to noise over weeks; wasted disk), classification corrected to design_weakness.
findings.refute_evidence: git blame ui.py:2843-2852 -> 5f91ba2 (2026-10-02), unchanged. docs/2026-10-02-claude-review-follow-up/IMPLEMENTATION.md:34 documents that 'the previous pair is retained' deliberately; no doc describes pruning or ageing.

judge.kurt_would_notice: He saves into CADkz/projects/<name>/ and drives most work over the bridge, so he would mostly see this after a real crash: a Recovery submenu with repeated 'Untitled part · checkpoint' and paired identical rows, no dates, and 'Close the existing project before opening another copy…' when he picks the row for the tab he already has open.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: SolidWorks' auto-recover list is dated and clears after use; here identical rows pile up with no way to tell today's crash from last month's scratch part and no way to forget any of them.
judge.risk: Pruning must never remove the only checkpoint of unsaved work (untitled documents have no source mtime to compare against), and grouping by document_id must keep the previous pair reachable because it is the corruption fallback that tests and read() rely on.

merged_from.title: Recovery checkpoints are never pruned: every new or recovered document leaves a permanent pair and unsaved ones stay in the Recovery menu forever
merged_from.evidence: recovery.py contains no unlink/remove/rmtree (grep); `_publish` only replaces the same DocumentId's pair and keeps `.previous.*` (98-104); `available` hides a pair only when its source_file exists and is newer (160-162), so documents never saved are listed indefinitely. Probe B8: three `new` documents + forced checkpoint, documents closed -> directory holds 6 files and available() lists 'Throwaway 0/1/2' with source_file None. ui.py:2854-2877 checkpoints every open document on idle after 30 s.
merged_from.scenario: Agents routinely `new` a document per dry run or rebuild (build_bridge.py:30 `s.call('new', ...)`; bone-mallet opens/creates per run); each one idle for 30 s gets a checkpoint pair the size of the model (dodec hub: 9.7 MB per FCStd, plus .previous copies). Kurt's Recovery menu accumulates 'Untitled part · checkpoint' rows from weeks ago.
merged_from.consequence: Disk growth in runtime/project-recovery and a Recovery menu where the one checkpoint that matters is buried; I could not inspect the live folder (out of scope) so current size is unknown.
merged_from.reproduction: scratch controller_probe.py section B8; or in the app: New, wait 40 s idle, close without saving, open Document > Recovery.
merged_from.proposed_change: RecoveryStore.retire(document_id): delete the pair (+ .previous) when a document is closed after a successful save newer than the checkpoint, or when the user discards an unsaved document in the native close prompt (hook Gui document close via DocumentState.slotDeletedDocument -> controller -> recovery.retire if `last[...]` revision was saved); cap unsaved pairs (keep newest 20 by saved_at) at startup; add 'Clear old checkpoints' under Recovery. Never delete a pair whose document is still open or has an unfinished sketch.
merged_from.dependencies: Needs the close hook to know whether the user chose Discard; otherwise prune only saved-and-closed documents plus an age cap.
merged_from.risk: Deleting the wrong pair defeats recovery: restrict to pairs whose source_file mtime >= saved_at (the same predicate available() already trusts) and to an explicit user action for unsaved ones.
merged_from.acceptance: Native test: new -> checkpoint -> save -> close -> pair gone; new -> checkpoint -> close unsaved -> pair kept and listed; startup cap keeps 20 newest. Gate: test_review_followup checkpoint/corrupt tests unchanged.

findings.title: No anti-aliasing: View/AntiAliasing is never set, so 2 px edges and sketch curves render stair-stepped (cosmetic, startup-only fix)
findings.lines: theme.py 225-280 (apply_native_light_preferences) and 53-59 (apply_view_theme); ui.py 4311-4336 (start order)
findings.evidence: No source writes View/AntiAliasing (grep). Fresh-profile View group (exp2) has no AntiAliasing key; the shipped template data/Gui/PreferencePackTemplates/View.cfg records AntiAliasing=0; exp2b render action: isSmoothing()=0, getNumPasses()=1. Magnified crops of validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4, current light shell) at x8 show hard 2 px black edge steps with no intermediate shades; docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6) x5 shows the same on the blue circle. FreeCADGui.dll carries the AntiAliasing parameter (2 string hits) so the control exists.
findings.scenario: Every view; most visible on diagonal silhouette edges, circles in sketches, and the hover outline.
findings.consequence: The canvas looks dated next to Onshape; 2 px aliased lines shimmer during orbit. Kurt's running app renders the same unless he changed the preference by hand (his profile was not read).
findings.reproduction: Crop any edge of the Oct 4 capture at 8x (scratch crop_top_edge_x8.png). In the app: Preferences > Display > 3D View shows Anti-aliasing None.
findings.proposed_change: Standard preset writes View/AntiAliasing=3 (FreeCAD's View3DInventorViewer::AntiAliasing order None, Smoothing, MSAA2x, MSAA4x, MSAA8x; confirm the integer in the running build's Preferences dialog before hard-coding) at startup before the first document view is created; presentation 4 (MSAA8x) with fallback to 3; draft 0. Gate on the GL renderer string (see software-GL finding). Verify whether a live change re-creates the QOpenGLWidget on this Qt6 build or needs 'applies to new views'; apply at startup either way.
findings.risk: MSAA on Intel iGPU is fine at 4x; on llvmpipe/RDP it multiplies fill cost (auto-draft needed); some drivers ignore GL_LINE_SMOOTH (mode 1), so prefer MSAA.
findings.acceptance: A framebuffer grab (viewer.grabFramebuffer) across a 45 deg silhouette edge shows >= 2 intermediate grey levels per step; orbit frame time on the acceptance plate within 10 % of the no-AA baseline on Kurt's GPU; headless suites unaffected.
findings.refute_reasoning: Facts hold: grep finds no writer of View/AntiAliasing anywhere in src/tools (the only 'Antialiasing' hits are QPainter hints in rollback_history.py:252 and sketch_references.py:238); theme.py:225-280 apply_native_light_preferences copies only colour keys from the Light pack and apply_view_theme (53-59) only sets the background; navigation.apply_navigation writes navigation keys only; the runtime template data/Gui/PreferencePackTemplates/View.cfg line 16 records AntiAliasing=0 and the fresh-profile View group (exp2_result.json) has no AntiAliasing key; exp2b_result.json shows gl_smoothing 0 / gl_passes 1. I viewed the finder's x8 crop of the Oct 4 model-workspace-1440.png (hard 2 px black steps, no intermediate shades) and the x5/x8 crops of the Oct 6 circle-drag-after.png (blocky blue circle): the stair-stepping is real, and both captures come from isolated validation sessions, i.e. shipped defaults; Kurt's live profile was not read. Nothing at HEAD changes this. I downgrade severity only: it is a pervasive but purely cosmetic rendering issue with no effect on geometry, picking or workflow, so impact is low even though the value of fixing it is high. Implementation caveat the finder half-flagged: FreeCAD's MSAA path replaces the viewer's QOpenGLWidget, and KurtShape installs about ten event filters keyed on that widget instance (navigation.py:134, hover_outline.py:260, sketch_cursor.py:72, sketch_regions.py:149, sketch_snapping.py:221, edge_picking.py:104, responsiveness.py:247/330, sketch_references.py:255/642, general_actions.py:305), so the key must be written at startup before the first view (start() at ui.py:4311-4336 already runs apply_theme/apply_navigation before documents open) and never flipped live without re-running the installers; QPainter overlays on the GL widget also need a check on a multisampled framebuffer.
findings.refute_evidence: runtime/.../data/Gui/PreferencePackTemplates/View.cfg:16 AntiAliasing=0, :7 UseSoftwareOpenGL=0. Crops viewed: scratch/area-b-viewport/crop_top_edge_x8.png, crop_circle_x5.png, scratch/verify/aa_b_circle_x8.png. Box ViewObject LineWidth default 2.0 (exp2_result.json) makes the steps 2 px. GPU on this machine is an Intel RaptorLake-S iGPU, GL 4.6 (scratch/verify/gl_probe_default.txt), so MSAA 4x is realistic; 8x unmeasured.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Stair-stepped silhouette edges and sketch circles on every part and a shimmer along edges while orbiting; nothing functional.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape and SolidWorks both anti-alias; the canvas reads as a decade old at first glance.
judge.risk: Startup-only write is trivial; the risk is in applying it live (viewport widget replacement orphans KurtShape's QOpenGLWidget event filters) and in untested interaction between MSAA and the QPainter overlays; gate on the renderer per B-09 and verify in a private session before shipping.

findings.title: Identical glyphs on different commands, including a redundant Boolean button in the model bar
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/presentation_icons.py 28, 30, 36, 45-47; ui.py 553-560, 572, 588, 597, 2043-2050; feature_tools.py 177-178; tools/generate-presentation-icons.py 122-128
findings.evidence: 'plane': 'plane' and 'show planes': 'plane' (lines 30/36); 'boolean' and 'boolean parts' both -> 'boolean' (28); 'fixed' and 'joints' -> 'fixed-joint' (45-47). ui.py 553-555 adds catalog primary 'Boolean' and 556-560 adds 'Boolean parts'; primary_feature_tool maps 'boolean' -> studio_tool('boolean_parts') (2046-2051), so both buttons run the same command. Generator: ASSETS['new-part'] == ASSETS['build-menu'] (122/128), 'patterns-menu' = linear-pattern (125), 'shape-tools-menu' = boolean (127). findings.scenario: Scanning the model bar to find Boolean, Plane or the view toggle; assembly bar Fixed vs Joints.
findings.consequence: Kurt clicks the wrong parallelogram (creates a datum plane instead of toggling plane visibility) and sees a duplicated button, which reads as unfinished.
findings.reproduction: Hover both parallelograms in the model bar (labels 'Plane' and 'Show planes'); click both two-cube buttons: both open the Boolean parts editor.
findings.proposed_change: Remove the explicit ('Boolean parts', ...) entry at ui.py 556-560 or drop 'boolean' from PRIMARY_TOOLS (feature_tools.py 177-179). Give view toggles their own family (plane + eye for Show planes), joints a chain glyph, menu triggers a variant (cube + chevron) instead of reusing the member asset; add a generator assertion that no two ASSETS strings are equal and no two LABEL_ICONS commands in the same bar share an asset.
findings.risk: Removing a button changes the design-surface recipe's expected action list.
findings.acceptance: Generator uniqueness check passes; per-toolbar icon cacheKeys are unique in the design-surface recipe.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read presentation_icons.py LABEL_ICONS (lines 28, 30, 36, 45-47): 'boolean' and 'boolean parts' both map to 'boolean'; 'plane' and 'show planes' both map to 'plane'; 'fixed' and 'joints' both map to 'fixed-joint'. Read ui.py 553-560 and 572: the loop over catalog['primary'] adds the catalog 'Boolean' tool (PRIMARY_TOOLS has contained 'boolean' since cb96ddf, 2026-10-02) and the next loop adds an explicit 'Boolean parts' action (df26c91, 2026-10-03); primary_feature_tool (2043-2050) maps tool.key 'boolean' to studio_tool('boolean_parts'), the same call the explicit button makes, so two buttons in one bar run one command. 'Plane' (primary datum_plane, label 'Plane') and 'Show planes' (line 572) sit in the same model bar with the same SVG; 'Fixed' (588) and 'Joints' (597) share the assembly bar. Generator lines 122/128, 125 and 127 reuse assets verbatim, and an md5 pass over resources/icons found three byte-identical pairs among 75 files (boolean==shape-tools-menu, linear-pattern==patterns-menu, build-menu==new-part). validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4, current shell) shows the two identical two-cube buttons and the two identical parallelograms. Nothing in git after Oct 13 touches these files, and no test or validation macro asserts icon uniqueness (design-surface-validation only compares Move face vs Extrude). What softens it: the 350 ms hover label and tooltips disambiguate, and the menu-glyph duplicates live inside the More submenu rather than beside their member buttons, so the two in-bar pairs (Boolean/Boolean parts, Plane/Show planes) are the real problem; the Fixed/Joints pair is on the hidden assembly bar.
findings.refute_evidence: md5sum resources/icons/*.svg: boolean.svg == shape-tools-menu.svg, linear-pattern.svg == patterns-menu.svg, build-menu.svg == new-part.svg (3 of 75). git blame: 'boolean' entered PRIMARY_TOOLS in cb96ddf (Oct 2) and the explicit ('Boolean parts', 'boolean_parts', 'PartDesign_Boolean') row came in df26c91 (Oct 3), so the duplicate control is an accretion, not a choice; docs/ui-refinement/IMPLEMENTATION.md lists the direct toolbar tools and never names Boolean twice. Model bar currently holds 26 commands, so dropping one keeps design-surface-validation's 'len(model_commands) >= 24' check green.

judge.kurt_would_notice: He sees the two identical cube-pair buttons every session and reads the pair as unfinished; he mostly drives modeling through the bridge, so the toolbar cost is small, but the Plane vs Show planes parallelograms cost him an opened-then-cancelled datum editor whenever he reaches for P by mouse.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape user expects Plane under reference tools and plane visibility on the view cube; two identical parallelograms in one row means a wrong click until positions are memorised, and two identical Boolean buttons reads as a bug in the product.
judge.risk: Low. Removing the explicit 'Boolean parts' row or 'boolean' from PRIMARY_TOOLS changes no behaviour; giving Show planes, Joints and the menu triggers their own assets touches only the generator and resources/icons. No validation macro references 'Boolean parts' by name; the model-command count stays above the 24 floor.

findings.refute_reasoning:

No commit since 4681ddf (2026-10-13) touched the icons, and docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md:118 (untracked) only proposes a silhouette pass, so this is not already solved. The real Oct 4 capture (validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png, enlarged 2x) does show fillet/chamfer and loft/draft as near-duplicates at a glance.

Refuted part: the "0.79 px hairline, anti-aliased mid-gray" strand and the quoted ink numbers assume device pixel ratio 1.0, which is what the finder's offscreen audit ran at (icon-audit/native_gray.log: "dpr 1.0"). A one-shot offscreen probe with the bundled interpreter shows QIcon's SVG engine rasterizes a 20 px request at DPR 1.5 as a 30x30 device-pixel pixmap, so the stroke is 1.19 device px, and every sampled glyph reaches the full ink darkness (peak 0.66 = #51575d): full-ink pixel counts go construction 0 -> 49, axis 3 -> 52, line 14 -> 42, point 8 -> 20 between DPR 1.0 and 1.5. On Kurt's display the line-art is not mid-gray. The line-art vs shaded-solid weight gap persists at 1.5 (construction 0.045 / axis 0.058 / line 0.057 vs fillet 0.224, about 5x), but that is the shared-weight question the finding itself defers to Finding 1, not a hairline defect. Minor overstatements: export (101) is a page plus arrow, not a cube; insert (110) is one cube plus a bent arrow, not two cubes; assembly (109) is two cubes with a connector.

What survives is a recognition weakness for three pairs and one cube+arrow trio on icon-only bars, judged visually rather than by any user test, in a shell whose Icon Row Rule (DESIGN.md:180) deliberately routes names to delayed labels, menus and search. That is a low-severity design weakness, medium confidence; it would rise toward the finder's medium only if Kurt works at 100% scaling, which the validation evidence does not show.
