judge.kurt_would_notice: Kurt drives much of his modeling through the bridge, where toolbar glyphs are irrelevant, and when he is in the GUI he will learn bar positions within a day (7th = Fillet, 8th = Chamfer) and stop looking at the glyphs. What he would actually notice is that the sketch bar (line, arc, spline, point, construction) reads as a faint, washed-out row next to the shaded cubes of the model bar, and that New part (1st button) and the Build submenu in More share the exact same glyph (generator lines 122/128). "Guessing game" overstates his case; "the sketch icons are too faint and a couple of pairs are twins" is closer.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Immediately. An Onshape/SolidWorks user scans by silhouette, and in those apps Fillet (rounded edge on a block) and Chamfer (clipped corner) are strongly differentiated, as are Loft (two stacked sections) and Draft (slanted face with an angle). Here they would misclick Fillet/Chamfer and Loft/Draft, cancel the wrong dialog, and then hover every button waiting the 350 ms for the label (toolbar_labels.py line 15). The sketch bar's hairline glyphs (0.79 px strokes in #51575d gray) would look like disabled tools to them.
judge.reasoning: Source confirmed as cited. tools\generate-presentation-icons.py line 137 emits stroke-width="0.95" in a 24 px viewBox; all four toolbars set a 20 px icon size (src/kurtshape/ui.py lines 491, 539, 582, 605), so strokes render at 0.79 px. The ASSETS table (lines 43-116) matches the finding: fillet/chamfer (51-53) are the same box with one corner treated; loft/draft (50/56) are both tapered tents; point/pierce (66/98) are both cross + circle; shape-tools-menu literally reuses the boolean asset (127), patterns-menu reuses linear-pattern (125), and new-part equals build-menu (122/128). The icon_for resolution map (docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/icon-audit/icon_for_resolution.json, runtime_catalog_icon_resolution.json) shows these originals are what the model and sketch bars actually display, and the Oct 5 real-app screenshot (runtime/ci-gui/design-surface/run-cc8d987e.../evidence/onshape-design/model-workspace-1440.png) shows the fillet/chamfer pair at x~491/540 as near-identical. The ink figures match icon_metrics_20px.json exactly (construction 0.035, axis 0.044, line 0.054, fillet 0.219; a 6x spread). I looked at toolbar_strip_1x.png and the 3x zoom myself: fillet/chamfer and loft/draft are twins at 20 px, and the sketch-bar line art is visibly lighter than the cubes. The 350 ms hover delay is the ToolbarLabels default (src/kurtshape/toolbar_labels.py line 15). The 0.95 stroke arrived in one commit (4681ddf, 2026-10-13, the generator's only commit) with no documented rationale, while the project's own plan (docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md line 81) asked for "controlled gray fill/shading and optical weight; do not reduce every tool to a generic thin outline" and line 186 for line weights tuned at deployed DPI, so the finding is aligned with stated intent rather than second-guessing a deliberate choice. Classification: design_weakness is honest. Nothing is broken, every button works, labels appear on hover, Search tools (Alt+C) exists; the problem is discriminability and optical weight, not a contract violation. Severity medium is right: the toolbar is the primary daily surface and an icon-only bar whose core pairs are indistinguishable undercuts the Onshape-familiar premise, but a wrong pick costs one cancelled dialog and nothing is lost or corrupted; the mitigations (hover label, search, learnable positions) keep it below high. Severity is correctly separated from effort. Two small corrections to the finding: (1) assembly/example/insert do not sit on the same bar as boolean, so that collision is mostly a menu-icon issue where text labels exist; the stronger same-surface duplicate it misses is new-part = build-menu; (2) extrude/move-face/transform differ by arrow direction and are distinguishable with a moment's attention, so that group is weaker evidence than the fillet/chamfer and loft/draft pairs. Effort M holds: the stroke change is minutes, but redrawing ~8 glyphs by composition, re-running the contact sheet at 20/40 and 1.5x, adding the bbox/darkness assertion to the design-surface recipe, and a blind sort with Kurt is 1-3 days. The acceptance criterion "ink spread <= 3x" is unlikely to be met by a stroke change alone (cubes rise with the stroke too) and may need the cube fills lightened; and the same icon family is used at 16 px in the feature panel and sketch edit panel (feature_panel.py line 22, sketch_edit_panel.py line 32), which the acceptance list omits.
judge.risk: Low-to-medium. The change is SVG regeneration with no callback changes, so functional risk is nil, but it touches all 77 icons across toolbars, menus and the 16 px feature history, so the heavier stroke must also be checked at 16 px (feature_panel.py line 22, sketch_edit_panel.py line 32), not just 20/40. A global 1.4 stroke will make the already-dark cubes heavier, so the "ink spread <= 3x" target may force lightening fills, widening the pass. Redrawn silhouettes break Kurt's position/shape memory once; keep families (cubes for solids, strokes for sketch) and change composition, not vocabulary. Existing design-surface evidence screenshots under runtime/ci-gui/design-surface will no longer match and any pixel-based checks need re-baselining.

findings.title: Messages unread dot counts the startup Report backlog and every native line regardless of severity, so it is already lit at launch
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 702-718 (append_message), 736-787 (make_messages; startup backlog at 787, contentsChange hook 776-784), 656-666 (notify error channel), 4311-4324 (start() order: maximize_on_primary_screen before Panel); src/kurtshape/startup.py maximize_on_primary_screen (setGeometry); tools/messages-validation.FCMacro 174-200
findings.evidence: append_message: 'if text.strip() and not self.messages_dock.isVisible(): self.unread_messages += 1' for every native=True line; make_messages appends the whole startup report once ('self.append_message(widget.toPlainText(), native=True)' 786-787) and connects every contentsChange (776-785). startup-origin.png (Oct 6) shows 'Messages •' lit right after 'New complete' on an empty document; model-workspace-1440.png the same. Report content in native-report-readable.png (Oct 4) is QIODevice thumbnail chatter.
findings.scenario: Any session: the dot is already on before Kurt does anything; an actual geometry error later changes nothing visible.
findings.consequence: Kurt learns to ignore the one quiet error channel; real failures (invalid geometry, failed Finish) are not distinguishable at the status bar.
findings.reproduction: Launch; look at the status bar: 'Messages •'. Open Messages: startup log lines, no error.
findings.proposed_change: Count severity, not lines: in the contentsChange hook classify each added block by its char-format foreground (theme already maps native colorError/colorWarning tokens, theme.py 292-299) and only increment for KurtShape notify(..., 'error') and native error/warning blocks; do not count the startup backlog. Render severity in the button: 'Messages' plain, 'Messages • 2' with error color when errors are unread; keep info lines copyable but uncounted.
findings.risk: Native highlighter formats are applied asynchronously; classify on the block after rehighlight or on the text prefix as a fallback.
findings.acceptance: messages recipe (tools/messages-validation.FCMacro, 34 checks) gains: dot off after startup; dot on after notify('x','error'); dot stays off after an info-only native line.
findings.refute_reasoning: The factual mechanism holds at HEAD f57d592 and the cited lines are correct: append_message (ui.py 702-718) increments unread_messages for any non-blank text while the dock is hidden, make_messages hides the dock (761) and then appends the whole Report view backlog once (787) and every later contentsChange batch (776-784), with no severity test anywhere. It is lit at startup in practice: start() (ui.py 4311-4324) calls maximize_on_primary_screen (startup.py, setGeometry) before Panel() is built, and the real session log runtime/freecad-launch.log line 220 shows "Wrn: QWindowsWindow::setGeometry: Unable to set geometry 2160x1299..." emitted at exactly that point, so the Report view already holds a warning when line 787 captures it; validation profiles additionally carry "Migrating Start Workbench..." plus seven QIODevice::read thumbnail lines (validation/onshape-design/messages.json messages_text; runtime/messages-behavior-audit/report-probe.json, all #000000 info fragments). The screenshots confirm: docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/startup-origin.png (Oct 6, not under validation/ as cited) shows "Messages •" beside "New complete" on an empty Untitled part, and validation/onshape-design/model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4) shows it after "Extrude complete". Nothing resets the count except opening the dock (723), no test covers unread after startup, and git log shows only eb3baf1/69dc29c/4681ddf touched this code, so it is not already solved. However, "verified_defect" and the consequence are overstated. Counting every native line is the documented and tested design, not a deviation: docs/workspace-behavior/IMPLEMENTATION.md line 7 describes the button as indicating "unread entries" while native output is retained "without interpreting every information/warning/log fragment as an application error", and tools/messages-validation.FCMacro lines 194-200 explicitly assert unread_messages > before_unread for PrintMessage, PrintWarning, PrintError and PrintLog and call the dot a "quiet indicator". The finding's own acceptance ("dot stays off after an info-only native line") would fail four of the existing 34 checks. And the dot is not "the one quiet error channel": notify(msg, "error") (ui.py 656-666) paints the status label red with the error text and does not start the 4.5 s restore timer, so it persists until replaced; _present_geometry_check (1624) notifies "Invalid geometry — see Messages" in red, and the recipe checks "A rejected controller operation shows red readable status". Real failures remain distinguishable at the status bar via that red label; the startup-lit dot is a low-signal UX weakness (startup backlog counted as unread, no severity in the count), not a defect that hides errors. Hence downgraded to design_weakness, low severity, high confidence in the facts.
findings.refute_evidence: startup-origin.png lives at docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/startup-origin.png (Oct 6 10:06), not under validation/. Startup backlog counts as exactly one unread (single append_message call), not one per line; the tooltip reads "Show messages · 1 unread". Real-session trigger even without Start-page thumbnail chatter: runtime/freecad-launch.log (Oct 17) has 0 QIODevice lines but the setGeometry Wrn at line 220, emitted by start()'s maximize_on_primary_screen before Panel/make_messages, and FreeCAD's OutputWindow shows warnings by default. theme.py report_colors mapping is at 293-298 (finding said 292-299). Existing recipe checks that conflict with the proposed acceptance: "Native messages normal/log is retained once ... and panel.unread_messages > before_unread" (macro 194-199) and "Unread log entries have a quiet indicator" (200); the recipe records button_text "Messages •" / unread 1 at finish (validation/onshape-design/messages.json) but never asserts the unread count immediately after startup. tests/ has no unit coverage of unread_messages. Working tree is clean apart from untracked docs/fable-deep-review/, which does not mention this.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Barely, today: he drives most sessions through the bridge, where errors come back as structured JSON responses, and at the shell he has almost certainly already tuned out a dot that is lit from the first frame of every launch (model-workspace-1440.png shows it lit after a clean "Extrude complete"). He would notice the fix the first time an OCCT/PartDesign recompute failure that only the native Report view reports lights "Messages • 1" in error colour while the status bar still says the feature completed; that is the one case where the shell currently gives him no cue at all.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Yes, on first launch. Onshape/SolidWorks users expect an unread/alert badge to mean something went wrong (Onshape paints the failed feature red and toasts it). They click "Messages •" on an empty document, find Qt thumbnail-cache chatter (QIODevice::read ... device not open, Start workbench migration), and file the panel as a verbose log rather than an alert channel. After that they rely on the status bar alone and miss native-only errors, exactly the failure mode the finding describes.
judge.reasoning:
Source confirmed. src/kurtshape/ui.py 702-718: append_message increments unread_messages for any non-blank text while the dock is hidden, regardless of severity; 772-787: every contentsChange on the native Report view document is mirrored as native=True, and line 787 appends the whole pre-attach backlog after line 761 has hidden the dock, so the backlog itself lights the dot. theme.py maps native colorError/colorWarning/colorText/colorLogging to the light tokens (267-273 and 292-299, as cited). validation/onshape-theme-repair/theme-startup.json "retained_native_report_formats" records what the backlog is on a real launch: one Start-workbench migration line plus a run of FreeCADStartThumbnails QIODevice warnings in the warning colour (#8c6005), so on any normal startup the dot is on before the user acts. model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4, both onshape-design and onshape-theme-repair copies) shows "Messages •" lit after "Extrude complete" on a healthy body. One evidence citation is wrong: there is no startup-origin.png and no Oct 6 PNG anywhere under validation/; the startup claim stands on the code path plus theme-startup.json, not on that screenshot.

Classification: the finding calls this a verified_defect, but tools/messages-validation.FCMacro lines 188-200 explicitly assert that each of PrintMessage, PrintWarning, PrintError and PrintLog raises unread_messages and that the dot then shows, and line 175 asserts the startup backlog is retained. The code does exactly what its own acceptance recipe specifies; what is wrong is the specification (count lines, not severity), which makes the indicator carry no information. That is a design_weakness. The observations are verified, which is why confidence stays high.

Severity medium is right and should stay separate from effort: KurtShape-originated failures already have a second channel (notify(..., "error") paints the status bar red and keeps it there; check_geometry writes verdicts), and bridge callers get structured errors, so the lost signal mainly affects native-only recompute errors and warnings seen at the shell. It is not high because no data is lost and the panel still contains the error; it is not low because an always-on alert trains both personas to ignore the only shell-level channel for native errors.

Effort S holds, with corrections to the proposal: (1) the highlighter writes block layout formats, not cursor char formats, so classify with block.layout().formats() (tools/theme-startup-validation.FCMacro line 96 already does exactly this), not "char-format foreground"; (2) ReportHighlighter's _q_reformatBlocks is connected to contentsChange at ReportOutput construction, before KurtShape connects, and runs synchronously, so the "asynchronous" risk is misdescribed; the real edge is fragmented lines, where a block is re-coloured with the latest paragraph type; (3) the existing recipe checks at 188-200 and 331-339 (PrintWarning as the hidden-unread fixture) must be revised, not merely extended as "gains", because they encode the opposite behaviour; (4) decide whether warnings count: the startup backlog is entirely warnings, so skipping the backlog is necessary but later Qt warnings would still light a warning-counting dot, which argues for counting errors only and showing warnings as a distinct glyph; (5) non-native info lines such as "geometry valid" at ui.py 1615 currently count too and should not. All of that is well under a day.
judge.risk: Low to moderate. The change inverts a documented acceptance behaviour, so the 34-check messages recipe must be updated in the same change or it goes red. The functional risk is a false negative: if a native error block's layout format is not yet applied when KurtShape's slot runs, or a fragmented line is re-coloured, an error could go uncounted and the shell would be quieter than today; FreeCAD does not prefix the message type in the text, so a text-prefix fallback does not exist. Mitigate by treating any block whose colour is not the info/log token as counting, and by adding a recipe check for a native PrintError emitted as two fragments.

(4) ui.py:771-787 connects the native Report view document to append_message(native=True), so native warnings already appear in Messages with an unread dot while the native bell also counts them: two channels for the same events. (5) git blame: ui.py 629 b65f066 (Oct 2), 630-631 69dc29c (Oct 3), 632 and 764-768 eb3baf1 (Oct 2); workspace_preferences.py 15-23 cb96ddf (Oct 2). git log --since=2026-10-04 on ui.py/theme.py/workspace_preferences.py: 13 commits, none touching status bar code; git status clean for those files. (6) runtime/user-data/user.cfg:17 (live launcher profile, launch-kurtshape.ps1:39-48 sets FREECAD_USER_HOME to runtime/user-data) has UserSchema=0 and no NotificationArea keys, so FreeCAD's default enabled bell applies. (7) Headless probe (bundled pythonw.exe -I, isolated FREECAD_USER_HOME/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/TEMP under scratchpad/verify, ~10 s): FreeCAD 1.1.4 App.Units.listSchemas gives 0 Internal 240mm^2->"2.40 cm^2", 1 MKS ->"2.40 cm^2", 6 MmMin ->"240.00 mm^2" (57.24mm->"57.24 mm"), 8 FEM ->"240.00 mm^2"; schemas 2,3,4,5,7,9 are inch/cm/m/ft based. Default schema is 0. So the remedy must set UserSchema to 6 (or 8), not merely "the mm-based schema", which is already active. (8) Docs acknowledging the gap without fixing it: docs/ui-refinement/IMPLEMENTATION.md:13 ("Native view dimensions and notification controls remain in the status bar"); docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md:95 (footer should show durable document/build/unit state; errors need severity); docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md:51 (proposed zoned status bar, concept only). (9) viewport_actions.py:91-96 falls back to native statusBar().showMessage only when no Panel.notify exists, so it is not an additional live channel in the app.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Every hover over a face larger than 100 mm^2 (which is nearly every face on the osteotome, mallet, drill and hub parts) puts "Area: x cm^2" at the left end of a footer whose own text says "Local document · mm" or "Editing sketch · mm" at the right. He already meets the native notification popup (docs/ui-refinement/IMPLEMENTATION.md:15 repaired its theme because he reported one), so when a native warning fires he sees it land twice: as a count on the FreeCAD bell (the probe shows it reading "7") and as "Messages •" from the Report-view mirror in ui.py:783. Since he drives most work through the bridge and reads the footer for "Extrude complete"-style feedback, the bell and the "57.24 mm x 36.93 mm" view-size readout are noise he would learn to skip rather than something that stops him; he is unlikely to care about DimensionWidget beyond wanting it gone.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape has no footer at all, so everything in this strip is new; a SolidWorks user expects the status bar to carry the document unit system and selection measurements in that unit. Hovering a face and reading "Area: 2.40 cm^2" beside an "mm" shell reads as a mis-set unit system. The bigger trap is "57.24 mm x 36.93 mm": in SolidWorks the status bar reports the size of what you selected, so a newcomer hovering the plate would plausibly take the viewport-extent readout for the face's dimensions. The blue-square dropdown with a count looks like an unrelated app's notification center and opens an unstyled FreeCAD menu, which is the one place the shell visibly stops being KurtShape.
judge.reasoning: Source confirmed as cited: ui.py:629-632 adds the KurtShape message with stretch 1, ui.py:764-768 adds the Messages button, and workspace_preferences.py:15-23 hides only NavigationIndicator (constructor plus a Show/Polish event filter). docs/ui-refinement/IMPLEMENTATION.md:13 states "Native view dimensions and notification controls remain in the status bar", so the retention was deliberate. The probe record is real: docs/responsive-modeling-upgrade/evidence/gui-ui-refinement.json:320-375 lists Gui::StatusBarLabel, Gui::DimensionWidget, Gui::InputHintWidget "hintLabel", QPushButton "notificationArea" (text "7") and the StatusBarArea in the live status bar. Both copies of hover-label-below-1440.png (validation/onshape-design and onshape-theme-repair, dated Oct 4, the current light shell) show exactly the footer described: "Area: 2.40 cm^2", the blue-square dropdown, "57.24 mm x 36.93 mm", "Extrude complete", "Messages •". The cm^2 is explained, not just observed: the validation profiles pin Units/UserSchema=0 and a headless probe under the bundled pythonw.exe shows schema 0 formats 240 mm^2 as "2.40 cm^2" while schema 6 (MmMin) gives "240.00 mm^2" with lengths unchanged, so the proposed one-int fix works. The Messages channel really has no severity (append_message/update_messages_button only count unread), so the stated dependency is genuine. Classification: design_weakness is honest; the behavior is intended and nothing malfunctions, though the cm^2-beside-mm inconsistency is the closest thing to a defect in it. Severity low is right: impact if true is clarity and brand coherence on a strip read constantly, with no blocked workflow, no lost message (each channel does show the warning) and no data risk; the newcomer mis-read of the view-size readout as a face dimension is the only concrete error it can induce. User value medium because the footer is read on every operation and is the one surface that still leaks FreeCAD, but it is polish. Effort S: setting UserSchema=6 in the project-local profile that launch-kurtshape.ps1 already owns (runtime/user-data) or at startup, plus findChild hides for DimensionWidget in the existing Show/Polish filter, is a few lines; the bell should stay until the Messages-severity finding lands, which is correctly scoped as a separate dependency.
judge.risk: Hiding or disabling notificationArea before Messages carries severity removes the native non-intrusive popups (they are anchored to that button, and NotificationAreaEnabled=false stops creating them), and IMPLEMENTATION.md:15 shows Kurt relies on seeing those today, so order matters. Switching Units/UserSchema to 6 changes every native UserString, not just the preselection label: property-editor values, native quantity spinboxes in task panels, volume readouts (cm^3 becomes mm^3) and the Measure tool; the bridge and core parse quantities (core.py:56, assembly.py:516) rather than format them, so bridge responses are unaffected, but validation profiles pin UserSchema=0 and any GUI assertion matching "cm^2"/"cm^3" text would need updating. MmMin also reports velocities in mm/min, harmless here. Hiding DimensionWidget drops a view-scale cue some FreeCAD users use; low. The InputHintWidget point is a check, not a claim: the probe shows hintLabel collapsed to 6 px when empty, so whether sketch hints survive beside the stretch-1 message is untested.

findings.title: Status label copy lacks an empty-document state and shouts 'Rebuild required' while a sketch is being edited
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 1388-1410 (status_detail, rebuild_reason_text), 299-300 (word-wrapped self.status), 1745-1753 (refresh applies it); core.py 1322-1324, 1341 (sketch_only / needs_rebuild derivation)
findings.evidence: 'measured = self.state.get("measurements"); if not measured: return "Sketches only · mm"' (1402-1404) fires for a new empty part: startup-origin.png (Oct 6) shows 'Sketches only · mm' with 'Features (0)'. 'if status == "needs_rebuild": return "Rebuild required · " + rebuild_reason_text(...)' (1400-1401) with default 'pending model changes' shows during an active sketch: circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6) left dock reads 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' wrapped over two lines while a circle is being drawn.
findings.scenario: Fresh document; any sketch edit.
findings.consequence: The first thing a new document says is wrong, and the dock shouts 'Rebuild required' during the most common action, training Kurt to ignore the status label.
findings.reproduction: New -> read the left status; Shift+S, pick Top, draw anything -> read it again.
findings.proposed_change: status_detail: distinguish empty ('No geometry yet · mm · Shift+S to sketch'), sketch_only ('Sketches only'), and suppress the needs_rebuild wording while self.active_sketch() or self.task ('Editing sketch · rebuild on Finish'); reserve 'Rebuild required' for the engine/build-stamp reasons.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe asserts the left status text for the three states.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py status_detail (1396-1410) and rebuild_reason_text (1388-1394), plus core._build_status (1310-1345) and the per-object status at 1387. The strings are exactly what the finder quotes. 'Sketches only · mm' is the fallback for any state without measurements; core assigns 'sketch_only' to a document with no solid, including an empty one (1341: 'valid' if solid else 'sketch_only'), so a fresh New document prints it: startup-origin.png (Oct 6) shows it with Features (0) / Parts (0). 'needs_rebuild' is set whenever any active Sketcher/PartDesign/Part object is Touched (1322-1324); an in-progress sketch is Touched, so the dock prints 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' (the default reason text at 1394) during every sketch: circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6) shows it wrapped on two lines (self.status has word wrap, 299-300). finish_sketch_edit recomputes and re-evaluates status (core 1636-1638), so the message clears on Finish; it is transient but appears during the most common activity. Not changed by any commit through f57d592; docs/2026-10-03-claude-review/CODEX_PROMPT.md 886 specified the 'Rebuild required · <reason>' wording, and no test or macro asserts either label (tests check build_status values only). Why downgraded: the labels faithfully render the core state machine (the model does need a rebuild after the sketch changes; the bridge reports the same 'needs_rebuild'), so this is misleading copy and a missing 'editing sketch' state in the mapping, not wrong state. That is a design weakness, not a verified defect; severity low because the label is advisory and nothing downstream acts on it.
findings.refute_evidence: Both Oct 6 captures are in docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/ and match the code paths line for line. CODEX_PROMPT.md 884-888 defines status copy only for valid / needs_rebuild / failed; 'Sketches only' predates it (b65f066, Oct 2) and was never specified for an empty document. core.finish_sketch_edit recomputes (1636-1638), so the rebuild wording does not persist after Finish.

judge.kurt_would_notice: He sees 'Rebuild required' at the bottom of the history dock in every sketch session and has already learned to ignore it, which is the cost: the same label is the one that carries the real engine-changed / saved-by-other-build reasons after open. Through the bridge he reads build_status directly and is unaffected.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: A SolidWorks user knows 'rebuild required' as the traffic-light after an edit and would half-expect it, but an Onshape user never rebuilds and would look for a problem; both would find 'Sketches only' on a document with no sketch odd before anything else is read.
judge.risk: Low. The change is a mapping in status_detail using self.active_sketch() / self.task, which refresh already consults at 1757; keep the engine/build-stamp reasons verbatim so the needs_rebuild notification on open (1374) and bridge semantics are untouched. No test pins the label strings.

merged_from.title: 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' is shown in the feature panel while a sketch is being edited (the model bar, with Rebuild, is hidden at that point)
merged_from.lines: ui.py:1396-1401 (status_detail), 1749-1752 (label set in refresh), 1250-1256 (inspect/refresh on status change during the lease), 3407 (model bar hidden while sketching); core.py:1321-1326 (Touched -> pending), 1341 (needs_rebuild); screenshots docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/ghost-circle-before.png and circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6)
merged_from.evidence: docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6, current light shell) bottom-left reads 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' while 'DragCircle' is in edit and the status bar says 'Sketch editing …'. core.py:1325-1326 marks any Touched Sketcher object as pending → status needs_rebuild; ui.py:1400-1401 renders that as 'Rebuild required'.
merged_from.consequence: Two status surfaces disagree; a newcomer may press Rebuild (disabled anyway) or worry the model is broken. Diminishes trust in the real 'Rebuild required · geometry engine changed' message.
merged_from.reproduction: Open any sketch and read the left status label.
merged_from.proposed_change: In status_detail, when self.active_sketch() (or state['active_sketch_edit']) show 'Editing <sketch label> · changes apply on Finish'; or in _build_status ignore the Touched flag of the leased sketch.
merged_from.acceptance: GUI recipe sketch-edit-state: left status never contains 'Rebuild required' during a lease unless a rebuild_reason is set.
merged_from.refute_reasoning: Viewed both Oct 6 screenshots (docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/ghost-circle-before.png and circle-drag-after.png, current light shell): bottom-left panel reads 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' while DragCircle is in edit, the native Sketch Edit task is open and the status bar says 'Sketch editing · ...'. Code at HEAD reproduces it: core._build_status (core.py 1321-1326) appends any Touched Sketcher::/PartDesign:: object to pending with no exemption for the leased sketch (sketch_edits is only reported as active_sketch_edit at core.py 1403, never consulted here), status becomes needs_rebuild at 1341, and ui.status_detail (1396-1401) renders needs_rebuild as 'Rebuild required · ' + rebuild_reason_text, which falls back to 'pending model changes' when no RebuildReason is stored. The label is set from refresh() at ui.py 1749-1752, and the panel re-inspects and refreshes whenever build_status changes during the lease (ui.py 1250-1256), so the moment the first geometry edit touches the sketch the left status flips. begin_sketch_edit itself (core.py 1601-1618) does not touch the sketch, so 'every sketch edit session' means every session with at least one edit, which is every real one. Git: the Touched line dates from the 2026-10-02 baseline (b65f066) and status_detail is unchanged through f57d592; not solved. One correction: the Rebuild button is not 'disabled anyway' while sketching, the whole model bar is hidden (ui.py 3407), so a newcomer cannot press it; the harm is the contradictory message and the diluted meaning of the real 'geometry engine changed' rebuild notice. Classification design_weakness, severity low are honest.
merged_from.refute_evidence: Both Oct 6 screenshots show the message with only a sketch in the document (no solids), where the label would otherwise read 'Sketches only · mm'. test_build_status.py asserts needs_rebuild in several places but never during a sketch lease, so a UI-side fix in status_detail touches no bridge contract or test.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Probably not day to day (he rarely watches the left status while sketching), but if a bridge script inspects mid-lease it sees build_status needs_rebuild, and the 'Rebuild required' wording stops meaning anything once it appears in every sketch session.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Two surfaces disagree: the status bar says 'Sketch editing' while the panel says the model needs a rebuild. They look for a Rebuild button (hidden in sketch mode), wonder whether the model is broken, and learn to ignore the one message that matters after an engine change.
judge.risk: Low for the UI fix (status_detail shows 'Editing <sketch label> · changes apply on Finish' when state['active_sketch_edit'] is set). Changing _build_status to ignore the leased sketch's Touched flag alters the bridge's build_status during a lease and should get its own test; prefer the presentation-side change.

findings.title: Clicking a selectable status/verdict label parks focus and silences every single-key shortcut
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 634-639, 631, 366, 2339; shortcuts.py 225-226, 271-280; tools/messages-validation.FCMacro 286-291 (validated StrongFocus contract)
findings.evidence: make_message_copyable: 'label.setTextInteractionFlags(TextSelectableByMouse | TextSelectableByKeyboard); label.setFocusPolicy(QtCore.Qt.StrongFocus)' applied to the footer message and both preview verdicts (631, 366, 2339). shortcuts.py _text_input returns True for 'isinstance(widget, QLabel) and widget.textInteractionFlags() & (TextSelectableByMouse|TextSelectableByKeyboard)' (276-277) and the filter then returns False for every key except Escape and Ctrl+S/N/O (226-227). README explicitly invites clicking these messages to copy them.
findings.scenario: Kurt clicks the footer message to copy an error, then presses N, F, L or Shift+S.
findings.consequence: Nothing happens until he clicks the viewport; it looks like shortcuts broke.
findings.reproduction: Click the footer text, press F: no fit. Click the canvas, press F: fit.
findings.proposed_change: Keep labels selectable but give them Qt.NoFocus (mouse selection and the context-menu Copy still work) or, if Ctrl+C must work, make _text_input treat QLabel as text input only for Ctrl/Shift chords (letters still route). Also add a visible focus cue for panes (QTreeWidget:focus { border-left: 2px solid accent }) since QAbstractItemView has border 0 (theme.py 113-116) and Tab passes ~28 toolbar stops before reaching the tree.
findings.risk: Keyboard-only copy from the label changes; document Ctrl+C via context menu.
findings.acceptance: tests/test_shortcuts QtRoutingTests: focus on a selectable QLabel, key 'F' -> fit callback invoked; Ctrl+C still copies.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py make_message_copyable (634-639): TextSelectableByMouse | TextSelectableByKeyboard plus StrongFocus, applied to the footer message (631), the extrude preview hint (366) and the studio preview hint (2339). Read shortcuts.py: _text_input (271-280) returns True for any QLabel with selectable flags, and the filter (225-226) then returns False for every key except Escape and local.save/new/open, so neither the KurtShape callbacks nor the 'native' entries (view.fit = F) are invoked. No KurtShape action carries a QAction shortcut (no setShortcut anywhere in ui.py), so there is no second path. Both the StrongFocus and the QLabel branch were added together in 69dc29c (Oct 3) and are unchanged at HEAD. README.md 75 invites clicking/right-clicking these messages. I settled the behavioural claim with a headless probe under the bundled pythonw (offscreen, isolated profile): a QLabel configured exactly as make_message_copyable does takes focus on a left click (focusWidget == QLabel); with it focused, F, N and Shift+S fire nothing through an installed ShortcutRouter while Ctrl+S still fires local.save; focus stays on the label after the pointer leaves; clicking the central widget restores F. The same probe shows the proposed remedy works: a NoFocus label keeps focus on the viewport stand-in, F fires, and a mouse drag still selects the label text. One correction to the proposal: tools/messages-validation.FCMacro 286-291 explicitly asserts focusPolicy == StrongFocus and keyboard selection + Ctrl+C on the focused status label, so NoFocus would need that recipe revised; narrowing the QLabel branch in _text_input to Ctrl/Shift chords and navigation keys keeps that contract and fixes the routing.
findings.refute_evidence: Probe script review-scratchpad/verify2/a11_focus_probe.py, output a11_out.txt: initial_focus_is_central true; text_input_label true; F_with_central_focus ['view.fit']; focus_is_label_after_click true; F/N/Shift+S_with_label_focus []; Ctrl+S_with_label_focus ['local.save']; focus_still_label_after_mouse_move true; F_after_reclick_central ['view.fit']; nofocus_label_click_keeps_central_focus true; nofocus_label_drag_selected_text 'Second status text for selection'. Runtime: PySide6 6.8.3 from the bundled FreeCAD 1.1.4.

judge.kurt_would_notice: This bites in exactly the flow README tells him to use: click the footer error to copy it for chat, then press N, F or Shift+S and nothing happens, with no cue that the status label owns the keyboard. One viewport click recovers it, but it reads as shortcuts breaking mid-session.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape and SolidWorks have no focusable status text, so a user who clicked the bottom message to read it would not suspect it and would assume the keyboard shortcuts are unreliable.
judge.risk: Low to medium. NoFocus on the three labels is a one-line change but contradicts the committed messages-validation recipe (StrongFocus + keyboard selection + Ctrl+C), so either that recipe changes or the fix goes into _text_input (let plain single keys through for QLabel). Preview hints inside editor dialogs already return False at the QDialog guard (228-229), so only the footer message routing changes.

merged_from.title: Read-only search field and selectable status labels take keyboard focus and swallow single-key tools
merged_from.evidence: SearchField is a QLineEdit(readOnly) with default StrongFocus; make_message_copyable gives the status message and the preview verdict TextSelectableByMouse|Keyboard plus StrongFocus. shortcuts.py:271-281 treats any QLineEdit (read-only included) and any selectable QLabel as a text input, and :226 then returns False for every key except Escape and Ctrl+S/N/O.
merged_from.scenario: Kurt clicks the toolbar search box (or closes the Alt+C dialog, which returns focus there), or clicks the red status message to select and copy an error, then presses L, C, D, N, F, P, S, Delete or Enter.
merged_from.consequence: The key does nothing (or Enter/Space reopens the search dialog) until he clicks the viewport; feels like a dead keyboard after reading an error.
merged_from.reproduction: GUI: click the status bar message, then press L inside a sketch; or click 'Search tools…', close the dialog with Escape, press Shift+E.
merged_from.proposed_change: Give SearchField Qt.NoFocus (it opens a dialog on click/Enter anyway) and give the copyable labels Qt.ClickFocus only, plus in _text_input treat a read-only QLineEdit and a QLabel as non-text (or route single-key shortcuts when the focused label has no selection). After the search dialog closes, return focus to the active MDI viewport.
merged_from.risk: Copy-by-keyboard on the label needs focus; ClickFocus keeps that while Tab navigation skips it.
merged_from.acceptance: GUI recipe: after clicking the status label, L starts a line; after closing Alt+C, Shift+E opens Extrude. Shortcut unit test for _text_input with a read-only QLineEdit.

findings.title: Left dock paints an inert "Feature history" title bar above the filter and "Features (N)" label; parts block repeats the active part in a combo and a bold row; marker caption wraps
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 131-133, 240-251, 262-268, 275-281, 1658, 1710-1715, 1724-1727, 1747, 1763; src/kurtshape/theme.py 75, 81; src/kurtshape/rollback_history.py 78-88
findings.evidence: QDockWidget('Feature history') with NoDockWidgetFeatures still paints its title bar (theme.py 81 styles it); below it 'Filter features' then QLabel 'Features (N)' #SectionTitle; model-workspace-1440.png shows 'Feature history' / filter / 'Features (2)' stacked, then after the tree 'Rollback · 2 / 2' (now the marker description), 'Parts (1)', a 'Body' combo and the bold body row. The proposed-shell-layout.png direction uses one 'Features (3)' header and an 'Active' tag.
findings.scenario: Every session; most visible on small windows where 90 px of header precede the first feature.
findings.consequence: Hierarchy reads muddled: two 'feature' headers, a part chooser that duplicates the bold row, and a marker caption that wraps to two lines.
findings.reproduction: Count header rows above 'Origin'.
findings.proposed_change: self.setTitleBarWidget(QWidget()) to drop the dock bar; one header row 'Features (N)' with the filter as an inline icon-field; show the active part as a right-aligned 'Active' tag in the parts row and demote body_choice to a context menu or keep it only when >1 owner; single-line marker caption with elision + tooltip.
findings.risk: Dock cannot be dragged (already NoDockWidgetFeatures), so no loss.
findings.acceptance: At 1024x700 the first feature row sits within 60 px of the toolbar; design-surface recipe checks header count.
findings.refute_reasoning: Holds as stated at HEAD f57d592 (working tree clean apart from untracked docs/fable-deep-review). Source: `Panel.__init__` (ui.py:131-133) builds the dock as `QDockWidget("Feature history")` with `NoDockWidgetFeatures` and never calls `setTitleBarWidget` (grep: only feature_panel.py:70 does, for the editor; `git log -S setTitleBarWidget -- ui.py` is empty), so Qt still paints the title bar, styled by theme.py:81 (`QDockWidget::title { padding: 5px 8px; border-bottom }`). `make_history` then stacks the filter field (240-248) and the `#SectionTitle` label (249-251, theme.py:75 `padding: 5px 8px`) above the tree: three chrome rows before "Origin". Below the tree `rollback_label` is word-wrapped (262-265) and receives `RollbackMarker.description()` (268, 1715; rollback_history.py:78-88). The parts block adds "Parts (N)" (275-277, 1747) plus `body_choice` (278-281), which is shown unconditionally in part-studio refresh (1658) even with a single owner, while the same active part is already bolded in the tree (1724, 1763) and named in its tooltip (1727). Captures from the current era confirm it: validation/sketch-edit-history/onshape-workflows/compact-workspace.png (2026-10-05, 1200x800 logical at DPR 1.5) shows "Feature history" / "Filter features" / "Features (4)" above Origin, ~87 logical px from toolbar bottom to the first row, and "Parts (2)" + a "UseBody" combo over rows "Body"/"UseBody"; validation/sketch-conversion-rollback/rollback/between-extrusion-and-hole-history.png (2026-10-05) shows the caption "After Plate extrusion · before Hole position" wrapped onto two lines at the dock's width. The finder's cited model-workspace-1440.png is 2026-10-04 and still shows the older "Rollback · 2 / 2" slider, but the finder already noted that; the Oct 5 captures show the same header stack with the current marker. The proposed direction matches docs/onshape-design-audit/proposed-shell-layout.png (2026-10-04): one "Features (3)" header, filter beneath, "Parts (1)" with a "Plate  Active" row and an "Active target for new features" caption; PLAN.md:178-182 asks that the active target be shown "distinctly from whichever row or geometry is selected". Nothing in git log or docs shows this was addressed. Classification design_weakness / low / high is right: it is cosmetic hierarchy, not a defect, and the dock is already undraggable so dropping the bar loses nothing. Implementation caveats the finding omits: tools/rollback-history-validation.FCMacro:211,240,260 assert exact `rollback_label.text()` strings, so single-line elision must be paint-level (elided display + tooltip) or the recipe updated; tools/assembly-gui-validation.FCMacro:216 asserts `features_title.text()` equals the assembly name in assembly mode (1804), so a merged header must keep that label; tools/history-lifecycle-validation.FCMacro:192-238 drives `body_choice` via itemData/findData, so demoting the combo should keep the widget (hidden) rather than remove it.
findings.refute_evidence: Current-era captures: validation\sketch-edit-history\onshape-workflows\compact-workspace.png (2026-10-05): three chrome rows above Origin, ~130 physical / ~87 logical px from toolbar to first row; "Parts (2)" + "UseBody" combo over Body/UseBody rows. validation\sketch-conversion-rollback\rollback\between-extrusion-and-hole-history.png (2026-10-05): caption "After Plate extrusion · before Hole position" wrapped to two lines. Reference direction: docs\onshape-design-audit\proposed-shell-layout.png and PLAN.md:178-182. No `setTitleBarWidget` on the Panel anywhere in ui.py history (`git log -S setTitleBarWidget -- src/kurtshape/ui.py` empty); `body_choice.show()` unconditional at ui.py:1658. Recipe couplings to preserve when fixing: tools/rollback-history-validation.FCMacro:211,240,260 (exact rollback_label text), tools/assembly-gui-validation.FCMacro:216 (features_title carries the assembly name), tools/history-lifecycle-validation.FCMacro:192-238 (drives body_choice by itemData). Design-surface recipe (tools/design-surface-validation.FCMacro) currently checks the editor header only, not the history dock's header count, so the finding's acceptance check would be a new assertion.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Yes, every session but not as a bug. He watches the left panel while the bridge adds features, and on the 235-430 px dock the stacked "Feature history" / filter / "Features (N)" plus the "Parts (1)" / "Body" combo / bold "Body" row cost him three or four history rows. The caption wrapping to two lines ("After Plate extrusion · before Hole position", validation/sketch-conversion-rollback/rollback/between-extrusion-and-hole-history.png, Oct 5) nudges the history/parts split as he drags the rollback marker. judge.newcomer_would_notice: Immediately. findings.title: Preview ghost is tessellated far finer than the committed model, so Confirm visibly coarsens geometry
findings.lines: 127-141 (render_mesh; 129 tessellate, 136 discretize), 179 (ProvisionalExtrusion), src/kurtshape/preview_worker.py:329
findings.evidence: Line 129 `vertices, triangles = material.tessellate(0.15)` and 136 `edge.discretize(Deflection=0.15)` (absolute, no angular parameter). exp1 on fresh cylinders r=2.5/25: tessellate(0.15) -> 252 vertices / 500 triangles regardless of radius (~126 segments per circle); exp3: fillet block tessellate(0.15) 6260 triangles vs 452 at the pinned display default (0.2 % / 28.65 deg); r=3 hole 26 segments natively. The committed object is drawn by ViewProviderPartExt with the per-object Deviation/AngularDeflection, not by this mesh.
findings.scenario: Extrude/Cut/Fillet preview on any curved profile, then Confirm.
findings.consequence: The translucent ghost shows round holes and smooth rounds; the accepted feature appears with 26-segment holes and 7-facet fillets. Kurt reads it as 'the result is worse than the preview'. Same in the running app.
findings.reproduction: Headless: scratch exp1_tessellation.py (shape_tessellate) and exp3. GUI: preview a 6 mm circle pad on the plate, Confirm, compare the hole wall.
findings.proposed_change: Tessellate the preview with the display rule: compute deflection = (sum of bbox extents)/300 * MeshDeviation and angular = MeshAngularDeflection (the same numbers ViewProviderPartExt will use) and mesh with MeshPart.meshFromShape(Relative=False) or BRepMesh via Part with explicit angular deflection, in both ProvisionalExtrusion (line 177-180) and the exact worker's render_mesh; use the preset's values so preview and result match at every preset. Keep the 500k/1M vertex guard (lines 132-133).
findings.dependencies: Preset values readable from preview_worker (pass them in the proposal/env).
findings.risk: Slightly coarser provisional ghost at draft; none at standard.
findings.acceptance: For the r=3 hole fixture the overlay rim segment count equals the committed ViewObject mesh segment count (+/-1) at each preset; existing extrusion-preview GUI recipe (validation/ui-refinement 625/625 orange pixel check) still passes.
findings.refute_reasoning: The cited code is exactly as described at HEAD f57d592: src/kurtshape/extrusion_preview.py:129 `material.tessellate(0.15)` and :136 `edge.discretize(Deflection=0.15)` inside render_mesh, which is the only mesh source for the ghost (provisional prism at :179 `render_mesh(unit, unit)`, exact worker at preview_worker.py:329, GUI fallback at :559). git blame shows the lines unchanged since 4681ddfd (2026-10-13); no later commit mentions tessellation/deviation; no test under tests/ references render_mesh, tessellate or Deviation. KurtShape sets no `Mod/Part` MeshDeviation/MeshAngularDeflection anywhere in src/ and the live profile runtime/user-data/user.cfg carries no override, so committed features draw with ViewProviderPartExt's defaults (0.2 % of summed bbox extents / 300, 28.65 deg). A headless probe under the bundled pythonw.exe (FreeCAD 1.1.4, OCCT 7.8.1) reproduces the finder's numbers: `Shape.tessellate(0.15)` yields 126 rim segments on a cylinder for every radius 0.5-100 mm (252 pts / 252 tris per lateral face), while the display rule emulated with MeshPart.meshFromShape(LinearDeflection=(sum extents)/300*0.2, AngularDeflection=0.5, Relative=False) gives 26-28 segments on an r=3 hole for plates from 30x20x8 to 200x150x20; a 90-degree r=2 fillet face meshes to 14 display facets (7 segments) vs 64 preview triangles. Even the Shift+R high-quality toggle (viewport_actions.py:231, Deviation 0.05 / 10 deg) caps at roughly 36 segments on r=3, still far coarser than the ghost. The item is already recorded, unfixed, as B-04 in docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md:104. Classification design_weakness / medium / high confidence stands; the GUI recipe validation/ui-refinement-preview/gui-result.json checks behaviour only, not mesh density, so the "still passes" acceptance clause is credible but adds no coverage.
findings.refute_evidence: Mechanism correction: the 0.15 mm figure is not what drives the ghost density. The probe shows `Shape.tessellate(d)` on an r=25 cylinder returns 126 segments for d = 0.05, 0.15, 0.5 and 2.0 alike (229 only at d = 0.01), i.e. FreeCAD 1.1.4's tessellate output is governed by an internal angular cap of about 0.05 rad (10x finer than the 0.5 rad display default), so simply changing the number passed to tessellate() cannot align it with the display; the fix must go through a mesher that takes an explicit angular deflection, as the proposal says, and the MeshPart.meshFromShape(Relative=False, AngularDeflection=0.5) emulation in the probe reproduces the committed counts (26-28 segments on r=3). Second nuance: the outline lines go the other way: `edge.discretize(Deflection=0.15)` on an r=3 circle gives 11 samples (10 segments) and on r=25 30 samples, so the ghost's rim outline is coarser than the committed 26-segment hole while its faces are finer; the acceptance criterion should cover both the face mesh and the outline. Probe script and output: review-scratchpad/verify\probe_tess.py and probe_out.txt. The "same in the running app" claim is inferred from the absence of any profile/source override rather than from a screenshot; no validation/ image shows the post-Confirm comparison. The proposal's dependency on "preset values" refers to quality presets that exist only in docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md section 3, not in code; at HEAD the only values to match are the per-ViewObject Deviation/AngularDeflection defaults (and the Shift+R toggle values if that mode is active).

judge.kurt_would_notice: Through the bridge, nothing: the `preview` op (core.py:1812) evaluates in a clone and returns measurements, no ghost is drawn, and the committed body is tessellated the same way regardless. In the GUI feature panels he sees a smooth translucent ghost, then on Confirm a 6 mm hole with ~26 sides and fillets with ~7 flats per quarter. He knows FreeCAD's tessellation habit and reaches for Shift+R; the mismatch itself is a shrug, the coarse committed display (B-01 territory) is what actually costs him when inspecting fillets.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape/SolidWorks never show a polygonal hole at default. They watch the hole go from round to a 26-gon and the fillet from smooth to 7 flats the instant they press Confirm, and may read it as the feature failing or the radius being wrong. They would hunt for a display-quality setting and find only an unlabeled Shift+R toggle.
judge.risk: Low. The ghost gets visibly chunkier at today's 28.65 deg default (fillet removal slivers become 7-facet wedges, harder to read in translucent orange), so shipped alone the fix trades a pretty preview for consistency; it only pays off paired with a better display default. The worker is a separate process, so the GUI must pass Deviation/AngularDeflection in the request (a Shift+R toggle mid-edit briefly mismatches again, harmlessly). Deflection must be computed from the committed body's bbox (result.shape), not the material sliver's, or counts still differ; the provisional unit-prism cache key must include the rule. The parity test should compare meshes rather than formula counts because OCCT halves the angular deflection for edges (hence 26 segments, not 13, at 28.65 deg). No geometry or data risk; the orange-pixel GUI recipe is tessellation-agnostic. Side benefit: smaller mesh JSON over the worker IPC on dense models.
judge.reasoning: Source confirmed: extrusion_preview.py:129 `material.tessellate(0.15)` and :136 `edge.discretize(Deflection=0.15)`, absolute with no angular term; ProvisionalExtrusion :179 and preview_worker.py:329 both call render_mesh, so every ghost (provisional and exact) uses this rule. The committed feature is drawn by ViewProviderPartExt at the per-object Deviation/AngularDeflection; nothing in src/ sets MeshDeviation/MeshAngularDeflection, and viewport_actions.toggle_high_quality (Shift+R) is the only quality control, consistent with the docs' 0.2 % / 28.65 deg pinned default. Scratch exp1/exp3 exist with outputs: tessellate(0.15) yields 252 vertices / 500 triangles for r=2.5 and r=25 (an angular cap near 0.05 rad), the r=2 fillet gives 6260 triangles vs 452 at the display default; exp3's cylinder equalities are a cached-triangulation artefact, not counter-evidence. Classification: design_weakness is honest. Both renderers draw the same exact BRep; the ghost is the more faithful picture, and no contract says the preview must match the display rule, so this is a consistency gap, not a defect. Severity: 'medium' overstates impact. The harm is perceptual and transient, with no wrong geometry, no lost work, a one-key workaround, and the thing that actually bothers users (the coarse committed display) is owned by the display-preset/B-01 item; the incremental cost of the mismatch is a moment of doubt in the GUI flow, which Kurt rarely uses for features. Low, at the low/medium boundary. user_value medium is conditional: standalone, coarsening the ghost is low value (it makes the preview uglier without improving anything); bundled with the Standard preset (0.2 % / 12 deg) and the ghost following the same rule, preview and result agree and both look better, plus cheaper exact-preview transport. Effort S holds for the mechanical change (bbox-relative deflection from the body's bbox, angular from the preference, MeshPart.meshFromShape Relative=False, values passed in the worker request, provisional key extended); asserting +/-1 parity against the live ViewObject mesh in a GUI test would push toward M. Recommend treating it as a sub-item of the display-preset work rather than an independent fix.
