findings.title: Constraint icons keep the Light pack's #E03131 while dimensions and constrained geometry are black
findings.symbol: apply_native_light_preferences.view_names (ConstrainedIcoColor copied from the pack); SKETCH_STATE_COLORS
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/theme.py 23-37 (SKETCH_STATE_COLORS lacks ConstrainedIcoColor), 239-248 (view_names copies it from the pack; key on line 241), 266 (override order); src/kurtshape/sketch_colors.py 289-302
findings.evidence: view_names includes ConstrainedIcoColor and the pack value is 3761320447 = #E03131 (red); SKETCH_STATE_COLORS turns every dimension colour to #000000. The Oct 4 sketch-editor-1440.png shows red constraint ticks; sketch_colors.py:289-290 reads ConstrainedIcoColor at runtime so it adapts to any value.
findings.scenario: Every sketch with coincident/horizontal/vertical constraints.
findings.consequence: Red glyphs read as errors on the light canvas (InvalidSketchColor is also red #FF0000), fighting the black/blue/red solver scheme Kurt approved.
findings.reproduction: Open any constrained sketch; compare glyph colour with the dimension text.
findings.proposed_change: Set View/ConstrainedIcoColor to the muted ink token (#59636C) in SKETCH_STATE_COLORS, keep InvalidSketchColor red; sketch_colors.py needs no change (it reads the parameter).
findings.risk: Hovered/selected constraint glyphs keep native highlight colours.
findings.acceptance: Glyphs grey, dimensions black, invalid state still red in a native sketch grab; sketch-colour recipe assertion updated.
findings.refute_reasoning: Holds at HEAD f57d592. src/kurtshape/theme.py:239-248 copies the Light pack's View/ConstrainedIcoColor (3761320447 = #E03131FF; confirmed in runtime/.../PreferencePacks/FreeCAD Light/FreeCAD Light.cfg line 138) and SKETCH_STATE_COLORS (lines 23-37) overrides all four dimension colours to #000000 but has no ConstrainedIcoColor entry; the override runs after the pack copy (line 266), so the same mechanism would work for the icon colour exactly as it already does for ConstrainedDimColor, which appears in both sets. Working tree is clean for theme.py and sketch_colors.py, and no commit after 4681ddf touches the key, so it is not already solved. The bundled lib/SketcherGui.pyd reads ConstrainedIcoColor and has no separate coincident-point colour key; sketch_colors.py:289-302 reads the parameter at runtime as its 'coincident_color' candidate and already recolours coincident points (macro check 'Unconstrained coincident point is blue rather than native constraint red' in tools/sketch-dimension-point-colors-validation.FCMacro:240), so only the constraint icons keep the pack red. Evidence correction: the finder's Oct 4 sketch-editor-1440.png predates the Oct 5 solver-colour change (it shows red dimensions and green geometry too), so it does not demonstrate the mismatch on its own. The first post-change capture, validation/sketch-presentation/sketch-dimension-point-colors/native-mixed-point-colors.png (Oct 5 16:02), shows black dimension labels, #0000FF free geometry, and Block constraint glyphs whose pixels sample at exactly (224,49,49) = #E03131 (PIL probe under the bundled pythonw). Scenario correction: coincident constraints draw no glyph natively (their point colour is already managed), so the affected cases are horizontal/vertical/parallel/Block and other icon-bearing constraints. No doc records a deliberate choice for glyph colour (docs/M1_PROGRESS.md:64 describes blue/black/red for geometry and conflicts only), so this is an untouched pack default, consistent with 'opportunity'/low. Note for the fix: tools/sketch-edit-state-validation.FCMacro:141-142 iterates SKETCH_STATE_COLORS, so a new key is asserted automatically (only the label text 'blue, black and red' would be stale); and DeactivatedConstrDimColor is #000000, so grey (#59636C) active glyphs would be lighter than deactivated black ones; black for active glyphs would match the 'black = constrained' scheme and avoid that inversion.
findings.refute_evidence: Post-change capture validation/sketch-presentation/sketch-dimension-point-colors/native-mixed-point-colors.png (2026-10-05 16:02): Block glyph pixels sample at (224,49,49)=#E03131, dimension text black, free line #0000FF. The cited Oct 4 validation/onshape-design/sketch-editor-1440.png is pre-change (red dimensions, green geometry) and should not be the evidence pointer. Light pack also sets ConstrainedDimColor=#E03131 and InvalidSketchColor=#FD7E14; KurtShape overrides those to #000000 and #FF0000 but leaves ConstrainedIcoColor. SketcherGui.pyd string table contains ConstrainedIcoColor and no Coincident*Color key.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Yes, on every sketch, but as noise rather than a trap. The Oct 5 "Fully constrained" grab shows everything he asked for (black geometry, black dimensions) except red ⊗ marks at every coincident vertex and red H/V ticks, and bridge-built sketches (add_polyline chains) carry a red mark at every corner. He already lives with FreeCAD's red constraint icons in the Tasks panel and the red horizontal axis line, so he will not mistake them for conflicts; he will read them as the solver-colour scheme he requested on Oct 5 being left one element short. Since he mostly views finished sketches through the bridge rather than editing them, it is a frequent minor irritation, never a blocker.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Immediately. Onshape draws constraint badges in grey/black and reserves red geometry for conflicts or over-definition; SolidWorks draws relations in green/teal and uses red/yellow for over-defined. A newcomer's first constrained sketch shows red marks on every coincident corner next to a "Fully constrained" label, and the glyph red (#E03131) is close enough to the conflict red (#FF0000) that they will ask whether something is wrong. They learn the convention within minutes, but it is a first-impression cost on the primary editing surface and it directly contradicts the Onshape semantic the audit plan commits to.
judge.reasoning: Verified: theme.py copies ConstrainedIcoColor from the Light pack (#E03131) and SKETCH_STATE_COLORS does not override it, while every dimension colour is forced to #000000 and InvalidSketchColor to #FF0000. The finding's cited image is wrong (both Oct 4 sketch-editor-1440.png copies predate the Oct 5 scheme and show red dimensions and green geometry), but the Oct 5 grabs native-mixed-point-colors.png and fully-constrained-native-black.png show exactly the described state: black dimensions, blue/black geometry, red glyphs. Classification: not "opportunity". The project explicitly took ownership of sketch colour semantics (theme.py docstring, M1_PROGRESS Oct 5 "blue free / black constrained / red conflict", PLAN.md "sketch solve status blue/black/red") and left one element red; that is an inconsistency inside a chosen design, i.e. a design_weakness, not an enhancement untethered from a shortcoming. Nothing is broken, so not a defect. Severity stays low: purely visual, no workflow or data impact, and the red partly matches native conventions already present (Tasks-panel icons, red horizontal axis). User value is medium rather than low because it appears on every sketch, on the most-used surface, Kurt personally requested the solver scheme, and the fix is one dict entry plus an assertion. Effort S: add the key to SKETCH_STATE_COLORS (it already runs after the pack copy, so ordering is correct), extend tools/sketch-dimension-point-colors-validation.FCMacro which currently records only the four dimension preferences, take one framebuffer grab, restart the app.
judge.risk: (1) sketch_colors.py:302 uses ConstrainedIcoColor as the native colour of coincident points; in the valid state the recolour pass overwrites it so the change is transparent, but when the sketch is invalid the pass is skipped and coincident points would natively show grey instead of red, so the conflict grab must be re-checked. (2) The proposed muted token #59636C may fall below legible contrast where glyphs sit over the grey rendered body face (as in fully-constrained-native-black.png); the ink token #2D3338 is the safer first try. (3) The change alone does not make "red = conflict" true on the canvas: the native red horizontal axis line and the red Tasks-panel constraint icons remain, so expectations should be set accordingly. (4) Hovered/selected glyphs keep native highlight colours, as the finding says. (5) Written to Kurt's user parameters via App.saveParameter(), same mechanism as the existing colours; needs an app restart to see.

findings.title: Formula whitelist rejects valid FreeCAD syntax (function argument separators, <<Label>> references, ^, %, ?:) and reports only a generic sentence
findings.lines: extrusion_edit.py:14, 240-241; reference_tools.py:204, 375-376; core.py:2693-2694; GUI entry points ui.py:2332 (fillet/chamfer Formula), ui.py:2702 (Feature settings Formula)
findings.evidence: EXPRESSION_PATTERN = r"[A-Za-z0-9_ .+*/()\[\]-]+". Experiment 2 §C: 'max(R.Constraints.Width, 5 mm)', '<<R>>.Constraints.Width / 2', 'R.Constraints.Width ^ 2 / 10 mm' and a trailing ';' were all rejected with 'Use a dimensional formula with named properties and arithmetic'; 'sqrt(R.Constraints.Width * 1 mm)' and '… * 0.5 + 1 mm' were accepted.
findings.scenario: Kurt types a FreeCAD expression he knows (label references, max/min with two arguments, powers) into Formula in Feature settings or the Extrude dialog.
findings.consequence: Rejected without saying which character is disallowed; label-based references are impossible even though FreeCAD's expression engine supports them, so renamed features must be referenced by internal Name.
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/area-c-everyday/exp2_units_expr.py §C.
findings.proposed_change: Allow ',', '<', '>', '^', '%' and ';' in the whitelist (or validate by App.Units/Expression parse: doc.getObject(x).evalExpression / App.Expression.parse in a try) and report the offending character or the native parse error text instead of the generic sentence.
findings.risk: Widening the whitelist is still not code execution (FreeCAD expression language); keep length limit.
findings.acceptance: Native test: the five expressions above are accepted or rejected with the native parser's reason; invalid references still fail with invalid_expression.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read extrusion_edit.py:14 (EXPRESSION_PATTERN = r"[A-Za-z0-9_ .+*/()\[\]-]+"), core.py 2690-2700 (set_expression: re.fullmatch against that pattern, generic 'Use a dimensional formula with named properties and arithmetic'), extrusion_edit.py 240-241 and reference_tools.py 204, 375-376 (the same whitelist duplicated for edit_extrusion and edit_dress_up), and the GUI entry points ui.py:2702 (Feature settings Formula -> set_expression) and ui.py:2332 (fillet/chamfer Formula -> edit_dress_up), so every GUI formula field hits the whitelist. Re-read the finder's experiment output (scratchpad/area-c-everyday/exp2_units_expr.out.txt): comma and semicolon max(), <<R>>, ^ and trailing ';' rejected, sqrt() accepted, exactly as claimed. Ran a 20 s headless probe with the bundled FreeCAD 1.1.4 (isolated env): the native engine accepts 'max(Ref.Length, 5 mm)', 'max(Ref.Length; 5 mm)', '<<My Ref>>.Length / 2' (=10), 'Ref.Length ^ 2 / 10 mm' (=40), 'Ref.Length % 7 mm' (=6) and 'a > 5 mm ? 3 mm : 4 mm' (=3), and rejects a trailing ';' with ParserError 'Failed to parse expression'. So the whitelist blocks valid FreeCAD syntax (two-argument functions are impossible, label references impossible, no power/modulo/conditional), and the one example the finder listed that FreeCAD also rejects (trailing ';') shows the second half of the claim: the native parse error text is never surfaced, only the generic sentence. Git log: the pattern was introduced 2026-10-13 (7d1c56a) and copied in 659b5e7; unchanged at HEAD. Classification design_weakness and severity low are honest: nothing breaks, the author has to rewrite the formula.
findings.refute_evidence: Headless probe (bundled FreeCAD 1.1.4, Qt offscreen, isolated FREECAD_USER_HOME): accepted 'max(a, b)', 'max(a; b)', '<<My Ref>>.Length / 2', 'a ^ 2 / 10 mm', 'a % 7 mm', 'a > 5 mm ? 3 mm : 4 mm'; 'a / 2 ;' raised ParserError. The whitelist is duplicated in three modules, so a fix must change all three or they drift.

judge.kurt_would_notice: He writes FreeCAD expressions daily; max(a; b) is the documented FreeCAD form and <<Label>> is how renamed features are referenced. Both bounce from the bridge and from the Formula fields with a sentence that does not say which character is the problem, so he has to guess or reference features by internal Name.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape/SolidWorks equations use max(a, b); typing that into Formula is rejected with no hint that the comma is the issue, and there is no way to tell a syntax slip from a disallowed feature.
judge.risk: Low. FreeCAD expressions cannot run Python, so widening the whitelist to ',', ';', '<', '>', '^', '%', '?', ':' is safe; keep the 512-char cap, catch the native ParserError on setExpression and return it as invalid_expression with the engine's text, and update the three duplicated patterns together (or share one).

findings.title: Disabled tools give no reason on hover, and activating an 'Unavailable right now' search result closes the dialog without notifying or triggering
findings.lines: tool_search.py:125-131 (availability), 133-144 (_context_reason); ui.py:2764 (trigger = QAction.trigger), 2814-2827 (activate), 3395-3402 (sync_edit_ui disables for native task / unmanaged); toolbar_labels.py:122-127; ui.py:1753-1754 (reference-file status text already names 'adopt a copy')
findings.evidence: tool_search.py:332-333 returns 'Unavailable right now' when entry.enabled is False; ui.py:2820-2822 notifies only for 'Switch to'/'Not available' and otherwise calls entry['trigger']() on a disabled QAction (a no-op under Qt 6). sync_edit_ui:3397-3402 disables file/model actions for an active native Tasks dialog and for unmanaged files with no hover reason; toolbar_labels shows only the name.
findings.scenario: A native Hole/Draft Tasks dialog is open, or a reference FCStd is inspected: the whole model bar is gray.
findings.consequence: Hovering gives a name but no reason; search closes and nothing happens. The newcomer does not know that the right-hand Tasks dialog must be closed or that 'Adopt copy' is the way in.
findings.reproduction: GUI: More → Cut → Hole (native dialog opens), hover Extrude; Alt+C, type fillet, Enter.
findings.proposed_change: Add Panel.unavailability_reason() ('Finish or cancel the open Tasks dialog first', 'Adopt a copy before editing this reference file', 'Finish the sketch first') and (a) pass it to toolbar_labels.register as a second line when the button is disabled, (b) return it from tool_search.availability via a reason provider, (c) notify it on activation instead of triggering.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: test_tool_search: a disabled entry carries the provided reason; GUI recipe: hover label shows two lines while a native task is active; activation of an unavailable entry notifies.
findings.refute_reasoning: tool_search.py is 144 lines, so the cited 330-336 are wrong; availability() is at 125-131 and returns 'Unavailable right now' whenever entry['enabled'] is False, before any context reason. ui.py:2764 builds entries with 'enabled': action.isEnabled() and 'trigger': action.trigger (the raw QAction slot); activate() at 2814-2827 closes the dialog, notifies only for 'Switch to'/'Not available' reasons, and otherwise calls the trigger. sync_edit_ui (ui.py 3395-3402) disables model_actions when native_feature_task_active() (Gui.Control.activeDialog() with no active sketch, ui.py 1172) or when state['managed'] is False, and file/history actions likewise, without setting any reason text. toolbar_labels._show_pending (122-127) renders only label, shortcut and the optional kurtshapeHelp property (set only on Check geometry, ui.py 575), so a disabled button's hover gives the name alone. Settled the Qt claim with a headless probe: the bundle ships Qt6Core.dll and the probe reports Qt 6.8.3, where QAction.trigger() on a disabled action does not emit triggered (fired=False), so Enter on an 'Unavailable right now' row really does nothing after the dialog closes. tests/test_tool_search.py covers only the context reasons (sketch/assembly), none for enabled=False. Minor overstatement: for an unmanaged reference file the status label already reads 'Reference file · inspect or adopt a copy · ...' (ui.py 1753-1754), so the 'Adopt copy' way in is visible there; the native-Tasks case has no explanation anywhere except the Tasks panel itself being open. Classification design_weakness, severity low are honest. Not already solved at HEAD.
findings.refute_evidence: Probe under the bundled interpreter: Qt 6.8.3, disabled QAction.trigger() fired=False, enabled fired=True. The search table does paint 'Unavailable right now' in the Availability column before activation, so the silence is on Enter/double-click, not in the list.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Opening More -> Cut -> Hole (native Tasks panel, see C-19) greys the entire model bar and the file actions; hovering shows names only, and Alt+C + fillet + Enter closes and does nothing. He knows to close the Tasks panel, so it costs him a second rather than confusion.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: The whole toolbar going grey with no explanation reads as a broken app; the only cue is the right-hand Tasks panel. Search tells them 'Unavailable right now' in grey but pressing Enter just closes it, with no toast saying to finish or cancel the open feature first.
judge.risk: Low. A Panel.unavailability_reason() must mirror exactly the conditions sync_edit_ui uses (native task, unmanaged file, active sketch) or hover text and enabled state drift apart; pass it through toolbar_labels.register as a second line and notify it from activate instead of calling the trigger.

findings.title: Active part is an unlabeled combobox; the history's Origin planes and the sketch placement help never say which part they belong to
findings.evidence: validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4, current shell): a bare combobox 'Body' under 'Parts (1)' with no caption; ui.py:279 the only explanation is a tooltip 'Part for new sketches and features'. part_selection (1909-1918) makes a clicked part active, but viewport selection does not; extrude() derives Add/New and the merge list from the sketch's owner, not the combobox (3449-3455), while Shift+S on Top/Front/Right uses the combobox's Body origin (1146-1147, 3217-3229).
findings.scenario: Two or more parts; Kurt clicks Part 2's face in the viewport, presses Shift+S, picks 'Top' from history.
findings.consequence: The sketch lands in whichever part the combobox names (often Part 1), with no visual sign in the viewport or on the sketch header; later the extrude defaults to New/Add based on that owner. Experts learn the rule; newcomers get features in the wrong part.
findings.reproduction: GUI: create two parts; select a face of Part 2 (do not click the Parts list); Shift+S then click Top; read the new sketch's Body in inspect.
findings.proposed_change: Caption the chooser ('New sketches and features go to') and echo the active part in the sketch placement help ('Top plane of Part 2 · change in Parts'); offer 'Make active' in the Parts context menu; when a viewport selection belongs to a different current part, offer the part in the placement editor as a second choice; show the active part's origin planes with the accent color during placement (PlaneHighlight already exists).
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe part-studio: the placement editor names the target part; selecting a face of another part during placement creates the sketch in that part (already true) and the status says so.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py make_history 271-298, SelectionObserver 110-125, active_body/plane/change_body 1123-1157, _operation 1335-1338, refresh 1716-1747, history_click 1866-1884, part_selection 1909-1918, capture_feature_selection 2103-2118, start_sketch 3195-3236, choose_support/begin_sketch 3251-3268, extrude 3434-3474, core.py _body 906-928 and _new_sketch 2062-2078, validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png, docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md 85-89, docs/HISTORY_LIFECYCLE.md 40-49. Held: 278-281 is a bare QComboBox whose only explanation is the tooltip 'Part for new sketches and features'; the Oct 4 screenshot shows 'Parts (1)' over an unlabeled 'Body' dropdown and a bold 'Body' row. 1722-1727 add only bold and a tooltip. 1909-1918 makes a Parts-list click activate the part; SelectionObserver.addSelection -> capture_feature_selection never touches body_choice, so viewport selection does not change the active part. 1146-1147 resolves the history's Top/Front/Right rows against active_body(); history_click 1872-1874 calls begin_sketch(plane=...) without a body, and _operation 1335-1338 injects owner(target) or self.active_body(), so an origin-plane sketch lands in the combobox's Body. 3449-3455 derive the Extrude default (New/Add) and merge list from the sketch's owner. Did not hold: the reproduction. start_sketch 3205-3210 inspects the current selection first and starts the sketch immediately on a selected Face with body=owner, so 'click Part 2's face, Shift+S, pick Top' never shows a Top choice; in placement mode a face click goes through choose_support 3251-3259 with body=owner too. The wrong-part outcome only arises when the user takes Top/Front/Right from the history (or create_plane 2293-2294) while the combobox names another part. Because Bodies normally sit at identity, Part 1's Top and Part 2's Top coincide geometrically, so the consequence is a defaults mismatch (Extrude opens on Add into Part 1 with Part 1 in the merge list) that the Extrude dialog's operation and scope controls can correct, not a feature in the wrong part. The sharper weakness is that the single 'Origin' group in the history and the placement help (3232 'Top, Front or Right in the history') never say whose planes they are. PLAN.md P2 (85-89) already records 'History, rollback and active part need clearer relationships', and HISTORY_LIFECYCLE.md:43 documents a prior bug from the same coupling.
findings.refute_evidence: ui.py:1364 makes a newly created part active after a 'New' result and 1670 restores the previous choice on refresh, so the combobox does follow creation; it only ignores viewport selection. The bridge is unaffected: create_sketch/create_plane take an explicit body (core._body raises ambiguous_body otherwise).

judge.kurt_would_notice: Barely. He knows the FreeCAD active-Body rule and passes body explicitly in bridge calls; in the GUI he would at most find the bare 'Body' dropdown odd.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape and SolidWorks have no 'active part'; an unlabeled dropdown under Parts reads as a filter. With two parts they would sketch on 'Top' expecting Part 2, then find Extrude defaulting to Add on Part 1 and have to change the scope by hand, without understanding why.
judge.risk: Low. Captioning the chooser, naming the part in the Origin group and placement help, and a 'Make active' context action are presentational; accent-colored origin planes reuse the existing PlaneHighlight path.

findings.title: Shift+H and Shift+Y reveal hidden hole-helper sketches and internal tool Bodies until the next operation (Isolate does not)
findings.lines: 3892-3898 (toggle_sketches), 3918-3922 (show_hidden part-studio branch); isolate 4183-4187 iterates raw objects but does not expose helpers
findings.evidence: toggle_sketches sets Visibility on every Sketcher::SketchObject; show_hidden on every sketch and Body/Tip; isolate on every Sketcher::/PartDesign:: object; none filters KurtShapeInternal, KurtShapeHoleHelper or KurtShapeUseOwner binders (hole_tools.py:217-223 marks hole bridge profiles internal).
findings.scenario: Press Shift+H to see all sketches on a part that has a bridge-created Hole or cross-body Use references.
findings.consequence: Hidden helper sketches/binders appear as extra geometry the user did not draw, can be selected, and stay visible until the next studio reconcile hides them again.
findings.reproduction: Headless: build a hole via the typed op on a sketch in another Body; GUI: Shift+Y.
findings.proposed_change: Filter with a shared predicate (not getattr(obj,'KurtShapeInternal',False) and not KurtShapeHoleHelper and not studio neutral results) in all three callbacks; for isolate, operate on current parts instead of raw objects.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: Native/GUI check: after Shift+Y no object with KurtShapeInternal is visible.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read src/kurtshape/ui.py toggle_sketches (3892-3898), show_hidden (3910-3922), isolate (4172-4188), refresh (1630+), plus hole_tools.py _internal/_bridge_profile (217-243), studio.py hide_internal/_show_bodies/reconcile (711-781), bodies.py bodies() (6-10), sketch_tools.py unconsumed_sketches (7-14), studio.py _eligible/order (176-186), docs/ONSHAPE_SHORTCUTS.md (Shift+H row 64, Shift+I row 82, Shift+Y row 104). HELD: toggle_sketches sets Visibility on every Sketcher::SketchObject with no KurtShapeInternal/KurtShapeHoleHelper filter; the Hole op (commit 1f0001e, at HEAD) creates its bridge profile as a Sketcher::SketchObject inside the user's Body marked internal and hidden (hole_tools.py 242-243, 217-222), so Shift+H reveals it. show_hidden's part-studio branch shows every sketch plus every Body and Body.Tip from bodies(), and bodies() does not filter KurtShapeInternal, so Shift+Y also reveals internal tool/boolean Bodies and their Tips (studio.py 1037-1043, modeling_geometry.py 527) as phantom solids overlapping the part; this is worse than the finder stated. refresh() never calls hide_internal; hide_internal only runs from reconcile/present (studio.py 723, 764), so the exposure persists until the next operation, as claimed. studio.order/_eligible excludes KurtShapeInternal objects, so the revealed helpers have no history row ('geometry the user did not draw'). sketch_owners() (ui.py 1133) and unconsumed_sketches already filter KurtShapeInternal, so the fix has in-repo precedent, and the assembly branch of show_hidden already restricts itself to instances (tools/assembly-gui-validation.FCMacro:262 verifies Shift+Y exposes nothing embedded in assemblies; no equivalent part-studio check exists; no test references toggle_sketches/show_hidden/isolate). DID NOT HOLD: the isolate claim is overstated. isolate only sets Visibility = (name in selection) on unselected objects and later restores the recorded values, so hidden helpers stay hidden and are restored hidden; it never reveals them. The 'cross-body Use references' part of the scenario is also overstated: Use binders are PartDesign::ShapeBinders (sketch_tools.py 284-285), mirror drivers are PartDesign::Plane and direction lines Part::Line, none of which toggle_sketches or show_hidden touch. Not fixed at HEAD (git log -S shows these functions unchanged since baseline b65f066). Severity stays low: visual-only, transient, no data change; the extra Shift+Y phantom-solid case is more confusing than the sketch case but still self-corrects on the next operation.
findings.refute_evidence: bodies.py 6-10 returns KurtShapeInternal Bodies, so show_hidden's `obj == body.Tip or obj == body for body in bodies(doc)` test shows internal boolean/tool Bodies and their Tips (studio.py 1043, modeling_geometry.py 527); studio.hide_internal (studio.py 767-781) is the existing predicate (KurtShapeInternal or neutral Part:: results with KurtShapeStudioOperation) that these callbacks should reuse; isolate has a separate, unverified oddity: selecting a Body (as the Parts list does via part_selection) and pressing Shift+I hides every PartDesign feature including the Tip, so the part itself disappears.

judge.kurt_would_notice: After the new Hole op or a studio boolean, pressing Shift+H or Shift+Y shows extra circles on the sketch plane or a ghost solid overlapping the part that has no history row; it vanishes after his next bridge operation, which looks like nondeterministic display. His running app predates 1f0001e so he has not yet met the hole-helper case, only the internal-Body case.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape/SolidWorks user expects Show hidden to reveal only things they hid; seeing geometry they never drew, selectable in the viewport but absent from the feature list, reads as a corrupt model and erodes trust in the history list.

Reuse studio.hide_internal's predicate in toggle_sketches/show_hidden (keep the assembly branch unchanged); the main risk is over-filtering a user sketch that a studio op marked internal by mistake, so a part-studio GUI check like the assembly macro's Shift+Y assertion should accompany it.

findings.title: Export always proposes 'my-part.step' (and lists the export under Recent projects); closing with an open sketch auto-commits rather than asking
findings.lines: 3185 (export default name), 2980-2981 (unsaved-doc save default), 4273-4276 (Close auto-commit); 2924 is context only
findings.evidence: ui.py:3185 default export path 'my-part.step' regardless of a saved project; 2980 'my-part.FCStd' for an unsaved doc; new() always names the document 'Untitled part' (2924); eventFilter 4273-4276 on QEvent.Close calls finish_sketch() (commit) with no prompt.
findings.scenario: Exporting the osteotome after saving it; closing KurtShape with a half-finished sketch.
findings.consequence: Every export dialog starts from 'my-part.step' and the previous export is overwritten by habit; a draft sketch is committed into the document on close instead of being asked about (recovery would have kept the draft).
findings.reproduction: Save a project as X.FCStd, then Export: filename field shows my-part.step. Open a sketch, close the main window.
findings.proposed_change: Default export name = Path(native_file).stem or state['name'] + '.step'; default save name from the document label; on Close with an active sketch ask Finish / Cancel sketch / Keep working (QMessageBox) before FreeCAD's own save prompt.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: export dialog default equals the project stem; close with an open sketch shows the three-way prompt.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py new (2922-2927), save (2967-2984), export (3179-3188), eventFilter Close branch (4273-4276), finish_sketch (3309-3341), checkpoint_projects/fill_recovery (2843-2875), fill_recent (2707-2714); settings.py grant_destination/remember (33-42); recovery.py capture/close (25-70, 132-136); core.py checkpoint (848-858) and the recover op (1493-1546). All cited line numbers are correct. HELD: export always proposes 'my-part.step' regardless of a saved project (3185); save proposes 'my-part.FCStd' only for a never-saved non-imported document (2980-2981); the Close branch calls finish_sketch() without asking (4273-4276). PARTLY HELD / OVERSTATED: (1) 'overwritten by habit' omits that QFileDialog.getSaveFileName shows the native overwrite confirmation, so it takes an extra click-through; the export directory is remembered via grant_destination->remember so only the filename is wrong. (2) The save-name sub-claim is moot: once saved, Save writes straight to native_file and Save As defaults to the native path, and new() always labels the doc 'Untitled part', so 'default save name from the document label' would only yield 'Untitled part.FCStd'. (3) The close auto-commit is low-stakes: if finish fails the close is refused (event.ignore()), the committed sketch then goes through FreeCAD's normal save-on-close prompt, and the finder's own parenthetical holds: checkpoint_projects runs while a sketch is in edit (it only skips during a live native tool, busy, dialog or mouse-down), recovery.capture stores 'sketch' and 'accepted_sketch', records survive a normal close (recovery.close only drains its executor), and the recover op reopens the draft in edit mode (core.py 1530-1546). Asking Finish/Cancel/Keep working is a reasonable preference but auto-commit is a defensible safe default. Not fixed at HEAD (git log -S 'my-part.step' and 'QEvent.Close' show only baseline b65f066). Net: a real but small polish item; the export-name half is the part with daily friction.
findings.refute_evidence: settings.grant_destination (settings.py 33-37) calls remember(path), which pushes the exported .step path onto recent_projects; fill_recent (ui.py 2707-2714) lists .step/.stp entries, so every STEP export appears in Recent projects and choosing it runs open_path -> import_step, creating a new document from the export rather than reopening the project. Qt's native save dialog confirms overwrites, so a habitual overwrite still requires accepting a prompt.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Every STEP export dialog starts at my-part.step so he retypes the part name each time (or accepts the overwrite prompt), and his Recent projects menu fills with .step exports that re-import as fresh documents when clicked. The close-with-sketch case he would rarely hit and recovery covers it.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape/SolidWorks users expect Export to default to the part's name; a fixed 'my-part' plus exports showing up in Recent projects looks unfinished. Closing with a sketch open and having it silently kept is less surprising to them than losing it would be.
judge.risk: Low. Default export name from Path(native_file).stem or the studio part name, and remember the directory without adding exports to recent_projects; a Close prompt is optional and must not regress the existing refuse-close-on-failed-finish path.

findings.title: Clicking a history row during a Fillet/Chamfer session clears the picked edges' native highlight while the dialog keeps them
findings.lines: ui.py 1879-1880 (history_click -> sync_native_selection), 2494-2516 (capture), 2511-2512 (skip already listed), 2571-2576 (edit-only re-add); history_selection.py 210-215 (not 470-475); feature_panel.py 298-322
findings.evidence: history_click calls history_controller.sync_native_selection() which does Gui.Selection.clearSelection() (history_selection.py:470-475) whenever a history row is clicked outside a sketch; the ReferencePicker keeps references/native_inputs (feature_panel.py:298-323), so the edges stay in the dialog but their native highlight disappears; capture() skips re-adding them (2511-2512).
findings.scenario: While picking fillet edges, Kurt clicks the Fillet's part or the sketch in history to orient himself.
findings.consequence: The viewport no longer shows which edges are in the fillet while the dialog says three are; confirming still fillets the listed edges. Mild trust loss; preview overlay still shows the result.
findings.reproduction: GUI: Shift+F, pick two edges, click a history row: highlight gone, rows remain.
findings.proposed_change: Skip sync_native_selection while self.studio_dialog is set, or re-add picker.native_inputs to Gui.Selection after the sync (as begin() does at 2575-2578).
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: dress-up-edit recipe: after a history click during edge picking, Gui.Selection still contains the picker's native inputs.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py history_click (1866-1884), capture()/cleanup()/begin() in studio_tool (2489-2583), the fillet/chamfer field block (2298-2320), SelectionObserver (110-125), capture_feature_selection (2101-2107); history_selection.py sync_native_selection (210-215; the finder's 470-475 is impossible, the file has 257 lines); feature_panel.py ReferencePicker.add/_remove_rows (298-345); edge_picking.py EdgeGate.allow and ClickFeedback (39-58, 96-123). The mechanism is unconditional in code: history_click resolves the row and, whenever no sketch is in edit, calls sync_native_selection, which does Gui.Selection.clearSelection() then addSelection(obj) for each selected row; there is no self.studio_dialog or edge_picking.active guard. During a fillet/chamfer dialog the EdgeGate rejects anything whose subelement is not 'Edge…' of an eligible solid, so the whole-object re-add of the history row is refused (if FreeCAD applied the gate only to viewport picks, the row object would instead be selected and capture() could flip the dialog's Part combo via fields['part'], 2498-2501; either way the edge highlight is gone). ReferencePicker keeps references/native_inputs, capture() only adds from the current (now empty) selection and skips already-listed inputs (2511-2512), and only the edit path's begin() re-adds native_inputs once at start (2571-2576), so nothing restores the highlight. commit() builds the request from picker.references, so the fillet still applies to the listed edges, matching the finder's consequence. ClickFeedback only reports gate refusals for QOpenGLWidget clicks, so the history click gives no message: silent divergence between dialog and viewport. Re-picking an already-listed edge is a harmless no-op that restores its highlight. No test or GUI recipe covers a history click during a studio dialog (tools/ grep: only assembly-gui-validation.FCMacro calls history_click, in assembly mode). Not fixed at HEAD (f57d592 changed fillet query references, not this path). Upgraded from hypothesis: the path is deterministic from the source, though not exercised at runtime in this review; severity stays low (cosmetic trust loss, no wrong geometry).
findings.refute_evidence: edge_picking.py 39-58: the gate refuses any non-Edge subelement, so sync_native_selection's whole-object addSelection of the clicked row cannot restore anything; edge_picking.py 101-108: refusal feedback is only wired to viewport mouse presses, so the user gets no notice. The same clearSelection also runs for Shell/Move face sessions (fields built at 2298-2300), which have no gate, so there the clicked row's object becomes selected and capture() may switch the Part combo (unverified).

judge.kurt_would_notice: While picking fillet edges he clicks the part or source sketch in the history to orient himself; the green edge highlights vanish although the dialog still lists them and the preview still shows the fillet, so he either re-picks (harmless no-op) or wonders whether the references were dropped.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: SolidWorks keeps the feature tree live during a fillet and preserves the selection; seeing highlights disappear with no message makes them assume the edges were lost and they re-pick or cancel, which slows the first fillet they try.
judge.risk: Low. Either skip sync_native_selection while self.studio_dialog is set, or re-add picker.native_inputs after the sync as begin() does (re-adds pass the edge gate since they are Edge subelements of the eligible target); verify the edit path still highlights existing edges and that Shell/Move face sessions do not switch Part on a history click.

findings.lines: 51-95 (build_entries, merge at 64); src/kurtshape/feature_tools.py:60,77,176-178; src/kurtshape/ui.py:548-555

findings.title: studio_tool is a 470-line method with 15 closures building 14 different dialogs; the GUI Hole is the native dialog, not the typed op
findings.lines: 2120-2590 (studio_tool), 2043-2051 (primary_feature_tool); src/kurtshape/hole_tools.py:3-33, 234-242, 473-474

Then add a `hole` spec so the toolbar Hole uses the typed op (keep the native dialog in More for parity).

findings.title: Per-document UI/controller state that is not keyed or reset: isolate visibility leaks across documents, stale last_failed_attempt after same-UUID reopen, workspace memory keyed by reusable document Name
findings.lines: 4171-4188 (isolate), 810-811 and 1641 (workspace_documents by Name); src/kurtshape/core.py:1021-1048 (attach), 1402 (inspect reports last_failed_attempt)
findings.evidence: `isolate`: `self.isolated_visibility = {}` is a flat dict of object names (4183) restored onto `self.document().getObject(key)` at the next call (4176-4181) regardless of which document is active. `attach` only sets `self.last_failures[id]` when `meta.LastFailure` is truthy (1045-1048) and never pops it, while every failure also stores the in-memory entry (1796); `_inspect` reports `self.last_failures.get(meta.DocumentId)` (1402). `workspace_documents[mode] = doc.Name` (1641) and lookup by Name (810-811); FreeCAD reuses freed document names.
findings.scenario: Isolate a feature in part A (Shift+I), switch to part B (Ctrl+Tab), press Shift+I: B's Sketch/Pad/Body visibility is set from A's saved values and A stays isolated. Open A, hit a rejected op, close A without saving, reopen A from disk: inspect still reports the old last_failed_attempt though the file carries none.
findings.consequence: Visibility corruption Kurt has to repair by hand; agents see a phantom failure after reopen; workspace switching may jump to an unrelated document that inherited a name.
findings.reproduction: Isolate case: GUI recipe with two documents as above. Reopen case: native test: new -> save -> pad with bad length -> close -> open same path -> inspect()["last_failed_attempt"] should be None.
findings.proposed_change: Key `isolated_visibility` by document Name and clear it in tick's document-change branch; in `attach`, `self.last_failures.pop(meta.DocumentId, None)` before loading from meta; key `workspace_documents` by DocumentId (or the observer instance_id).
findings.acceptance: The two tests above plus a Ctrl+Tab/workspace recipe assertion; no change elsewhere.
findings.risk: Low.

findings.title: Resource leftovers without sweep or rotation: stale snapshot archives survive sessions, kurtshape.log is append-only, write grants accumulate
findings.lines: 46-53 (__init__ no sweep), 55-60 (_delete), 135-147 (retire/close); src/kurtshape/preview_worker.py:141-196 (daemon reaper releases pins); src/kurtshape/core.py:1786-1793 (log append); src/kurtshape/settings.py:33-37 (grant_destination)
findings.evidence: runtime/snapshots holds snapshot-ae96b27f...FCStd dated 2026-10-15 19:37 alongside two files from today's 01:28 session (names/dates only were listed); SnapshotStore never scans its directory on construction and deletes only records it created this process; a pinned record is deleted on lease release, which happens on the daemon 'KurtShape-preview-cleanup' thread after process kill/wait, so interpreter exit can skip it. kurtshape.log is opened in append mode with no cap. `grant_destination` adds every Save/Export parent folder to `project_roots` permanently with no UI to review or prune.
findings.scenario: Many sessions over weeks; a crash or kill during a preview; a Save As into an odd folder once.
findings.consequence: Snapshot archives (one full FCStd copy per document per session, 600 KB here, larger for real parts) accumulate silently; a failure storm (see tick finding) grows the log unbounded; bridge write scope widens permanently after any GUI Save As.
findings.reproduction: ls runtime/snapshots (dates older than the current process start); read SnapshotStore.__init__; read settings.json project_roots after a Save As to a new folder.
findings.proposed_change: SnapshotStore.__init__: remove `snapshot-*.FCStd` not referenced by this process (keys are per-process instance ids, so all pre-existing files are stale). Reuse responsiveness.BoundedJsonlWriter's rotation pattern for kurtshape.log (cap size, keep two generations). Show grants in Settings with a Remove button and record grant time; optionally expire grants not used for 30 days.
findings.acceptance: Unit test: constructing a store over a directory containing foreign snapshot files deletes them; log rotation test; Settings dialog lists and prunes grants (GUI recipe). Gate: test_snapshots, theme/settings recipes.
findings.risk: Deleting a snapshot pinned by another live KurtShape instance sharing the same session dir; the README says one normal instance per default session, and private sessions use their own dirs.

findings.title: FreeCAD's own AutoSaver (every 60 s, GUI thread) runs alongside KurtShape recovery; a second writer that bypasses the idle gate and the responsiveness evidence
findings.lines: 4313-4317 (start sets RecoveryEnabled/AutoSaveEnabled/AutoSaveTimeout=1); docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md:118 ('Native recovery/autosave remains enabled at one minute in the app profile'); src/kurtshape/ui.py:2854-2877 (checkpoint_projects idle gate)
findings.evidence: start() forces AutoSaveEnabled=True with a 1-minute timeout and saves the parameter; KurtShape's own recovery is idle-gated, mouse-button-gated and bounded to one capture per pass (2859-2877), while FreeCAD's AutoSaver serializes every modified document on its own timer on the GUI thread; M1_PROGRESS.md:19 lists 'native recomputation/autosave' as unreproduced pause sources.
findings.scenario: Dragging a sketch endpoint or orbiting a large part exactly when the minute timer fires.
findings.consequence: A periodic stall whose size scales with the document, not attributable through KurtShape's monitor (it is not a KurtShape command), and two recovery mechanisms with different retention semantics; FreeCAD's recovery dialog can also appear at startup before KurtShape hides the Start page.
findings.reproduction: Open the 1000-solid fixture, enable the responsiveness stall log, idle-drag for 3 minutes with AutoSaveEnabled on, then off; compare stalls at minute boundaries. Not measured here (concurrent CPU load).
findings.proposed_change: Decide explicitly: either disable native AutoSave while KurtShape recovery is active (keep RecoveryEnabled false too, since its dialog depends on autosave files) and document that KurtShape Recovery is the only path, or raise the timeout and gate it behind the same idle predicate by toggling AutoSaveEnabled from checkpoint_projects. Record the decision in OPERATION_CONTRACT.md:118.
findings.acceptance: Stall-log comparison shows no minute-boundary stalls; review-recovery-crash recipe still recovers drafts; documentation updated.
findings.dependencies: Area on responsiveness may own the measurement.
findings.risk: Losing FreeCAD-native crash recovery for unmanaged documents (setting is global).

findings.title: Runtime assumptions are implicit: no fail-fast version check, deprecated exec_ alongside exec, direct shiboken6 imports, nine independent session-dir computations
findings.lines: 4311-4341 (start); exec_ in ui.py (8 sites), feature_panel.py, general_actions.py (2) vs .exec in shortcuts.py; shiboken6 imported in hover_outline.py, sketch_references.py, theme.py, toolbar_labels.py, ui.py; KURTSHAPE_SESSION_DIR read in core.py:1787, settings.py:10, shortcuts.py:44,91, ui.py:218, responsiveness.py:200 and the three workers

Nothing asserts these at startup; a different FreeCAD on PATH would fail somewhere inside a tick with a traceback into the hidden Report view.
findings.scenario: Kurt launches with a system FreeCAD or a future 1.2 runtime; a contributor runs the FCMacro outside launch-kurtshape.ps1.
findings.consequence: Late, confusing failures instead of one readable message; `exec_` removal in a PySide upgrade would break menus/dialogs in eleven places.
findings.reproduction: Code reading; grep counts above.
findings.proposed_change: Add `runtime_check.py` called first in start(): assert FreeCAD (1,1), OCCT 7.8, PySide6 6.8.x, Python 3.11, Assembly module path; on mismatch show one Messages/status error and refuse to install the panel. findings.acceptance: Unit test for runtime_check with faked versions; grep shows one session-dir computation and zero exec_; startup recipe passes.
findings.risk: Low.

findings.title: Numeric and path validation is implemented four times with different limits and error codes
findings.lines: 53-72 (number: unit-aware, 1e6 limit, invalid_argument), 75-85 (write_path), 1922 (import path check); src/kurtshape/assembly.py:512-526 (_number: 1e7 limit, invalid_assembly_motion), 174 (source path check); src/kurtshape/selectors.py:714-719 (_measure: numbers only, invalid_selector); src/kurtshape/extrusion_preview.py:284-311 (_proposal per-key normalisation); src/kurtshape/modeling_geometry.py:39-41 (wrapper dropping unit)

findings.scenario: An agent sends quantity strings uniformly ('22 mm') across pad, selector filters and assembly moves.
findings.consequence: Inconsistent acceptance and error codes; new ops copy whichever helper is nearest; the preview normaliser must be updated by hand when an op gains a numeric field.
findings.reproduction: Headless: dispatch resolve_selector with radius '22 mm' (invalid_selector) vs pad length '22 mm' (accepted).

findings.acceptance: Unit matrix of inputs x validators; selector parameter tests extended with quantity strings; contract notes the shared rules.
findings.risk: Accepting quantity strings in selectors changes replay digests only for new requests.

findings.title: Exception-handling conventions: 48 broad catches, 26 silent passes, no logging layer, and two semantic fallbacks that silently change intent
findings.lines: 2082-2097 (reference_from_geometry falls back to a literal reference), 772-787 (Messages mirrors the hidden Report view); src/kurtshape/core.py:192-197 (native_intent drops unreadable properties from the revision digest); grep: 48 `except Exception` sites, 26 `except ...: pass` across src
findings.evidence: `reference_from_geometry` wraps selector authoring in `except Exception: pass` (2096-2097) and returns `{feature, subelement}`, so a fillet picked in the GUI may be stored as a literal reference that breaks on regeneration while the user believes a query was authored; `native_intent` skips a property whose getter raises (192-197), so an intermittently failing getter flips the digest (spurious revision rotation) or stable failure hides edits to that property (the preview worker explicitly refuses this tolerance, preview_worker.py:215-228). No `logging`/App.Console wrapper exists; uncaught Qt-slot exceptions reach Messages only through the Report-view mirror, with the unread counter as the sole cue.
findings.scenario: Picking a face whose Surface type is unmapped (torus) in a studio dialog; a third-party object with a failing property.
findings.consequence: Silent downgrade of reference quality; hard-to-diagnose revision churn; developers cannot grep one log API.
findings.reproduction: Pick a toroidal face for shell in the GUI and inspect the stored `selectors` of the feature: literal reference rather than a query.
findings.proposed_change: Add `log.py` (debug/info/warning/error -> App.Console with dedupe and optional file sink); turn semantic fallbacks into explicit outcomes: `reference_from_geometry` notifies 'stored as literal reference' and records the exception; `native_intent` records the failing property name in the digest instead of skipping it (stable but visible). Keep genuinely benign catches (icon lookup, Windows permission retries) but comment why.
findings.acceptance: Grep shows no bare `except Exception: pass` without a comment; test that a failing property appears in native_intent output as {"<unreadable>": name}; dress-up GUI recipe asserts the notification when a literal fallback happens.
findings.risk: Changing native_intent output rotates revisions once for affected documents; acceptable since revisions are session-scoped.

findings.title: GUI-committed actions run three inspections (bridge mutations two) plus a refresh; the two warm inspections are avoidable bookkeeping
findings.lines: ui.py:1326 (pre-op inspect), 1342 (dispatch), 1359 (refresh), 1245-1250 and 1266 (tick re-inspect and the only clear of the refresh flag); core.py:1731 (post-op inspect), 1558-1560 (expected_revision check); document_state.py:86
findings.evidence: ui.py:1326 `self.core.dispatch({'op': 'inspect', ...})` before every non-create op; core.py:1731 `result = self.inspect(doc, measure)` at the end of `_dispatch`; the mutation sets the observer `refresh` flag (document_state.py:86) which only `tick` clears (ui.py:1266), so the next tick fails the early return at 1245 and dispatches another inspect (1250). S10 medians: inspect warm 14.7 ms (Plate60) / 35.2 ms (Studio), changed 38.3 / 222 ms; S11: a warm inspect still deep-copies 124 summaries and reruns `_build_status` (O(objects)).
findings.scenario: Any set_parameter, pad confirm, undo, bridge mutation.
findings.consequence: 30-70 ms of pure bookkeeping per action on the benchmark fixtures, scaling with object count (two warm inspections are avoidable; the changed one is needed); on the Studio fixture this is a visible share of the 963 ms non-native overhead.
findings.reproduction: bench-gui with a counter on `core.timings.record('inspection', ...)` per `Panel.operation`: expect 3 samples per set_parameter today.
findings.proposed_change: In `_operation`, skip the pre-op inspect when `self.state['revision'] == core._meta(doc).Revision` and not `core.needs_refresh(doc)` (the controller re-validates `expected_revision`); after the op's own `refresh()`, set `observer.state(doc)['refresh'] = False` when `self.state['revision']` equals the document revision so `tick` does not re-inspect; keep the tick path for external native edits.
findings.dependencies: None; GUI recipes assert state freshness.
findings.risk: Missing an external native edit between op and tick — mitigated because native edits bump change_serial/refresh after the flag is cleared.
findings.acceptance: One `inspection` event per committed GUI action in bench-gui (two when the op itself needs the pre-read); tip_edit.inspection_ms in bench_core unchanged; interface/part-studio recipes pass.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read src/kurtshape/ui.py 1175-1300 (tick) and 1291-1400 (_operation), core.py 1424-1500 and 1690-1810 (_dispatch), document_state.py 80-92 (invalidate), core.py 997 (needs_refresh), core.py 1084-1104 (sync). The chain holds exactly as described for GUI-committed actions: _operation dispatches a warm inspect at ui.py:1326 for every non-create op, _dispatch ends with inspect at core.py:1731, the mutation's slotChangedObject -> invalidate sets state['refresh']=True (document_state.py:86), and the only place that clears it is Panel.tick ui.py:1266, so the next tick fails the early return at 1245 and inspects again at 1250 (it normally does not refresh again because revision/status match). git blame: lines 1245/1250/1326 date from 5f91ba2e (2026-10-02), 259a61bc (2026-10-03), 559e034d (2026-10-04); untouched by 24bab02/1f0001e/f57d592, so not fixed at HEAD. Two corrections: (1) bridge mutations bypass _operation (bridge.tick -> controller.dispatch directly), so they run two inspections, not three; (2) the S10 numbers the finder quotes are real (S10-MEASUREMENTS.md: warm 14.69/35.22 ms, changed 38.27/222.17 ms; S11: 124 summary copies and _build_status 4.3-5.8 ms per warm inspect) but the avoidable part is two warm inspections = ~29 ms of a 403 ms Plate tip edit and ~70 ms of a 1156 ms Studio tip edit (6-7%), which is not perceptible as a distinct symptom. Severity medium is inflated; the impact is a single-digit-percent bookkeeping tax that scales O(objects). The proposal is sound in principle: when needs_refresh is False, intent_dirty and native_recomputed are also False (both are only set via invalidate, which sets refresh), and _dispatch re-validates expected_revision at core.py:1558-1560, so skipping the pre-op sync/inspect cannot let a stale revision through.
findings.refute_evidence: grep for the refresh flag across src/kurtshape: set only in document_state.py:86 and ui.py:4251 (sketch mouse release), cleared only in ui.py:1266. The GUI error path adds a fourth inspect at ui.py:1345 on failure. Panel.tick also runs sketch/dress-up/region sync before reaching the inspect, so a processed action's next tick is not just the inspect cost.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Not as a distinct symptom: on his daily parts the two extra warm inspections add tens of milliseconds to a parameter edit that is dominated by native recompute; he would only see it as three 'inspection' samples per action in the diagnostics timings, and as a growing tax on larger parts (warm inspect is O(objects): ~124 summaries at ~14 ms, so a 1000-object part pays ~200 ms of avoidable work per committed edit).
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing attributable; the edit feels as fast or slow as the native rebuild.
judge.risk: Low-moderate. Skipping the pre-op inspect must stay gated on needs_refresh so sync() still rotates the revision after external native edits. Clearing the observer flag must happen right after the dispatch's own inspect (before refresh()/apply_navigation touch view properties), otherwise a derived change made by the refresh itself could stay unreconciled until the next real change.

findings.title: Every dequeued bridge request, including reads and already-cancelled ones, triggers a GUI inspect and full refresh; bridge throughput is capped at one request per 25 ms tick
findings.lines: ui.py:1216-1218 (processed), 1245 (early return requires not processed), 1250 (inspect), 1255-1256 (refresh), 221-223 (25 ms timer), 1178 (no dequeue while busy); bridge.py:16 (timeout), 18 (maxsize 32), 56-64 (request_status bypasses the queue), 76-79 and 90-91 (queue_full -> HTTP 400), 102-118 (one dequeue per tick, True even when cancelled)
findings.evidence: ui.py:1218 `processed = self.bridge.tick()` is True for any request; 1245 `if self.state is not None and not processed and ...: return` so a read request falls through to 1250 `dispatch(inspect)` and 1255 `if processed or ...: self.refresh()`. bridge.py:18 queue maxsize 32 (bursts above 32 get HTTP 400 queue_full), 16 request_timeout 30 s; one `pending.get_nowait()` per tick (104).
findings.scenario: An agent polls `inspect`/`capabilities`/`list_documents` while Kurt models, or scripts a long sequence of small operations.
findings.consequence: Each read costs the GUI thread a warm inspect (15-35 ms on the fixtures) plus a refresh (~10 ms, icons, parameters) in the same 25 ms tick that handles Kurt's input; a 10 Hz poller keeps the GUI 30-50% busy; scripted modeling is capped at 40 requests/s even for trivial reads; a bridge mutation on a big model blocks the GUI exactly like a user action (same `dispatch`).
findings.reproduction: Run tools/assistant_client.py in a loop of 200 `inspect` requests against a private session (projects/dodec-hub/start-session.ps1) while the GUI orbits via QTest; count `Panel.refresh` calls and `event_loop_delay` p95; measure requests/s.
findings.proposed_change: Refresh only when the processed request's op is not in READ_OPS or when revision/build_status/document changed (the existing predicate already covers the latter); drain up to N queued READ_OPS per tick within an ~8 ms budget and leave mutations at one per tick; report `queue_wait_ms` already present.
findings.risk: A read that changes derived state (check_geometry is in READ_OPS and does change geometry_check) must still refresh — keep check_geometry/preview in the refresh set.
findings.acceptance: 100 `inspect` requests cause 0 `Panel.refresh` calls and no `inspection` events beyond the requests themselves; read throughput > 100 req/s; mutation ordering unchanged.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read bridge.py in full (128 lines), ui.py 1175-1270 (tick), 215-230 (25 ms QTimer), core.py 247 (READ_OPS) and 1446-1476 (capabilities/request_status/list_documents early returns), tools/assistant_client.py:17, tests/test_bridge.py 205-225 and 445-461, docs/OPERATION_CONTRACT.md 104-118, EXECUTION.md 525/557 and STATUS_REPORT.md 56 (refresh timings). The mechanics hold exactly: Bridge.tick dequeues at most one request per call (bridge.py:104) and returns True whenever it dequeued anything, including a request already cancelled by its 30 s timeout (107-118; tests/test_bridge.py:459-461 asserts tick() is True with zero controller calls); Panel.tick sets processed from it (ui.py:1218), the early return at 1245 requires 'not processed', so a capabilities/inspect/list_documents/diagnostics read falls through to a GUI-thread inspect at 1250 and 'if processed or ...: self.refresh()' at 1255-1256. Queue maxsize 32 (bridge.py:18) with queue.Full -> HTTP 400 (76-79, 90-91) and request_timeout=30 (16) are as stated. Throughput: one dequeue per 25 ms tick, and zero while core.busy/preparing (1178). What is inflated is the consequence: the '10 Hz poller keeps the GUI 30-50% busy' scenario is hypothetical; tools/assistant_client.py is one-shot, request_status reads are answered on the HTTP thread without entering the queue (bridge.py:56-64, contract line 104), and Kurt's documented workflow is sequential scripted steps, where each read costs one warm inspect (15-35 ms on the fixtures) plus a refresh whose cost is unmeasured on these fixtures (S08 measured 103 ms median per refresh on a 1000-solid fixture after the icon fix, so it can exceed the finder's ~10 ms on big models). The 25 ms floor per request is invisible next to native recompute time. So the design weakness is real and cheap to fix, but its impact on actual use is low; it becomes medium only for a client that polls reads continuously. Not changed by any commit since 2026-10-03 (blame 259a61bc for line 1245).
findings.refute_evidence: capabilities, request_status, diagnostics and list_documents return from _dispatch before touching the active document (core.py:1446-1472), yet still trigger the active document's inspect+refresh in tick. tests/test_bridge.py:459-461 shows a timed-out, never-started request still makes tick() return True, so the Panel refreshes for work that never ran. No bundled client or project script polls reads in a loop (grep of tools/assistant_client.py and projects/dodec-hub).

judge.kurt_would_notice: During an agent-driven build he might feel brief orbit/pan hitches whenever the script issues reads between steps, and a scripted sequence of trivial reads cannot exceed ~40 requests/s; neither registers against native recompute time. He would only see a clear effect if an agent polled inspect continuously while he modelled.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing; the bridge is not part of the Onshape/SolidWorks-style GUI workflow.
judge.risk: Low-moderate. check_geometry is in READ_OPS but changes the inspect's geometry_check field without rotating the revision (status_detail shows 'checked'), and failed mutations update last_failed_attempt without a revision change, so the refresh predicate must compare those fields too, not only revision/build_status/document. Draining several reads per tick must respect core.busy and the tick budget, and keep one mutation per tick so expected_revision semantics do not change.

findings.title: Exact-preview mesh transport is JSON parsed and flattened on the GUI thread at a fixed 0.15 mm deflection; the 8-entry exact cache is bounded by count, so large curved parts cost 0.4-1.8 s per exact result and up to ~2 GB resident
findings.lines: preview_worker.py:113-137 (json.loads at 119); extrusion_preview.py:127-139, 592-594, 664-665, 715-728, 957-960, 1014; hover_outline.py:37-39
findings.evidence: preview_worker.py:119 `json.loads(path.read_text(...))` in the GUI poll; render_mesh caps at 500,000 vertices / 1,000,000 triangles (132-133) with absolute deflection 0.15 mm regardless of model size; overlay builds Python index lists (593); `exact_cache` keeps up to 8 full meshes (957-960). Probe: 3,032 vertices -> 287 KB JSON, json.loads 4.3 ms; linear scaling implies ~50 MB and ~0.7-1 s per result at the cap, and ~0.5 GB for eight cached meshes.
findings.scenario: Exact preview on a large or curved part (fillets, patterns) where 0.15 mm tessellation produces hundreds of thousands of triangles.
findings.consequence: A sub-second GUI stall when each exact result arrives and large resident memory in the GUI process; the Coin upload of a 1M-triangle overlay also stalls.
findings.reproduction: responsiveness-preview recipe on a part with a filleted pattern; read `preview_ipc` and `preview_overlay` timings and GUI process working set across 8 proposals.
findings.proposed_change: Scale display deflection with model diagonal (e.g., 0.0005 x diagonal, min 0.05 mm) as hover_outline already does (hover_outline.py:38-39); transport vertices/triangles as binary float32/int32 files (struct/array) and feed `SoCoordinate3.point.setValues`/`coordIndex.setValues` from flat sequences; bound `exact_cache` by total bytes.
findings.risk: Coarser display mesh is visibly different on small features — keep a minimum deflection.
findings.acceptance: `preview_ipc` p95 < 20 ms and overlay < 50 ms on a 200k-triangle fixture; cache memory bound test; existing mesh-reuse checks pass.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read at HEAD f57d592. src/kurtshape/preview_worker.py:113-137 NativePreviewWorker.poll does json.loads(path.read_text()) and it is driven from DebouncedExtrusionPreview._poll on a 20 ms QTimer (extrusion_preview.py:664-665, 905), i.e. the GUI thread. render_mesh (extrusion_preview.py:127-139, not 127-141) tessellates at an absolute 0.15 mm, discretizes outline edges at 0.15 mm and only refuses above 500,000 vertices / 1,000,000 triangles; it serializes vertices as 3-float tuples. CoinExtrusionOverlay.show flattens the triangle list in Python (592-594) and feeds pivy setValues from Python lists; the exact mesh replaces the already-visible provisional on arrival (_display 715-728). exact_cache keeps up to 8 ExtrusionResult objects each holding the parsed mesh (957-960) and survives idle() for the whole feature-dialog session (clear() at 1014 drops it). hover_outline.py:37-39 already scales deflection by max(diagonal*0.0005, 0.01), so the proposed precedent is real. What held: every cited mechanism. What did not hold: the finder's numbers are underestimates. A pure-Python probe under the bundled pythonw 3.11 (no FreeCAD, scratch only) reproduced the 3k-vertex figure (4.5 ms json.loads vs the finder's 4.3 ms) and showed superlinear growth: 50k verts/100k tris = 5.4 MB JSON, 92 ms loads + 20 ms index flatten, 27 MB resident; 150k/300k = 16.8 MB, 401 + 67 ms, 81 MB; at the cap 500k/1M = 57 MB JSON, 1553 + 214 ms, 269 MB resident per parsed mesh. So a cap-size result freezes the GUI ~1.8 s before the pivy upload (not 0.7-1 s), and eight cached meshes can reach ~2 GB of GUI-process memory (not ~0.5 GB). What is unverified: how often real models reach 100k+ triangles at 0.15 mm absolute deflection; prismatic parts with holes stay well under 50k (<~120 ms stall), so this bites on filleted/patterned/large curved parts only. No test under tests/ exercises preview_too_large or mesh size, and no doc records the JSON transport as a deliberate decision. Not fixed at HEAD (git log for both files: last touched 3df4faa/659b5e7, transport unchanged since cb96ddf).
findings.refute_evidence: Probe script and output: review-scratchpad/verify2/e10_json_probe.py and e10_probe_out2.txt (json.loads timed without tracemalloc; resident size via tracemalloc on a second parse). The 'preview_ipc' and 'preview_overlay' timings (extrusion_preview.py:935, 726) already exist to measure this in a real session. Bridge 'preview' requests use the synchronous clone evaluator, not this worker path.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only in the GUI Extrude/Remove dialog on a big filleted or patterned part: a visible hitch each time the exact ghost lands after the provisional, and the app's working set climbing during a long dialog session. His bridge-driven builds (AGENTS.md path 1/2) never touch this worker path, so scripted modeling is unaffected.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape/SolidWorks previews do not hitch on each parameter edit; on larger parts the exact-ghost stall reads as sluggishness, on small parts nothing.
judge.risk: Scaling deflection with the model diagonal coarsens small features on large parts (0.0005 x 1 m = 0.5 mm); a binary transport must keep the allow_nan=False/identity/sequence validation and update tests/test_snapshot_transport.py, test_extrusion_preview.py and test_preview_worker_leases.py; a bytes bound on exact_cache changes cache-hit behaviour the UI relies on after idle().

findings.title: Stall diagnostics are scoped to Sketcher_Create* tools by design; outside sketching the app retains only ~13 s of event-loop samples and no record of what was running during a stall
findings.lines: responsiveness.py:99-101, 117-143 (124 gate), 160-165, 200-202, 212-222, 302-308; timing.py:10; core.py:1461-1463; ui.py:2879-2888; tests/test_responsiveness.py:56-74; docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/IMPLEMENTATION.md:27
findings.evidence: responsiveness.py:101 `re.fullmatch(r'Sketcher_Create[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}', value)` and 124 `if delay >= self.threshold_ms and stalled_command:` — a 3 s stall during an extrude confirm or recovery capture writes nothing; `event_loop_delay` lands in a 512-sample deque (timing.py:10) = the last 12.8 s at 25 ms; ui.py:2887 `input_to_feedback` is recorded when `refresh()` finishes, not at paint/swap (the Monitor marks `paint_event`/`frame_swapped` separately but only for the active QOpenGLWidget). Native progress-bar event pumping can keep the 25 ms pulse alive during a recompute, so a long native stall may not even appear as event-loop delay. On Kurt's machine `runtime/diagnostics/` does not exist (no record ever written).
findings.scenario: Kurt reports 'it froze for a few seconds' after the fact.
findings.consequence: The lead cannot attribute real-session stalls to recovery capture, commit recompute, STEP admission or sketch fill from the running app; measurement must be reconstructed in recipes.
findings.reproduction: Call `{'op':'diagnostics'}` on a session after a known 2 s stall: event_loop_delay worst shows it only if within the last ~13 s; no stall record exists unless a sketch tool was active.
findings.proposed_change: Record any pulse delay >= 100 ms with the current command (InteractionTrace.current kind/name), active document object count, phase and the last Timings label started (saveCopy/recompute/fingerprint wrappers), into the bounded JSONL writer for all contexts; replace the fixed deque with bounded per-label histograms plus a retained 'worst 32 stalls' list; make `input_to_frame_swapped` the headline latency; expose counts in `diagnostics`.
findings.dependencies: BoundedJsonlWriter already handles disk bounds; tests/test_responsiveness.py.
findings.risk: Privacy of record contents (keep plain values, no paths/labels) as the existing writer does.
findings.acceptance: A GUI recipe injecting a 300 ms sleep inside `Controller._recompute` produces one stall record naming the operation; diagnostics report shows the stall after 60 s of idle ticks.
findings.refute_reasoning: All factual claims hold at HEAD. responsiveness.py:99-101 `command()` accepts only `Sketcher_Create[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}`; pulse() at 117-143 writes a record only when `delay >= threshold_ms and stalled_command` (124), so a 3 s stall during an extrude confirm, recovery capture or STEP admission writes nothing, and the test suite pins that as intended (tests/test_responsiveness.py:56 `..._nonsketch_stalls_create_no_file`). The design doc confirms the deliberate scope: docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/IMPLEMENTATION.md:27 ('Sketch event-loop pauses over 500 ms now produce bounded local diagnostics at runtime/diagnostics/sketch-stalls.jsonl'). timing.py:10 keeps a 512-sample deque per label; the Monitor records `event_loop_delay` every 25 ms pulse (responsiveness.py:212, 222) so the window is ~12.8 s, and the `diagnostics` op (core.py:1461-1463) returns only `timings.report()` medians/p95/worst plus engine and recovery facts, nothing about which command or phase was active. ui.py:2879-2888 records `input_to_feedback` when refresh() finishes and its own comment calls it a legacy metric that is not a presented frame; paint_event/frame_swapped are marked only for the active QOpenGLWidget (responsiveness.py:302-308, 329-334). The live session dir is the repo runtime folder (launch-kurtshape.ps1:5,11,46) and `ls runtime` shows no `diagnostics` directory, so no stall record has ever been written there. One nuance: `input_to_frame_swapped` already exists as a Timings label via InteractionTrace.mark (responsiveness.py:160-165, 308), so making it the headline is a reporting change, not new instrumentation. The native progress-bar event-pumping caveat is plausible (FreeCAD's sequencer processes events during long recomputes) but was not verified here. Classification design_weakness is honest: this is a deliberate, tested scope decision whose cost is diagnosability, not a defect. Severity is lower than medium because nothing the user does is affected; the impact is on how long each 'it froze' report takes to attribute.
findings.refute_evidence: `ls runtime` at HEAD lists ui-refresh-diagnostics and review-startup-diagnostics but no `diagnostics` folder; launch-kurtshape.ps1 sets KURTSHAPE_SESSION_DIR to that runtime folder, so the writer path runtime/diagnostics/sketch-stalls.jsonl has never been created. `diagnostics` op schema: timings.report() + engine + recovery_directory + checkpoint_interval_seconds only.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing while modeling. When he reports 'it froze for a few seconds' after a confirm or a checkpoint, the app has no record he or the lead can read back unless it happened inside a sketch tool within the last ~13 s; the answer has to be reconstructed in recipes.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing; diagnostics are invisible to them.
judge.risk: Low for the app (diagnostics must stay off the modeling thread and bounded, which BoundedJsonlWriter already provides); medium for the tooling, because `timings.report()` consumers (bench harness, tests, Q-batch comparisons) depend on the deque/report shape and would need updating if histograms replace it.

findings.title: A rejected bridge request writes LastFailure into the document without the Modified guard used by every other metadata write
findings.evidence: core.py:1796-1797 `self.last_failures[...] = {"request": request, "error": error, "rejected": True}; self._meta(doc).LastFailure=json.dumps(...)` with no `_modified`/`_restore_modified` around it, whereas 1343-1347 wraps `meta.BuildStatus = status` in exactly that guard and SKETCH_PLANE_CONTRACT.md:43 explains why (property writes set the GUI Modified flag). Probe B3/B4: after a save, `{"op":"save","path":5}` and a bad set_parameter both left meta.LastFailure = the full rejected request JSON (262 bytes) while the revision stayed unchanged.
findings.scenario: Kurt saves, an agent sends one wrong feature name (missing_reference) or a path typo; the title flips to '· Modified', closing the app prompts to save, and the next save persists the rejected request text (including absolute paths) into the FCStd.
findings.consequence: False unsaved marker and a 'did I lose something?' moment; also a minor privacy wart (rejected requests with paths end up inside shared FCStd files).
findings.reproduction: GUI needed: save a part; `python -B tools/assistant_client.py --json '{"op":"set_parameter","feature":"Nope","parameter":"Length","value":1,"document_id":...,"expected_revision":...}'`; observe the title suffix (ui.py:1770-1772). Headless proof of the write: scratch controller_probe.py B3/B4.
findings.proposed_change: Wrap the LastFailure write in `modified = self._modified(doc)` / `self._restore_modified(doc, modified)`; or keep last_failures in memory only and persist LastFailure in `_save` just before saveCopy; set the property status NoModify via `meta.setPropertyStatus('LastFailure','NoModify')` at creation (core.py:88-100).
findings.risk: None; inspect's last_failed_attempt still comes from memory.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe (tools/run_gui_recipe.ps1 interface or a new small one): save -> rejected bridge request -> Gui document Modified is False and the title has no suffix. Native test: LastFailure write leaves revision and intent signature unchanged (already true, keep as gate).

findings.title: Missing required fields and wrong-typed identifiers surface as operation_failed with a Python KeyError/TypeError message, a traceback in kurtshape.log and a persisted LastFailure
findings.evidence: core.py:1499 `path = Path(request["path"]).resolve()`, 1728 `self._save(doc, request["path"])`, 1730 `self._export(doc, request["path"], ...)`: KeyError when absent. `_doc` 1058-1059 `self.documents.get(identifier)` raises TypeError for an unhashable document_id. Probe B3: {op:save} / {op:export} / {op:open} / {op:recover} all -> `operation_failed | 'path'`, kurtshape.log gained tracebacks, and LastFailure recorded the request. ARGS (core.py:253-300) lists allowed fields but there is no required-field table; unknown fields are rejected cleanly (1439-1441).
findings.scenario: An agent omits `path` or sends document_id as a list; it gets 'operation_failed: 'path'' with no hint, the app's log grows a traceback per attempt, and the document's LastFailure changes.
findings.consequence: Opaque errors for the most common scripting mistake; log noise that hides real failures.
findings.reproduction: controller_probe.py B3; or `python -B tools/assistant_client.py --json '{"op":"save","document_id":"...","expected_revision":"..."}'`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `REQUIRED = {'open':{'path'},'recover':{'path'},'save':{'path'},'export':{'path'},'import_step':{'path'},'adopt':{'path'},...}` next to ARGS and check it right after the unknown-field check (1439-1441) raising `invalid_argument` with `missing:[...]`; validate `document_id`/`expected_revision`/`request_id` are strings in `_doc`/dispatch; expose both tables through capabilities (see build-identity finding).
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: Native tests: each op without its required field -> invalid_argument with missing list, no kurtshape.log growth, LastFailure unchanged; unhashable document_id -> unknown_document.

findings.title: Default write roots include the whole CADkz\Codex tree, i.e. the checkout itself (tracked fixtures are writable by the bridge)
findings.lines: 17-18; src/kurtshape/core.py:37-38
findings.evidence: settings.py:18 `self.roots = {root.parent.resolve(), self.project_directory.resolve()}` where root is the kurtshape checkout, so CADkz\Codex (containing the repo, examples/acceptance-plate.FCStd, validation fixtures) is a default root; probe B7 lists it. docs/2026-10-03-claude-review/CODEX_PROMPT.md:164 records the proposal (P1-12: narrow to projects + explicit grants with Revoke) as 'unchanged until Kurt decides'.
