findings.title: Performance checks are opt-in and record-only; the planned switch to --enforce never happened, and the existing rule cannot fail without a target miss confirmed by a second run
findings.lines: tests/test_build_status.py 761-775; tests/perf_fixture.py 106-126; tests/support.py 30-32; run-checks.ps1 27; .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml 78-112; tools/perf/report.py 39-52, 80-81, 116; tools/ci/run-local.ps1 26-28; tools/perf/budgets.json
findings.evidence: test_build_status.py 775 `support.perf_only(self)` skips the four methods unless KURTSHAPE_PERF=1 (support.py 30-32); windows-ci.yml 81 perf job `continue-on-error: true`; tools/perf/budgets.json keeps phase0/phase1 targets with 'open' misses; README 119 'enforcement is opt-in'; docs/long-run/STATUS.md 116-130 lists open targets (changed inspect 41 ms vs 20, first preview 8.1 s vs 50 ms).
findings.scenario: A change doubles inspection cost; run-checks.ps1 passes.
findings.consequence: Performance regressions are discovered by Kurt's hands, not by the gate; the documented targets are honest but unenforced.
findings.reproduction: run-checks.ps1 without -Full: four perf skips; CI perf job cannot fail the workflow.
findings.proposed_change: Keep correctness and timing separate as documented, but add a cheap relative gate: bench_core `--baseline runtime/bench/local-baseline.json --enforce` in run-checks -Full with the existing 1.2x+5 ms rule, and a scheduled CI trend artifact; print the four perf results in the GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY table even when non-blocking.
findings.risk: Noisy machines (this review's runs overlapped with a regression run) produce false alarms; the second-run confirmation rule in budgets.json already mitigates.
findings.acceptance: run-checks -Full fails when a metric exceeds baseline by the configured factor on two consecutive runs; the summary table shows the four timings.
findings.refute_reasoning: Every cited fact holds at HEAD, and the situation is slightly stronger than stated. tests/support.py 30-32 perf_only skips unless KURTSHAPE_PERF=1; tests/test_build_status.py 761-775 (class at 761, setUpClass gate at 765, support.perf_only at 775) applies it to the four methods; run-checks.ps1 27 sets KURTSHAPE_PERF=1 only with -Full. Even under -Full the four methods only record: tests/perf_fixture.py write_report 106-126 stores budget_met/open per metric and asserts nothing on timing (docstring 'Keep absolute misses open; correctness and final paired gates are separate'); test_idle_and_post_change_inspection_budget asserts only correctness, so a doubled inspect cost passes. .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml 78-81 perf job is continue-on-error and its report.py call (110-112) omits --enforce, so the step can only throw on unavailable sections (108); it writes nothing to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (only run_native_tests.step_summary 405-417 does). tools/ci/run-local.ps1 26-28 runs bench_core at 20 holes with no --enforce, and report.py 39-43 / budgets.json minimum_plate_holes=60 means plate budgets are not even evaluated there. README 119 'enforcement is opt-in'; docs/long-run/STATUS.md 114-131 lists open targets (changed inspect 41.166 vs 20 at line 119, first preview 8116.546 vs 50 at line 121). Two corrections to the finder's framing: (1) this was a documented, deliberate staging decision, not an oversight: docs/2026-10-03-claude-review/CODEX_PROMPT.md 653, 943, 2366, 2413 say the perf job is non-blocking 'at first' and --enforce --phase phase0 should be switched on after 5 stable nightly samples, and STATUS.md 131 says 'Use --enforce for future default studio benchmarks'; neither was ever wired into a runner. (2) The proposed fix is weaker than described: report.py 49-52 and 80-81 fail a metric only when it exceeds BOTH its absolute target AND best x1.2+5 ms on two independent runs (--confirm; budgets.json requires_second_run), so 'bench_core --baseline local-baseline.json --enforce' in run-checks -Full still cannot fail on a single run, and a metric inside its absolute target (tip overhead 62 ms vs 150) can double without being flagged at all. A gate that catches the finder's own scenario needs a new relative-only rule, a maintained local baseline on Kurt's machine and a noise policy (STATUS.md 131: 'Initial timings varied broadly'). Also: the manual paired-benchmark process the docs rely on has actually been exercised (Q03 confirmation run, S10 in docs/architecture-responsiveness-upgrade/EXECUTION.md 713-721), so regressions are detected late rather than never, which keeps severity low.

judge.kurt_would_notice: run-checks.ps1 -Full prints no timing status at all; the only trace of a miss is the per-method JSON under the run's evidence/build-status folder. He would notice a regression by feel, as a slower bridge round-trip (tip edit + inspect) or a longer first preview, or at his next manual paired benchmark, never from the gate.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing directly; only the downstream effect if a regression ships and the app feels slower than it did.
judge.risk: Medium. A relative gate on one developer machine is noisy; false failures would get ignored or disable the gate. Keep the two-run confirmation or wide slack, print the four results into the step summary and the run-checks console first (that part is S), and treat hosted perf history as unverified until the GitHub cache actually holds 5 stable samples (HEAD is pushed, but whether the workflow has run was not checked here).

findings.title: Closing a document tab is FreeCAD-native: the native Unsaved-document prompt's Save bypasses KurtShape's staged save, `.recovery.FCStd` sibling, Recent list and project-root grant
findings.lines: ui.py:4273-4276 (only main-window close, sketch leases only); ui.py:496-516 (Document menu has no Close); shortcuts.json (no close binding); ui.py:1231-1243 and 1270-1285 (tick teardown / reset after the document is gone, 25 ms timer at ui.py:223); ui.py:2976-2984 + settings.py:33-43 (Save -> grant_destination -> remember); core.py:2793-2811 (staged save, ZIP check, .recovery.FCStd); general_actions.py:180-191 (_can_switch guards switching only)
findings.evidence: The MDI tab 'x' (visible in every workspace screenshot) and Ctrl+F4 go to FreeCAD, which shows its own 'Unsaved document … Save/Discard/Cancel' box; 'Save' runs the native Document.save/saveAs: no ZIP verification, no .recovery.FCStd, no Recent entry, native default directory, and KurtShape's `Gui…Modified` bookkeeping is skipped. A KurtShape Extrude editor or sketch-placement state open on that document is torn down by tick() only after the document has already been deleted (1242-1243).
findings.scenario: Kurt closes the bracket tab with unsaved changes, answers Save in the FreeCAD prompt, saves to the FreeCAD default folder; later 'Recent projects' does not list it and no .recovery.FCStd exists.
findings.consequence: Two save paths with different guarantees; the one reached from the most natural gesture is the weaker one. Also the only place where FreeCAD's own wording/dialog chrome appears in the everyday journey.
findings.reproduction: GUI: modify a part, click the tab 'x', observe the native prompt; choose Save on an unsaved document and compare with Ctrl+S behaviour (dialog folder, Recent, .recovery.FCStd).
findings.proposed_change: Install an event filter on each QMdiSubWindow (hook `maximize_document_view`/tick where subwindows are enumerated, ui.py:1159-1175) for QEvent.Close: if the document is modified show a KurtShape QMessageBox 'Save changes to <name>?' with Save (-> Panel.save(), then proceed), Don't save, Cancel; cancel KurtShape tasks explicitly before proceeding (`cancel_task`, `studio_dialog.reject`); after our save set `Gui.getDocument(name).Modified = False` so FreeCAD does not prompt again. Alternatively register a Std_CloseActiveDoc override via the shortcut router. Record 'discarded' for finding 7.
findings.risk: medium: must not double-prompt or block FreeCAD's own close while a native task is active; verify with the hidden GUI recipe.
findings.acceptance: GUI recipe: close a modified tab -> KurtShape prompt; Save writes via staged save (file + .recovery.FCStd when overwriting, Recent updated); Don't save closes without prompt from FreeCAD; closing while an Extrude editor is open cancels the editor before the document disappears.
findings.refute_reasoning: The structural claim holds at HEAD f57d592: Panel.eventFilter intercepts only `watched is self.main and QEvent.Close`, and only when a sketch lease is live (ui.py:4273-4276, blame b65f066/5f91ba2e, Oct 2, untouched since); grep of src finds no QMdiSubWindow close filter and no Std_CloseActiveDoc override; the KurtShape Document menu offers New/Open/Export/Recent/Recovery/Adopt/Repair but no Close (ui.py:496-516); shortcuts.json has no close binding, so the tab 'x' (visible in failure.png and reopened-native-assembly.png) and FreeCAD's own Ctrl+F4 reach FreeCAD's Unsaved-document prompt. KurtShape's Save goes through Panel.save -> settings.grant_destination -> remember (ui.py:2976-2984, settings.py:33-43) and Controller._save's staged write + ZIP check + `.recovery.FCStd` sibling (core.py:2793-2811), none of which a native Document.save touches, so the Recent and staged-save deltas are real. Three parts are overstated, which is why this is downgraded rather than confirmed: (1) 'no backups' ignores that FreeCAD's own save keeps .FCBak backups by default and KurtShape never disables CreateBackupFiles (start() only sets RecoveryEnabled/AutoSave, ui.py:4315-4318), so only the passive `.recovery.FCStd` sibling is missing, and KurtShape's Recovery menu does not list those siblings anyway (fill_recovery reads core.recovery.available(), ui.py:2843-2845); (2) 'Gui...Modified bookkeeping is skipped' is moot because a native save clears Modified itself; (3) the 'next tick' teardown is 25 ms (ui.py:223), tick rejects the studio dialog / cancels the task on document change (ui.py:1231-1243) and resets the panel when no document remains (ui.py:1270-1285), and the preview code guards with core._is_open (extrusion_preview.py:265, 979), so no crash or stuck state is evidenced. FreeCAD itself refuses to close a document while a Task dialog (sketch edit) is active, so the sketch-lease case is not exposed either (FreeCAD behaviour, not verified in this repo). Net impact if hit: FreeCAD-worded dialog chrome, a native Save As defaulting to FreeCAD's folder rather than the project directory, no Recent entry, no `.recovery.FCStd` sibling and no project-root grant; nothing is lost. That is a low-severity design weakness, not medium.
findings.refute_evidence: grep of src/kurtshape for QMdiSubWindow|Std_CloseActiveDoc|closeEvent|QEvent.Close: only responsiveness.py:264 (parent lookup) and the main-window filter at ui.py:4273. git log -S'QEvent.Close' on ui.py shows no later close handling. ui.py:4315-4318 sets RecoveryEnabled/AutoSaveEnabled/AutoSaveTimeout only; CreateBackupFiles is untouched, so FreeCAD's native .FCBak backup remains active for native saves. Tests under tests/ only call App.closeDocument directly (test_assembly.py:288-336, test_review_followup.py:363-444); none exercise the GUI close path.

judge.kurt_would_notice: The FreeCAD 'Unsaved document' box when he clicks a tab's x, and that a project saved from it is missing from Recent projects and defaults to FreeCAD's folder rather than CADkz/projects; a path saved that way is not granted as a project root, so a later bridge `save` to a sibling path outside CADkz/Codex or CADkz/projects would be rejected by write_path. He drives saves through the bridge, so he hits this rarely.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: The only FreeCAD-branded dialog in the everyday journey appears on the most natural gesture (closing a tab); its Save opens a native Save As in a different default folder and the project then does not show up under Recent projects. Discard works as expected; no data loss.
judge.risk: A KurtShape close prompt must clear Gui Modified after its own save or FreeCAD's canClose will prompt a second time; it must not interfere with FreeCAD's refusal to close while a Task dialog is active; tab-close filters need registering for subwindows created by New/Open/import/bridge (hook where maximize_document_view enumerates QMdiArea subwindows). Kurt's running app is unaffected until restart.

findings.title: Insert picker leaks internal type names, offers no way to tell solids apart, and has no 'insert all'
findings.lines: ui.py:906-932 (dialog; row text 917-921; single selection, one insert per exec); assembly.py:356-361 (candidates fields), 320-322 (STEP solid labels)
findings.evidence: validation/assembly-step-import/insert-step-solid-picker.png shows 'Dodec pipe mount · Solid 2 · Part::Feature · 1 solid(s)' three times with nothing to distinguish the solids; for FCStd sources the row shows 'PartDesign::Body'. A six-solid STEP requires six Insert → file dialog → picker cycles.
findings.scenario: Kurt inserts the hub STEP and must guess which 'Solid N' is the pipe bar.
findings.consequence: Trial-and-error inserts; FreeCAD type identifiers in a user-facing list.
findings.reproduction: GUI: Assembly -> Insert -> any multi-solid STEP.
findings.proposed_change: assembly.candidates adds `bbox_mm` (BoundBox lengths) and `volume_mm3` from the already-loaded temporary document; the dialog shows 'Solid 2 · 40 × 60 × 80 mm · 73.5 cm³' with 'Body'/'Solid' instead of TypeId; allow multi-selection and an 'Insert all N' button that dispatches sequential insert operations (or one new `insert_assembly_parts` op in a single transaction) and keeps a single undo step.
findings.risk: low
findings.acceptance: Unit test on candidates() payload; GUI check that the picker shows dimensions and no '::'; inserting all three hub solids yields three instances in one go.
findings.refute_reasoning: assembly.candidates returns only id/name/type(TypeId)/solid_count (assembly.py:356-361), STEP solids are labelled '<stem> · Solid N' (assembly.py:320-322), and the picker renders `name · TypeId · N solid(s)` in a default single-selection QListWidget with one insert per dialog (ui.py:906-932; row text at 917-921, blame 10c333ff Oct 2, unchanged). insert-step-solid-picker.png shows 'Dodec pipe mount · Solid 1/2/3 · Part::Feature · 1 solid(s)' with nothing else to distinguish them, and assembly-body-choice-dialog.png shows 'PartDesign::Body' for FCStd sources. The help text explicitly says 'Repeat Insert for another independent instance', so a six-solid STEP is six Insert -> file dialog -> picker cycles. Severity low is right: it is friction and trial-and-error, not incorrect output.
findings.refute_evidence: tests/test_assembly.py:120-122, 340-341, 373-375, 412-413 assert only candidate ids and solid_count, so adding bbox/volume fields is additive. insert_assembly_part already accepts source_id, so the bridge can loop inserts today; the GUI cannot. Each insert re-copies, re-hashes and re-opens the source file in _source_document (assembly.py:304-343).

judge.kurt_would_notice: Little: through the bridge he reads assembly_candidates and loops insert_assembly_part with source_id. In the GUI he would guess which 'Solid N' is the pipe bar and repeat Insert per solid.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: FreeCAD type identifiers in a user-facing list, three identical-looking 'Solid N' rows, and no multi-select or Insert all, unlike Onshape's insert dialog which previews and inserts several parts at once.
judge.risk: Volume on complex STEP solids can be slow in the picker; prefer BoundBox lengths (cheap) and compute volume lazily or skip it. Sequential inserts from a multi-select re-read the source per instance and produce one undo step per insert; a single-transaction 'insert all' op is extra M-scale work with its own tests.

findings.title: Reference-file (unmanaged FCStd) state is explained only by the muted status line; disabled modeling tools give no reason, Ctrl+S silently becomes Adopt, and Adopt proposes a generic filename
findings.lines: ui.py:1753-1754 (status text, only explanation; muted via theme.py:71), 1766-1772 (identity label has no reference marker), 1366-1367 ('Open complete' toast; 1368-1375 add nothing for unmanaged), 3401-3407 (model/assembly actions disabled with ordinary tips; toolbar_labels.py:124-127 shows a reason only via 'kurtshapeHelp'), 2971-2972 + 4197 + shortcuts.json:137 (Ctrl+S routes to adopt), 2994 (default 'adopted-part.FCStd'; core.py:1398 exposes native_file, core.py:1888-1889 rejects the source path), 844-846 / 2132-2133 / 3191-3192 / 3527-3528 / 4037-4038 / 4108-4109 (click-time guards only)
findings.evidence: Opening a plain FreeCAD file yields a document whose entire toolbar is greyed; the only explanation is the bottom-left status text, and the Document menu's 'Adopt copy' tip ('Create an editable copy of the inspected file') is the sole pointer. Save (Ctrl+S) silently becomes Adopt (2971-2972) with a dialog proposing adopted-part.FCStd.
findings.scenario: Kurt opens an FCStd a friend made in FreeCAD; everything is disabled and he does not know why until he reads the status line.
findings.consequence: Mild confusion; the Adopt copy name discards the source name.
findings.reproduction: GUI: Open any FCStd without a KurtShapeProject object.
findings.proposed_change: After an unmanaged open, toast 'Reference file · tools are read-only · Document → Adopt copy to edit' (ui.py:1368 block); set a 'kurtshapeHelp' property/tooltip on disabled modeling actions ('Adopt a copy to edit this reference file'); in Panel.adopt default the filename to `Path(doc.FileName).stem + '-copy.FCStd'` beside the source.
findings.risk: low
findings.acceptance: GUI check: opening an unmanaged file shows the toast and the Adopt dialog proposes '<source>-copy.FCStd'.
findings.refute_reasoning: Every cited line holds at HEAD f57d592 and none of the three newest commits (24bab02, 1f0001e, f57d592) touch this code; git -S dates the 'adopted-part.FCStd' default to 5f91ba2 and the 'Reference file · inspect or adopt a copy' status text to cb96ddf. Verified: (1) ui.py:1753-1754 is the only standing explanation; the label is QLabel#KurtShapeDocumentStatus, muted colour (theme.py:71), word-wrapped, bottom of the left panel, no severity property ever set on it; update_document_identity (ui.py:1766-1772) shows only name + ' · Unsaved/Modified', no reference marker. (2) ui.py:1366-1367 emits 'Open complete' for op='open'; the 1368-1375 follow-ups cover only orphan helpers, rebuild_reason and import_step, so there is no unmanaged-specific toast. (3) ui.py:3401-3407 disables model_actions and assembly_actions when state.managed is false; their tooltips stay the ordinary ones, and the hover label (toolbar_labels.py:124-127) appends a reason only when a 'kurtshapeHelp' property is set, which happens today for one action (ui.py:575). (4) save() at ui.py:2971-2972 returns adopt() for unmanaged documents; Ctrl+S is bound to local.save (shortcuts.json:137, tests/test_shortcuts.py:110) and mapped to self.save (ui.py:4197), so Ctrl+S silently opens the 'Adopt a copy' dialog defaulting to last_directory/'adopted-part.FCStd' (ui.py:2994) although state['native_file'] carries the source path (core.py:1398) and core._adopt already refuses the source path itself (core.py:1888-1889), so a stem+'-copy' default is safe. (5) The click-time guards 'Adopt a copy before editing this reference file.' exist at ui.py:844-846, 2132-2133, 3191-3192, 3527-3528, 4037-4038 and 4108-4109 and fire only from still-enabled entry points (double-click sketch, native commands, context menu). Design intent is documented (README.md:61 'Unmanaged FCStd opens for inspection; Adopt copy creates a managed copy'; docs/2026-10-02-claude-review-follow-up/UPDATE_PLAN.md:117 says to offer Adopt 'after showing supported/unsupported objects', which the GUI only does as an error after clicking Adopt, ui.py:2989-2991). Core adoption semantics are tested (tests/test_review_followup.py:355-391, tests/test_build_status.py:661-704, tests/test_assembly.py:635-647) but no test pins the GUI wording or the default filename. The finder's probe (area-h-assembly/exp_assembly.py, env/exp_assembly.log) never exercised the unmanaged state, so the finding is code-derived, but the code paths are unambiguous. One overstatement: 'entire toolbar greyed' is wrong; Fit/Normal/3D/Show planes are not modeling actions and New/Open/Save/Export stay enabled, so only the modeling tools, Rebuild, Check geometry, More and the assembly bar go grey. Classification design_weakness / low / high is honest as filed.
findings.refute_evidence: Not fixed at HEAD: recent commits touched only selectors, holes and fillet/chamfer references. Modeling-tool greying is partial (view tools and the document bar stay enabled). The bridge path is already explicit: inspect returns managed=false plus an 'operations' list limited to READ_OPS | CREATE_OPS | {adopt} (core.py:1404-1408) and mutations reject with code 'unmanaged_document' (core.py:1555-1556), so this is a GUI-only discoverability gap. No GUI test or recipe asserts the 'Reference file' wording or the adopt default name, so changing them is low-risk.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Rarely through the GUI: he knows the inspect-then-adopt design (he approved the UPDATE_PLAN) and through the bridge he gets managed=false, the restricted operations list and an explicit unmanaged_document error, which is the surface he mostly drives. What he would notice is the nuisance of retyping a filename when Adopt proposes 'adopted-part.FCStd' instead of the source stem, and that Ctrl+S on a reference file pops an Adopt dialog with no toast saying why.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Immediately on opening a plain FreeCAD file: sketch/extrude/assembly tools go grey with no banner or hover reason, the only explanation is a muted status line at the bottom of the left panel, and 'Open complete' suggests everything worked. In Onshape or SolidWorks every opened file is editable, so this reads as a broken install until they find Document → Adopt copy or press Ctrl+S and are surprised by an 'Adopt a copy' dialog proposing a generic name.
judge.risk: Low. Three localized edits: one extra notify after op=='open' when managed is false (ui.py:1368 block); set/clear a 'kurtshapeHelp' property and tooltip on model_actions and assembly_actions inside sync_edit_ui so the hover label and the More-menu tooltips explain the disabled state, remembering to restore the original tip when the document becomes managed or is closed; and derive the adopt default from Path(state['native_file']).stem + '-copy.FCStd' (falls back to the old default when native_file is None), which core already protects against colliding with the source. No test pins the current wording; the only real risk is leaving a stale help text on actions after adoption, which sync_edit_ui already runs after 'adopt' (ui.py:1360-1362) so it is easy to cover.

findings.title: Help button and the 'Repair leftover helpers' entry fall back to the generic cube-and-wrench 'tools' glyph (Recent projects has no icon at all, not the fallback)
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 472-483 (478-479), 505, 512-513, 528-532; src/kurtshape/presentation_icons.py 20-48, 132-150; tools/generate-presentation-icons.py ASSETS (recent at 102, tools at 108)
findings.evidence: bind_tool_menu: 'if menu.menuAction().icon().isNull(): menu.menuAction().setIcon(icon_for(menu.title()))' with title 'Help'; LABEL_ICONS has no 'help' key and resources/icons has no help.svg, so icon_for falls through to 'return _original("tools")'. Experiment table (out/icon_for_resolution.json) lists Help, Recent projects, Repair leftover helpers as fallbacks. validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4, current theme) shows the cube+wrench glyph with a chevron at the Help position (x~1925).
findings.scenario: Looking for help/shortcuts in the document row.
findings.consequence: The one button a new user needs reads as a 'tools' or 'settings' control; two gear-like glyphs sit side by side.
findings.reproduction: Hover the third-from-right button in the document row: label says 'Help', glyph is a cube with a wrench.
findings.proposed_change: Add 'help' (circled question mark), 'recent' is already an asset, 'repair' (wrench on document) to generate-presentation-icons.py ASSETS and LABEL_ICONS; keep 'tools' only as the last-resort fallback.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: icon_for('Help') returns help.svg; design-surface recipe asserts the Help menu action icon cacheKey != tools asset.
findings.refute_reasoning: Help holds: make_toolbars creates QMenu('Help') at ui.py 528 with no icon and bind_tool_menu (472-483) sets icon_for('Help') at 478-479; presentation_icons.LABEL_ICONS (20-48) has no 'help' key, resources/icons has no help.svg, command is None so _command_native returns None, and icon_for falls to _original('tools') at 150. model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4, current theme) shows the cube-and-wrench glyph with a chevron immediately left of the Settings gear. 'Repair leftover helpers' holds too: self.tool(document_menu, ...) at 512-513 goes through tool_icon -> icon_for with no mapping. 'Recent projects' does NOT hold: the submenu is created at 505 and added with document_menu.addMenu(recent) with no icon set at all, and fill_recent (2706-2714) never sets one, so it shows no glyph rather than the tools glyph; the finder's claim came from its own icon_for('Recent projects') experiment table (docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/icon-audit/icon_for_resolution.json), not from the UI. The fallback is documented as being for 'rare unmapped commands' (presentation_icons.py 133-137), so using it for a primary document-row button is a genuine defect. Unchanged since 4681ddf; not fixed at HEAD. Severity low is right.
findings.refute_evidence: LABEL_ICONS already maps 'shortcuts', 'example', 'recent' and 'recovery', so the Help submenu's children have icons while the Help trigger itself does not. tools/generate-presentation-icons.py already defines a 'recent' asset (line 102) that is never attached to the Recent projects submenu.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Hardly; he opens shortcut help with Shift+/ and knows what the buttons do, though two gear-like glyphs side by side in the document row look odd.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Looking for a '?' they see a cube-and-wrench next to a gear and may read it as a second settings/tools control, delaying their discovery of the shortcut help.
judge.risk: Very low: add 'help' and 'repair' SVG assets to generate-presentation-icons.py, map them in LABEL_ICONS, optionally setIcon(icon_for('recent')) on the Recent submenu; regenerate icons and refresh the contact sheet.

findings.title: Document tabs leak FreeCAD MDI titles (': 1*') and a red close glyph
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/theme.py 137-139 (QTabBar rules), apply_theme (clears the native stylesheet, sets Fusion); ui.py 1756, 1828 (main window title only), 1766-1772 (document-row Unsaved/Modified marker)
findings.evidence: Only QTabBar::tab colors are styled; close buttons and titles are native. model-workspace-1440.png: tabs read 'Untitled part : 1*' and 'Design acceptance plate : 1*' with a red X on the active tab while the document row already says '· Unsaved'. refresh sets only main.setWindowTitle (1756).
findings.scenario: Two or more open documents.
findings.consequence: Tabs show view numbers and a star that duplicate the document row, plus the only saturated red in the shell on a non-destructive control.
findings.reproduction: Open two documents; read the tab strip.
findings.proposed_change: Style QTabBar::close-button { image: url(resources/icons/cancel.svg) } with hover state; install an event filter on QMdiSubWindow WindowTitleChange that rewrites ' : N' and '*' to the document label (hypothesis: FreeCAD MDIView::onRelabel re-applies, so rewrite in the filter rather than once); or leave the star and drop the suffix in the document row to avoid duplication.
findings.risk: Fighting native title updates; verify no flicker.
findings.acceptance: Tab text == document label (+ ' *' at most); no red close icon in a 1440 capture.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read theme.py: the only QTabBar rules are 137-139 (tab colours, selected accent underline, disabled); there is no QTabBar::close-button rule. apply_theme clears FreeCAD's generated stylesheet (main.setStyleSheet('')), installs KurtShape's own and sets Fusion, so the close glyph is Qt's common-style default (normal red X on the selected tab, disabled gray on others), which is exactly what model-workspace-1440.png (Oct 4) shows next to 'Untitled part : 1*' and 'Design acceptance plate : 1*'. Searched src/kurtshape for setWindowTitle/setTabText/tabBar: only the main window title is set (ui.py 1756, 1828) plus dialogs; nothing touches QMdiSubWindow titles, so the tab text is FreeCAD's 'Label : viewNumber[*]'. update_document_identity (1766-1772) already renders '· Unsaved' / '· Modified' in the document row, so the star duplicates it. Nothing in the log through f57d592 changes this, and DESIGN.md 240 ('Local document tabs use an accent active indicator and native local-file identity') shows the native title was accepted knowingly, which is why design_weakness is the honest class. The finder's severity (low) and effort stand for the stylesheet part; rewriting titles is the part that needs verification because FreeCAD re-applies them on relabel and activation.
findings.refute_evidence: grep over src/kurtshape for setWindowTitle finds only the main window and dialogs; no QMdiSubWindow or tab text is set anywhere. DESIGN.md 240 and the onshape-design-audit plan (docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md 113, 152) describe the tab strip without specifying its text, so the ' : 1' view number and the star were never designed, only inherited.

judge.kurt_would_notice: He sees ': 1*' and the red X in every session and reads it as leftover FreeCAD, but it costs him nothing; the star is in fact the only unsaved cue visible when the document row is elided, so dropping it without a replacement would be a regression for him.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape user would read ' : 1' as an instance or version count and the saturated red X as a destructive control; it is the one place the shell visibly stops being KurtShape.
judge.risk: Low for a QTabBar::close-button stylesheet and for removing one of the two unsaved markers; medium if sub-window titles are rewritten, because FreeCAD's MDIView re-sets the title on relabel and activation, so a WindowTitleChange event filter is needed and must be verified against document switching and the Start page close at ui.py 4337-4340.

findings.lines: src/kurtshape/theme.py 95-99 (indicator/padding and inert ::menu-button rules), 163, 179; src/kurtshape/ui.py 472-481 (bind_tool_menu, setPopupMode at 477), callers 466/499/532/568; feature_panel.py 252
findings.evidence: 'QToolButton::menu-indicator { subcontrol-position: right bottom; } QToolButton[popupMode="1"] { padding-right: 20px; }' but bind_tool_menu uses 'button.setPopupMode(QtGui.QToolButton.InstantPopup)' (value 2), so no menu button gets the padding and the indicator is drawn inside the 4 px padding over the glyph's corner. model-workspace-1440.png: hamburger, Help, More, and in sketch-editor-1440.png the Geometry/Constraints/Edit triggers show a chevron tucked under the bottom-right of the symbol.
findings.scenario: Any menu trigger in the toolbars.
findings.consequence: Menu buttons look cramped and inconsistent with the proposed layout's clean chevron spacing.
findings.reproduction: Zoom the toolbar: chevrons touch the glyphs.
findings.proposed_change: Use QToolButton[popupMode="2"] { padding-right: 12px; } and ::menu-indicator { subcontrol-position: right center; width: 8px; height: 5px; } (arrow image already supplied by _native_arrow_stylesheet).
findings.risk: Toolbar grows ~8 px per menu button; overflow recipe at 800 px still passes.
findings.acceptance: Design-surface capture shows chevrons right of the glyph with >= 2 px clearance.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read src/kurtshape/theme.py 85-100 and 160-191 and ui.py 430-481 plus every bind_tool_menu caller (466, 499, 532, 568) and feature_panel.py 252. Facts that held: (1) theme.py 96 'QToolButton[popupMode="1"] { padding-right: 20px; }' is the Qt-docs boilerplate for MenuButtonPopup (=1); every production menu trigger is set to InstantPopup (=2) in bind_tool_menu (ui.py 477), and grep finds no MenuButtonPopup anywhere under src/ (only the synthetic split button in tools/theme-validation.FCMacro:172), so the padding rule and the ::menu-button rules at 97-99 are inert in the app. (2) theme.py 95 only restates Qt's default (menu-indicator at bottom-right of the padding box), and the ::menu-arrow image at 179 applies to MenuButtonPopup only, so InstantPopup triggers get the base style's PE_IndicatorArrowDown inside the 4 px padding, over the glyph corner. Line 163 (image:none for KurtShapeReferenceMenu) shows the author knows the indicator draws on InstantPopup buttons. (3) I cropped and 4x-enlarged the Oct 4 captures (validation/onshape-design/model-workspace-1440.png: hamburger and More trigger; sketch-editor-1440.png: Geometry/Constraints/Edit triggers): the arrow sits under the glyph's bottom-right and touches the Geometry glyph's circle, as described. (4) Not fixed at HEAD: git blame shows lines 95-96 unchanged since b65f066 (Oct 2); 4681ddf (Oct 13) only recolored ::menu-button hover/disabled; git diff HEAD on theme.py/ui.py is empty; InstantPopup has been used since b65f066, so the Oct 4 captures reflect current code. What did not fully hold: the causal framing is loose — nothing is 'wrong' in Qt terms (this is the standard Qt/FreeCAD InstantPopup corner arrow); the deviation is from the design target in docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md:42,158,233 ('small chevrons' like Onshape) and proposed-shell-layout.png, which draws chevrons beside the glyph. Line refs are accurate. Classification design_weakness / low is honest.
findings.refute_evidence: Crops saved under scratchpad/verify2 (more-button.png, hamburger.png, sketch-groups.png) from the Oct 4 current-shell captures. validation/onshape-design/model-workspace-1024.png shows the model bar already overflowing into a '>>' extension at 1024 px, so any added padding-right pushes one more glyph into overflow. Only six triggers are affected: Document (hamburger), Help, More, and the three sketch groups Geometry/Constraints/Edit (feature_tools.py 181-182).

judge.kurt_would_notice: Almost certainly not: FreeCAD's own toolbars draw the same corner arrow, he has used these triggers since Oct 2, and the bridge path never shows a toolbar. At most a 'slightly cramped' impression when zoomed.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: An Onshape user expects the small chevron beside the icon; the tucked-under arrow (touching the Geometry glyph's circle) reads as cramped and makes it marginally less obvious which buttons open a dropdown, but hover labels and tooltips keep discovery intact.
judge.risk: Low. Two stylesheet lines, but: the [popupMode="2"] attribute selector is evaluated at polish time, which works here only because apply_theme runs before Panel builds the toolbars (ui.py 4318-4322) — any later setPopupMode needs unpolish/polish; +12 px on six triggers nudges one more model-bar glyph into the '>>' overflow at 1024 width; theme.py 163 (hidden indicator on the reference-row menu) must stay; the toolbar hover label anchor should be re-checked. Needs a theme/appearance capture, which this review did not run.

findings.title: Empty new document offers no in-canvas guidance
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/ui.py 2922-2927 (Panel.new), 4329-4335 (start fallback), 629 and 655-690 (footer text lifecycle), 549 and 1679 (existing tooltip hints), 3214-3234 (guidance that appears only after Shift+S); docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md:194
findings.evidence: start() calls panel.new() which shows an axis cross only; startup-origin.png (Oct 6): blank white canvas, 'Features (0)', 'Parts (0)', 'Sketches only · mm', footer 'New complete'. The only hint is the mouse-navigation sentence in the idle footer (629).
findings.scenario: First launch, or after New.
findings.consequence: A professional first impression is a blank page; Kurt (or a collaborator) must know Shift+S and the plane picking rule from the README.
findings.reproduction: Launch the app.
findings.proposed_change: A dismissible QLabel overlay parented to the MDI viewport (hidden once the document has a feature): 'Shift+S to sketch · click Top/Front/Right · Alt+C to search tools', styled with muted ink, plus an 'Example' link; consistent with the proposed layout's quiet canvas caption.
findings.risk: Must not intercept picks: WA_TransparentForMouseEvents.
findings.acceptance: Overlay visible on an empty document, gone after the first sketch, absent in validation captures of modeled parts.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read ui.py start() 4318-4341 and Panel.new 2922-2927: the non-demo path calls panel.new(), which runs the 'new' operation, resets the view and turns on the axis cross only. docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/startup-origin.png (Oct 6, current light shell) shows exactly that: blank white canvas, axis cross, 'Features (0)', 'Parts (0)', 'Sketches only · mm', footer 'New complete'. grep for overlay/caption/empty-state text in src finds nothing, and no module parents a widget to the MDI view for this purpose. git log shows no commit since Oct 6 touching this. So the core claim holds. The finder's evidence sentence is inaccurate in one detail: the mouse-navigation sentence at 629 is not an 'idle' hint — notify() (655-665) replaces it with 'New complete' and restore_status (668-690) then shows 'Local document · mm · ready', so the idle footer carries no sketch hint at all; the hints that do exist are the Sketch button tooltip 'Create sketch · Shift+S' (549), the plane-row tooltip 'select after Shift+S to start a sketch' (1679), Help > Shortcuts/Example (526-528) and the visible 'Search tools… Alt+C' placeholder (71). Also, once Shift+S is pressed the app does guide: editor text 'Click a planar face in the model, or Top, Front or Right in the history. One click starts the sketch.' and footer 'New sketch · select a plane or planar face' (3231-3234). The gap is therefore only the pre-action blank state. Importantly, this is a planned, unimplemented design item: docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md:194 requires 'A blank studio should show a restrained prompt: choose a plane and start a sketch, with the actual shortcut. Keep the canvas mostly empty… Avoid dashboard cards or invented onboarding workflows', and EXECUTION.md (the implementation record) never mentions it. One correction to the proposal's framing: the centered 'Native FreeCAD viewport / Quiet canvas' text in proposed-shell-layout.png is a schematic placeholder for the viewport, not a designed caption; PLAN.md:194 is the real authority, and it argues for a single muted line, not a dismissible card with links. Classification opportunity / low is honest.
findings.refute_evidence: startup-origin.png is dated 2026-10-06 (current shell). No QMdiArea-parented hint widget exists in src (feature_panel.py 124-127, general_actions.py 302, responsiveness.py 208-278 and sketch_cursor.py 76-78 use the MDI area for other purposes). Onshape and SolidWorks also open a blank studio, so the blank canvas is conventional; the design doc still asks for the restrained prompt.

judge.kurt_would_notice: No. He models daily, knows Shift+S and the plane-pick rule, and most of his documents are created through the bridge's 'new' op, where a caption would only flash until the first feature arrives (and must vanish then, or it becomes noise on every new document).
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Mildly. An Onshape/SolidWorks user is used to a blank studio with planes in the tree and finds the Sketch glyph (tooltip 'Create sketch · Shift+S') and the 'Search tools… Alt+C' field without help; the one real stumble, picking a plane after Shift+S, is already explained the moment they press it. A one-line muted caption would shave the first minute, not more.
judge.risk: Low-to-moderate for a small change: an overlay over the Quarter/QOpenGLWidget viewer must be WA_TransparentForMouseEvents or it steals plane/axis-cross picks and hover; it must be per-document (one QMdiSubWindow per tab), hidden during sketch edit, feature editors, Assembly mode and as soon as any feature exists, and re-evaluated on document switch. The finder's fuller variant (dismissible, 'Example' link, remembered dismissal) is closer to M and drifts toward the 'invented onboarding' PLAN.md:194 warns against. Compositing over the GL view should be checked on Kurt's display, which hidden-window captures do not prove.

findings.title: Overlay line widths and FreeCAD's default edge width are unscaled framebuffer pixels, so apparent edge weight varies with display scale
findings.lines: src/kurtshape/hover_outline.py:157; src/kurtshape/extrusion_preview.py:604; src/kurtshape/sketch_references.py:365
findings.evidence: hover_outline.py:157 `style.lineWidth = 2.5`, extrusion_preview.py:604 `style.lineWidth = 2`; fresh defaults View/DefaultShapeLineWidth 2, sketch ViewObject LineWidth 2 / PointSize 4 (exp2c). Coin line width is a GL line width in framebuffer pixels; the 150 % captures (2160 px wide for a 1440 px window) show 2 px edges, i.e. 1.33 logical px, while sketch_snapping.py:45 already treats pick radius as framebuffer pixels and scales it. No code scales any width by devicePixelRatioF.
findings.scenario: Kurt's 150 % monitor vs a 100 % external display or a 200 % laptop.
findings.consequence: Edges look thin and aliased at 150 %, heavy at 100 %, hairline at 200 %; the hover outline's 2.5 px vs model 2 px distinction disappears at high DPI.
findings.reproduction: Compare crop_top_edge_x8.png (2 physical px) with a 100 % capture of the same scene.
findings.proposed_change: Introduce a shared `display_scale()` (devicePixelRatioF of the active view) and multiply overlay widths by it; write View/DefaultShapeLineWidth per DPI bucket at startup (2 at <=125 %, 3 at 150 %, 4 at 200 %) through the preset mechanism; leave sketch widths native unless Kurt asks.
findings.dependencies: Preset mechanism; verify Coin width units on this Qt6 HiDPI path (unverified).
findings.risk: Existing GUI recipes that count pixels (e.g. 625/625 orange interior) are unaffected because they test fills, not lines.
findings.acceptance: At 100/150/200 % the model edge measures ~2 logical px in grabs; hover outline stays ~1.25x the edge width.
findings.refute_reasoning: Core claim holds and is now measured, not just argued. Code: hover_outline.py:157 sets lineWidth 2.5, extrusion_preview.py:604 sets 2, and a third constant the finder missed, sketch_references.py:365, sets 3 (sketch source-edge highlight). grep over src/ shows devicePixelRatioF is used only for pointer-to-framebuffer coordinates (hover_outline.py:233, general_actions.py:313, sketch_references.py:552/585, sketch_snapping.py:231), the pick radius (sketch_snapping.py:45, via begin(pixel_ratio)) and cursor pixmaps; no width is ever multiplied, and KurtShape never writes View/DefaultShapeLineWidth (docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md line 104 confirms the app sets nothing for line widths). Measurement: in validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png (2160x1380, DPR 1.5 per sibling design-surface.json) the vertical model edges are exactly 2 framebuffer px of (25,25,25) at x=722-723 and x=1381-1382, and a run-length histogram over the viewport peaks at 2 with nothing at 1 or 3, so a width-2 edge is 1.33 logical px at 150%; this reproduces the finder's number without their missing crop_top_edge_x8.png / exp2c evidence (neither is in the repo). Corrections: (1) the hover consequence is mischaracterised. In validation/onshape-interaction-pass/view-interaction/face-hover.png (1401x1023 = 934x682 logical x 1.5) every hovered edge profile is 3 px, e.g. x=288-289 black then x=290 blue (41,107,224), y=222 blue then y=223-224 black: 2.5 rasterises to a 3-px line and the model's own 2-px edge wins the overlap, so the hover shows only as a 1-framebuffer-px fringe on one side (0.67 logical px at 150%). The '2.5 vs 2' ratio is not what governs visibility, and the proposed acceptance 'hover stays ~1.25x the edge width' would still yield a 1-px fringe after scaling (4 vs 3) unless the overlay also wins the depth tie. (2) The 'preset mechanism' dependency does not exist at HEAD (no 'preset' in src/); it is the unimplemented Quality-presets proposal in visual-proposals README section 3, which already lists 'DefaultShapeLineWidth 2 (3 at 150 %, 4 at 200 %)', so the finding partly restates a known proposal. (3) The scenario is hypothetical: all 45 recorded validation device_pixel_ratio values are 1.5 and no 100% capture exists; on the one display Kurt is known to use, the effect is 1.33-logical-px edges and a 0.67-logical-px hover fringe. (4) Writing DefaultShapeLineWidth per DPI only affects newly created view providers; LineWidth persists per object in saved documents, so files made at another scale keep their old width. (5) Point sizes were not measured; same glPointSize mechanism is plausible but unverified. This is inherited upstream FreeCAD behaviour, consistent within a display (overlays and model edges share the same framebuffer-pixel units) and inconsistent only across display scales. Classification design_weakness and severity low stand; confidence stays medium because the user-facing impact rests on an unverified multi-display scenario and the hover part needed correcting.
findings.refute_evidence: Measured at DPR 1.5: model edge = 2 framebuffer px (validation/onshape-theme-repair/model-workspace-1440.png, x=722-723 and x=1381-1382, colour (25,25,25)); hover outline renders as a 3-px line whose 2-px overlap is won by the model edge, leaving a 1-px blue (41,107,224) fringe (validation/onshape-interaction-pass/view-interaction/face-hover.png, left edge x=288,289 black / x=290 blue; top edge y=222 blue / y=223,224 black). Third hardcoded width missed by the finder: src/kurtshape/sketch_references.py:365 lineWidth = 3. No preset mechanism in src at HEAD; per-DPI DefaultShapeLineWidth is already proposed in docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md section 3 (line 109) and README line 104 states KurtShape sets nothing for line widths. All 45 validation device_pixel_ratio records are 1.5; no 100% or 200% capture exists in the repo, and the finder's crop_top_edge_x8.png / exp2c are not in the repo.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing today. His only tested display is 150 % (docs/INTERFACE_PASS.md: "The tested display scale is 150%"), so the 2-physical-px (1.33 logical) edges are simply what KurtShape has always looked like to him, and they match stock FreeCAD. When he models through the bridge he never sees the two overlays the finding cites (face hover outline, extrusion preview outline); only native model edges apply, and those are FreeCAD's own DefaultShapeLineWidth behavior. He would notice only if he docks to a 100 % external monitor (every edge, the blue hover outline and the orange/blue extrusion outline become 50 % heavier) or opens the app on a 200 % laptop (edges and the 3-px sketch-reference line in sketch_references.py:365 drop to hairlines, 4-px sketch points become 2 logical px). Even then it reads as "lines a bit thick/thin", not as a malfunction, and picking still works because pick radii are already DPR-scaled.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: On a 150 % display an Onshape/SolidWorks user sees thin, visibly stair-stepped edges (the crop shows no MSAA; src/ writes no View/AntiAliasing) and attributes it to "the FreeCAD look", not to display scale; the width itself is close to Onshape's ~1 CSS-px edges. On a 200 % laptop (Surface/4K, common for newcomers) edges and sketch points become hairline/tiny, which makes sketch vertices harder to see, though snapping and picking remain correct. Nobody would perceive the cross-display inconsistency unless they use two displays with different scale; the aliasing is what they would actually complain about, and width scaling does not fix that.
judge.reasoning: Source confirmed at HEAD f57d592: src\kurtshape\hover_outline.py:157 `style.lineWidth = 2.5`; src\kurtshape\extrusion_preview.py:604 `style.lineWidth = 2`; and an uncited third constant src\kurtshape\sketch_references.py:365 `style.lineWidth = 3`. No lineWidth/PointSize anywhere in src/ is multiplied by a ratio, while devicePixelRatioF is used in six places (hover_outline.py:233, sketch_references.py:190/552/585, sketch_snapping.py:45, general_actions.py:313, ui.py:3293/4063) to convert logical pointer coordinates and pick radii to framebuffer pixels, with sketch_snapping.py:43-44 stating the framebuffer-vs-logical distinction explicitly. The 150 % captures check out: validation/onshape-design/*-1440.png are 2160x1380. The reviewer's crop (scratchpad area-b-viewport/crop_top_edge_x8.png, not in the repo) shows a ~2-physical-px unantialiased edge, consistent with LineWidth 2 being GL framebuffer pixels (DPR scaling would give 3 px). exp2c_result.json shows fresh ViewObject LineWidth 2.0 / PointSize 4.0, matching FreeCAD stock defaults. Classification design_weakness is honest: nothing deviates from FreeCAD's designed behavior (stock FreeCAD has the same framebuffer-pixel widths), so it is not a defect; KurtShape handles the DPI distinction for picking but not for drawing, which is an inconsistency in its own design. The 100 %/200 % consequences are deductive, not observed (docs/onshape-design-audit/PLAN.md:226 lists those scales as untested), which justifies medium confidence; the mechanism itself is near-certain. Severity low is right: purely cosmetic, no blocked workflow, no misleading state, and invisible on a single-scale setup. Two overstatements in the finding: (1) the "2.5 vs 2 px distinction disappears at high DPI" is moot at any DPI, since GL drivers commonly round line widths and the hover outline is distinguished by its blue colour, not by 0.5 px; (2) "aliased" is a separate MSAA issue that width scaling will not change. The proposed_change has a real flaw in its second half: there is no preset mechanism in src/ (only a proposal in docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md section 3), and more importantly DefaultShapeLineWidth is only read when a ViewProvider is constructed and the resulting LineWidth is saved per object in the document, so writing it per DPI bucket at startup bakes the scale into FCStd files, leaves existing objects at the old width (mixed widths in one document), and does not follow a window dragged between monitors of different scale. The overlay half (a shared display_scale() helper applied to the three Coin constants, reading the GL widget's devicePixelRatioF at show time) is genuinely S and low-risk; the model-edge half should be dropped or reworked at M. Effort S therefore applies to the part worth doing. The acceptance criterion as written (edge ~2 logical px at 100/150/200 %) cannot be met via DefaultShapeLineWidth without the document side effects above.
judge.risk: Overlay scaling: low; it touches three constants in GUI-only code paths the bridge never exercises, and existing pixel-count GUI recipes test fills, not lines. Writing View/DefaultShapeLineWidth per DPI bucket: moderate and not recommended as proposed; LineWidth persists per object in GuiDocument.xml, so files would render differently across machines, old and new parts in one document would differ in width, and a window moved between monitors would not follow. Wide GL lines (>1) may be clamped or ignored on core-profile or some Intel/software renderers, so a 4-px request at 200 % could silently degrade; verify with a real GL context, since headless probes report "No valid GL context found".

findings.title: Preset work needs a renderer gate: nothing detects software OpenGL (CI, RDP) or the Intel iGPU, so a future MSAA/fine-tessellation preset would crawl there
findings.lines: launch-kurtshape.ps1 44-54 (launch environment); .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:152 (QT_OPENGL=software)
findings.evidence: The launcher sets no QT_OPENGL and KurtShape never inspects the GL renderer; bin/opengl32sw.dll is bundled and the View.cfg template exposes Preferences/OpenGL/UseSoftwareOpenGL, so a software fallback is possible. exp2b could not create a GL context offscreen ('QOpenGLWidget is not supported on this platform'), so the Python path to GL_RENDERER is unverified.
findings.scenario: Kurt uses RDP, a VM, or a machine where Qt falls back to opengl32sw; or a future preset enables MSAA 8x on an Intel iGPU.
findings.consequence: A presentation preset could turn orbit into a slideshow with no explanation; today the opposite risk is that quality stays at draft everywhere because nothing adapts.
findings.reproduction: Launch with QT_OPENGL=software in a private session (projects/dodec-hub/start-session.ps1 style) and try MSAA 8x in Preferences.
findings.proposed_change: After the first View3DInventor exists, make its QOpenGLWidget current and read glGetString(GL_RENDERER/GL_VENDOR) via QOpenGLContext.currentContext().functions(); if it matches llvmpipe / GDI Generic / Microsoft Basic Render Driver, force the draft preset and show a one-line notice in Settings; cap MSAA at 4x for Intel. Record the renderer string in the Messages log and in export provenance's engine block.
findings.risk: makeCurrent on the viewer widget during startup must not disturb Quarter's context; do it in a QTimer after first paint.
findings.acceptance: Settings shows the detected renderer; forced draft on llvmpipe in the private-session test; no change on a hardware GPU.
findings.refute_reasoning: Facts hold: launch-kurtshape.ps1 sets no QT_OPENGL (env block is lines 44-54, not 48-60; 55-60 is the validation branch), no source inspects the GL renderer (the only OpenGL references are className()=='QOpenGLWidget' checks), bin/opengl32sw.dll is bundled (tools/ci/check-runtime-layout.ps1:7 asserts it) and the View.cfg template exposes OpenGL/UseSoftwareOpenGL. The finder's open question (can Python read GL_RENDERER) is now settled by an earlier verifier's scratch/verify/gl_probe.py: QOpenGLContext + QOffscreenSurface + getProcAddress(glGetString) works under the bundled PySide6 6.8.3, reporting 'Intel(R) RaptorLake-S Mobile Graphics Controller' GL 4.6 by default and 'Gallium 0.4 on llvmpipe' Mesa 12.0.0-rc2 GL 3.0 via opengl32sw.dll with QT_OPENGL=software; so feasibility confidence rises to high. But as a finding it is contingent: today nothing writes anti-aliasing or tessellation above FreeCAD's defaults, so no user is hurt, and the 'quality stays at draft because nothing adapts' half is just B-02/B-03 restated. It is a requirement to build into the preset work, not a standalone medium-severity item; severity low. Two points strengthen it as a gate: .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml:152 runs every GUI recipe with QT_OPENGL=software, so an ungated MSAA default would slow CI, and Kurt's own daily GPU is an Intel iGPU, so the 'cap MSAA at 4x on Intel' clause applies to his machine, not only to RDP/VM scenarios. Nothing at HEAD implements it.
findings.refute_evidence: scratch/verify/gl_probe_default.txt and gl_probe_software.txt (earlier verifier): GL_VENDOR/GL_RENDERER readable from Python; software path loads opengl32sw.dll (llvmpipe, GL 3.0). tools/ci/check-runtime-layout.ps1:7 bundles opengl32sw.dll. Offscreen Qt cannot create a QOpenGLWidget (exp2 outputs), so the detection must be tested with QOpenGLContext+QOffscreenSurface, not a view.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing today. After a presentation preset exists, orbit could stutter at MSAA 8x on his Intel iGPU or in an RDP session with no explanation unless this gate is in place.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing today; only a slideshow viewport in a VM or remote session once presets ship.
judge.risk: Low: a one-time read of the GL strings on the GUI thread after the first view exists, matched against llvmpipe / GDI Generic / Microsoft Basic Render Driver / Intel; must be done with the context current and logged, and must not block startup if the query fails.

findings.title: Sketch region fill: DESIGN.md/README still say light gray (#ebebeb) and apply() comment still says Strict LESS after a558615 switched to blue tint + LEQUAL

findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: Docs, token and code agree; everyday-ui recipe pixel assertion updated to the token.
findings.refute_reasoning: Every factual claim checks out at HEAD f57d592. src/kurtshape/sketch_regions.py:99-100 has COLOR = (0.55, 0.72, 0.95) and TRANSPARENCY = 0.65; line 252 sets SoDepthBuffer.LEQUAL; lines 334-335 in apply() still say "stay on the exact sketch plane. DESIGN.md:164 still says "light gray (#ebebeb) unpickable display fill" and README.md:35 says "light gray interior"; neither was updated by a558615 or the four later commits (5490cb4, 617c537, b2415ff, 5e9824f). No token exists: theme.py COLORS/SKETCH_STATE_COLORS have no region-fill entry and the literal appears only at sketch_regions.py:99. Nothing under tests/ references SketchRegionFill, LEQUAL or the colour, so no test pins the behaviour. Not already solved: docs/EVERYDAY_UI.md:43 and :60-63 correctly document the tint and its Windows 34/34 recipe validation, but that does not fix DESIGN.md, README:35 or the stale comment. Two corrections to the finder's evidence/proposal: (1) the validation/ captures (newest 2026-10-05) predate the Oct 14 change, so their grey fill is expected history, not evidence the current build is grey; (2) tools/everyday-ui-validation.FCMacro:176 already reads panel.sketch_regions.COLOR rather than a literal, and tools/sketch-regions-validation.FCMacro:218-235 already asserts a "translucent blue tint" (its predicate is still named gray), so the acceptance item about the recipe is mostly met. Rendering itself is correct and validated; this is purely a docs/comment/token inconsistency, so design_weakness / low / high confidence stands.
findings.refute_evidence: git show a558615 -- src/kurtshape/sketch_regions.py: "-COLOR = (0.92, 0.92, 0.92)" -> "+COLOR = (0.55, 0.72, 0.95)", "+TRANSPARENCY = 0.65", "-...SoDepthBuffer.LESS" -> "+...SoDepthBuffer.LEQUAL", "+offset = coin.SoPolygonOffset()"; the apply() hunk with "Strict LESS preserves coplanar line pixels" is absent from that diff. git blame -L 333,336 attributes the comment to 4681ddf (kazzurt, 2026-10-13). git show 5e9824f -- DESIGN.md adds the line "Closed defining regions receive a light gray (`#ebebeb`) unpickable display fill" on 2026-10-16. He would only hit this through an agent he directs: one tuning sketch presentation from DESIGN.md would expect #ebebeb grey, and one touching z-fighting would read the line-335 comment ("strict LESS", "exact sketch plane", offset 0.0) and could restore LESS or drop the polygon offset, reintroducing the coplanar-face fight that a558615 fixed. judge.newcomer_would_notice: A newcomer reading README.md:35 ("light gray interior") before first use would then see a blue tint and briefly wonder whether they are in the right build; no functional impact. The tint itself is familiar: Onshape shades closed regions with a faint translucent fill and SolidWorks' shaded sketch contours are a translucent blue-grey, so the on-screen behaviour needs no explanation.
judge.reasoning: The cited lines, commit and doc sentences all exist as described. The disagreement is directly reproducible by reading sketch_regions.py:99-100 against DESIGN.md:164 and README.md:35, and the line-335 comment is a verified stale remnant of the LESS/no-offset era (a558615 changed LESS to LEQUAL and added SoPolygonOffset without touching it). That makes this a verified documentation defect, not a design weakness: the design decision (translucent tint so a region does not read as a hole) was made deliberately and is recorded in EVERYDAY_UI.md:43 and the commit message; the defect is that two living documents and one load-bearing comment were not updated. Severity stays low because there is no user-visible product impact; the only hazard is a maintainer or agent being misled on z-fighting, and the sketch-regions recipe guards that path. User value is low for the same reason. The finding's 'decide the colour' step is unnecessary and the Oct 6 capture date is actually Oct 5; neither changes the verdict.
