Moving the colour into theme.COLORS: small; keep SketchRegionFill.COLOR as the attribute (tools/everyday-ui-validation.FCMacro:176 reads it) or update that recipe, and note that the sketch-regions and everyday-ui GUI recipes only run on Kurt's Windows GUI, so a token refactor stays unverified until he runs run_gui_recipe.ps1 -Recipe sketch-regions.

findings.title: Only the toolbar New command shows the origin axis cross; Open, import, recover and bridge-created documents never do
findings.lines: 2922-2927 (Panel.new); 2942-2961 (open_path); 1255-1263 (bridge-presented documents); 1356-1360 (CREATE_OPS routed through maximize_document_view at 1159-1164); 817 and 881 (direct operation("new") callers)
findings.evidence: `new()` calls navigation.reset_new_document_view() then `Gui.activeDocument().activeView().setAxisCross(True)` (2925-2926); setAxisCross is called nowhere else (grep), View/ShowAxisCross is not written, and the axis cross is viewer state, not saved in the FCStd. Origin planes: App::Origin ViewObject default Visibility False, planes True (exp2c); ui.py:3222-3229 shows them only during placement; toggle_planes (3883-3890) exists. Oct 6 startup-origin.png (new) shows the RGB cross; Oct 4 model-workspace-1440.png (opened example) shows none.
findings.scenario: Kurt starts a new part (cross at origin), opens yesterday's part (no cross, no planes) and loses his bearings in an empty-looking white canvas until he zooms.
findings.consequence: Inconsistent spatial reference between sessions; empty opened sketch-only documents can look blank.
findings.reproduction: New (cross visible) vs Open any FCStd (no cross).
findings.proposed_change: Pick one policy and apply it in both paths (a `prepare_view(view)` helper called from maximize_document_view, which both new and open already route through at ui.py:1259/1358): either always show the small origin triad (setAxisCross True) or rely on the corner coordinate system only; consider Onshape-style faint origin planes visible by default (App::Plane transparency ~80 %) with a Shift+? toggle, decided with Kurt.
findings.risk: A visible cross can be picked by native selection; it is not, but it can occlude small sketches at origin.
findings.acceptance: New and Open produce identical origin presentation; GUI recipe asserts view.hasAxisCross() equality across both paths.
findings.refute_reasoning: The axis-cross half holds by code reading at HEAD f57d592: src/kurtshape/ui.py:2922-2927 Panel.new calls navigation.reset_new_document_view() then Gui.activeDocument().activeView().setAxisCross(True); grep over src/, tests/, tools/, docs/ finds no other setAxisCross/hasAxisCross call and no write of the View/ShowAxisCross preference (also absent from the live profile runtime/user-data/user.cfg and every validation user.cfg). open_path (2942-2961) only calls isometric()+fit(); operation() routes every CREATE_OPS document ({"new","open","recover","import_step"}, core.py:253) through maximize_document_view (ui.py:1159-1164), which only applies the viewer theme and maximizes the MDI window; the bridge-presented path (ui.py:1255-1263, 'processed') only calls activate_body() and navigation.apply_navigation(). docs/SOLIDWORKS_NAVIGATION.md:50-55 states only the New command uses the camera reset and says nothing about the cross; git status shows ui.py clean and the setAxisCross line dates from baseline b65f066, so nothing fixed it. No test asserts the cross (tests/test_navigation.py:42 covers only the camera reset). Two corrections downgrade the finding. (1) The origin-planes half of the title is wrong: planes are hidden identically in both paths and only shown during sketch placement (3222-3229), toggled by toggle_planes (3883-3890) and restored by cancel_placement (3238-3245); there is no new-vs-open difference there. (2) The Oct 4 model-workspace-1440.png is not an 'opened example': tools/design-surface-validation.FCMacro:326 creates that document with panel.operation("new", name="Design acceptance plate") (the screenshot shows 'Unsaved' and 'Extrude complete'), i.e. a created document that bypassed Panel.new. That actually widens the inconsistency: the typed/bridge 'new' (ui.py:1255-1263), the Part Studio fallback (ui.py:817) and create_assembly (ui.py:881) all call self.operation("new") directly and get neither the 100 mm camera reset nor the cross, so the real rule is 'toolbar New only' rather than 'new vs opened'. Startup-origin.png (Oct 6) does confirm the GUI-New cross. Severity stays low: the corner coordinate-system triad is present in both screenshots, so orientation is never fully lost; the cost is an empty-looking canvas for sketch-only or bridge-created documents.
findings.refute_evidence: grep setAxisCross/hasAxisCross/ShowAxisCross: only src/kurtshape/ui.py:2926 in source; validation/onshape-shortcuts-command-probe.json hits are plain workbench command lists (/workbenches/*/commands), not a policy. runtime/user-data/user.cfg (live profile, Oct 17) has 0 ShowAxisCross entries. tools/design-surface-validation.FCMacro:74-78 call() -> panel.operation(op) and :326 call("new", name="Design acceptance plate") produced model-workspace-1440.png (validation/onshape-design and onshape-theme-repair, Oct 4), so that image shows a created, not opened, document. docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/startup-origin.png (Oct 6) shows the RGB cross at origin with planes hidden and the corner triad present. Origin planes: ui.py:3222-3229 show during placement, 3238-3245 restore, 3883-3890 toggle, 4014 and history_selection.py:117 force Origin visible when a plane is shown; identical for new and opened documents. git log -S setAxisCross: introduced in b65f066 (Oct 2 baseline), unchanged through HEAD f57d592.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Barely. His daily path is the bridge, and a bridge `{"op":"new"}` goes through ui.py:1259, which never calls setAxisCross or reset_new_document_view, so he already lives mostly without the triad: a blank white canvas with only the navigation cube and the bottom-right axis indicator until the first feature lands, then F to fit. He might register that GUI New shows a little RGB triad and Open/bridge documents don't, and shrug. The "loses his bearings" scenario is overdrawn: open_path already calls isometric()+fit(), so an opened part is framed; only an empty or sketch-only file lands on a blank canvas, and the corner coordinate system and view cube still give orientation.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Somewhat. Onshape shows faint origin planes and an origin marker in every Part Studio; SolidWorks keeps the origin triad on by default. A newcomer opening a KurtShape file sees neither (planes default hidden, cross absent) and may feel unmoored for a moment, but the Feature history lists Origin/Top/Front/Right, P toggles the planes, and sketch placement shows them. They would more likely ask "where are the planes" than notice the New-vs-Open triad difference.
judge.reasoning: The core observation is verified in code: `Panel.new()` (ui.py:2926) is the sole setAxisCross caller; open_path, import_step, adopt and bridge-created documents never get it, and the cross is per-viewer state that a new document window does not inherit, so New shows the triad and Open does not. Classification as design_weakness is honest: nothing is broken or wrong, the triad was added to give an empty new document something to see (reset_new_document_view docstring), and the gap is that the same courtesy is not extended to other creation paths. Three evidence corrections: (1) model-workspace-1440.png is a macro `panel.operation("new")` document, not an opened example, and a pad on the origin could occlude the depth-tested cross, so that image proves nothing either way; (2) the title's claim that origin planes follow different policies is wrong, planes follow one stored-visibility policy in both paths, only the axis cross diverges; (3) the proposed plane toggle already exists as P on the toolbar. The inconsistency is actually wider than stated (bridge new, import_step, adopt, KURTSHAPE_DEMO open all lack the cross), which strengthens the one-helper fix in maximize_document_view, reached from ui.py:1259 and 1358. Severity low: cosmetic orientation cue, orientation is always available from the view cube and corner axes, and geometry is auto-fitted on open. User value low: neither persona would ask for it, though consistency is cheap. Effort S: a setAxisCross(True) in maximize_document_view (or a prepare_view helper) plus a GUI recipe assert; the Onshape-style faint-planes-by-default idea is a separate preference decision for Kurt that interacts with the placement-mode visibility save/restore at 3222-3229.
judge.risk: Low. The FreeCAD axis cross sits in an SoSkipBoundingGroup, so it does not affect fit, and it is not a ViewProvider, so it cannot be selected. Residual: it is a depth-tested lineWidth-2 node at fixed screen scale, so it can overdraw tiny sketch geometry at the origin and doubles up with the Sketcher's own root-point cross in edit mode; calling it on every document switch is idempotent. Defaulting origin planes visible would be the riskier half: it touches placement-mode plane_visibility snapshot/restore, toggle_planes, and saved-file state, and should be Kurt's call.

findings.title: Save verifies the staged archive (testzip) and copies the recovery file synchronously on the GUI thread; STL and conservative STEP exports run BRepCheck, meshing, sha256 and full measurements synchronously too, a documented and deliberately deferred limitation
findings.lines: core.py:2793-2811, 2813-2853, 1731-1744; ui.py:2968-2984, 3041-3078 (fallback with WaitCursor), 1218-1222 + bridge.py:102-116 (GUI-thread dispatch); recovery.py:64-84 (existing background pattern)
findings.evidence: core.py:2798 `doc.saveCopy(stage)` then 2801-2803 `zipfile.ZipFile(stage).testzip()` (decompresses the whole archive), 2806 `shutil.copy2(path, .recovery.FCStd)` and 2807 `os.replace`; `_export` 2845 `hashlib.sha256(stage.read_bytes())`, 2823 BRepCheck per target (`check(obj, compute=True)`), 2846 `_geometry(..., 'full')` — all before `inspect` (1731) and `Modified=False` (1744).
findings.scenario: Ctrl+S on a large project; STL export; STEP export that falls to the synchronous path (clean metadata, Link sources, assemblies).
findings.consequence: The freeze after Save is saveCopy plus a full decompress-and-CRC pass plus a file copy; for a 50 MB archive that is hundreds of ms of avoidable GUI time; STL export adds a full-model BRepCheck and tessellation synchronously with no painted feedback.
findings.reproduction: Time `command_save` minus `recovery_snapshot_gui`-class saveCopy on Plate60 via bench-gui; patch `zipfile.ZipFile.testzip` with a timer.
findings.proposed_change: Paint 'Saving…' first (S15 pattern); run testzip/sha/copy on the recovery file executor and report completion via the existing poll (keeping saveCopy synchronous); for STL export reuse the STEP child pattern (the STL writer only needs the detached world shapes already serialized in the snapshot).
findings.dependencies: Save contract (success reported only after verification) must remain: report 'Saved' only when the executor finishes; the GUI Modified flag reset moves to that completion.
findings.risk: A failed verification after the user has continued editing — keep the staged file and show an error; the previous file is untouched until replace.
findings.acceptance: `command_save` - saveCopy duration <= 5 ms on Plate60; save/export recipes pass; failure injection into testzip leaves the previous file and shows the error.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read at HEAD. src/kurtshape/core.py:2793-2811 Controller._save: saveCopy to a .saving.FCStd stage (2798), zipfile.testzip over the whole archive (2800-2803), shutil.copy2 of the previous file to .recovery.FCStd (2804-2806), os.replace (2807); all synchronous, no feedback. _export 2813-2853: BRepCheck per target with compute=True (2823), world-shape compound, STL meshing at 0.05 mm / 0.1 rad or exportStep, sha256 over stage.read_bytes() (2845), _geometry(..., 'full') (2846; volume/area/bbox/COM, memoized at core.py:962-979), then the sidecar and pair replacement. inspect runs at 1731 and Modified=False at 1744 only afterwards. Dispatch happens on the GUI thread for both the UI (ui.py:2984 operation('save'), no task_feedback and no wait cursor) and for bridge requests (bridge.py:102-116 tick runs controller.dispatch inside panel.tick, ui.py:1218-1222). The STEP child path exists (prepare_step_export, core.py:531-605) but falls back to the synchronous _export for STL, busy, unmanaged, active transaction, assemblies, no local dependencies, non-valid build, clean (non-Touched) metadata, no targets, App::Link sources and unstable roundtrips (ui.py:3041-3043 _step_export_fallback), matching the finder's list. One inaccuracy: the fallback does show feedback: QApplication.setOverrideCursor(WaitCursor) (ui.py:3061) is applied immediately even though the 'Exporting…' label text is set without a repaint; Save has no feedback at all. Magnitude is an extrapolation, not a measurement: testzip + copy2 on the typical few-MB project is tens of ms and saveCopy dominates; the 'hundreds of ms at 50 MB' claim is plausible but unmeasured, and geometry.check is memoized so the BRepCheck may be a cache hit. Already documented as a deliberately deferred gap: docs/engine-responsiveness-review/REVIEW.md Finding 6 ('Save, import and export also remain synchronous'); docs/architecture-responsiveness-upgrade/EXECUTION.md lines 33, 150, 213, 469, 589-597 ('Keep Save unchanged', 'Explicit Save was not modified', 'STL and conservative contexts retain synchronous fallback'). The recovery module already runs testzip/sha/copy/replace on a one-thread executor (recovery.py:64-84 _publish_cached), so the proposed pattern exists in-tree. tests/test_core.py:60-62 pins the .recovery.FCStd copy but not synchronous timing.
findings.refute_evidence: Both the UI and bridge paths block the GUI, but bridge callers depend on 'save'/'export' replying only after the file is on disk (AGENTS.md flow: save -> export -> BumpMesh consumes the STL; tests/test_core.py:60-66 reads the exported files right after the call). Any off-thread verification must keep that reply contract or add a completion poll.

judge.kurt_would_notice: A short freeze after Ctrl+S or Export that is mostly saveCopy/meshing, which the proposal keeps synchronous anyway; through the bridge his scripts rely on the synchronous reply (save then export then read the STL), so he would not want the bridge semantics changed. Only a very large archive makes the avoidable part visible.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing beyond ordinary desktop-CAD Save/Export hitching; Onshape users miss continuous saving but that is a different feature.
judge.risk: Medium: deferring testzip/copy/replace changes Save's durability contract (ok must still mean the file is verified on disk before Modified=False and before the bridge replies); STL via the STEP child needs the fingerprint/admission machinery (core.py:531-605) extended to STL and assemblies, which the docs excluded on purpose.

findings.title: Monitor.active_view_key walks the active subwindow's widget subtree per frame swap/paint; sketch fills and sketch history re-read placements/visibility on a 0.5 s reconciliation, not per 25 ms tick
findings.lines: responsiveness.py:232-240, 242-250, 302-307, 329-334; sketch_regions.py:304-311 (early return), 331-343 (placement read on presentation passes and the 0.5 s reconcile); sketch_history.py:118-139; ui.py:222-223 (25 ms tick)
findings.evidence: responsiveness.py:246 `for widget in window.findChildren(QtGui.QWidget)` runs in `active_view_key()` which is called from `ui_updated`, `frame_swapped` (306) and every QOpenGLWidget paint event (332) — a widget-tree walk per frame during orbit; sketch_regions.py:333 `sketch.getGlobalPlacement()` for every visible sketch on every 25 ms tick; sketch_history.py:129-139 iterates all objects reading ViewObject.Visibility every 0.5 s while a sketch is edited.
findings.scenario: Orbiting at 60 fps; models with many visible sketches.
findings.consequence: Small but constant input-thread cost (sub-ms per frame today; grows with widget count and visible sketches); not a measured frame drop.
findings.reproduction: bench-gui 'Unchanged idle tick' (0.020 ms for 20 pockets) with 100 visible sketches; time `Monitor.eventFilter` for Paint events during a QTest orbit.
findings.proposed_change: Cache the active view key per QMdiSubWindow (invalidate on subWindowActivated/destroyed) instead of findChildren per event; in sketch_regions compare a cheap placement token only when the observer reported Placement/Group/Tip changes (already tracked via slotChangedObject 189) rather than per tick.
findings.risk: None material.
findings.acceptance: Paint-event filter cost < 20 µs; unchanged idle tick stays <= 0.05 ms with 100 visible sketches.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read at HEAD. responsiveness.py:242-250 Monitor.active_view_key does window.findChildren(QtGui.QWidget) on the active QMdiSubWindow and returns at the first visible QOpenGLWidget; it is called from ui_updated (232-240, only on feedback_complete/notify), frame_swapped (302-307, once per swap) and the eventFilter Paint/Show branch (329-334, only when the watched widget is itself a QOpenGLWidget). That part holds, but the walk covers only the active 3D subwindow's handful of widgets and stops early, so it is sub-ms and does not grow with model size; the finder itself says it is not a measured frame drop. The sketch_regions claim is wrong on frequency: SketchRegionFill.apply (sketch_regions.py:304-311) returns before any sketch loop unless presentation_dirty or membership_dirty, and those are set by observer slots (slotChangedObject 179-189) or by the 0.5 s safety reconciliation (305-310, which also rescans doc.Objects for sketches). sketch.getGlobalPlacement() (331-343) therefore runs for each visible sketch about twice a second and on changes, not on every 25 ms tick (ui.py:222-223 ticks at 25 ms). sketch_history.apply (118-139) does iterate self.desired reading ViewObject.Visibility every 0.5 s while a sketch is edited, as stated. docs/responsive-modeling-upgrade/IMPLEMENTATION.md:55 records the unchanged idle tick at 0.020 ms for 20 pockets; no test or report shows any of this reaching frame time. No change since 4681ddf/a558615. Net: a true but minor micro-optimization with one overstated sub-claim; honest classification is opportunity, not a design weakness.
findings.refute_evidence: bench_gui.FCMacro:57-63 measures tick_idle_ms and the event-filter cost per event (us_per_event_with/without), which is the right place to show any change; nothing here appears in a budget.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing. Orbit cost is dominated by Coin rendering; a sub-ms findChildren on a five-widget subtree and a 2 Hz placement scan are below perception even with many visible sketches.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing.
judge.risk: Low: caching the view key per subwindow must invalidate on subWindowActivated/destroyed and when the QOpenGLWidget is recreated; replacing the 0.5 s reconcile with observer tokens could miss native providers that change display without a property event (the comment at sketch_regions.py:306-307 explains why the reconcile exists).

findings.title: Benchmark harness gaps (all already documented): headless preview phases not exported, studio budget inert under measure=false, regression gate never fails on absolute misses, inert 50 ms synchronous preview target, and no dense/assembly/imported/cold fixtures or input-to-paint budget
findings.lines: bench_core.py:138-161, 335-358, 417-427; report.py:22-32, 44-56; budgets.json:6-39, 41-50; bench_gui.FCMacro:133 (controller_timings dump); responsiveness.py:164-178 (existing input_to_* metrics)
findings.evidence: bench_core.py:335-358 records only first/update totals although `ExtrusionEvaluator.evaluate` records `preview_phase_*` into core.timings (extrusion_preview.py:523-524); report.py:49-52 fails only when `current > target` AND `> best*1.2+5` on two independent runs (an unmet absolute target alone never fails, as REVIEW.md Finding 7 noted); budgets.json studio budget requires measurement_level true and a Q00b-era 160-object baseline, so `--measure false` (the S10 policy) returns 'needs a recorded Q03 median' (report.py:28-32); phase1 `preview_first_ms: 50` targets the synchronous clone evaluator, which the architecture made irrelevant (the async adapter's provisional is the user-facing latency).
findings.scenario: The lead reruns benchmarks on a quiet machine to decide priorities.
findings.consequence: Results cannot attribute preview time to load/model/material, studio budgets silently do not apply, and the only user-facing latency (input to first painted provisional/exact) is not in any budget.
findings.reproduction: Run bench_core.py --fixture studio --measure false and inspect `budgets.reason`; inspect a report's timings keys for preview_phase_*.
findings.proposed_change: Export per-phase medians from captured `preview_phase_*`/`preview_worker_phase_*` events in Benchmark.capture; add fixtures: dense sketch (300 circles), 120-hole plate (archive growth), imported STEP (examples/acceptance-plate.step), assembly (assembly recipe fixture); add a bench-gui metric for `input_to_frame_swapped` and provisional-to-paint; re-baseline budgets at HEAD with `measure=false`; keep 'absolute open' reporting but add an opt-in absolute gate for the user-facing provisional and tick metrics.
findings.risk: None.
findings.acceptance: Reports contain phase medians and the new fixtures; budgets evaluate for both fixtures at measure=false; a documented absolute gate exists for provisional paint latency.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read at HEAD. tools/perf/bench_core.py:335-358 Benchmark.preview returns only preview_first_ms/preview_update_ms and does not use self.capture() (138-161), so the preview_phase_* samples ExtrusionEvaluator records (extrusion_preview.py:523-524) never reach the headless report's timings; bench_gui.FCMacro:133 does dump panel.core.timings.report() as controller_timings, so a GUI run would carry per-phase medians there (partial mitigation the finder missed; budgets still ignore them). report.py:49-52: suspected requires current > target AND current > best*1.2+5, and failed additionally requires an independent confirmation run; an unmet absolute target alone is reported as 'open target' and can never fail, exactly as docs/engine-responsiveness-review/REVIEW.md:83 (Finding 7) already states. budgets.json:6-39 studio policy has measurement_level true and a 160-object Q00b baseline; report.py:22-32 returns 'Studio budget needs a recorded Q03 median for this measurement level' whenever the report's measurement_level differs, so the S10 policy of measure=false (docs/architecture-responsiveness-upgrade/EXECUTION.md:711-717) never evaluates it. phase1 preview_first_ms: 50 targets the synchronous ExtrusionEvaluator; docs/responsive-modeling-upgrade/IMPLEMENTATION.md:57-58 says those diagnostics 'do not measure the new asynchronous adapter's provisional feedback', and measured values are 800-8700 ms (S10-MEASUREMENTS.md:75,94; fable-deep-review/evidence/controller-benchmarks-2026-10-17.md:17), so the budget is inert. The fixture gaps are likewise documented (S10-MEASUREMENTS.md:39: dense-sketch, assemblies, private projects, memory, cold processes, rendering and input-to-paint remain unmeasured). One correction to the proposal: input_to_frame_swapped already exists as a Timings metric from InteractionTrace (responsiveness.py:164-178; tests/test_responsiveness.py:223-230); what is missing is a benchmark that drives real input and a budget for it. Everything holds; it is a correct consolidation of known, documented gaps rather than a new discovery. No change to tools/perf since 559e034.
findings.refute_evidence: REVIEW.md Finding 7 and S10-MEASUREMENTS.md 'Findings and remaining gaps' already list the gate and fixture gaps; this finding adds the concrete report.py/budgets.json line-level causes and the bench_core preview capture omission.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing directly; he does not run tools/perf. Indirectly, priorities set from these reports can misattribute preview time and miss an absolute latency miss, which is a project-steering risk rather than something felt in the app.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing.
judge.risk: Low: tooling only. Re-baselining budgets at HEAD could mask a real regression if done from a noisy run; an absolute gate must stay opt-in so a slower machine does not turn CI red; new fixtures (assembly, imported STEP) need the same hash/fixture manifests the S10 methodology requires.

findings.title: Closed-document entries are never pruned from Controller.documents/signatures/last_failures and orphan snapshot-*.FCStd files from crashed sessions are never swept; selector contexts are already capped at 16 (not a gap)
findings.evidence: core.py:1033 `self.documents[meta.DocumentId] = doc`, 1050 `self.signatures[...]`, 1796 `self.last_failures[...]` are only popped on failure paths; `_prune_closed_sketch_edits` (1078-1082) prunes sketch_edits only, so closed documents' wrappers/strings accumulate per session (small). SnapshotStore has no startup sweep: runtime/snapshots on Kurt's machine holds a 5.7 KB snapshot from Oct 15 19:37 left by an earlier session alongside the current session's files. selectors.py:290/366-371 each `_Context` copies world shapes (`_world_shape` -> `.copy()`), up to 16 contexts per document (49, 1087), invalidated on any domain change but retained while idle — up to 16 copies of every result solid in memory on multi-boundary selector use.
findings.scenario: Multi-day session opening/closing many documents; selector-heavy studio left idle.
findings.consequence: Slow growth of small Python state and leftover snapshot files; transient multi-x geometry memory while idle (not a leak, but unmeasured).
findings.reproduction: Open/close 200 documents via bridge and check `len(core.documents)`; list runtime/snapshots after killing a session; measure working set after resolving selectors at 16 history boundaries.
findings.proposed_change: Pop `documents/signatures/last_failures` in `DocumentState.slotDeletedDocument` (core already receives it, document_state.py:188-200); sweep `snapshots/snapshot-*.FCStd` and worker folders older than the session at Controller init when no live PID owns them; cap `_Context._world_shapes` by total shape count or drop contexts after an idle timeout.

HELD (part 2): SnapshotStore (snapshots.py:45-52) deletes only records it created; close() (142-147) retires only _current; no constructor or Controller-init sweep exists. runtime/snapshots on disk holds snapshot-ae96b27f...FCStd (5,746 bytes, 2026-10-15 19:37) beside two files from the current session (Oct 17 01:28/01:29). Closed entries therefore come only from GUI File-Close of distinct projects; reopening the same project ID overwrites its entry (1021-1033). (b) Every reader of self.documents guards with _is_open (core.py:1465, 1476; ui.py:808, 1244, 2867; general_actions.py:183; step_capture.py:41), so a stale entry cannot raise and costs one App.listDocuments() per iteration; the retained objects are a dead DocumentPy wrapper (the C++ document is freed on close), a sha256 hex signature (incremental_intent.signature) and a small last_failure dict (requests carry file paths, never payloads: _import_step requires an absolute path). Growth is bytes per GUI-closed document. (c) The 'worker folders older than the session' half of the proposed sweep has no observed problem: runtime/exact-preview-workers and runtime/geometry-check-jobs are both empty. (d) The selector-context part is an existing deliberate bound, not a gap: _CONTEXT_LIMIT = 16 (selectors.py:49) with LRU eviction (1083-1090), dropped on any structure/history/topology/placement change (document_index.py:17), and covered by test_part_studio.py:134-136 ('Distinct history consumers cannot retain unbounded native shapes') and test_selector_preparation.py:181/225. _world_shapes is populated lazily: only objects that reach world_shape() through a literal seed (399) or the full-enumeration fallback (359, via rows) are deep-copied (obj.Shape.copy(), 225). judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing in daily modeling. There is no bridge close-document op, so his bridge sessions never grow these dicts at all; only GUI File-Close of distinct projects adds a few bytes each. He would at most spot a stray 5.7 KB snapshot-*.FCStd in runtime/snapshots left by a session that was killed, and only if he browses that folder. No slowdown or memory growth is attributable to any of the three items; the selector-context bound is one he effectively already accepted when 4681ddf landed with its test.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing. No UI surface, message, timing or memory effect is visible; an Onshape/SolidWorks user closing and opening projects through the GUI sees normal behaviour.
judge.risk: Pruning the three dicts in slotDeletedDocument (or extending _prune_closed_sketch_edits) is near-zero risk because every reader already tolerates a missing/closed entry; the one subtlety is attach's duplicate_document_id check (core.py:1021-1024), which must keep working for a reopened copy. A startup sweep of runtime/snapshots carries real risk because the directory is shared by any process that runs without KURTSHAPE_SESSION_DIR (Kurt's app plus a headless Controller or a second session): an unconditional sweep could unlink another live session's pinned snapshot, so it must be age- or PID-owned and must tolerate Windows file locks. Changing the selector-context policy is not recommended without a measurement first; the current cap is tested behaviour.

findings.title: Launcher only checks that freecad.exe exists; runtime layout and versions are verified at install (archive hash) and in CI, not at launch, and engine_stamp omits the engine build hash
findings.lines: launch-kurtshape.ps1 96; install-runtime.ps1 21, 26-28; tools/ci/check-runtime-layout.ps1 7-23; run-checks.ps1 12; core.py 102-103, 1279-1289
findings.evidence: launch-kurtshape.ps1 96: `if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $exePath)) { throw 'Run install-runtime.ps1 first.' }` is the only runtime check; install-runtime.ps1 21 verifies the archive SHA256 then 27 runs `7z x ... -y` over any existing folder, leaving no manifest; tools/ci/check-runtime-layout.ps1 checks five files plus versions but is wired only into CI and tools/ci/run-local.ps1; core.py 102-103 `engine_stamp()` returns ('1.1.4','7.8.1') only, while App.Version() also carries the git hash 4fd3bf320... (headless probe) that is not part of the document stamp.
findings.scenario: A future 'compatible native runtime' with the deferred Sketcher point-color patch (docs/M1_PROGRESS.md 37-44) is extracted over runtime/freecad-1.1.4, or an extraction is interrupted, or a DLL is replaced by an antivirus quarantine.
findings.consequence: The app starts with mixed binaries; documents opened get EngineFreeCAD='1.1.4' as before so `engine_changed` never fires even though the kernel build differs; failures surface as unexplained native crashes rather than a clear 'runtime mismatch' at launch.
findings.reproduction: Source logic is unambiguous (launch-kurtshape.ps1 96; install-runtime.ps1 27). To demonstrate: in a scratch RuntimeRoot copy, delete bin/FreeCAD.pyd and run `launch-kurtshape.ps1 -RuntimeRoot <copy> -PrintOnly` then without -PrintOnly: the launcher proceeds to Start-Process.
findings.proposed_change: install-runtime.ps1: extract into `freecad-1.1.4.extracting-<guid>`, then rename atomically, and write `runtime/freecad-1.1.4/.kurtshape-runtime.json` {archive_sha256, extracted_utc, file_count, total_bytes, freecad_version, git_hash}. launch-kurtshape.ps1: refuse when the manifest is missing or the archive hash differs from the pinned constant, and (cheaply) verify the five layout files plus bin/python311.dll sizes; expose `-SkipRuntimeCheck` for experiments. core.py engine_stamp(): include App.Version()[7] in a new `EngineBuild` property used only for `rebuild_reason` reporting (not for blocking), and show it in capabilities.engine_build.
findings.risk: Adding a hard launch gate could block Kurt if the manifest is absent on the existing install; first release must write the manifest for an already-extracted runtime (a `-Adopt` switch).
findings.acceptance: tools/ci/check_runtime_layout.py reads and validates the manifest; tests/test_runtime_layout.py asserts the manifest's git_hash equals App.Version()[7]; a deliberately corrupted scratch runtime makes the launcher exit non-zero with a one-line reason.
findings.refute_reasoning: Read: launch-kurtshape.ps1 96 (Test-Path on freecad.exe is the only runtime check; confirmed), install-runtime.ps1 16-28 (archive SHA256 pinned and verified at 21, then 7z x -y into runtime/freecad-1.1.4 over whatever exists at 27, no manifest written; confirmed), tools/ci/check-runtime-layout.ps1 (five bin files plus a python probe of versions and Mod/Assembly; wired only in .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml 58 and tools/ci/run-local.ps1 17; run-checks.ps1 12 checks only python.exe exists), core.py 102-103 (engine_stamp = version[:3] + OCC version; confirmed), tests/test_runtime_layout.py (pins 1.1.4/7.8.1 and rejects another version for Assembly only). Probe: App.Version()[3]='20260928 (Git shallow)', [7]=engine git hash. What did not hold: the consequence 'engine_changed never fires even though the kernel build differs' ignores core.py 1281-1289, where _check_engine compares doc.getProgramVersion() with f'{v[0]}.{v[1]}R{v[3]}' and sets RebuildReason='saved_by_other_build' for any document saved by a differently stamped FreeCAD build; OPERATION_CONTRACT.md 29 documents this. A patched runtime built on a different date would therefore be detected on open for existing documents; only a build that reproduces the identical revision string would slip through. The scenarios are speculative: nothing in the repo currently replaces runtime files, docs/M1_PROGRESS.md 37-44 explicitly plans to keep the current portable runtime as a fallback and to 'build and test a separate compatible native runtime before switching the launcher', and an interrupted extraction or AV quarantine of a core DLL would make freecad.exe fail at load rather than run with mixed binaries. The absence of a launch-time integrity check is real and cheap to close, but the stated impact is mostly hypothetical and partly already mitigated, so severity drops to low. Classification remains design_weakness because the missing check is verified; the mixed-binary consequence is a hypothesis.
findings.refute_evidence: core.py 1283-1289: same_build = recorded_version == '1.1R20260928 (Git shallow)'; reason = 'engine_changed' if stored stamp differs else 'saved_by_other_build' if not same_build else 'engine_unrecorded'. tests/test_runtime_layout.py 29-33 proves the Assembly module path rejects a non-1.1.4 version. .github/workflows/windows-ci.yml 56-58 runs install-runtime then check-runtime-layout on every CI run, so a damaged canonical archive would be caught there; only a locally damaged extraction is unguarded.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing in normal use. Only if runtime/freecad-1.1.4 were damaged (interrupted re-extraction, AV quarantine) would he see freecad.exe crash at start or misbehave instead of a one-line 'runtime mismatch, run install-runtime.ps1' message.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Nothing; install-runtime.ps1 plus the launcher work as expected on a clean machine.
judge.risk: Low. A manifest written by install-runtime.ps1 and a cheap size/presence check in the launcher add no modeling risk; a full hash of the 1+ GB runtime at every launch would be too slow, so the check must stay manifest-based, and a -SkipRuntimeCheck escape is needed for experiments with a patched runtime.

findings.title: GUI Insert always re-frames the assembly in isometric fit-all, discarding the current view orientation
findings.lines: ui.py:933-939 (fit + deferred frame_import after insert), 963-966 (frame_import: isometric + fit), 3857-3858 (isometric -> view_isometric_keep_sketch); navigation.py:200-207
findings.evidence: insert_assembly_part reuses the STEP-import helper, which was written to fit a freshly imported document; for an assembly it runs after every occurrence insertion, resetting orientation to isometric and fitting all.
findings.scenario: Kurt orients the assembly to Front to line up a bracket, inserts the next part, and the view jumps back to isometric fit-all; with ten parts this happens ten times.
findings.consequence: Friction on the most repeated assembly action; the deferred fit also fires after the user may already have started orbiting.
findings.reproduction: GUI: Assembly -> Insert twice while in Front view.
findings.proposed_change: In insert_assembly_part drop isometric(): keep the camera, and only `fit()` when the new occurrence's bounding box lies outside the current view (compare `obj.Shape.BoundBox` with the viewer's visible volume) or offer 'zoom to new instance' via general_actions.zoom_to_selection after `select_feature(result['created_feature'])`. Keep frame_import for open_path only.
findings.risk: low
findings.acceptance: GUI check: set Front view, Insert -> camera orientation unchanged; a part inserted far outside the view is still visible (fit triggered). Existing STEP-import fit check unchanged.
findings.refute_reasoning: The code does exactly what the finder says: after a successful insert, Panel.insert_assembly_part calls self.fit() and then defers frame_import (ui.py:933-939); frame_import calls isometric() then fit() (ui.py:963-966); isometric() is navigation.view_isometric_keep_sketch (ui.py:3857-3858), which applies a fixed isometric rotation (navigation.py:200-207). So every GUI Insert reorients to isometric and fits all. git blame puts these lines in 10c333f (2026-10-02, the original assembly commit) and they are unchanged at HEAD, so this was a deliberate reuse of the STEP-import framing rather than a regression. Two qualifications: the finder verified this by reading code only (no runtime run), though the code is unambiguous; and the clause about the deferred fit firing 'after the user may already have started orbiting' is overstated, since QTimer.singleShot(0) runs on the next event-loop pass. Inserts sent over the bridge go through core.dispatch and never touch Panel.insert_assembly_part, so scripted inserts keep the camera. Severity low is right; classification corrected to design_weakness because it is intended behaviour that is wrong for repeated inserts, not a broken code path.
findings.refute_evidence: git blame ui.py:933-939 -> 10c333f 2026-10-02; frame_import itself dates from 565566b (STEP import). docs/assembly-workflow/WORKFLOW.md says nothing about framing on insert.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Only when inserting with the toolbar button: the view jumps to isometric fit-all after each insert. His bridge-driven insert_assembly_part calls do not reframe, so his usual workflow is unaffected.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Onshape and SolidWorks keep the camera when inserting components; lining the assembly up in Front view and having it jump to isometric after every one of ten inserts is visible, repeated friction.
judge.risk: Low. The open question is product behaviour: drop isometric() and keep fit(), fit only when the new occurrence is outside the view, or not fit at all (a new instance lands at the origin, usually already in view). Keep frame_import for open_path/import_step.

refuted.title: Raster grayscale fallbacks may render soft on mixed-DPI desktops while SVG originals stay crisp
refuted.evidence: grayscale_icon builds pixmaps with 'native.pixmap(QtCore.QSize(size,size), mode, Off)' once per icon at the application's device pixel ratio at first use and caches by cacheKey (_native_cache). Originals are SVG QIcons (81-84) and rescale per screen. THEME-REPAIR.md notes Kurt's actual scaling was 150%; startup.py comments mention a mixed-DPI desktop.
refuted.scenario: Dragging the window to a monitor with a different scale, or first use on a 125% screen then moving to 100%.
refuted.consequence: Fallback glyphs (Use, Hole, constraints) would look blurrier than their neighbours, amplifying finding 1.
refuted.reproduction: Verify offscreen: run native_gray.py with QT_SCALE_FACTOR=1.25 then request pixmap(QSize(20,20)) on a QScreen with DPR 1 (or compare availableSizes vs actual pixmap devicePixelRatio); in the app, compare Use vs Pierce on each monitor.
refuted.proposed_change: If confirmed: regenerate the gray cache per devicePixelRatio (key by (cacheKey, dpr)) or move to the alpha-tint renderer from finding 1 using QIconEngine so Qt renders per request.
refuted.acceptance: Pixel diff of a fallback glyph at DPR 1.0 and 1.5 shows no resampling blur.
refuted.refute_reasoning: The cited lines are correct (RASTER_SIZES at src/kurtshape/presentation_icons.py:17, grayscale_icon at 103-118; only one commit, 4681ddf, ever touched the file; no tests under tests/ cover it). The mechanism is only half right and the consequence does not materialise. (1) The bundled runtime is Qt 6.8.3/PySide6 (the finder's own native_gray.log prints "6.8.3"). QIcon.pixmap(QSize, mode, state) without a DPR argument uses qApp.devicePixelRatio(), which Qt documents as the HIGHEST DPR among all connected screens, not the screen the window is on. So the cache is not "built at first use on whatever screen"; its DPR is the desktop maximum regardless of where the window sits, and the "first use on a 125% screen then moving to 100%" scenario cannot occur as described. (2) The real native sources are 64 px rasters at DPR 1 (Gui.getIcon wraps a BitmapFactory pixmap; the finder's native_gray_metrics.json shows every gray icon's availableSizes capped at [20,24,32,40,48,60,64] even though RASTER_SIZES asks for 80/96, and one icon, PartDesign_CompPrimitiveAdditive, is a 16 px raster). (3) An offscreen PySide6 probe with QT_SCALE_FACTOR=1.5 running the real grayscale_icon on a 64 px raster native confirms the cache holds 30/36/48/60/64 px entries tagged DPR 1.5. Requesting the icon at DPR 1.5 returns the 30 px entry bit-exactly (mean/max diff 0.0 vs a direct render). Requesting at DPR 1.0 (the "other monitor" case) returns a 30→20 downscale whose pixels differ from a single-step 64→20 render by mean 0.00-0.07 and max 1.3-1.7 on a 0-255 scale, with identical edge-sharpness (mean gradient 17.04 vs 17.06, 23.65 vs 23.66, 16.79 vs 16.79 for pierce/fillet/dimension). That is below any visible threshold; the finder's own acceptance criterion ("pixel diff at DPR 1.0 and 1.5 shows no resampling blur") already holds at HEAD, and the proposed per-DPR cache key would change nothing visible. (4) Gray fallbacks are somewhat softer than SVG neighbours (e.g. fillet 23.65 vs 26.00, dimension 16.79 vs 20.10), but that gap comes from downscaling a 64 px (or 16 px) raster source and is the same on every screen; it is finding 1's domain, not a DPR-cache effect. Net: the cross-screen softness claim is refuted; what remains is at most a cosmetic tidy-up (pass an explicit DPR or use a QIconEngine) with no measurable benefit.
refuted.refute_evidence: Probe: C:\Users\Kurtz\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Kurtz-Documents-KURT\9cc762af-5a57-4f05-b709-6c7a1f497693\scratchpad\verify\dpr_probe.py (output in probe_out.txt beside it), run offscreen with the bundled pythonw.exe, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, QT_SCALE_FACTOR=1.5, no FreeCAD import, no app launch. Output: "qt 6.8.3 app.devicePixelRatio 1.5"; raster64 natives -> gray availableSizes [30,36,48,60,64] device px; request 20@1.0 -> 20x20 dpr 1.0, 20@1.25 -> 25x25, 20@1.5 -> 30x30, 20@2.0 -> 40x40; DPR1.0 cached-vs-direct mean|diff| 0.04/0.07/0.00, max 1.3/1.7/0.0, sharpness equal; DPR1.5 diff 0.00. Native base size evidence: docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/icon-audit/native_gray_metrics.json (22 icons sizes [20,24,32,40,48,60,64], 1 icon [16]) and native_gray.log ("app True 6.8.3 dpr 1.0"). Qt docs: QGuiApplication::devicePixelRatio "Returns the highest screen device pixel ratio found on the system". Callers: ui.py:428 tool_icon -> icon_for(..., native=Gui.getIcon(...)), ui.py:1681/1726/1737/1813 history/parts rows with native=obj.ViewObject.Icon; originals at presentation_icons.py:81-84 are QIcon(path.svg) (QSvgIconEngine, per-request render) as the finder said. Caveat on the probe: a synthetic SVG-engine native (not the real-world case) showed large diffs between a direct 20 px render and the 30->20 cached path, attributable to the test SVGs' stroke rasterisation, not to the cache; it does not bear on FreeCAD's raster natives. Unverified aside outside this finding's scope: _native_cache is keyed by native.cacheKey(), and obj.ViewObject.Icon likely constructs a fresh QIcon (new cacheKey) on every call, so each refresh() of unmapped "Part" rows may add new entries to _native_cache rather than hitting it.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Nothing from this mechanism. What he does see on his 150% desktop is finding 1: the gray raster fallbacks (Use, Hole, 18 of 19 sketch constraints, 63 of 104 installed catalog tools per the review's own runtime_catalog_icon_resolution.json) are heavier and darker 64px FreeCAD silhouettes beside 24-grid line originals, and that looks the same on every monitor. A 150%-built cache shown on a 100% screen measures identical edge sharpness to a 100%-built one, so dragging the window between monitors changes nothing he could see. He models mostly through the bridge, so toolbar glyph quality is low-exposure for him anyway.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: In sketch mode the constraints and geometry bars mix two icon languages, which reads as unfinished next to Onshape's uniform set; that is finding 1. They would not perceive any monitor-to-monitor sharpness difference in the fallbacks because there is none measurable, and one tool (Additive primitives, a 16px native raster) is soft everywhere regardless of DPI.
judge.reasoning:
Source confirmed at C:\Users\Kurtz\Documents\KURT\CADkz\Codex\kurtshape\src\kurtshape\presentation_icons.py: RASTER_SIZES line 17, SVG originals lines 81-84, grayscale_icon lines 103-118 calling native.pixmap(QSize(size,size), mode, Off) and caching by cacheKey. Supporting claims check out: startup.py line 17 mentions the mixed-DPI desktop, docs/onshape-design-audit/THEME-REPAIR.md line 27 says actual scaling was 150%, the bundle is Qt 6.8.3/PySide6 with lib/qt6/plugins/iconengines/qsvgicon.dll present, so the originals really do render per request. The review's own probe (docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/icon-audit/native_gray.py, log, metrics) ran only at DPR 1.0 and shows native sources are 64px rasters (availableSizes cap at 64; Additive primitives is 16px).

Mechanism: in Qt 6, QIcon.pixmap(QSize) with no DPR uses qApp.devicePixelRatio(), which is the highest DPR of any attached screen, so the gray cache is always built at the max DPR regardless of which screen is used first; the finding's 'first use on 125% then move to 100%' framing is wrong in that detail, but the two-step resample (64 -> size*maxDPR -> size) on lower-DPR screens is real.

Probe (one headless PySide6-only run, offscreen, isolated env, in the scratchpad verify folder: dpr_probe.py / dpr_probe.json): a 64px raster QIcon fed through the real grayscale_icon with pixmap() answered at DPR 1.5 produced entries [30,36,48,60,64] exactly as predicted; requesting 20 and 24 logical at DPR 1.0 returned correctly tagged 20x20/24x24 pixmaps whose alpha edge-gradient sharpness equals the 100%-built cache to two decimals (e.g. 51.85 vs 51.85 for pierce at 20; 44.17 vs 44.17 at 24) with mean pixel diff 0.08-0.22/255 and max 2-23 on isolated pixels; requesting at DPR 1.5 hits the exact 30/36px entries. Qt's smooth downscale of a 64px source is effectively idempotent here, so there is no resampling blur to see. Three glyphs tested (pierce, remove, fillet); the content differs from FreeCAD's gradient-heavy icons but the scaling path is identical, so the conclusion transfers.

Judgment: the finding filed itself honestly as a low-confidence hypothesis, and the probe refutes the visible consequence. Classification stays hypothesis (not a verified defect, not a design weakness worth a ticket); severity low because even if true the impact would be marginal softness on glyphs already visually inconsistent per finding 1. Recommend closing it or folding one sentence into finding 1, whose QIconEngine/alpha-tint renderer would make per-DPR caching moot. Keying _native_cache by (cacheKey, dpr) is harmless and trivial but buys nothing visible. Side note for whoever touches this code: tool_icon() in ui.py (lines 418-428) calls Gui.getIcon per action and the tree rows pass obj.ViewObject.Icon, each a fresh QIcon with a new cacheKey, so _native_cache never hits across calls and grows on tree refreshes; that is a separate, minor efficiency observation, not this finding.
judge.risk: None. The proposed DPR-keyed cache is a one-line safe change but delivers no visible improvement; doing nothing carries no risk either. The only caveat on the verdict is that the probe used a 64px raster rendered from a KurtShape SVG rather than a real FreeCAD icon; the Qt scaling path is the same, so the no-blur result holds.

merged.title: Face hover outline colour is hard-coded instead of following View/HighlightColor; matches the live profile's blue preselection only by coincidence
merged.evidence: Outline (0.16,0.42,0.88) #296BE0 vs native SelectionColor #3B5BDB (exp2b) and native preselection #007A00 for edges/vertices; three different cues for two states.
merged.scenario: Hover a face (blue outline), hover an edge (green), click (blue fill).
merged.consequence: Hover does not read as one state; the blue outline on a blue-selected neighbour face is hard to see.
merged.reproduction: Hover then click adjacent faces on the plate.
merged.proposed_change: Drive the outline colour from the same theme token as View/HighlightColor (after the selection-colour finding) and keep selection distinct; width 1.25x edge width scaled by DPI.
merged.acceptance: One hover hue for faces/edges/vertices; selection hue distinct; grab assertions.
merged.refute_reasoning: The code fact holds: src/kurtshape/hover_outline.py:154 hard-codes material.diffuseColor = (0.16, 0.42, 0.88) (#296BE0) and line 157 a fixed 2.5 px width; nothing in src/ reads View/HighlightColor, no test or macro asserts the colour, and git log (4681ddf 2026-10-13, 659b5e7 2026-10-15) shows no later fix, so it is not already solved. But the finding's evidence, scenario and consequence are wrong for the running app. The #3B5BDB selection / #007A00 preselection figures are fresh-profile defaults (docs/fable-deep-review/visual-proposals/README.md:104; validation-session user.cfg files such as runtime/view-interaction-validation/run-*/user-data/user.cfg). The live profile that launch-kurtshape.ps1 points FREECAD_USER_HOME at (runtime/user-data/user.cfg, group View, lines 179 and 183, written 2026-10-17) holds HighlightColor=611232767=0x246EABFF (#246EAB, blue preselection) and SelectionColor=899696639=0x35A047FF (#35A047, green selection); no repo code sets these (grep of src/tools/docs finds only reads, and tools/theme-startup-validation.FCMacro:128 records them as preserved native values). In that profile the face outline (#296BE0) and the native edge/vertex preselection (#246EAB) are both blue and close in hue while selection is green, so hover already reads as one state and there is no blue outline over a blue-selected neighbour. Even in a fresh profile the "hard to see" consequence does not hold: validation/onshape-interaction-pass/view-interaction/face-selected.png (Oct 4) shows the selected face lit to pale #cdf3ff (result.json selected_interior_color) with the dark-blue outline plainly visible on it. What remains is a theming-hygiene weakness: the outline colour is a literal rather than derived from View/HighlightColor, so it coincides with the native hover hue only because of Kurt's preference choice and diverges (blue line vs green native edge hover) in any fresh or reset profile, e.g. every validation session. Low severity, no user-visible defect in the live shell.
merged.refute_evidence: Live profile values: runtime/user-data/user.cfg lines 179/183 under <FCParamGroup Name="View"> (line 149): HighlightColor 611232767 -> #246EAB, SelectionColor 899696639 -> #35A047; same values in runtime/design-workspace/user-data/user.cfg (2026-10-06). Fresh/validation profiles (runtime/appearance-model-validation/*/user.cfg, runtime/view-interaction-validation/run-*/user-data/user.cfg): HighlightColor 7995647 -> #007A00, SelectionColor 995875839 -> #3B5BDB. No setter: grep for HighlightColor/SelectionColor in src/ and tools/ finds only reads (src/kurtshape/theme.py sets sketch colours only; tools/theme-startup-validation.FCMacro:128 lists SelectionColor/HighlightColor as preserved). Rendering: validation/onshape-interaction-pass/view-interaction/result.json records hover interior #92989e and selected interior #cdf3ff with the outline present in both face-hover.png and face-selected.png; tools/view-interaction-validation.FCMacro checks only that the hover changes no interior pixel, never the outline colour. docs/SOLIDWORKS_NAVIGATION.md:31 and docs/onshape-workflows/IMPLEMENTATION.md:32 describe the outline only as "transient blue boundary"; DESIGN.md:164 requires native selection/preselection highlights to stay distinct, which the live profile satisfies. The native edge-hover in sketch edit (validation/sketch-presentation/sketch-references/hover-body-edge-before-u.png) is a separate blue sketch adapter, not View/HighlightColor.

merged.title: Read-only search field and selectable status labels take keyboard focus and swallow single-key tools
merged.evidence: SearchField is a QLineEdit(readOnly) with default StrongFocus; make_message_copyable gives the status message and the preview verdict TextSelectableByMouse|Keyboard plus StrongFocus. shortcuts.py:271-281 treats any QLineEdit (read-only included) and any selectable QLabel as a text input, and :226 then returns False for every key except Escape and Ctrl+S/N/O.
merged.scenario: Kurt clicks the toolbar search box (or closes the Alt+C dialog, which returns focus there), or clicks the red status message to select and copy an error, then presses L, C, D, N, F, P, S, Delete or Enter.
merged.consequence: The key does nothing (or Enter/Space reopens the search dialog) until he clicks the viewport; feels like a dead keyboard after reading an error.
merged.reproduction: GUI: click the status bar message, then press L inside a sketch; or click 'Search tools…', close the dialog with Escape, press Shift+E.
merged.proposed_change: Give SearchField Qt.NoFocus (it opens a dialog on click/Enter anyway) and give the copyable labels Qt.ClickFocus only, plus in _text_input treat a read-only QLineEdit and a QLabel as non-text (or route single-key shortcuts when the focused label has no selection). After the search dialog closes, return focus to the active MDI viewport.
merged.risk: Copy-by-keyboard on the label needs focus; ClickFocus keeps that while Tab navigation skips it.
merged.acceptance: GUI recipe: after clicking the status label, L starts a line; after closing Alt+C, Shift+E opens Extrude. Shortcut unit test for _text_input with a read-only QLineEdit.

merged.title: 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' is shown in the feature panel while a sketch is being edited (the model bar, with Rebuild, is hidden at that point)
merged.lines: ui.py:1396-1401 (status_detail), 1749-1752 (label set in refresh), 1250-1256 (inspect/refresh on status change during the lease), 3407 (model bar hidden while sketching); core.py:1321-1326 (Touched -> pending), 1341 (needs_rebuild); screenshots docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/ghost-circle-before.png and circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6)
merged.evidence: docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/circle-drag-after.png (Oct 6, current light shell) bottom-left reads 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' while 'DragCircle' is in edit and the status bar says 'Sketch editing …'. core.py:1325-1326 marks any Touched Sketcher object as pending → status needs_rebuild; ui.py:1400-1401 renders that as 'Rebuild required'.
merged.consequence: Two status surfaces disagree; a newcomer may press Rebuild (disabled anyway) or worry the model is broken. Diminishes trust in the real 'Rebuild required · geometry engine changed' message.
merged.reproduction: Open any sketch and read the left status label.
merged.proposed_change: In status_detail, when self.active_sketch() (or state['active_sketch_edit']) show 'Editing <sketch label> · changes apply on Finish'; or in _build_status ignore the Touched flag of the leased sketch.
merged.acceptance: GUI recipe sketch-edit-state: left status never contains 'Rebuild required' during a lease unless a rebuild_reason is set.
merged.refute_reasoning: Viewed both Oct 6 screenshots (docs/sketch-interaction-reliability/evidence/screenshots/ghost-circle-before.png and circle-drag-after.png, current light shell): bottom-left panel reads 'Rebuild required · pending model changes' while DragCircle is in edit, the native Sketch Edit task is open and the status bar says 'Sketch editing · ...'. Code at HEAD reproduces it: core._build_status (core.py 1321-1326) appends any Touched Sketcher::/PartDesign:: object to pending with no exemption for the leased sketch (sketch_edits is only reported as active_sketch_edit at core.py 1403, never consulted here), status becomes needs_rebuild at 1341, and ui.status_detail (1396-1401) renders needs_rebuild as 'Rebuild required · ' + rebuild_reason_text, which falls back to 'pending model changes' when no RebuildReason is stored. The label is set from refresh() at ui.py 1749-1752, and the panel re-inspects and refreshes whenever build_status changes during the lease (ui.py 1250-1256), so the moment the first geometry edit touches the sketch the left status flips. begin_sketch_edit itself (core.py 1601-1618) does not touch the sketch, so 'every sketch edit session' means every session with at least one edit, which is every real one. Git: the Touched line dates from the 2026-10-02 baseline (b65f066) and status_detail is unchanged through f57d592; not solved. One correction: the Rebuild button is not 'disabled anyway' while sketching, the whole model bar is hidden (ui.py 3407), so a newcomer cannot press it; the harm is the contradictory message and the diluted meaning of the real 'geometry engine changed' rebuild notice. Classification design_weakness, severity low are honest.
merged.refute_evidence: Both Oct 6 screenshots show the message with only a sketch in the document (no solids), where the label would otherwise read 'Sketches only · mm'. test_build_status.py asserts needs_rebuild in several places but never during a sketch lease, so a UI-side fix in status_detail touches no bridge contract or test.

judge.kurt_would_notice: Probably not day to day (he rarely watches the left status while sketching), but if a bridge script inspects mid-lease it sees build_status needs_rebuild, and the 'Rebuild required' wording stops meaning anything once it appears in every sketch session.
judge.newcomer_would_notice: Two surfaces disagree: the status bar says 'Sketch editing' while the panel says the model needs a rebuild. They look for a Rebuild button (hidden in sketch mode), wonder whether the model is broken, and learn to ignore the one message that matters after an engine change.
judge.risk: Low for the UI fix (status_detail shows 'Editing <sketch label> · changes apply on Finish' when state['active_sketch_edit'] is set). Changing _build_status to ignore the leased sketch's Touched flag alters the bridge's build_status during a lease and should get its own test; prefer the presentation-side change.

merged.title: Recovery checkpoints are never pruned: every new or recovered document leaves a permanent pair and unsaved ones stay in the Recovery menu forever
merged.evidence: recovery.py contains no unlink/remove/rmtree (grep); `_publish` only replaces the same DocumentId's pair and keeps `.previous.*` (98-104); `available` hides a pair only when its source_file exists and is newer (160-162), so documents never saved are listed indefinitely. Probe B8: three `new` documents + forced checkpoint, documents closed -> directory holds 6 files and available() lists 'Throwaway 0/1/2' with source_file None. ui.py:2854-2877 checkpoints every open document on idle after 30 s.
merged.scenario: Agents routinely `new` a document per dry run or rebuild (build_bridge.py:30 `s.call('new', ...)`; bone-mallet opens/creates per run); each one idle for 30 s gets a checkpoint pair the size of the model (dodec hub: 9.7 MB per FCStd, plus .previous copies). Kurt's Recovery menu accumulates 'Untitled part · checkpoint' rows from weeks ago.
merged.consequence: Disk growth in runtime/project-recovery and a Recovery menu where the one checkpoint that matters is buried; I could not inspect the live folder (out of scope) so current size is unknown.
merged.reproduction: scratch controller_probe.py section B8; or in the app: New, wait 40 s idle, close without saving, open Document > Recovery.
merged.proposed_change: RecoveryStore.retire(document_id): delete the pair (+ .previous) when a document is closed after a successful save newer than the checkpoint, or when the user discards an unsaved document in the native close prompt (hook Gui document close via DocumentState.slotDeletedDocument -> controller -> recovery.retire if `last[...]` revision was saved); cap unsaved pairs (keep newest 20 by saved_at) at startup; add 'Clear old checkpoints' under Recovery. Never delete a pair whose document is still open or has an unfinished sketch.
merged.dependencies: Needs the close hook to know whether the user chose Discard; otherwise prune only saved-and-closed documents plus an age cap.
merged.risk: Deleting the wrong pair defeats recovery: restrict to pairs whose source_file mtime >= saved_at (the same predicate available() already trusts) and to an explicit user action for unsaved ones.
merged.acceptance: Native test: new -> checkpoint -> save -> close -> pair gone; new -> checkpoint -> close unsaved -> pair kept and listed; startup cap keeps 20 newest. Gate: test_review_followup checkpoint/corrupt tests unchanged.

merged.title: Agents cannot tell which KurtShape build is running: capabilities and the session file carry engine and contract only, no source revision; argument tables are not exposed
merged.symbol: Controller._dispatch capabilities branch; Bridge.__init__ session file; Controller.ARGS
merged.evidence: capabilities returns contract, contract_revision, session_id, measurement, geometry_check, operations (names only), preview_operations, import_formats, assembly, retry, request_size_limit_bytes, engine (probe B1 key list); no build/git field and no per-op argument lists although `Controller.ARGS` has 73 entries (B10). Session file keys: contract, contract_revision, pid, session_id, token, url (probe A9). AGENTS.md:44 keeps a hand-written list of which commits need an app restart; Kurt's running app (started 01:28) lacks hole/add_polyline/describe_dress_up and only op-name probing reveals that. The assistant_client never checks that the session `pid` is alive (bridge.close unlinks the file only on clean shutdown, 120-128), so a crashed app leaves a stale file that AGENTS.md step 1 treats as 'running'.
merged.scenario: Every agent session today: read capabilities, compare op names against docs, guess whether a fix is loaded; after a crash, read a stale session file and fail with a connection error.
merged.consequence: Wasted probing, wrong assumptions about behavior differences between checkout and running app (exactly the situation this review had to caveat).
merged.proposed_change: At Controller import compute `BUILD = {git_head, git_dirty?, source_sha256 of src/kurtshape/*.py, started_at}` (read .git/HEAD and refs/packed-refs with stdlib; fall back to source hash when .git is unreadable due to the Windows ownership check) and return it in capabilities, diagnostics and the session file; add `arguments:{op:sorted(ARGS[op])}` and `required` to capabilities; assistant_client.send verifies the session pid is alive (ctypes OpenProcess) and prints 'app build X vs checkout Y' on mismatch.
merged.dependencies: Required-field table from the validation finding.
merged.acceptance: test: capabilities.build.git_head == `git rev-parse HEAD` of the checkout under test (or source_sha256 matches a recomputed hash); session file includes build and started_at; client refuses a session whose pid is dead with a clear message.

merged.title: Session retry cap (4096 IDs) is reachable in a day of iterative agent builds and the only remedy is an app restart
merged.evidence: request_ledger.py:15 `session_request_limit = limit * 8` (4096); 38-39 rejects `request_capacity_reached` once records+expired reach it; `expired` never shrinks. A full dodec-hub bridge build is ~70 tracked mutations (projects/dodec-hub/build-bridge.log, 73 lines); bone-mallet rebuilds in place every run (build_mallet_kurtshape.py:52-56 delete_features then full rebuild, ~40 mutations); failed attempts consume IDs too. ~60-100 iterations in one app session exhaust it. Memory is not the issue: a 26-feature plate inspect result is 15 KB (probe B1), so 512 cached results are ~8 MB.
merged.scenario: A long modeling day against the same running app (Kurt leaves it open; AGENTS.md discourages restarts) ends with every mutation rejected as request_capacity_reached; the agent must ask Kurt to restart with unsaved work open.
merged.consequence: Hard stop mid-build with a message that reads like a server fault.
merged.reproduction: Count: `grep -c '^ok' build-bridge.log` per run x number of runs in a session; or register 4096 IDs in a unit test (test_bridge.py:443 shows the path with limit=1).
merged.proposed_change: Make the tombstone set an LRU bounded by count and age (e.g. 65536 entries or 24 h), keep the 512-result cache, and report `retry.remaining_requests` in capabilities and `queue_wait_ms`-style in each mutation response so clients see the ceiling coming; document that eviction of a tombstone re-enables the ID (acceptable: IDs are UUIDs).
merged.risk: A replay of a very old ID after tombstone expiry would execute again; UUID clients never resend old IDs, and a 24 h floor keeps the exactly-once window realistic.
merged.acceptance: Test registers 10000 unique IDs without capacity error while the result cache stays at 512; capabilities exposes remaining count. Verification still needed: confirm with Kurt how long the app typically stays up and how many rebuild iterations a session sees.
